title: Review of Investment Management Model for the Sinking Fund
topics: investment;
brief: The Toronto Investment Board votes on authorizing hiring an independent investment consultant to assess whether an Outsourced Chief Investment Officer (OCIO) model would suit management of the city's Sinking Fund — delegating functions like asset allocation and manager selection to an external firm — and, if the consultant recommends it, to help run the OCIO search and selection. The item affects how the city's debt repayment reserves are managed. The board decides.

title: Investment Plan Update

The plan also seeks authority to hire Aon for an Asset Liability Management study in 2026. The item affects how the city's invested funds balance long-term returns against near-term cash needs. The board decides.

title: Dissolution of TO Live's Environmental, Social and Governance Committee and Appointment of Members to TO Live’s Finance and Audit, and Human Resources and Stakeholder Relations Committees
topics: advisory committees; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups
brief: Dissolving its Environmental, Social and Governance Committee and transfer its responsibilities to the Human Resources and Stakeholder Relations Committee, effective immediately upon approval, goes to the TO Live board for approval. The board chair's proposal says very few matters have come through that committee, its meetings have frequently been cancelled, and keeping it separate has made quorum difficult on the board's other committees. The board is also asked to confirm the membership of its two remaining committees, the Finance and Audit Committee and the Human Resources and Stakeholder Relations Committee, placing former ESG committee members and newly appointed board members, while the board chair steps down from the HR committee he previously chaired.

brief: A new Executive Compensation policy (Policy 235), developed to align with the City of Toronto's guiding principles for senior executive pay, goes to TO Live's board for approval. The policy sets the framework for how executive compensation is determined. The board will decide whether to approve it.

title: Indigenous Action Plan - Update
body: TO Live - Environmental, Social and Governance Committee
topics: First Nations; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples
brief: This is a procedural item: TO Live's board is asked to receive an update on the agency's Indigenous Action Plan for information. No policy change is proposed.

title: 2026 Six-Month Occupational Health and Safety Status Report
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will receive the 2026 six-month occupational health and safety status report, covering employee accident rates and related safety initiatives for the first six months of 2026. The Chief Human Resources Officer recommends the board receive the report for information.

title: 2026 Six-Month Guest Safety Report
topics: zoos;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will receive the 2026 six-month guest safety report, covering guest incidents and related public safety initiatives for the first six months of the 2026 calendar year. The Chief Human Resources Officer recommends the board receive the report for information.

title: Attendance and Revenue Report - July 2026
topics: financial reports, zoos; annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will receive the attendance and revenue report for July 2026, with visitor statistics and revenue results for January 1 through July 31, 2026 and a dashboard of key metrics. The Chief Transformation Officer recommends the board receive the report for information.

title: Toronto Zoo Operational Update
topics: zoos;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will receive a verbal update on zoo operations from Dolf DeJong, Chief Executive Officer of the Toronto Zoo. No recommendation is attached.

title: Ontario Bat Conservation Research Update
topics: conservation, wildlife; bats; coyotes; deer; foxes; raccoons; skunks; snakes; wild animals, environmental conservation; environmental improvements; environmental management; environmental protection; environmental stewardship; greening
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will receive a presentation from Alannah Lymburner and Alexandra Israel, Field Conservation Stewards, on recent fieldwork conducting conservation research with endangered Ontario bats. The presentation is for information; no decision is described.

title: Annual Chief Executive Officer Performance Review
topics: Toronto Transit Commission; ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the TTC Board will conduct the annual CEO performance review, led by the People, Culture and Governance Committee. The committee sets the CEO's performance objectives, completes the annual evaluation required by the CEO's employment contract, including an assessment of the CEO's integrity and the culture of integrity established, and reports results to the Board. The Board is asked to adopt the recommendation in Confidential Attachment 1 and keep it private.

title: Fitness For Duty Grievance Update
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, legal matters; legal issues, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the TTC Board will receive an update on the fitness-for-duty arbitration decision and next steps. On July 13, 2026, Arbitrator Trachuk allowed ATU Local 113's policy grievance challenging the TTC's random drug and alcohol testing under its Fitness for Duty Policy, and ordered the reinstatement of all eight grievors in the related test cases. The Board is asked to approve the confidential recommendation and keep the information private under client-solicitor privilege.

title: 1555 Birchmount Road - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 26 139212 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal law, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the owner of 1555 Birchmount Road is appealing a property standards order issued April 7, 2026 (file 26 139212 PRS 00 IV) to the Property Standards Committee. The committee hears the appeal and can uphold, amend, or rescind the order.

title: 1555 Birchmount Road - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 26 139211 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: an appeal of the property standards order for 1555 Birchmount Road goes before the Property Standards Committee. The order was issued April 7, 2026 (file 26 139211 PRS 00 IV). The committee will decide whether the order stands, changes, or is cancelled.

title: Fort York Integrated Operations and Heritage Stewardship Study
topics: community development, economic development, heritage designation; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing, community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to receive, for information, a report describing plans for an Integrated Operations and Heritage Stewardship Study of the Fort York National Historic Site, the nationally significant heritage asset and archaeological site owned and operated by the city as one of its Toronto History Museums. As the surrounding area intensifies, the site faces pressure to balance public programming and learning, community needs, heritage conservation, archaeological protection, public access and revenue-generating activities. The study would set a coordinated approach to managing the site. No approval of the study or policy change is being requested at this stage.

title: 2273, 2277 and 2279 Bloor Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 15-storey mixed-use building with 60 homes and retail at grade is proposed at 2273, 2277 and 2279 Bloor Street West. The 5,545 square metre building includes 116 square metres of retail and a 0.4-metre right-of-way widening along the Bloor Street West frontage, within a Protected Major Transit Station Area. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change, which would add 60 homes to Bloor Street West.

title: 1730 Bloor Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 25-storey mixed-use building with 200 homes is proposed at 1730 Bloor Street West, with retail at grade and office space on the ground floor and part of the second floor. The 14,569 square metre building includes 454 square metres of non-residential space and a 0.4-metre right-of-way widening along the Bloor Street West frontage. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change, which would add 200 homes to Bloor Street West.

title: 570, 572, 574,576 Sherbourne Street, and 29 and 37 Linden Street - Alterations to and Demolition of Attributes on Designated Heritage Properties and Removal of a Building Under Part IV, Sections 33 and 34(2) of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: [activities in planning and development], buildings, demolitions, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Alterations to the designated heritage properties at 570, 572, 574 and 576 Sherbourne Street and 29 and 37 Linden Street, removal of the heritage building at 29 Linden Street, and a Heritage Easement Agreement go to City Council for approval. Council approved a 69-storey residential tower on the site in October 2024; the applicant has since revised the proposal to add more Sherbourne Street land and tower massing while reducing the tower's height. The decision determines how the heritage properties are treated as the revised tower proceeds.

title: Authorization to Study the Yorkville Village Core as a Potential Heritage Conservation District
topics: heritage conservation districts, heritage designation, research; heritage districts; historic areas, studies; surveys (research)
brief: Studying the Yorkville Village Core as a potential Heritage Conservation District under Section 40(1) of the Ontario Heritage Act goes to City Council for authorization. The study area was recommended in the December 2025 Bloor-Yorkville Cultural Heritage Resource Assessment, and Council already directed heritage planning staff in April 2026 to take the steps, including community consultation, toward a possible study. Authorization would start the formal process of determining whether the area merits heritage district protection.

title: 79 Whitehall Road - Application to Demolish a Structure and Erect a New Structure in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District
topics: [activities in property], applications, demolitions, heritage conservation districts; application process, heritage districts; historic areas
brief: Demolishing an existing detached garage and building a new detached carport at the rear of 79 Whitehall Road, a C-rated property in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District, goes to City Council for approval. Heritage planning staff consider the proposal consistent with the district plan and recommend approval. The decision determines whether the carport can be built.

title: 8 Robert Street- Alterations to a Designated Property under Part V, Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act- Approval
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Alterations to the designated heritage property at 8 Robert Street, at the southern edge of the Harbord Village Heritage Conservation District, to convert the 1915 former Christian Workers' Church chapel into a four-unit residential building, go to City Council for approval. The work includes a two-storey roof addition with a mechanical penthouse, removal of most of the roof, conservation of all four elevations and the solid wood front door, restoration of the six original stained-glass windows, and exterior paint removal. The decision determines whether the chapel conversion can proceed.

title: 162 Douglas Drive - Application to Demolish a Structure and Erect a New Structure in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District
topics: demolitions, heritage conservation districts, structures; heritage districts; historic areas
brief: Demolishing an existing detached garage and building a new 1.5-storey garden suite at the rear of 162 Douglas Drive, a C-rated property in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District, goes to City Council for approval. Heritage planning staff consider the proposal consistent with the district plan and recommend approval. The decision determines whether the garden suite can be built.

title: 468-470 Queen Street West- Demolition of a Designated Heritage Property under Part V, Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act- Approval
topics: [activities in planning and development], demolitions, heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Demolishing the building at 468 to 470 Queen Street West, a non-contributing property within the Queen Street West Heritage Conservation District, goes to City Council for approval. The demolition would make way for a new public park at the corner of Queen Street West and Augusta Avenue, and heritage planning staff support the application as consistent with the district plan. The decision determines whether the park can proceed on the site.

title: 72 Henry Street, 258 Wallace Avenue, and 80 Ward Street - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Adding 72 Henry Street, 258 Wallace Avenue and 80 Ward Street to the city's Heritage Register for their cultural heritage value goes to City Council for approval. The 72 Henry Street property, in the Kensington-Chinatown neighbourhood between College and Cecil streets, holds a 2.5-storey detached house-form building constructed between 1886 and 1887, immediately south of the site proposed for a 45-storey tower. Listing recognizes the properties' heritage value but does not designate them.

title: 3044 Dundas Street West - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage conservation districts, heritage designation, heritage preservation; heritage districts; historic areas, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Adding 3044 Dundas Street West (including entrance addresses 3046 and 3048) to the city's Heritage Register for its cultural heritage value goes to City Council for approval. The circa-1908 commercial main-street red-brick building at the northwest corner of Dundas Street West and McMurray Avenue is noted for its Romanesque Revival architecture and ground-level storefronts, and for contributing to the Dundas streetscape and the early development history of the Junction area. Listing recognizes the building's heritage value but does not designate it.

title: 2345 Yonge Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, building plans, zoning bylaws; building records, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This appeal report concerns the application for two mixed-use towers of 56 and 54 storeys (179.5 and 173.5 metres) on a 10-storey base at 2345 Yonge Street. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on April 9, 2026, after Council did not decide within the Planning Act timeframe. Staff recommend that the City Solicitor and appropriate staff attend the tribunal hearing to oppose the application in its current form while continuing discussions with the applicant; City Council decides on the instructions.

title: 262-266 St. George Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, residential properties, zoning bylaws; residential real estate, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This appeal report concerns the application for an 18-storey residential building (61 metres) with 121 homes, including 14 replacement rental units, at 262 to 266 St. George Street, which would demolish 40 dwelling rooms and three rental homes. The application was revised in December 2025 to increase height and density and to redesignate the lands from Neighbourhoods to Apartment Neighbourhoods; the applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on April 24, 2026, after Council did not decide in time. The report recommends City Council's directions to the City Solicitor for the tribunal hearing.

title: 445 to 451 Adelaide Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This appeal report concerns the application for a 17-storey non-residential building with 144 hotel suites at 445 to 451 Adelaide Street West, which would demolish four existing heritage properties. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on May 15, 2026, after Council did not decide within the Planning Act timeframe. Staff recommend that the City Solicitor and appropriate staff attend the tribunal hearing to oppose the application in its current form while continuing discussions with the applicant; City Council decides on the instructions.

title: 4 Gilead Place - Official Plan and Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: official plan amendments, zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse the application for a 20-storey residential tower (80.5 metres) with 297 homes at 4 Gilead Place. Staff say the development does not fit the existing or planned context of the site, that the site cannot appropriately accommodate the proposed form, and that the height, massing, setbacks and stepbacks are not acceptable given the site's size, configuration and location. The decision would block the tower as proposed.

title: 120 Eglinton Avenue East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: official plan amendments, planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse the application for a 70-storey mixed-use tower (219 metres) with 555 homes at 120 Eglinton Avenue East. The proposal would not replace the site's existing 5,475 square metres of office space, which the Official Plan requires to be replaced in full, and staff say it does not conform to the Official Plan or the Yonge-Eglinton Secondary Plan. The decision would block the tower as proposed.

title: 324 Cherry Street and 429 and 455 Lake Shore Boulevard East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The previously approved four-block Master Plan at 324 Cherry Street and 429 and 455 Lake Shore Boulevard East would be intensified under this application, with 14 mixed-use buildings including ten towers from 28 to 53 storeys. Full buildout would deliver 4,969 new homes in about 325,000 square metres of floor area (308,750 residential and 16,250 non-residential), with affordable housing and a childcare centre in the first phase, an enhanced parks and open spaces network, and a revised local street network; the report also sets out figures of $552, and $1103,. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes.

title: 1450 and 1500 O'Connor Drive Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment and Draft Plan of Subdivision Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Three mixed-use buildings and one residential building ranging from 14 to 28 storeys are proposed at 1450 and 1500 O'Connor Drive, with 863 homes and about 71,500 square metres of floor area including at least 2,260 square metres of non-residential space. The development includes a new public street, a new public park along O'Connor Drive and two publicly accessible open spaces; the non-residential space includes a daycare in Building D and ground-floor retail and commercial uses, with 513 vehicle and 966 bicycle parking spaces. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan, zoning and subdivision applications.

title: 238-280 Wellesley Street East and 650 Parliament Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A large infill development is proposed at 238 to 280 Wellesley Street East and 650 Parliament Street: a 58-storey mixed-use tower, a 9-storey residential building and a 21-storey mixed-use tower, with 1,115 new homes and 3,164.5 square metres of new non-residential space including 464.5 square metres of community space. The project extends Rose Avenue as a public street from Wellesley Street East to the south side of 77 Howard Street and adds a new 1,894 square metre public park; the existing four rental apartment buildings on the site hold 2,251 rental homes. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change.

title: 329-337 Queen Street East, 135R-141R and 139-141 Berkeley Street - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: [activities in planning and development], applications, demolitions, rental housing; application process, rental properties; rental units
brief: Demolition of 7 rental homes at 329 to 337 Queen Street East and 135R to 141R and 139 to 141 Berkeley Street, to be replaced by 7 rental units in the new 49-storey development on the site, goes to City Council for approval. The proposal includes a Tenant Assistance Plan giving existing tenants the right to return to replacement units at similar rents, plus $20,000.00 in financial compensation to mitigate hardship. The demolition decision is tied to the zoning approval for the 545-unit tower.

title: 329 to 337 Queen Street East, 135R to 141R and 139 to 141 Berkeley Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 49-storey mixed-use building (162.7 metres) with 545 homes, including seven rental replacement units, is proposed at 329 to 337 Queen Street East and 135R to 141R and 139 to 141 Berkeley Street. The project includes about 350 square metres of ground-floor non-residential space and a new 143 square metre on-site park, and would demolish seven rental homes, each to be replaced, with tenant assistance for the displaced tenants. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change, with a holding provision, alongside the related rental demolition application.

title: 47-65 Huntley Street, 2-18, 24, and 26 Linden Street and 1-11 Selby Street - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: [activities in planning and development], applications, demolitions, rental housing; application process, rental properties; rental units
brief: Demolition and replacement of 29 rental homes at 47 and 65 Huntley Street, 3 and 11 Selby Street and 2, 8, 12 and 16 Linden Street goes to City Council for approval. The related development was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, which approved the Official Plan and zoning amendments in principle in May 2024, and the proposal includes a Tenant Assistance Plan giving existing tenants the right to return at similar rents, plus $20,000.00 in financial compensation to mitigate hardship. The demolition decision is tied to the tribunal-approved redevelopment of the site.

title: 500 Dundas Street East - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 35-storey mixed-use building (122.2 metres) with 413 homes and at least 200 square metres of non-residential space is proposed at 500 Dundas Street East. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change. The decision would add 413 homes to the Dundas Street East area.

title: 215 Lake Shore Boulevard East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A multi-tower development is proposed for the western half (Phase 2) of 215 Lake Shore Boulevard East, changing a 2018 tribunal-approved mid-rise plan to allow 70- and 14-storey buildings along Lake Shore Boulevard East and a 60-storey building along Chloe Cooley Street. The project would deliver 1,383 homes, including about 195 affordable units, plus 347 square metres of retail, 468 square metres of community agency space and 2,130 square metres of publicly accessible open space; the report also sets out figures of $552, and $1103,. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes.

title: 1875 to 1901 Eglinton Avenue West, 137 Kirknewton Road and 156 Dynevor Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 34-storey mixed-use building with 446 homes is proposed at 1875 to 1901 Eglinton Avenue West, 137 Kirknewton Road and 156 Dynevor Road. The 33,237 square metre development includes 910 square metres of retail and 1,914 square metres of amenity space, plus a publicly accessible open space of over 100 square metres and a six-metre public laneway at the south end of the site that would be conveyed to the city. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes, which would add 446 homes near Eglinton Avenue West.

title: 1439 Bloor Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 33-storey apartment building with 377 homes, including 6 affordable rental units, and 994 square metres of retail and commercial space is proposed at 1439 Bloor Street West. The application considered the city-initiated Bloor Street planning framework from St. Helen's Avenue to Perth Avenue. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change, which would add 377 homes to the Bloor Street West area.

title: 34 to 50 Southport Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, urban planning, zoning bylaws; city planning; community planning; regional planning, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 32-storey building with 397 homes is proposed at 34 to 50 Southport Street, replacing the 2012 approval for 26- and 29-storey buildings plus 16 townhouses. The report sets out financial terms of $552, per short-term unit and $1103, per unit, along with $475,000.00, as part of the recommendations. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes, with a holding provision.

title: 65 Ookwemin Street - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning approvals, urban planning, zoning bylaws; city planning; community planning; regional planning, development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Zoning changes at 65 Ookwemin Street would allow low-scale non-residential uses – community, cultural, recreational, sport, entertainment and retail – while restricting certain industrial uses, to activate the site in the interim. A separate application proposing four mixed-use towers of 45, 32, 31 and 20 storeys is before the Ontario Land Tribunal and not yet in force; this application proposes no changes to height, density or built form. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change.

title: 237, 249 and 251-253 Victoria Street - Official Plan Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: An Official Plan amendment is proposed to set a block plan through a Site and Area Specific Policy for 237, 249 and 251 to 253 Victoria Street. An earlier 2022 application sought a 24-storey mixed-use building with 256 homes at 237 Victoria Street alone, and the owner appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in June 2023 after Council did not decide in time; the new application covers the full block including the properties to the north. City Council is asked to approve the amendment, which would set the planning framework for the block.

title: 64 Wellesley Street East - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Alterations to the designated heritage property at 64 Wellesley Street East, under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act, and amending the existing Heritage Easement Agreement, go to City Council for approval. The property holds the Wellesley Apartments, a five-storey multi-unit building constructed in 1931 and designated for its association with the pre-Second World War apartment building type. The application is needed because a previously approved zoning amendment for the site has been revised.

title: 64-66 Wellesley Street East and 552-570 Church Street - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Amending Report
topics: [activities in planning and development], demolitions, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: A revised rental housing demolition application for 65 rental homes at 64 to 66 Wellesley Street East and 552 to 570 Church Street goes to City Council for approval. Council approved the demolition in July 2023 alongside a 31-storey, 405-unit proposal; the applicant has since proposed a 36-storey, 409-unit building, and this report replaces the original recommendations to keep the 65 replacement rental units secured. The proposal includes a Tenant Assistance Plan with the right of return at similar rents and $20,000.00 in financial compensation to mitigate hardship.

title: 64-66 Wellesley Street East and 552-570 Church Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 36-storey mixed-use tower (122.5 metres) with 409 homes, including 65 replacement rental units, and 852 square metres of non-residential space is proposed at 64 to 66 Wellesley Street East and 552 to 570 Church Street. An Official Plan amendment is needed to allow a tall building in the Wellesley Wood Character Area, and a related rental demolition application will be considered alongside. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes, with a holding provision.

title: 79, 81, and 93 Ontario Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: [activities in planning and development], applications, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; application process, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 16-storey building (64 metres) with 98 homes and 78 square metres of non-residential space is proposed at 79, 81 and 93 Ontario Street. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change, with a holding provision. The decision would add 98 homes to the Ontario Street area.

title: 115 Jarvis Street, Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: [activities in planning and development], rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 50-storey mixed-use tower (164.5 metres) with 596 homes and 226 square metres of non-residential space is proposed at 115 Jarvis Street. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change, with a holding provision. The decision would add 596 homes to the Jarvis Street area.

title: 164-166 Isabella Street and 168 Isabella Street - Alterations to Designated Heritage Properties Under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: [activities in planning and development], agreements, heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation, tenancy agreements
brief: Alterations to the designated heritage properties at 164 to 166 and 168 Isabella Street, under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act, and a Heritage Easement Agreement, go to City Council for approval. The properties include an 1887 semi-detached residence built by James Hewlett in a late-19th-century vernacular interpretation of the Gothic Revival style, with symmetrically organized gables and a steeply pitched, complex roofline. The decision determines how the heritage buildings are conserved as the new tower is built.

title: 164-168 Isabella Street - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, planning approvals, rental housing, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals, rental properties; rental units
brief: Demolition and replacement of 38 rental homes at 164 to 166 Isabella Street, as part of the new 70-storey development on the site, goes to City Council for approval. The proposal includes a Tenant Assistance Plan giving existing tenants the right to return to replacement rental units at similar rents, plus $20,000.00 in financial compensation to mitigate hardship; in total, 50 replacement rental units are planned, including 12 studios replacing 25 existing dwelling rooms. The demolition decision is tied to the zoning approval for the 599-unit tower.

title: 164-168 Isabella Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 70-storey residential tower (228.5 metres) with 599 homes is proposed at 164 to 168 Isabella Street, including 50 rental replacement units, while two heritage buildings on the site would be preserved and moved closer to Isabella Street. The project would demolish 38 rental units and 25 rental dwelling rooms, replacing them with 50 rental units (including 12 studios for the dwelling rooms), with tenant assistance for the displaced tenants. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes, which redesignate the site from Neighbourhoods to Apartment Neighbourhoods.

title: 90 to 94 Isabella Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: approval, planning, urban planning, zoning bylaws; city planning; community planning; regional planning, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 69-storey residential tower (220.5 metres plus an 8-metre mechanical penthouse) with 818 homes is proposed at 90 to 94 Isabella Street, reconfiguring the 69-storey approval Council granted in December 2023. The tower floor plate would shrink and rotate from an east-west to a north-south orientation, removing the previously approved massing over 94 Isabella Street. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change.

title: 30-32 and 38-40 Huntley Street, 122-124 Isabella Street - Alterations to Attributes on Designated Heritage Properties Under Part IV Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: agreements, heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation, tenancy agreements
brief: Alterations to the designated heritage properties at 30 to 32 and 38 to 40 Huntley Street and 122 to 124 Isabella Street, under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act, and a Heritage Easement Agreement, go to City Council for approval. The three properties are designated under Part IV of the Act, while 34 Huntley Street is listed on the heritage register but staff found it does not meet designation criteria, and it would be demolished as part of the development. The decision determines how the heritage buildings are conserved as the new towers are built.

title: 30-34 and 38-40 Huntley Street and 112-124 Isabella Street - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval

brief: Demolition of 32 rental homes at 30 to 32 and 38 to 40 Huntley Street and 120 to 124 Isabella Street, to be replaced by 32 rental units in the new two-tower development on the site, goes to City Council for approval. The proposal includes a Tenant Assistance Plan giving existing tenants the right to return to replacement units at similar rents, plus $20,000.00 in financial compensation to mitigate hardship. The demolition decision is tied to the zoning approval for the 56- and 60-storey towers.

title: 30-34 and 38-40 Huntley Street, 112-124 Isabella Street, and a Portion of 1 Mount Pleasant Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning approvals, urban planning, zoning bylaws; city planning; community planning; regional planning, development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Two residential towers of 60 and 56 storeys (206 and 196 metres) with about 1,419 homes, including 32 rental replacement units, are proposed at 30 to 34 and 38 to 40 Huntley Street, 112 to 124 Isabella Street and air space above the office building at 1 Mount Pleasant Road. The project would demolish 34 Huntley Street, conserve 122 to 124 Isabella Street in place, and relocate and conserve 30 to 32 and 38 to 40 Huntley Street. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes, which include redesignating the lands to Mixed Use Areas.

title: 77 Howard Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 41-storey infill tower (139.5 metres) with 460 homes and 420 square metres of ground-floor non-residential space is proposed at 77 Howard Street, while the existing 24-storey rental apartment building on the site would be retained. A 713 square metre on-site parkland dedication is proposed at the northeast corner of the site. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change, with a holding provision.

title: 27 Grosvenor Street and 26 Grenville Street - Zoning By-law Amendment and Amendment to Section 37 Agreement - Decision Report - Approval
topics: [activities in planning and development], rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This item amends the 2021 approval for the two-tower development at 27 Grosvenor Street and 26 Grenville Street, changing the secured non-profit childcare centre so it sits entirely on the first floor instead of across the first and second floors. The centre keeps its 685 square metres of interior and 290 square metres of exterior space and six on-site parking spaces, while the new layout removes the need for internal staircases and elevators. City Council is asked to approve the amendment to the Section 37 agreement.

title: 137-149 Church Street and 18-20 Dalhousie Street Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The approved tower at 137 to 149 Church Street and 18 to 20 Dalhousie Street would grow from 54 to 61 storeys (175 to 201.5 metres), with the tower setback from the south property line reduced from 10 to 6.5 metres. The existing three-storey designated heritage building at 147 Church Street would be conserved and integrated into the base building. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change.

title: 1075 Bay Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The approved development at 1075 Bay Street would change under this application: required non-residential space would drop from 12,100 to a minimum of 1,815 square metres of non-residential and/or affordable housing space, while height would rise from 59 to 62 storeys (210.1 to 222 metres). An open space of about 265 square metres is proposed at the southeast corner of the site fronting Inkerman Street. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes, which trade non-residential floor area for height and affordable housing flexibility.

title: 2010-2050 Yonge Street and 15 Lola Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning & development (sc), residential properties, zoning bylaws; residential real estate, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 15-storey mixed-use building (60 metres) with 274 homes and 1,453 square metres of ground-floor commercial space is proposed at 2010 to 2050 Yonge Street and 15 Lola Road. The development would absorb a city-owned public laneway that currently serves the site and 20 Glebe Road West, which would need to be permanently closed through a separate process with the developer acquiring the lands, and off-site parkland is proposed at 24 Manor Road East. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change.

title: 1913-1951 Yonge Street, 10-22 Davisville Avenue, and 17-21 Millwood Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The approved two-tower development at 1913 to 1951 Yonge Street, 10 to 22 Davisville Avenue and 17 to 21 Millwood Road would grow taller under this application: the northern tower from 38 to 48 storeys (158.3 metres) and the southern tower from 45 to 55 storeys (179.3 metres). Elements of the original approval are kept, including 5,783 square metres of retail, preservation of the heritage building at 1913 Yonge Street, dedicated grocery store space, a privately-owned publicly-accessible open space, a north-south mid-block connection and off-site parkland dedication, with additional community benefits including $200,000.00 and $400,000.00. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change.

title: 148-158 and 162 Soudan Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: [activities in planning and development], applications, demolitions, rental housing; application process, rental properties; rental units
brief: Demolition of 17 rental homes at 148 and 162 Soudan Avenue, to be replaced by 17 rental units in the new 53-storey development on the site, goes to City Council for approval. The proposal includes a Tenant Assistance Plan giving existing tenants the right to return to replacement units at similar rents, plus $20,000.00 in financial compensation to mitigate hardship. The demolition decision is tied to the zoning approval for the 639-unit tower.

title: 148-158 and 162 Soudan Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 53-storey residential tower (175.4 metres) with 640 homes is proposed at 148 to 158 and 162 Soudan Avenue, including 17 replacement rental units and a new 173.9 square metre park. The project would demolish 17 rental homes, replacing each one, with a Tenant Assistance Plan giving existing tenants the right to return at similar rents plus financial compensation for hardship. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change, with a holding provision, alongside the related rental demolition application.

title: 835-839 Yonge Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; application process, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A mixed-use development with two towers of 49 and 41 storeys (162 and 139 metres) is proposed at 835 to 839 Yonge Street, with 922 homes and at least 750 square metres of non-residential space. The project includes a 672 square metre privately-owned publicly-accessible space at the northeast corner of Yonge and Church streets and retention of the heritage-designated facade at 835 Yonge Street, with a holding provision on the zoning. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change, with a related heritage alterations report considered alongside it.

title: 420-444 Yonge Street and 1-23 College Street (College Park) - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Amend an Existing Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage preservation, heritage properties, planning; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Alterations to the designated heritage property known as College Park at 420 to 444 Yonge Street and 1 to 23 College Street, under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act, and amending the existing Heritage Easement Agreement, go to City Council for approval. The approval is connected to the proposed three mixed-use towers of 65, 75 and 96 storeys that would rise above the seven-storey Ross and Macdonald building at the southwest corner of Yonge and College. The decision determines how the heritage building is altered and protected as the towers are built on top of it.

title: Advancing Work on Bremner Boulevard Pedestrian Safety Improvements
topics: business improvement areas, safety; bia; business improvement associations, public safety
brief: Work would advance on pedestrian safety improvements for Bremner Boulevard, a busy downtown street home to the CN Tower, which hosts up to two million visitors a year and marks its 50th anniversary this year. Community members and local institutions have raised the need for better pedestrian safety, and Transportation staff have been counting traffic at key intersections and exploring crosswalk options; more staff engagement with stakeholders is still needed. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking the Toronto and East York Community Council to keep the work moving.

title: Ontario Place Construction Management Plan for Pedestrian and Cycling Safety and Traffic Management
topics: [activities in planning and development], cycling, pedestrians, safety; bicycling, pedestrianization, public safety
brief: A Construction Management Plan is being sought for the Ontario Place redevelopment, after the province cut short the city's usual planning approval process and the normal city oversight of how the development is built was skipped. Construction will use the Lake Shore Boulevard West corridor, which staff confirm is heavily trafficked and close to Exhibition Place events like the CNE and the Toronto Caribbean Festival, and must cross the busy Martin Goodman Trail. The Toronto and East York Community Council is being asked to require the plan so pedestrian, cycling and traffic safety are managed during construction.

title: 420-444 Yonge Street and 1-23 College Street - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, demolitions, rental housing; application process, rental properties; rental units
brief: A rental housing demolition application is proposed for 420 to 444 Yonge Street and 1 to 23 College Street, to tear down 210 rental homes and replace them with 216 rental units in the first phase of the new development, inside a 65-storey tower. The proposal includes a Tenant Assistance Plan giving existing tenants the right to return to replacement units at similar rents, plus financial compensation of $20,000.00 to mitigate hardship. City Council is asked to approve the demolition application.

title: Improving Permit Parking on Old Weston Road
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations, permit parking; no parking, on-street permit parking; parking permits, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Permit parking would be introduced on the east side of Old Weston Road between Davenport Road and St. Clair Avenue West, where residents say current rules do not reflect neighbourhood needs. Many households have limited garage access and rely on curbside parking; the change would create about 25 on-street permit spaces and align the section with surrounding neighbourhood rules. Councillor Alejandra Bravo is bringing the proposal to the Toronto and East York Community Council for a decision.

title: 420-444 Yonge Street and 1-23 College Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, official plan amendments, zoning, zoning bylaws; bylaws, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A three-tower mixed-use development is proposed above the heritage-designated building at 420 to 444 Yonge Street and 1 to 23 College Street, with towers of 65, 75 and 96 storeys (227, 247 and 320 metres) built in three phases. The project would deliver 2,342 homes, including 216 replacement rental units, 6,000 square metres of event space for The Carlu, at least 23,500 square metres of hotel, commercial and retail space, and conservation of the seven-storey College Park building. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes.

title: Queen Street West - Accessible Loading Zone
topics: accessibility, loading zones; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones
brief: An accessible loading zone is proposed on Queen Street West, east of Walnut Avenue, to support TTC Wheel-Trans service for a household with limited mobility whose registration the applicant documented. Transportation Services supports the installation, which would remove two pay-and-display parking spaces during the zone's operating hours; the Toronto Parking Authority was consulted and has no objection. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the zone.

title: Yorkville Street Closure for the Toronto International Film Festival Celebration
topics: road closures; street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Yorkville Avenue would close from September 8 to September 14, 2026, for an expanded Rogers-sponsored “Red Carpet” celebration of the Toronto International Film Festival. Last year's event ran under a four-day road closure permit and drew a popular response; the 2026 proposal needs more than four days, which requires an exception to the city's street-event rules, and has the support of the Bloor Yorkville BIA and the GYRA residents association. The item asks City Council to authorize Transportation Services to approve the closure.

title: Davisville Avenue Accessible Loading Zone
topics: loading zones, parking prohibitions, permit parking; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, no parking, on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: An accessible loading zone is proposed in front of the new aquatic and multi-use community centre on the Davisville Junior Public School and Spectrum Alternative School site. The zone would give curbside access to accessible vehicles with side or rear loading ramps, such as Wheel-Trans, and to permit holders during pick-up and drop-off. The item asks City Council to adjust the stopping prohibitions on the north side of Davisville Avenue to create the zone.

title: 240 McCaul Street - Official Plan and Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Ronald McDonald House Charities Toronto wants to build a 19-storey building (61.2 metres) with 200 hotel suites at 240 McCaul Street, providing short-term accommodation for families receiving treatment at nearby hospitals. The site would need to be redesignated from Neighbourhoods to Mixed Use Areas in the Official Plan. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes, which would give families of hospital patients a place to stay close to care.

title: Reclassify Creek Place Laneway
topics: roads; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads)
brief: Creek Place in Ward 19 would be reclassified from a laneway to a public street, after residents faced long-standing problems with road servicing and access to their properties. Four properties at the north end front onto Dawes Road with rear access from Creek Place, while nine at the south end rely on it as their primary access; the right-of-way widens from four to six metres at the Donora Drive entrance to about eight metres further south. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the reclassification, which is intended to give residents a sustainable servicing solution.

title: Naming 144 Stephenson Avenue Park in Honour of Gene Domagala
topics: [activities in planning and development], naming, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: The new park at 144 Stephenson Avenue would be named in honour of Gene Domagala, a longtime Beaches-East York resident known for decades of community service and volunteerism. Mr. Domagala is described in the motion as widely respected across generations in the community, where he earned the nickname the unofficial “Mayor of the Beach.” City Council is asked to approve the naming.

title: Church Street and Wellington Street East - Commercial Loading Zones
topics: parking, parking machines, parking regulations, transportation; parking by-laws; parking bylaws, pay and display machines; pay-and-display machines, transportation services
brief: Commercial loading zones would be established on the west side of Church Street (between Colborne Street and a point 29 metres south) and on the north side of Wellington Street East (between a point 42.5 metres east of Scott Street and Leader Lane), at the request of the Old Town Toronto BIA after parking was lost on Colborne Street. The zones are public facilities that anyone actively loading or unloading merchandise may use, with no exclusive rights, and the changes carry parking charges of $7.00 and $4.50. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the zones, which would help local businesses receive deliveries.

title: 191-199 College Street and 74-76 Henry Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The approved 31-storey development at 191 to 199 College Street and 74 to 76 Henry Street would grow to 45 storeys (158.5 metres) under this application, with the unit count rising from 490 to 684 homes, including 545 affordable rental units. An Official Plan amendment is needed to change the site-specific policies reflecting the revised height and massing. City Council is asked to approve the changes, which would add nearly 200 more homes, most of them affordable rentals, to the College Street site. The earlier 2024 approval for this site, covering 408 affordable rental units, carries a $27.7 million financial impact in city records.

title: Re-opening 2026.TE31.32 - 666 Spadina Avenue - Encroachment Appeal - Walkway Platform and Bollards
topics: bollards, encroachments, sidewalks;
brief: Reopening its March 13, 2026 decision rejecting an encroachment request at 666 Spadina Avenue is up for a decision by the Toronto and East York Community Council. The building was constructed with its commercial ground floor several inches above the sidewalk and no internal ramp for barrier-free access, violating its site plan and provincial accessibility rules; the developer's request to fix it by encroaching onto the sidewalk was refused. Since then the ward councillor has negotiated a settlement agreement with the developer, and wants the matter reopened to allow the fix so the long-vacant storefronts can be used.

title: 14 Grange Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A small residential development is proposed at 14 Grange Avenue: a five-storey building at the front of the lot and a 4.5-storey building at the rear around a central courtyard, with 22 homes and no vehicular parking. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes needed to allow the project. The decision would add 22 homes to the Grange Avenue area.

title: Chin Radio Building - Loading Zone
topics: loading zones, parking regulations, signs; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, parking by-laws; parking bylaws, signage
brief: Parking rules in front of the CHIN Radio building at 622 College Street, east of Grace Street, would change to add passenger pick-up and drop-off space for the building's media, medical and technology offices and event terraces. CHIN Radio told the ward councillor the current parking prohibition does not meet the building's needs, and staff found inconsistencies in the traffic by-law for the posted parking rules on that section of College Street. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the loading zone changes.

title: Dundas Street West - Parking Amendments
topics: on-street parking, parking, parking regulations; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Parking rules on Dundas Street West between Bathurst Street and Denison Avenue would change to allow curbside parking in the one lay-by area on the south side, removing the existing peak-period parking and stopping restrictions. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik brought the request on behalf of the Scadding Court Community Centre and nearby businesses, which say the current rules make deliveries and short-term parking difficult. City Council is asked to amend the parking and traffic by-laws.

title: Continuing Commitments to Liberty Village Neighbours by Keeping Metrolinx Exhibition Station Construction off of Strachan Avenue and Neighbourhood Streets
topics: construction, traffic, transportation infrastructure; building, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, transportation network; transportation networks
brief: Metrolinx construction for Exhibition Station should stay off Strachan Avenue and Liberty Village's neighbourhood streets, under this proposal responding to residents' traffic concerns. The community, which has only one main east-west road, is worried about a new Metrolinx haul route that would let trucks pass unrestricted through the Strachan Gate to reach the construction site. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to keep the haul route commitments in place so residents and local workers can keep moving through the neighbourhood safely.

title: 701 Fleet Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A three-storey athletic training facility for the Toronto Tempo, Canada's first team in the Women's National Basketball Association, is proposed at 701 Fleet Street on city-owned land. The project would be developed under a long-term lease between the city and the Tempo, with the public getting access to the facility during the team's off-season and periodically during the season, and would also create new public parkland. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes; the lease terms will come in a separate report to the Executive Committee.

title: Through Restriction at Bloor Street West and Pauline Avenue/Collegiate Road

brief: A through-traffic restriction is proposed where the new Collegiate Road will connect Croatia Street to Bloor Street West at Pauline Avenue, as part of the development at 1141 Bloor Street West, 980 Dufferin Street and 90 Croatia Street. The new road and a traffic signal replacing the existing pedestrian crossover are expected to carry hundreds of vehicles to and from Dufferin Mall, and Pauline Avenue residents are concerned drivers will cut through the surrounding residential neighbourhood. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the restriction to limit traffic infiltration.

title: 181 to 195 Dundas Street West and 63 Centre Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 41-storey mixed-use building is proposed at 181 to 195 Dundas Street West and 63 Centre Avenue, with retail at ground level, non-residential uses on floors 2 to 20 and 135 homes above. The project needs an Official Plan amendment because it would be visible behind the protected silhouette of City Hall's West Tower, and staff say it represents appropriate intensification near the existing and planned context. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes.

title: Chinatown Tomorrow Planning Initiative - Final Report
topics: Official Plans, [activities in planning and development], development, planning; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: A West Chinatown Planning Framework and related Official Plan and zoning changes to guide growth and community investment in the West Chinatown area go to City Council for adoption. The framework is the product of the Chinatown Tomorrow initiative, an interdivisional project begun in 2019 with extensive public consultation, covering the public realm, small businesses, housing and livability, cultural heritage and built form. Adoption would set the rules shaping future development and capital investment in the neighbourhood.

title: 1113-1125 Dundas Street West - Construction Staging Area

brief: Pomerleau is building a 10-storey affordable housing building on the south side of Dundas Street West, east of Ossington Avenue, and needs to close the south sidewalk and part of the eastbound curb lane for construction staging. The closure would run for 24 months, from September 1, 2026 to September 1, 2028, with pedestrians routed through a temporary covered and protected walkway in the closed lane. City Council is asked to approve the closure because the TTC runs a transit service on Dundas Street West; the work temporarily removes five parking-machine spaces, and the applicant will pay the lost parking revenue at $4.50.

title: Improving Pedestrian Safety on Crescent Road - Non-Delegated
topics: parking, parking prohibitions, parking regulations, pedestrians, safety; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws, pedestrianization, public safety
brief: This is the companion to the Crescent Road safety motion: while one motion covers measures the community council can decide itself, this motion amends parking rules on Crescent Road between Cluny Drive and South Drive, which requires City Council approval. The parking changes are part of the response to cut-through drivers mounting the sidewalk and blocking the Rosedale 82 bus. City Council decides.

title: 1280 to 1286 College Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws, zoning designations; permitted use requests; permitted uses, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 9-storey apartment building with 76 homes is proposed at 1280 to 1286 College Street, and City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes needed to allow it. Staff say the proposal fits the city's plan for growth near transit stations and along its Avenues. The decision would add 76 homes to the College Street area.

title: Eglinton Avenue East and Lillian Street - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: pedestrians, safety, traffic control systems; pedestrianization, public safety, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Transportation Services wants traffic control signals installed at Eglinton Avenue East and Lillian Street, following its assessment of pedestrian crossing protection at the intersection. City Council must vote on the decision because the TTC runs a transit service on Eglinton Avenue East. The signals are intended to make the intersection safer for pedestrians and other vulnerable road users.

title: College Street and Manning Avenue - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: pedestrian crossovers, pedestrians, safety; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, pedestrianization, public safety
brief: Transportation Services wants traffic control signals installed at College Street and Manning Avenue, along with a ban on mid-block crossings on College Street at Manning. City Council must vote on the decision because the TTC runs a transit service on College Street. The signals are intended to make the intersection safer for pedestrians and other vulnerable road users.

title: 1167 to 1175 Bloor Street West, 34 to 42 Brock Crescent and 90 Croatia Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: A 14-storey mixed-use building is proposed at 1167 to 1175 Bloor Street West, 34 to 42 Brock Crescent and 90 Croatia Street, with 52 homes, 14 supportive group living units, plus retail and institutional space. The applicant is the non-profit Safehaven Project for Community Living, which provides rooming, respite and transitional care for children and adults with medical complexities or disabilities. City Council is asked to approve the needed Official Plan and zoning changes. The decision would add 66 homes to the area, including 14 supportive units for people with disabilities, on a site already occupied by Safehaven near a major transit station.

title: Temporary Adjustments to Traffic and Parking Regulations for 2026 Distillery Winter Village (Non-Delegated)
topics: parking, toronto transit commission, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, ttc
brief: A decision on approving the matching set of temporary traffic and parking rules for the 2026 Distillery Winter Village (November 12, 2026 to January 3, 2027) covering transit-served streets — including Parliament Street, Mill Street, and Front Street East — that only city council can change sits with City Council.

title: Temporary Adjustments to Traffic and Parking Regulations for 2026 Canadian National Exhibition (Non-Delegated)
topics: parking regulations, traffic, transportation; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, parking by-laws; parking bylaws, transportation services
brief: The decision on approving the matching set of temporary traffic and parking rules for the 2026 CNE (August 21 to September 7) covering transit-served streets — including Dufferin Street and Springhurst Avenue — that only city council can change rests with City Council. The measures would limit traffic infiltration into neighbourhood streets and prioritize parking for residents.

title: Donlands Avenue - Parking Amendments

brief: Whether to make the corner parking ban on the west side of Donlands Avenue north of Aldwych Avenue stricter — changing it to a standing prohibition — so the curb stays clear for better sightlines for turning drivers and safer school pickup and drop-off now sits with City Council. Council approval is required because the TTC runs transit on Donlands Avenue.

title: 1497 and 1501 Queen Street West - Alterations to Designated Heritage Properties and Demolition of Heritage Attributes on a Designated Heritage Property under Sections 33 and 34(1)1 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: [activities in planning and development], agreements, demolitions, heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, tenancy agreements
brief: City Council has the final say on whether to approve alterations to the heritage-designated buildings at 1497 and 1501 Queen Street West — including partial demolition of heritage features at 1501 — under Sections 33 and 34(1)1 of the Ontario Heritage Act, and to enter into a heritage easement agreement. The changes would expand the existing Parkdale Activity Recreation Centre campus, adding affordable housing and community services in a new building behind the partially retained facades. Both properties are designated under Part IV of the Heritage Act.

title: Oriole Parkway - Parking By-law Amendments
topics: by-laws, parking, parking regulations; bylaws, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Changing parking rules on Oriole Parkway between Eglinton Avenue West and Chaplin Crescent to fit a road resurfacing and streetscape project — a sodded, tree-lined centre median with curb extensions — due for completion in 2026 is on City Council's agenda. The changes would remove three paid parking spaces between Eglinton and College View Avenue and add a net gain of two permit parking spaces. Council approval is required because the TTC runs transit on Oriole Parkway.

title: Various Developments to be Excluded from Permit Parking in the Toronto and East York Community Council Area - Non-Delegated

brief: Excluding a list of new developments on transit-served streets from the on-street overnight permit parking program, so residents and visitors of those buildings would no longer qualify for permits goes to City Council for a decision. Council approval is required because the TTC runs transit on the listed streets. Staff say the realignment and exclusions are feasible and raise no objections.

title: Various Developments to be Excluded from Permit Parking in the Toronto and East York Community Council Area
topics: development, municipal codes, parking, permit parking; developing land; development (land); land development, on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Up for a decision before the Toronto and East York Community Council: exclude a list of new developments — in the permit parking area attachments — from the on-street overnight permit parking program, so residents and visitors of those buildings would no longer qualify for permits. Staff say the realignment and exclusions are feasible and raise no objections. The council has delegated authority to make a final decision.

title: Elizabeth Street and Elm Street - Traffic Control Signals

Properties Limited and Lawrence Blankenstein under an agreement dated September 12, 2019. The report also recommends releasing the related performance security. brief: A draft plan of subdivision for 9940 Sheppard Avenue East would create development blocks for residential uses, a new public park, an environmental buffer, a new public street running north from Sheppard Avenue East (east of Meadowvale Road) to connect with Meadowvale Road, plus road widenings and reserves. title: Introduction of Committee Reports, New Business and Business Previously Requested from City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council formally introduces the committee reports coming forward to this meeting, including reports from the Executive Committee, Audit Committee, Board of Health, Civic Appointments Committee, and Economic and Community Development Committee. The item sets the agenda for what council will consider. No decision is made at this step.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council confirms the minutes from its regular meeting of June 24 and 25, 2026. No policy decision is involved.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council opens its meeting with O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is involved.

title: Lawrence Heights Revitalization Phases 2 and 3 - Infrastructure Reimbursement and Budget Update
topics: housing, infrastructure; homes; residences
brief: Toronto Community Housing's Lawrence Heights revitalization is getting an infrastructure reimbursement and budget update for phases two and three. The report covers the TCHC-led project spanning pre-development through construction, engagement, and resident relocation. TCHC aims to create more than 10,000 new homes across Toronto by 2035 through its 10-year development plan with the city.

title: Site Plan Application Fee Review
topics: fees, site plan control; administrative fees; admission fees; admission prices; rates; service charges; user charges; user fees, site plan approvals
brief: Fees for Site Plan Control applications are up for an update. City Council is asked to approve a revised fee schedule reflecting service improvements identified through the city's Site Plan Process Review. The report builds on the 2024 development application fee review, which council approved with a modest increase in May 2025. The changes affect what builders pay to have their site plans reviewed.

title: Billy Bishop Airport Proposed Expansion: Response to Council Request for Information on Housing and Transportation Impacts
topics: airports, housing services;
brief: City staff are reporting back on the proposed Billy Bishop airport expansion's housing and transportation impacts, though the picture is incomplete. Since March 2026, the Toronto Port Authority and the province have announced expansion plans through press conferences and interviews outside the governing Tripartite Agreement, and the city says it has received no specific plans or details. The province passed Bill 110, the Building Billy Bishop Airport Act, on May 28, 2026, and the Planning and Housing Committee is asked to receive the report for information.

title: 53 Strachan Avenue (Entrance Address 805 Wellington Street West) - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property, Demolition of Heritage Attributes and of a Building under Sections 33, 34(1)1 and 34(1)2 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Strachan House at 53 Strachan Avenue, a City-owned former planing mill dating to 1888, faces alterations and partial demolition alongside the demolition of a building at entrance address 805 Wellington Street West. City Council is asked to approve the work under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and to enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement. The agreement would preserve the surviving heritage attributes of what was once one of Canada's largest planing mills.

title: Toronto Builds: 53 Strachan Avenue and 805 and 805A Wellington Street West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Two buildings are proposed for 53 Strachan Avenue and 805 and 805A Wellington Street West: an eight-storey Building A with 81 supportive housing units on the east portion, and a 28-storey Building B with 296 homes, 60 of them affordable rentals, on the west portion.
