City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments to allow the Toronto Builds project. An Official Plan amendment is needed to redesignate the site.

title: Toronto Builds: 78 Springhurst Avenue and 1 to 3 Close Avenue (Dunn House Phase 2) - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: [buildings by height], official plan amendments, rezoning, social housing; community housing; housing allowance; housing projects; low income housing; non profit housing; non-profit housing; public housing; rent geared to income assistance; rent geared to income housing; rent subsidies; rent supplement; subsidized housing; subsidized rent; subsidized units, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: An eight-storey rental building with 54 homes, known as Dunn House Phase 2, is proposed at 78 Springhurst Avenue and 1 to 3 Close Avenue under the Toronto Builds program. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes for the project, part of the Social Medicine Housing Initiative advanced with University Health Network and United Way Greater Toronto. The plan includes demolishing one occupied affordable rental unit at 78 Springhurst Avenue.

title: 235 and 245 Yorkland Boulevard - Official Plan Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: The lands at 235 and 245 Yorkland Boulevard would shift from employment to mixed-use under a proposed Official Plan amendment. City Council is asked to approve removing the site from Employment Areas and redesignating it from General Employment Areas to Mixed Use Areas. A site-specific policy would secure a new public road, a public park, and affordable housing units on the site.

title: Expiry Date for Protection of Heritage Properties Listed Under the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Heritage properties listed but not designated on municipal registers across Ontario will lose even their limited 60-day protection on December 31, 2026, opening the door to demolitions. A councillor is asking for support to advocate to the provincial government to protect the at-risk properties before the expiry. The Planning and Housing Committee will consider the advocacy request.

title: Ookwemin Minising - Draft Plan of Subdivision Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, subdivision (land); subdivision of land
brief: This is a procedural item: council is being advised that the Executive Director, Development Review, intends to approve the draft plan of subdivision for Ookwemin Minising under delegated authority. The plan covers lands along Cherry Street, Commissioners Street, Munition Street, Ookwemin Street, and Villiers Street, in line with the council-approved Precinct Plan and zoning. No council decision is required.

title: 6278 Kingston Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The John Morrish House at 6278 Kingston Road in Scarborough's Highland Creek neighbourhood is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate the one-storey detached house under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The house fronts onto Kingston Road west of Meadowvale Road.

title: 55 Sudbury Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: A property at 55 Sudbury Street in Little Portugal is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The property sits at the junction of Sudbury Street and Dovercourt Road, along the north side of the main rail corridor at the southern tip of Ward 9.

title: 55 Elm Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The 1891 Renaissance Revival commercial building at 55 Elm Street, entrance at 650 Bay Street, is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The three-storey building, completed for the Canadian Temperance League, anchors the southwest corner of Bay and Elm streets.

title: 39 Wynford Drive - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: A four-storey commercial property at 39 Wynford Drive in Flemingdon Park is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The property sits on the southeast corner of Wynford Drive and Gervais Drive, a block northeast of Eglinton Avenue East and Don Mills Road.

title: 32 Bright Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Costigan Cottage at 32 Bright Street in Corktown, a detached single-storey wood-frame worker's cottage, is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The cottage sits on the west side of Bright Street between King Street East and Queen Street East.

title: 2 Hedgewood Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: A property at 2 Hedgewood Road in the Bridlepath-Sunnybrook-York Mills area, near Yonge Street and York Mills Road at the edge of the West Don River Valley, is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The designation would legally protect the property's cultural heritage value.

title: 18 Great Oak Drive - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: City Council is moving to protect the Moore Farmhouse at 18 Great Oak Drive in Etobicoke's Islington Heights neighbourhood by stating its intention to designate it under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The property sits on the north side of Great Oak Drive, west of Islington Avenue and south of Rathburn Road. Designation would give the city legal tools to protect the farmhouse's heritage attributes.

title: 180 Queens Drive - Proposed Designation By-law Under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
topics: heritage preservation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The owner of 180 Queens Drive has objected to the city's plan to designate the property, and council must decide whether to proceed. City Council is asked to affirm its May 2026 decision stating its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The property sits on the northeast corner of Queens Drive and Pine Street.

title: 1377 Sheppard Avenue West (Downsview West District) - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: land use, planning, urban planning, zoning, zoning bylaws, zoning designations; city planning; community planning; regional planning, permitted use requests; permitted uses, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a large mixed-use development at 1377 Sheppard Avenue West (Downsview West District) — 845,000 square metres of floor area (about 756,000 residential and 89,000 non-residential), with buildings from 6 to 60 storeys and about 9,250 homes, including 10 percent of residential floor area secured under holding provisions. The owner would also commission public art worth at least $1 million as an in-kind contribution, secured by a letter of credit or surety bond before the first above-grade building permit is issued. The approval would reshape the Downsview West area with thousands of homes.

title: 1-11 Vinci Crescent - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a 14-storey residential building with 299 units at 1-11 Vinci Crescent, redesignating the lands from Neighbourhoods to Apartment Neighbourhoods, with 126 vehicle and 225 bicycle parking spaces at a density of 7.03 times the lot area. The approval would add hundreds of homes.

title: Permanent Closure of a Portion of the Public Lane Abutting 145 Sheppard Avenue East
topics: lanes, laneways, road closures; back alleys; mews, street closures; temporary highway closings, traffic lanes; turn lanes; turning lanes
brief: Transportation Services recommends permanently closing a portion of the public lane south of Sheppard Avenue East, west of Willowdale Avenue, between 145 and 181 Sheppard Avenue East, finding the lands can be permanently closed to implement the settlement council approved through Item 2024.CC24.9 for the area's development applications. Because it closes a public highway, City Council must vote on it.

title: Consumers Road and Yorkland Boulevard (North Intersection) - Traffic Control Signals
topics: road safety, roads, traffic control systems, transportation (sc); circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Transportation Review and Traffic Operations request approval to install traffic control signals at the north intersection of Consumers Road and Yorkland Boulevard, saying the assessment justifies them for the safety of all road users. Because the TTC operates on Consumers Road, City Council must vote on it. The signals affect drivers, pedestrians and cyclists at the intersection.

title: Gateway Boulevard and Linkwood Lane - Traffic Safety Improvement
topics: improvement, safety, traffic; enhancement; rehabilitation (property), motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, public safety
brief: Staff developed a Neighbourhood Streets Plan for Flemingdon Park investigating speeding, road safety for vulnerable road users and other mobility issues, and the plan proposes changes on Gateway Boulevard and Linkwood Lane — two roads where the TTC operates transit service. Because of the TTC service, City Council must vote on the changes. The plan affects drivers, pedestrians and transit riders in the area.

title: Authority to Enter into an Agreement with Metrolinx Respecting the Brentcliffe Shotcrete Wall
topics: agreements, construction, light rail transit, projects, transportation; building, lrt, tenancy agreements, transportation services
brief: Staff seek City Council authority to enter into an agreement with Metrolinx respecting the Brentcliffe Shotcrete Wall — built by Metrolinx as a temporary construction support for Tunnel Boring Machine Launch Shaft 3 for the Eglinton Crosstown LRT, at the East Portal area on the south side of Eglinton Avenue East, east of Brentcliffe Road. After tunnelling and backfilling, the lower part of the wall is buried while the upper part remains. The agreement settles responsibility for the leftover structure.

title: Metrolinx Yonge North Subway Extension - Long-Term Temporary Road Closures, Time Extension of the Temporary Delegation of Authority
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, construction, road closures, subway stations, traffic; building, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, street closures; temporary highway closings, ttc
brief: Metrolinx's Yonge North Subway Extension needs long-term temporary lane closures, turning restrictions and pedestrian and cycling impacts around Yonge Street and Steeles Avenue to excavate the large underground Steeles Station box within the Yonge Street right-of-way. Staff ask North York Community Council to extend the temporary delegation of authority covering the closures and restrictions. The work affects drivers, pedestrians, cyclists and transit riders at the busy intersection.

title: 5, 7, 9, 11, and 15 Park Hill Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal Report
topics: applications, official plan amendments, rezoning; application process, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: An application for a 48-storey building with 505 units, 93 vehicle parking spaces and 289 bicycle spaces at 5, 7, 9, 11 and 15 Park Hill Road — which would demolish five detached dwellings — was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on February 25, 2026. Staff's appeal report sets out the City's position on the application for the Tribunal.

title: 15 - 25 Poyntz Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, demolitions, rental housing; application process, rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve demolishing 8 rental units at 23 and 25 Poyntz Avenue, with the units replaced in the new development on the site; the report cites $20,000.00. No Tenant Assistance Plan is proposed because all existing units are vacant. A related 48-storey, 535-unit development application for the site is also before council.

title: 15 - 25 Poyntz Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, multi-residential properties, official plan amendments, planning & development (sc), rezoning; bylaws, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a 48-storey building (163.6 metres to the top of the mechanical penthouse) with 535 residential units — including 8 rental replacement units — 170 square metres of retail, an on-site parkland dedication and landscaped public space at 15–25 Poyntz Avenue. The application is described as consistent with the Provincial Planning Statement. The approval would add hundreds of homes including replacement rentals.

title: 5 Fairview Mall Drive - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, redevelopment, zoning bylaws; rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a multi-phase redevelopment at 5 Fairview Mall Drive with three mixed-use and residential towers — 33, 43 and 45 storeys — with 1,302 dwelling units, a shared underground garage, replacement of the existing medical office building and a new landscaped area with public access, under a holding provision. The approval would reshape the mall-area site with more than a thousand homes.

title: 922 Millwood Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, multi-unit dwellings, official plan amendments, planning & development (sc), zoning; bylaws, multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a 7-storey (21 metres plus mechanical penthouse and rooftop amenity) residential building with 44 units and 83 square metres of ground-floor retail at 922 Millwood Road, accessed from Krawchuk Lane — scaled down from an earlier 8-storey proposal. The approval would add homes and a small shop on Millwood Road.

title: 2450 and 2452 Bayview Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, planning & development (sc), seniors housing, zoning; bylaws
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a 7-storey (22.81 metres plus mechanical penthouse and rooftop amenities) seniors residence at 2450 and 2452 Bayview Avenue with 141 units offering independent living, assisted living and memory care suites, plus 54 parking spaces. The application is described as consistent with the Provincial Planning Statement. The approval would add seniors housing with care options on Bayview Avenue.

title: 590 and 592 Roehampton Avenue, 7, 9, 11, 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 25, 27 and 29 Glenavy Avenue and 7 Glazebrook Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, planning & development (sc), residential properties, zoning; bylaws, residential real estate
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve redesigning the block at 590–592 Roehampton Avenue, 7–29 Glenavy Avenue and 7 Glazebrook Avenue from Neighbourhoods to Mixed Use Area — including Mixed Use Area 'C' and the Bayview Focus Character Area in the Yonge-Eglinton Secondary Plan — with a zoning amendment under a holding provision. The approval would open the block to mixed-use redevelopment.

title: 20 Brentcliffe Road and 100 Vanderhoof Avenue - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, official plan amendments, zoning; application process
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a 32-storey mixed-use building (102.9 metres plus 6-metre mechanical penthouse) at 20 Brentcliffe Road and 100 Vanderhoof Avenue with 383 residential units — six of them affordable rental — 1,816 square metres of ground-floor non-residential space, two levels of underground parking and a 469-square-metre parkland dedication at the northeast corner. The approval would add hundreds of homes including affordable rentals.

title: 39, 41 and 43 Wilket Road and 1 Tudor Gate - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, multi-unit dwellings, zoning bylaws; application process, multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve two six-storey (22.5 metres plus 4.5-metre mechanical penthouse) residential buildings at 39, 41 and 43 Wilket Road and 1 Tudor Gate; the Tudor Gate building would have 10 units and 11 parking spaces including one visitor space, accessed from a private driveway. The proposal adds homes on the two sites.

title: 25 Cedarcroft Boulevard - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: apartments, by-laws, redevelopment, residential properties, zoning; bylaws, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization, residential real estate
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a 29-storey residential building with 316 units at 25 Cedarcroft Boulevard under a holding provision, while retaining the existing 13-storey building with 132 rental units and adding one rental unit to it; the surface parking lot would be removed for the new building. The approval would add hundreds of homes while keeping existing rental units.

title: 765 Steeles Avenue West - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, municipal facilities, properties (real estate), zoning; bylaws, city facilities; municipal buildings, property; real estate
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a City-initiated zoning amendment at 765 Steeles Avenue West, following motion 2026.MM40.28, to give the City more flexibility in the use, design, finishing and equipping of a future City facility secured through Section 37 provisions — with $2.5 million cited in the report. Staff are also directed to explore funding options to finish, furnish and equip the facility. The change affects what public facility the community gets on the site.

title: 200 Gateway Boulevard - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, development, residential properties, zoning bylaws; bylaws, developing land; development (land); land development, residential real estate, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a mixed-use development at 200 Gateway Boulevard with a 48-storey residential tower (534 new units) and a 13-storey residential building (132 new units) with at-grade commercial uses, while retaining the existing 17-storey apartment building on the site. The approval would add more than 660 new homes while keeping the existing rental building.

title: Don Mills Regeneration Area Study Leslie Site - Final Report
topics: community & life (sc), official plan amendments, projects, regeneration areas;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve an Official Plan Amendment setting a renewed vision for the Leslie Site (1121 and 1123 Leslie Street) — shifting it from employment uses to a new mixed-use community under the Don Mills Regeneration Area Study. The framework supports a transit-oriented community leveraging the Eglinton Crosstown LRT, while protecting the part of the City's Natural Heritage System crossing the north end of the site. The amendment shapes future housing and jobs on the site.

title: 537, 539, 541, 543, 545, 547 and 551 Eglinton Avenue East and 59 and 61 Hoyle Avenue - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment Application- Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a 35-storey (111.95 metres plus 6-metre mechanical penthouse) mixed-use building with 383 dwelling units and about 250 square metres of commercial space at 537–551 Eglinton Avenue East and 59 and 61 Hoyle Avenue, with a 6-metre laneway connection at the rear. The Official Plan amendment would redesignate the lands. The approval would add hundreds of homes on Eglinton Avenue.

title: 245 Eglinton Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application- Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, official plan amendments, rezoning; application process, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a mixed-use building at 245 Eglinton Avenue East with two 59-storey towers (about 190 metres each plus 6-metre mechanical penthouses) on a connected 3- and 4-storey base with retail at grade — 1,202 residential units, 2,802 square metres of retail and 4,837 square metres of amenity space. The approval would add more than a thousand homes on Eglinton Avenue.

title: 605, 607, 609, 611, 613, 615 and 617 Lawrence Avenue West - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve demolishing 8 rental units in 7 detached houses at 605, 607, 609, 611, 613, 615 and 617 Lawrence Avenue West, with the units replaced in the new development on the site. A Tenant Assistance Plan gives existing tenants the right to return to replacement rental units at similar rents plus financial compensation — the report cites $20,000.00. A related development application for the site is also before council. The decision affects 8 renter households.

title: Parking and Transit Consideration Requests
brief: A member motion highlights rapid intensification across North York including Ward 18 (Willowdale), especially around the North York Centre and Yonge North secondary plan areas along Yonge Street, and asks North York Community Council to consider parking and transit requests. The motion notes growing pressure on transportation networks and curbside parking as density rises, with the broader community still relying heavily on cars and surface transit despite Line 1 subway access in parts of Willowdale. It seeks attention to local infrastructure as growth continues.

title: 605, 607, 609, 611, 613, 615 and 617 Lawrence Avenue West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, applications, rezoning; application process, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a 13-storey mixed-use building (42.45 metres plus 4.5-metre mechanical penthouse) with 266 units — including 8 rental replacement units — at 605, 607, 609, 611, 613, 615 and 617 Lawrence Avenue West, under a holding provision. The Official Plan amendment would redesignate the lands from Neighbourhoods to Mixed Use Area. The approval would add hundreds of homes, including replacement rentals, on Lawrence Avenue.

title: Transmittal of the Accountability Officers' Reports on the Results of Applying Specified Auditing Procedures to Financial Information Other Than Financial Statements for the Year Ended December 31, 2025 - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: lobbying; lobbyist registrars; lobbyist registry; lobbyists
brief: This is a procedural item: external auditor Kwok and Associate has completed the annual audit of financial information for the City's three Accountability Officers — the Integrity Commissioner, Lobbyist Registrar and Ombudsman — for the year ended December 31, 2025, as required by the Municipal Code. Mayor Olivia Chow's motion, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, transmits the reports to City Council for information. Council is only asked to receive the reports; no further action is required.

title: Authorizing Development Charge Refunds for Condominium Projects Converting to Purpose-built Rental Tenure - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
topics: refund, rental housing; reimbursement, rental properties; rental units
brief: Toronto charges different development-charge rates by housing tenure, with purpose-built rentals eligible for discounts — but the City currently has no authority to refund the difference when a project that already paid condo-rate charges converts to rental before occupancy. Mayor Olivia Chow's motion, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas, asks City Council to authorize those development charge refunds so projects converting from condominium to purpose-built rental pay the correct rate. The change removes a financial barrier for developers who switch projects to rental housing.

title: Parking Amendments to Accommodate Emergency  Loading for University Health Network, 750 Dundas Street West - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: parking spaces; parking spots
brief: Paramedics and ambulances regularly attend 750 Dundas Street West, a University Health Network medical facility across from Toronto Western Hospital, but the curbside is signed No Parking and afternoon rush-hour No Stopping with no curb cut — forcing crews to lift loaded stretchers over the curb. Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, asks City Council to amend the parking rules so the curb stays clear for ambulances at all times and to add a curb cut; the motion references a $4.50 figure in connection with the parking regulation. The change affects emergency access to the medical facility.

title: Authority to Accept Donations Raised Through Fundraising Campaign for the Restoration of the Sir Casimir Gzowski Monument - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: memorials; monuments; permanent memorials
brief: The Sir Casimir Gzowski Monument, built in 1968 in a City park of the same name through collaboration between the Ontario Institute of Engineers, Toronto's Polish community and the City, honours the engineer knighted by Queen Victoria in 1890. Mayor Olivia Chow's motion, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, asks City Council to authorize the City to accept $50,000 raised through a fundraising campaign toward restoring the monument. The memorial is part of the City's Public Art and Monuments Collection.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 53 to 63 Sheppard Avenue West and 62 to 68 Bogert Avenue for Improvements to the Schoolyard at St. Edward Catholic School - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: St. Edward Catholic School at 1 Botham Road in Willowdale has a schoolyard with poor drainage and uneven grading that leaves the field waterlogged and unusable after rainfall, limiting safe outdoor activities for students and community recreation. Councillor Lily Cheng's motion, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley, asks City Council to release $50,000 in Section 37 developer funds from the development at 53 to 63 Sheppard Avenue West and 62 to 68 Bogert Avenue for schoolyard improvements. The fix would restore reliable use of the outdoor space for students and local residents.

title: Advancing the Pakistani Canadian Community Centre - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: community centres, motions; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, council decisions; decisions (council)
brief: More than 160,000 Greater Toronto Area residents are of Pakistani origin, and the community — concentrated in the eastern part of the city — is underserved by cultural and community facilities. Mayor Olivia Chow's motion, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside, asks City Council to have staff advance the Pakistani Canadian Community Centre Project's plan for a multicultural, multi-purpose community centre that would also serve residents city-wide. The project has been working with intergovernmental partners toward a centralized space for the large and growing community.

title: Amending Item 2025.EX23.3 - Metrolinx Ontario Line - Temporary Lane Closures on the Don Valley Parkway and F.G. Gardiner Expressway and Temporary Delegation of Authority - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: traffic, traffic data; cordon count programs; ridership; traffic counts; traffic information; traffic measurement; traffic studies, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: This is a procedural item: Metrolinx needs additional overnight lane closures on the Don Valley Parkway and F.G. Gardiner Expressway in August 2026, beyond the two days council approved in May 2025, to finish installing access scaffolding for the Lower Don Bridge for the Ontario Line. Councillor Paula Fletcher's motion, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, asks City Council to amend Item 2025.EX23.3 to allow the extra closures. Drivers on both expressways would face more overnight lane restrictions while construction is completed.

title: Weekend and Holiday Standing Prohibition on Barkdene Hills - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: parking, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: Barkdene Hills, a residential street near the Scarborough Bluffs, sees heavy traffic and parking demand on spring and summer weekends and holidays, and cars parked on both sides can restrict traffic flow, reduce visibility and block access for residents, emergency services and waste collection. Councillor Parthi Kandavel's motion, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow, asks City Council to impose a weekend and holiday standing prohibition on the street. Because Barkdene Hills carries a TTC bus route, the decision must come from City Council rather than staff.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2026.MM42.60 - Advancing a Redevelopment Strategy for the Toronto Builds site at 770 Don Mills Road - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: community development; community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development
brief: The City-owned surface parking lot at 770 Don Mills Road, steps from the Crosstown LRT's Don Valley Station and the Ontario Line, is being planned by CreateTO as a transit-oriented, mixed-income redevelopment with an elementary school, park space, retail, childcare and market and affordable housing. Councillor Jon Burnside's motion, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, asks City Council to advance a redevelopment strategy for the Toronto Builds site. With the Crosstown now open and the Ontario Line under construction, the motion seeks to move the mixed-use project forward.

title: Stop the Province’s Land Grab, Give Toronto Island and Parkland Back to Toronto - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: airports;
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow's motion, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, asks City Council to oppose the Province's legislation to expropriate City land — Little Norway Park and the entirety of the Toronto Islands, including Hanlan's Point Beach — and to demand the land be returned to Toronto. The motion states the province moved to expropriate after announcing plans to expand the Island airport, and cites potential impacts on housing, parks, air and water quality, congestion and wildlife. Ownership of the Islands affects island residents, beachgoers and everyone who uses the waterfront parkland.

title: 2455 St. Clair Avenue West - The Class 4 Noise Area Designation - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: environment (sc), noise; amplified music; construction noise; loud music; noise pollution; traffic noise
brief: The Committee of Adjustment approved a six-storey mixed-use building with ten residential units and ground-floor retail at 2455 St. Clair Avenue West on February 26, 2026, with a condition tied to the site's proximity to a rail yard and rail facilities. Councillor Frances Nunziata's motion, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, asks City Council to designate the site a Class 4 noise area, consistent with the Committee's condition for a peer-reviewed Rail Noise and Vibration Impact Study and Air Quality Study. The designation sets how noise from nearby rail is managed for the building's future residents.

title: Authority to Accept Donations Raised Through Fundraising Campaign for Moss Park Arena Improvements - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: donation; bequest; toy drive
brief: Moss Park Arena's interior — washrooms, boardroom, snack bar, pro-shop, Zamboni room and multipurpose rooms — is slated for renovation from June 2027 to May 2028. Councillor Chris Moise's motion, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, asks City Council to authorize the City to accept donations raised through a fundraising campaign toward the improvements, with the motion citing figures of $300,000, $238,000, $25,000 and $50,000. Moss Park is one of eight City arenas run by volunteer Arena Boards of Management, so community-raised money supplements City spending on the local rink.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.TE27.6 - 149 College Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: after City Council approved a 60-storey mixed-use building at 149 College Street in December 2025 and enacted By-law 1567-2025, Community Planning found a wording error — the by-law unintentionally stops certain institutional uses from counting toward the required minimum non-residential floor area. Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, asks City Council to re-open and amend the 2025 approval to correct the error. The fix preserves the original intent and does not change the approved development.

title: Amending Item 2018.TE34.48 - 114 and 120 Church Street and 59 Richmond Street East - Amendment of Section 37 Agreement to Address Corner Rounding Property Rights Transfer - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the 2018-approved 45-storey (149.5-metre) mixed-use building at 114 and 120 Church Street and 59 Richmond Street East needs its registered Section 37 community-benefits agreement amended to address how corner-rounding property rights transfer to the City. Councillor Chris Moise's motion, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, asks City Council to amend Item 2018.TE34.48 to make the fix. It corrects the legal mechanics of the land transfer; it does not change the approved development.

title: 251 Windermere Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: after the Committee of Adjustment refused a driveway-widening variance at 251 Windermere Avenue and the applicant appealed to the Toronto Local Appeal Body on July 7, 2026, Councillor Gord Perks's motion, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, asks City Council to have the City Solicitor appear at the appeal. The June 17, 2026 refusal covered maximum driveway width and front yard landscaping under Zoning By-law 569-2013. Council routinely directs the Solicitor to defend Committee of Adjustment decisions at appeal.

title: Advancing the Bridletowne Neighbourhood Centre/Community Hub - by Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: community centres, land use designations; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes
brief: The City has spent more than a decade planning a multi-service community hub on 5.2 City-owned acres at 1355 Bridletowne Circle — bought in 2011 for about $5.9 million — to bring community space, programs and services to the Finch-Warden/Steeles-L'Amoreaux/Bridletowne area. Councillor Nick Mantas's motion, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, asks City Council to advance the project by transferring the site at nominal cost to the YMCA of Greater Toronto. The hub would unlock long-planned community infrastructure in an area of significant need.

title: Renaming Main Sewage Treatment Playground to Ashbridge’s Bay Sports Hub - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: playgrounds, wayfinding; adventure playgrounds; indoor playgrounds; playground structures
brief: Main Sewage Treatment Playground, an 11.2-hectare park at Eastern Avenue and Emdaabimok Avenue with tournament-sized pickleball courts, two basketball courts, a rugby field, a baseball diamond and a skatepark, would be renamed the Ashbridge's Bay Sports Hub. Councillor Paula Fletcher's motion, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, asks City Council to approve the new name to reflect the area and the park's range of sports. The well-used park sits on Toronto Water land and serves the local community, especially in summer.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Reconstruction of Church Street in Coordination with Water Main Replacement - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: [water management equipment], funding; financing
brief: Councillor Chris Moise's motion, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, asks City Council to release Section 37 developer funds toward reconstructing Church Street in coordination with water main replacement, in the heart of the Church-Wellesley Village — the geographic and cultural centre of Canada's largest LGBTQ2S+ neighbourhood. The motion lists figures of $17,910,366.30, $9,120,000, $2,567,709.73, $1,619,812.80, $1,662,954.26, $1,600,000, $1,352,368.34 and $109,643.42. Rebuilding the street affects residents, businesses and visitors in a major gathering destination and tourist area.

title: Supporting Employment Uses through the Review of the Former City of Scarborough Employment Districts Zoning By-law in Scarborough North - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: by-laws, zoning; bylaws
brief: Ward 23 holds a significant share of Toronto's Employment Area lands, but many are still governed by the former City of Scarborough Employment Districts Zoning By-law 24982, whose legacy definitions, permissions and site-specific exceptions create uncertainty for businesses seeking to establish, adapt or expand. Councillor Jamaal Myers's motion, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, asks City Council to have the review of the Scarborough zoning by-law bring employment-use rules in line with the current Official Plan and provincial policy for Employment Areas. It affects employers and job lands in Scarborough North and across the ward boundary.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Pole Wraps for the Cabbagetown Southwest Heritage Conservation District - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: Councillor Chris Moise's motion, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, asks City Council to release $107,000 in Section 37 developer funds to the Downtown Yonge Business Improvement Area, as trustee, to buy and install wrapped hydro poles across the Cabbagetown Southwest Heritage Conservation District. Council endorsed the district's heritage plan in 2024 and the Ontario Land Tribunal approved it later that year. The wraps add street-level design detail in a downtown neighbourhood known for its Victorian architecture.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds - Collaborating with the Friends of Allan Gardens on the Development of the Greenhouse Link Building - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: The proposed Greenhouse Link Building, advanced by the Friends of Allan Gardens, would double the conservatory's footprint in the downtown park that has been open to the public since 1860. Councillor Chris Moise's motion, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, asks City Council to release $9 million ($9,000,000) in Section 42 park funds toward the project, with the motion listing figures of $3,388,294.67, $2,864,683.82 and $2,747,021.51 alongside the total. The building is part of the vision for expanding and modernizing Allan Gardens' conservatory and garden spaces.

title: Exploring Partnerships to Create a New Community Centre with Toronto's Filipino Community - by Councillor Neethan Shan, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: community centres; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes
brief: More than 270,000 Toronto residents are of Filipino origin, and Scarborough's large Filipino community is underserved by cultural and community facilities. Councillor Neethan Shan's motion, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, asks City Council to have staff explore replicating the successful models of the Chinese Cultural Centre of Greater Toronto and the Tamil Community Centre to create a permanent Filipino cultural and community centre. The motion responds to ongoing community discussion about a permanent space to serve the community's needs and celebrate its culture.

title: Exploring Alternative Options to Clarify Complex Intersections - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: intersections, roads; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads)
brief: At Bayview Avenue and Bayview Heights Drive in Don Valley West, the 'Do Not Block the Intersection' sign marks a zone drivers cannot see clearly, so the intersection keeps getting blocked — leaving drivers turning north onto Bayview with few safe gaps and higher crash risk on a stretch that has already seen accidents. Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin's motion, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe, asks City Council to have staff explore clearer signage or layout options for this and similar confusing intersections. It matters to drivers, pedestrians and cyclists who rely on road markings they can actually see.

title: Advancing Local Priorities in Thorncliffe Park - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: Thorncliffe Park, a densely populated neighbourhood and longtime arrival point for newcomers, is being reshaped by the Ontario Line and a future Thorncliffe Park station. Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin's motion, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, asks City Council to direct City Planning to set local priorities — better streetscapes, parks, public spaces and walking and cycling connections — so residents benefit as the area grows. The motion follows staff and community engagement that identified opportunities for new housing, jobs, community facilities and parks alongside the transit investment.

title: Advancing Digital Sovereignty for the City of Toronto - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
brief: The item asks council to advance digital sovereignty for the City of Toronto, framing it as autonomy over the city's digital infrastructure, data and intellectual property in line with the federal Digital Sovereignty Framework. The motion cites the June 4, 2026 launch of Canada's AI for All national AI strategy, committing over $2.3 billion in federal spending over five years around trust, opportunity and sovereignty, and points to cities like Copenhagen, Aarhus and Amsterdam taking homegrown approaches. It asks council to consider a Toronto approach that balances reliance on foreign-owned technology, prioritizes Canadian solutions and aligns with federal efforts.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Transportation Services for the Reconstruction and Beautification of the Oakwood Avenue and Vaughan Road Parkette - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: The item asks council to release $48,732.87 ($48,700) in Section 37 funds to Transportation Services for the reconstruction and beautification of the Oakwood Avenue and Vaughan Road traffic island, with the Oakwood Village Business Improvement Area. Planned 2028 road work on Vaughan Road is a chance to redesign the island, closing the Oakwood northbound right slip lane to expand it with new amenities, green space and community placemaking signage from the Oakwood Village Streets Plan consultation. The $48,732.87 is drawn from $8,458 from the 458 Oakwood Avenue development and $40,274 from a second source account.

title: Ensuring Due Diligence on Data Centres in Scarborough Southwest - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: Centres, databases;
brief: The item asks council to ensure due diligence on the proposed STACK Infrastructure data centre expansion at 3650 Danforth Avenue in Scarborough Southwest, where more than 100 residents attended a community meeting with concerns about scale, electricity and water demands, noise, backup generators, local employment and community benefit. The motion notes the facility is advancing through delegated site plan approval without a public meeting or council vote while the city's Toronto-specific data centre policy work is still underway. It asks that the application be assessed against the forthcoming guidance, community interests be considered throughout, and council weigh whether and how the application should be paced.

title: Toronto Goes Dynamite! Welcoming BTS on BTS Boulevard - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
brief: The item asks council to celebrate BTS's North York concerts with honorary BTS Boulevard signage along Yonge Street, tying into the Korean Festival at Mel Lastman Square the same weekend. The motion authorizes Economic Development and Culture, with Transportation Services, to negotiate sponsorships for commemorative street signs letting fans take photos as they head through Korea Town North's restaurants and shops. The authorization is conditional on securing the needed licences and permissions from intellectual property rights holders.

title: Reimagining the Future of the Former Ontario Science Centre Public Consultation Report - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
brief: The item asks council to receive the Spring 2026 community engagement report on reimagining the former Ontario Science Centre site at 770 Don Mills Road, led by Save Ontario's Science Centre, Moriyama Teshima Architects and councillors Matlow and Burnside. The report presents a community-informed vision for the site's revitalization and return to public use after the province announced the relocation in April 2023 and abruptly closed the building in June 2024. The motion notes the province's own consultants recommended repairing the building rather than closing it, and that the province has not shared its plans despite several council motions asking for engagement.

title: Assessing the Impact of the Data Centre located at 48 Lowe’s Place - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
brief: The item asks council to have Development Review staff urgently meet with the applicant for the data centre at 48 Lowe's Place in Etobicoke North and the local councillor to assess whether more mitigation is needed for community concerns about water and hydro use and noise. The applicant began approvals in 2021 and is pursuing conditional occupancy, and residents have raised concerns about the facility's impacts. The motion asks for recommended solutions, if needed, at the December 9 and 10, 2026 council meeting, tied to council's earlier direction on a Toronto-specific approach to data centres.

title: 404 Rustic Road - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: This is a procedural item: Authorizing the City Solicitor to appeal the Committee of Adjustment's approval of a rear-yard garden suite at 404 Rustic Road, which at about 29.5 percent larger than the by-law permits, to the Toronto Local Appeal Body and resolve the matter for the city, would get Council's approval. The Etobicoke York panel approved the application on June 25, 2026; the solicitor already appealed before the July 15 deadline to preserve the city's rights. The motion lets the solicitor retain an external consultant to advise on the plan.

title: Ensuring Community Protections and Electrification Commitments for the Bloor-Lansdowne GO Station - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: noise, noise complaints; amplified music; construction noise; loud music; noise pollution; traffic noise
brief: The item asks council to secure community protections and electrification commitments for the new Bloor-Lansdowne GO station on the Barrie line, after Metrolinx put electrified service plans on indefinite hold. The motion says no noise barriers are proposed for the densely populated residential stretch by the station, where idling trains, diesel exhaust, vibration and crossing bells over 70 decibels will rise as trains arrive every 7.5 minutes in either direction. While many nearby residents support transit expansion, the motion says it must not come at the expense of their health, pressing for noise and vibration mitigation and renewed electrification commitments.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Toronto Chinatown Land Trust for a Mixed-Use Affordable Housing and Cultural Hub - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: The item asks council to provide $700,000 in Section 37 funds to the Toronto Chinatown Land Trust to help buy the mixed-use building at 81 Huron Street in Ward 11, an anchor for the recently designated West Chinatown Cultural District. The non-profit land trust works to preserve community space, affordable housing and commercial space in West Chinatown, where demand for culturally appropriate affordable housing far exceeds supply and existing affordable space is being lost. The $700,000 total is made up of a $500,000 component, from source accounts of $43,982.87 and $456,017.13, and a $200,000 component, from source accounts of $56,078.39 and $143,921.61.

title: Strengthening Toronto’s Multi-Tenant Houses Framework: Enforcement and Path to Compliance - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: enforcement, housing; homes; residences
brief: The item asks council to review how the city-wide Multi-Tenant Houses framework, adopted in 2022 and effective March 2024, is working in practice. The motion seeks updates on enforcement tools and implementation supports like the renovation program and operator concierge service that help operators through licensing, noting the framework was meant to set consistent safety and licensing standards while preserving deeply affordable rooming-house homes. The reports would inform council's understanding and identify continuous-improvement opportunities.

title: Avenue Road and Eglinton Avenue West - Traffic Amendments - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: The item asks council to have Transportation Services report in the first quarter of 2027 on whether the longstanding northbound left-turn prohibition at Avenue Road and Eglinton Avenue West can be removed without overly delaying traffic. Residents say the prohibition pushes turning drivers onto neighbouring streets including Oriole Parkway. The motion asks for the analysis to determine if the turn can be allowed back.

title: Intergovernmental Collaboration to Deliver Transit for Humber Bay Shores - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: intergovernmental relations, public transit; federal-municipal relations; governmental relations; inter-governmental relations; intergovernmental cooperation; provincial-municipal relations, local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: The item asks council to formalize intergovernmental collaboration to deliver transit for Humber Bay Shores, after the developer paused plans for the Christie's site at Park Lawn Road and Lake Shore Boulevard, leaving the future of the planned Park Lawn GO Station unclear. City staff had worked with Metrolinx since 2019 to link the site's redevelopment to the station and build its business case. The motion seeks a formalized working group keeping the city, Metrolinx and the developer at the table on GO service for the growing South Etobicoke area.

title: Amending Item 2022.SC33.12 - 25 Sewells Road and 182 to 250 Brenyon Way to Dedicate a Public Highway - by Councillor Neethan Shan, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: highways; freeways; motorways; parkways
brief: This is a procedural item: The item asks council to amend its 2022 approval for the 25 Sewells Road and 182 to 250 Brenyon Way rental apartment development so a reserve strip along Sewells Road and Brenyon Way is dedicated as a public highway. The reserve, a sliver of land from a historic subdivision, sits between the site and the existing road and blocks the city from acquiring a required road widening through site plan approval. Dedicating it lets the applicant satisfy the site plan conditions.

title: 29 Church Street - Discontinuing City of Toronto Residential Collection Services - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: solid waste management; solid waste management planning; swm; waste management
brief: The item asks council to discontinue city residential waste collection at 29 Church Street in York, a nine-storey, 63-unit apartment building with waste problems dating to 2013. The motion cites chronic overflow from an undersized storage area on Church Street, loose garbage on neighbouring properties, rodent burrowing, offensive odours, and repeated Municipal Licensing and Standards enforcement, including a RentSafeTO score of 82 out of 100. It proposes ending municipal service so the property owner must arrange private collection.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Toronto Metropolitan University for Campus Public Realm Plan - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: universities; educational institutions
brief: The item asks council to release $1,837,974.68 ($1.84 million) in Section 37 funds from the 363-391 Yonge Street and 3 Gerrard Street East developments to Toronto Metropolitan University for its Campus Master Plan public realm improvements. The money would fund streetscape and public realm construction on the main campus, forwarded once the university signs an undertaking on the funds' use and reporting. The motion continues TMU's two-decade effort to make the campus feel part of, not apart from, downtown.

title: Improving the Development Review Process for Faster Housing Delivery - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: The item asks council to improve the development review process for faster housing delivery, noting the city's target of 285,000 new homes by 2031. The motion credits the 2024 creation of the Development Review Division and its customer service standards for improving statutory review timelines by over 80 percent, but says challenges remain in parts of the process outside that division, in Corporate Real Estate Management, Legal Services, Transportation Services and others. It asks council to direct further streamlining so approvals are timely and predictable, especially for affordable housing where delays add costs non-profit builders cannot absorb.

title: Merton Street Streetscape Improvements - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: improvement, roads; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: The item asks council to have Transportation Services consult the Merton Street community, between Yonge Street and Mount Pleasant Road, and report in late 2027 on streetscape improvements for the corridor. The motion says concentrated construction and shifting traffic patterns have raised pedestrian safety concerns, narrow sidewalks, limited sightlines and unsafe mid-block crossings, on a street serving seniors, people with disabilities, a daycare and key links to Davisville station, the Beltline Trail and Mount Pleasant Cemetery. Some public realm work will come through development applications; the motion targets the gaps.

title: Authorization to Release Section Section 37 Funds for 1240, 1246, 1250 Weston Road - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: The item asks council to release $1,455,897.98 ($1.46 million) in Section 37 funds from the 8 to 16 Locust Street development for 70 new affordable rental units and 58 new rent-controlled units at 1240, 1246 and 1250 Weston Road in Ward 5, built by the Learning Enrichment Foundation, which will also provide 21 rental replacement units. The funds flow through a municipal capital facility agreement with disbursements at construction and occupancy milestones.

title: Renaming a City Park in Honour of Daniel Stopnicki - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: naming, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: The item asks council to study renaming a city park in Eglinton-Lawrence in honour of Daniel Stopnicki, the beloved teacher, mentor and interactive-media innovator who was killed in April 2026. Stopnicki taught and coordinated programs at Seneca Polytechnic and Centennial College, led companies as a chief technology and innovation officer, and championed a grassroots campaign for a local off-leash park. The motion asks Parks and Recreation, with the local councillor's office, to review options under the city's commemorative framework; his father Roberto is a longtime Transportation Services director.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Capital Upgrades at Karma Co-op - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: capital budgets;
brief: The item asks council to release $42,000 in Section 37 funds from the 316 Bloor Street West development for urgent garbage storage upgrades at Karma Co-op, the only community food cooperative in Ward 11. The motion frames the work in the context of residents' concern about rising food costs, noting co-ops keep quality food affordable while paying living wages through mutual aid and no commercial profit margins. Council has also asked for a broader report in mid-2027 on supporting non-profit food cooperatives.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Heritage Toronto for Production and Installation of a Plaque Commemorating Monica Lewis - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: plaques; heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques
brief: The item asks council to release $10,000.00 ($10,000) in Section 37 funds to Heritage Toronto for a plaque commemorating Monica Lewis and her business Monica's at 1553 Eglinton West. Starting as a record store in the late 1960s and becoming a beauty and cosmetics hub in the 1980s, Monica's served Toronto's Caribbean community and the growing Black population across Southern Ontario for decades before closing during the pandemic amid LRT construction disruption. Lewis died May 20, 2026, and the plaque marks her business's cultural significance to Little Jamaica and beyond.

title: Planning for Curbside Management when Autonomous Vehicles Arrive - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: The item asks council to have Transportation Services start developing a curbside management strategy that accounts for vehicles for hire and autonomous vehicles, with a progress update to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee in 2027. The motion says councillors already hear complaints about inadequate loading space for passengers and cargo, and that autonomous vehicles could worsen congestion and curb competition even as they offer safety and cost advantages. It follows expert advice that cities should plan curbside management now.

title: Expanding Parkland to Serve the Growing King-Spadina and Wellington Place Neighbourhoods - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to direct Parks and Recreation to actively pursue partnerships and creative ways to grow the parkland network in King-Spadina and Wellington Place, where provision rates of 0.9 to 3.9 square metres per person sit far below the city-wide average of 28 and are expected to decline. The entire downtown neighbourhood falls within an Area of Parkland Need, with limited inventory and small parcels complicating acquisition. The push aligns with the King Spadina Secondary Plan, the heritage conservation district, the Downtown Plan and the King Spadina Public Realm Strategy.

title: Improving Coordination Closures to Fight Congestion - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: congestion, improvement; enhancement; rehabilitation (property), gridlock
brief: The item asks council to back the Chief Congestion Officer and Transportation Services in using a transit-focused approach when coordinating closures with the TTC, city departments and regional agencies this year and beyond. The motion contrasts a difficult Mother's Day, when subway, Don Valley Parkway, UP Express and event closures hit at once, with the successful coordinated transportation plan for Toronto's six FIFA 2026 matches. It frames better closure coordination as a key fight against congestion.

title: Expanding Parkland to Serve Liberty Village - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: parks, redevelopment; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to direct Parks and Recreation to actively pursue partnerships and creative ways to expand parkland in Liberty Village, a downtown neighbourhood where much of the area is classified as an Area of Parkland Need and provision rates are expected to fall as residential growth continues. The motion notes limited inventory and competitive market conditions make acquisition difficult. The push aligns with the Official Plan Amendment 914 Liberty For All study, the Garrison Common North Secondary Plan and the Liberty Village Public Realm Strategy.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds for the 819 Yonge Street - Park Development Project - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: The item asks council to release $5,000,000 ($5 million) in Section 42 funds from Ward 11 developments for the new Indigenous placekeeping park at 819 Yonge Street and 876 Church Street. Council previously authorized a construction management agreement with the 148 Yorkville Avenue owner to secure, design and build the park; this motion covers the remaining costs to fully design and build it out, including demolition, engineering studies and related work. The official figures also list $3,000,000 and $2,000,000 as component amounts of the $5,000,000 release.

title: Accepting an In-Kind Donation from the L6 Foundation to Construct Playground at Balmy Beach Park - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: donation, playgrounds; adventure playgrounds; indoor playgrounds; playground structures, bequest; toy drive
brief: The item asks council to accept an in-kind donation worth up to $1,000,000 ($1 million) from the L6 Foundation, a Toronto not-for-profit, for refurbishing the playground at Balmy Beach Park at 1 Beech Avenue. City staff would review the scope and design, and Parks and Recreation would lead community consultation. Council authority is required because the donation exceeds the $50,000 threshold in the city's Donation Policy, and the motion also authorizes the donation and construction agreement.

title: Supporting the Realization of the Tamil Community Centre  - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Neethan Shan
topics: community centres; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow is asking council to support the realization of the Tamil Community Centre, a multi-purpose facility for the Tamil community and the broader Morningside Heights and northeast Scarborough area with a gymnasium, indoor walking track, auditorium, library, museum and archival space, programming rooms, outdoor sports facilities and social, cultural and mental health programming. The city has contributed a long-term nominal lease of city-owned land and waived planning fees, with a Community Access Agreement opening the spaces to surrounding residents. The source lists $26 million in connection with the centre; the provided text is truncated so the figure's context is not fully shown.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Fire-Safety Improvements to the Snack Bar at Milliken Park Field House - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: emergency plans, public safety & protection (sc); building evacuation plans; business continuity plans; fire escape plans; fire safety plans
brief: The item asks council to release $8,000 in Section 37 funds for fire-safety improvements to the snack bar at the Milliken Park Field House, where the South Asian Cultural Health Association for Youth and Seniors runs the TRUPTI Social Café. A commercial kitchen fire suppression system is needed for safe, code-compliant on-site food preparation and to support community food programming. The money comes from unspent Steeles Avenue East development funds originally allocated to the Milliken Park Community Recreation Centre expansion, redirected under By-law 1145-2025.

title: The Mayor's Seat: Restoring Direct Mayoral Accountability on the Toronto Police Service Board - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: police services; police; policing
brief: The item asks council to support restoring the mayor's seat on the Toronto Police Service Board, saying the mayor should take the head-of-council seat the province's Community Safety and Policing Act reserves for them or their designate. The motion cites the police service's $1.43 billion 2026 budget as the city's largest single line item and the per-capita officer ratio falling from 208 per 100,000 residents in 2010 to 172, a 17 percent decrease. It argues that direct mayoral accountability on the board matches the statutory design that safety responsibility rests with the person voters elected to lead the city.

title: Activating Unused Seasonal Recreational Facilities in the Off-Season - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: recreation centres, recreational facilities; rec centers; rec centres; recreation centers, recreation facilities; recreational amenities
brief: The item asks council to explore activating unused seasonal recreational facilities, like inactive ice pads, in the off-season with programming such as temporary pickleball courts or camp space. The motion says demand for recreation will keep growing with the city, and that consistent off-season use would improve access and could support the city's youth employment objectives through short-term summer jobs for students. Parks and Recreation would report back in the first quarter of 2027 on opportunities.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to the Laneway Project for Ryerson Avenue Upgrades - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: laneways; back alleys; mews
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to release $95,000.00 ($95,000) in Section 37 funds to the Laneway Project for upgrades to the laneway near Ryerson Avenue, beside the Alexandra Hotel and Ryerson Public School. The Friends of Alexandra Park group proposed beautifying the underused laneway, which suffers from poor lighting, illegal dumping and graffiti, with planting, lighting, murals, signage and site improvements. The motion frames the work as creating a safer, more welcoming shared corridor for residents, families and vulnerable populations.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to the Oakwood Village Business Improvement Area for Streetscape Improvements - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: budgets, business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations, budgets and accounts
brief: The item asks council to release $100,000.00 in Section 37 funds from the 1603 Eglinton Avenue West development for custom branding and vinyl wraps in the Oakwood Village Business Improvement Area, along Oakwood Avenue from Earlsdale Avenue to Bude Street. The streetscape work would give the corridor a distinctive visual identity, add colour and vibrancy, and help deter graffiti and vandalism. The funds would be forwarded once the BIA signs an undertaking on their use and reporting.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Support Community Stewardship Improvements at the Rosewood Pollinator Community Garden - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: The item asks council to release $1,000.00 in Section 37 funds for the Rosewood Pollinator Community Garden, a stewardship initiative run by the Scarborough Rosewood Community Association on city-owned land in Agincourt North. The garden provides native pollinator habitat plus environmental education, biodiversity and volunteer stewardship, and needs modest capital support for water storage and related infrastructure. The funds come from unused contributions under the McCowan Road and Finch Avenue zoning, redirected at the Chief Planner's discretion for a community benefit in the vicinity.

title: Modernizing the City’s Permit Parking Program and Managing On-Street Parking Demand in Toronto's Growing Neighbourhoods - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: growth, permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: The item asks council to review and modernize the city's permit parking program as Davenport neighbourhoods see growing competition for on-street spaces. The motion notes that multiplex permissions have added gentle density, and that the current program lets households get unlimited permits for multiple vehicles at one address, reducing availability for other residents, visitors and service providers. It asks Transportation Services to study permit eligibility and reasonable limits, framing the review as a fairness measure that could also support sustainable travel choices.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2026.EX31.8 - Amendments to the Toronto Transit Commission Records Retention Schedule (Municipal Code Chapter 219, Records, Corporate (Local Boards)) - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, records; ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: The item asks council to reopen and amend its May 2026 consent approval of the TTC records retention schedule amendments, which were procedurally ineffective. The Municipal Code requires the Corporate Records Retention Committee to review proposed retention amendments before council can consider them, but the proposal was never brought to the committee before the TTC communicated it to council. The motion corrects the procedural defect so the amendments can be properly considered.

title: Increase Resources for Tree Maintenance and Arborist Staffing - by Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: trees, urban forest; ash trees
brief: The item asks council to order an assessment of increasing staffing for tree maintenance and arborist work, reporting back in the first quarter of 2027 with budget impacts. The motion says many neighbourhoods face long delays in routine tree pruning, creating safety concerns, obstructed sidewalks and visibility problems, while the city's commitment to grow the tree canopy to 40 percent by 2050 adds to the workload. The report would cover the current pruning backlog, the additional arborists and forestry staff needed for a sustainable pruning cycle, and related costs.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2026.TE31.38 - 49 Ontario Street (Phase 1) - Construction Staging Area - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: construction, permit parking; building, on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: This is a procedural item: The item asks council to reopen and amend its April 2026 approval for the 49 Ontario Street construction staging area after the developer revised its timeline. The motion moves the Ontario Street staging period to run September 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027, covering a 5.5-metre-wide portion of the east sidewalk and boulevard allowance north of Adelaide Street East. It also updates the associated daily occupation rate from $4.25 to $4.50 for that period.

title: Pedestrian Safety Improvements Surrounding Yonge Street and Eglinton Avenue - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: pedestrians, safety; pedestrianization, public safety
brief: The item asks council to install pedestrian scrambles, with all-way pedestrian phases, at Yonge Street and Eglinton Avenue, which sees about 4,500 pedestrians an hour, and at Roehampton Avenue and Orchard View Boulevard. The motion says the scrambles would cut pedestrian delay, handle the crossing demand from the TTC and new Crosstown LRT stations, and reduce pedestrian-vehicle conflicts, coordinated with signal retiming at neighbouring intersections. It also proposes added signage for the one-way designations on Roehampton and Broadway Avenues.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Hate Has No Home Here - a Rainbow Crosswalk for R.H. McGregor School - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: 2SLGBTQIA+; gay; homosexual; lesbian; queer; transgender; two-spirit
brief: The item asks council to release $35,000 in Section 37 funds to install a rainbow crosswalk at Durant Avenue and Mortimer Avenue for R.H. McGregor School, after a student-made Pride flag on the school fence was destroyed by fire in June. The school community responded with dozens of flags and submitted a petition with hundreds of names asking for a permanent sign that Hate Has No Home Here. The funds come from the 201 Carlaw Avenue and 66 Boston Avenue development's Section 37 agreement for the pedestrian crossover installation.

title: Advancing a Heritage Conservation District for Corktown - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: heritage conservation districts, neighbourhoods; cultural neighbourhoods; ethnic neighbourhoods; neighborhoods, heritage districts; historic areas
brief: The item asks council to have staff study the Corktown neighbourhood, between Shuter Street, Front Street and Eastern Avenue, Berkeley Street and the Don River, for a possible heritage conservation district. The motion notes the area's listed heritage properties identified through the 2019 King Parliament Secondary Plan and its evolution from Indigenous habitation and the founding of York through 19th-century residential and commercial life to working-class and industrial uses. The review request follows a canvass of residents and outreach from heritage advocate Coralina Lemos.

title: Proclaiming July as Caribbean Heritage Month - by Councillor Neethan Shan, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: [people in culture], heritage designation;
