brief: The item asks council to proclaim July as Caribbean Heritage Month, honouring the more than 315,000 Torontonians of Caribbean heritage and their contributions to the city's economic, social, political and cultural life. The motion cites the Toronto Caribbean Carnival, nearly 60 years old and drawing more than 2 million visitors a year with an economic injection of between $467 million and $532 million, plus Caribbean-owned business hubs like Little Jamaica and Scarborough, home to about 90,000 residents of Caribbean origin. It frames the proclamation as recognizing a formative part of Toronto's identity.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Ward 18 Participatory Budgeting Projects - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: Through Ward 18's participatory budgeting process, residents chose park improvements for the Willowdale East and Newtonbrook East neighbourhoods, including seating, picnic tables, a gazebo, a pickleball court, adult fitness equipment and ping pong tables. Councillor Lily Cheng's motion asks council to release $500,000 in Section 37 funds from the 5182 Yonge Street development so the locally supported projects can proceed. The cash flow is $50,000 in 2026 and $450,000 in 2027.

title: Seeing the Forest and the Trees: Preserving the Green Space, Ravines, Structures and Tree Canopy with Public Accessibility, Security and Maintenance at the Forest Valley Outdoor Centre - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: urban forest;
brief: The item asks council to order a new strategic plan for the Forest Valley Outdoor Centre in York Centre (Ward 6), the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority lands the city manages with a rich history as a day camp and school-board outdoor site. With the school board's seasonal lease ending and the city likely to keep managing the lands and buildings, the motion says the site needs a plan to stay well-maintained, safe and active while preserving its green space, ravines and tree canopy. It asks Parks and Recreation to lead the plan under a renewed conservation authority agreement.

title: Supporting Continued Investments in the Toronto Harbour Nautical Centre at Harbourfront Centre - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: community centres, investment; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to amend the city's 1997 lease with Harbourfront Centre to permit a 25-year licence for York Bay Marine Services Inc. to keep operating the Toronto Harbour Nautical Centre, which offers sailing, powerboating, paddling and boat-rental programming on the central waterfront including for Harbourfront Centre's children's camp. The operator says it has already invested about $450,000 in the facility but cannot finance further capital and leasehold improvements under a shorter-term arrangement. The current lease lets Harbourfront Centre grant subleases of up to five years, so a city amendment is needed for the longer term.

title: Authority to Accept Federation of Canadian Municipalities Grant to Advance Safe School Travel Planning and Street Design to Macklin Public School - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: road safety, schools; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums
brief: The item asks council to authorize Transportation Services to enter a $125,000 grant agreement with the Federation of Canadian Municipalities' Green Municipal Fund for safe school travel planning and street design at Macklin Public School. Staff applied for the grant to support the approved Ingleton Boulevard road safety project under the Alton Towers Neighbourhood Connection plan, improving road safety including for school children and access to schools. The grant would fund travel planning, engagement, education and capital enhancements like widened sidewalks, crossings, speed humps and cycle tracks, coordinated with the road's 2027 resurfacing.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds Gardiner Gateways East Project - Intersection and Underpass Improvements at Lower Jarvis, Lower Sherbourne, Lower Parliament and Cherry Streets - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: projects, public realm; public spaces
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to release Section 37 funds for the Gardiner Gateways East project: intersection and underpass improvements at Lower Jarvis, Lower Sherbourne, Lower Parliament and Cherry Streets under the Under Gardiner Public Realm Plan. The plan, approved in April 2024 with The Bentway for the 7-kilometre elevated corridor, calls for pedestrian lighting, wayfinding and placemaking to improve north-south crossings, supported by the Waterfront and Old Town BIAs' strategies. The official figures list $1,094,007.50 for the project, with component amounts of $300,798.70, $168,614.84, $493,552.22, $105,713.40, $25,328.34 and $2,992.50.

title: Billy Bishop Way Revisited: Leveraging a Road Less Travelled - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: development, roads; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), developing land; development (land); land development
brief: The item asks council to have the Downsview Major Streets Environmental Assessment team study making Billy Bishop Way the main north-south bus and truck route through the Downsview Lands, instead of concentrating that traffic on the proposed Dufferin Street extension. With 115,000 new residents and 52,000 new jobs expected over 30 years across 15 neighbourhoods, residents of the Downsview Ancaster community fear the Dufferin extension would carry thousands of cars, trucks and TTC vehicles daily through their area. The motion says designating Billy Bishop Way for buses, trucks and other through traffic would take pressure off Dufferin and relieve the Ancaster community to the west.

title: Amending Item 2025.TE22.3 - 72 Perth Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: The item asks council to amend its 2025 approval for 72 Perth Avenue to delay the required 131-square-metre on-site parkland dedication until up to 30 months after the first above-grade building permit is issued. The applicant says conveying the park before that point, as previously required after council reduced the dedication from 134 square metres, would cause hardship with construction timelines. The motion lets construction and conveyance coincide with completion of all site activity.

title: A Fair Approach to Removing Nuisance Trees in the City - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: planning & development (sc), trees; ash trees
brief: The item asks council to make tree removal rules fairer for residents with nuisance trees, saying the current tree replacement policy can cost property owners upwards of $10,000 to $15,000 and feels punitive. The motion directs Environment, Climate and Forestry, as part of the planned 2027 Tree By-law report back, to review resident feedback and recommend ways to balance nuisance-tree impacts with canopy goals, update compensation ratios where removal is appropriate, and consider financial relief programs for nuisance-tree permits. It frames the change as balancing the 40-percent-canopy goal with equity for residents.

title: Avoiding the Allen Road and Eglinton Redux: Getting People Where They Want to Go in Downsview - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza
topics: business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations
brief: The item asks council to order an early transportation planning study for the Downsview Lands area, warning that redevelopment plans bringing an estimated 115,000 new residents and 52,000 new jobs over 30 years could repeat the Allen Road and Eglinton congestion experience. The DUKE Heights Business Improvement Area, with more than 4,000 businesses employing over 32,000 people, says the current plans with two major north-south streets, the Dufferin extension and Billy Bishop Way, would bring severe congestion to Sheppard Avenue West. The motion asks for solutions covering the area from Sheppard West to north of Steeprock, between the Barrie GO tracks and Allen Road.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for a Heritage Plaque for CHUM Radio - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: plaques; heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques
brief: The item asks council to release $10,000.00 ($10,000) in Section 37 funds for a Heritage Toronto plaque honouring CHUM Radio near Yonge Street and Jackes Avenue, where the station was based at 1331 Yonge Street. The motion recalls CHUM-AM switching to rock on May 27, 1957 with Elvis's All Shook Up, pioneering rock broadcasting in Toronto with visits by Elvis and the Beatles, and CHUM-FM's 1968 rock launch, with the station recognized by the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as significant in music history. The plaque marks CHUM's impact on Toronto's music and broadcast culture.

title: Heritage Designation Study - Sneaky Dee’s - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The item asks council to have the Chief Planner evaluate the Sneaky Dee's property at 431 College Street for heritage designation, after the applicant withdrew a July 3, 2026 redevelopment application that would have demolished the venue. The motion describes the generations-old music venue as a launching pad for local artists and a piece of Toronto's cultural identity, and says the Save Sneaky Dee's campaign drew thousands of supporters. Volunteers have begun assembling evidence for the designation review.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2026.MM42.49 - 447 Horsham Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Withdraw Appeal from Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor  Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: land, planning & development (sc); property
brief: This is a procedural item: The item asks council to reopen and amend its June 2026 decision on 447 Horsham Avenue so the City Solicitor withdraws the city's appeal to the Toronto Local Appeal Body. The committee had approved a three-storey, six-unit apartment building there, and the solicitor appealed June 22 to preserve the city's rights before council directed it. Since then, the councillor's office, planning staff and the applicant have worked with neighbours on improvements, including east-side window changes to reduce overlook, and the motion would end the city's challenge.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds for Barbara Hall Park Off-Leash Area - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: dog off-leash areas; dog parks; dogs off leash parks; dogs off-leash parks; leash free areas; leash free dog walking areas; leash free parks; leash free zones; leash-free areas; leash-free dog walking areas; leash-free zones; off leash areas; off leash parks
brief: The item asks council to release $1,520,000 ($1.52 million) in Section 42 parkland funds from a nearby Ward 13 development for the Barbara Hall Park off-leash area redesign. Consultation since spring 2023 with the neighbourhood and the Barbara Hall Park Dog Park Association produced a recommended design with new gates, fences, bins, seating, tree planting, tree guards and a drinking fountain. The funds let construction start in 2027 as planned.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Support Indigenous Placekeeping in Allan Gardens - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: First Nations; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples
brief: The item asks council to release $350,000 in Section 37 community benefits for Indigenous placekeeping capital improvements in Allan Gardens, with $75,000 of that going to the Friends of Allan Gardens for engagement with Indigenous communities and organizations. The groups would co-steward a long-term vision and select a community-identified name for the project. Allan Gardens is a historic gathering place for Indigenous peoples, and since 2022 a Sacred Fire maintained by Fire Keepers has burned there in mourning and ceremony for children recovered from former residential school grounds.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Deliver an Association of Community Centres Space in Regent Park - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: The item asks council to release $9,000,000 ($9 million) in Section 37 funds to deliver a new Association of Community Centres space in Regent Park, co-located with the future Parliament Street District Library branch in the neighbourhood's future civic square. Secured through the Regent Park Phases 4 and 5 approvals, the community-governed facility would give residents, grassroots groups and local initiatives affordable space and serve as a civic anchor for Downtown East. The $9,000,000 total comprises $100,000 and $8,900,000 components drawn from source accounts of $3,564,754.62, $4,428.83, $3,671,421.16 and $1,759,395.39.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Clock Tower Trail Wayfinding and Placemaking Pole Wraps - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: The item asks council to release $120,000 in Section 37 funds for Clock Tower Trail wayfinding and placemaking pole wraps in downtown Toronto. The pedestrian route loops through Bay Cloverhill and Church Wellesley, connecting parks, public spaces and public art, and takes its name from the historic St. Charles Clock Tower at 484 to 488 Yonge Street, running between Charles Street East and McGill Street on both sides of Yonge. Transportation Services would procure and install wraps on existing poles to create cohesive visual cues along the trail.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Toronto Community Housing for Security Cameras - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: security, social housing; community housing; housing allowance; housing projects; low income housing; non profit housing; non-profit housing; public housing; rent geared to income assistance; rent geared to income housing; rent subsidies; rent supplement; subsidized housing; subsidized rent; subsidized units
brief: The item asks council to release $2,350,000 ($2.35 million) in Section 37 funds to Toronto Community Housing for new CCTV cameras and related infrastructure at 275, 285 and 295 Shuter Street and 275, 325 and 375 Bleecker Street in St. James Town and Moss Park. Tenant safety meetings with police, the city's violence intervention unit and community agencies surfaced concerns about unauthorized entry, trespassing and building security; costs beyond these funds fall to Toronto Community Housing. The official figures list $1,880,000 and $470,000 as component amounts of the $2,350,000 total.

title: Authority to Accept Donations from Midtown Ravines Group for the Vale of Avoca Improvement Project - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: donation; bequest; toy drive
brief: The item asks council to accept donations totalling $50,000 from the Midtown Ravines Group, a registered charity of ten residents' associations, for the Vale of Avoca Improvement Project in the Yellow Creek ravine near Yonge and St. Clair East. The project, led with the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority, will develop a coordinated plan to stabilize the creek, mitigate erosion hazards threatening trails, staircases and adjacent properties, and improve ravine access and experience. The conservation authority released a request for proposals in 2026 for the evaluation, engagement and design work.

title: Toronto Transit Commission Infrastructure Capacity and Development - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: public transit, public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: The item asks council to address the gap between the pace of development approvals and unfunded TTC capacity, warning that rush-hour crowding will worsen as new buildings fill up. The motion cites College Station, built in 1954, where on average one-third of peak trains are too full for everyone to board, and says the TTC's development comments protect its physical infrastructure but do not address whether the system can serve the new population. It points to the unfunded 2019 Capacity Expansion Plan as an implicit but incomplete reliance, without federal and provincial funding for the needed capacity.

title: Enhancing Tenant Safety Through a Review of Toronto Community Housing Corporation CCTV Camera Coverage, Visitor Verification Measures and Related Policies - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: privacy, residential tenants, tenants; renters; tenancy agreements
brief: The item asks council to order a review of Toronto Community Housing camera coverage, visitor verification measures and related policies to enhance tenant safety across the city's public housing communities. Recent safety meetings at Moss Park Apartments and the Wellesley Community Centre surfaced tenant concerns about building security, unauthorized entry, trespassing, package theft and residents' inability to see who is at their door, affecting seniors, families, newcomers and people living alone. TCHC has begun environmental design reviews and committed to reviewing cameras and access control; the motion seeks a broader citywide review.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Building Roots - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: The item asks council to release $70,000 in Section 37 funds to Building Roots, a registered charity serving Moss Park, to buy and install a new shipping container expanding its operations. Since 2013 the organization has run food security and community-building programs, distributing about 185,000 pounds of fresh food in 2025 and supporting an average of 800 community members each week. The money comes from the 245 to 285 Queen Street East development's Section 37 agreement.

title: Authorization to Release Section 45 Funds from the Development at 8 Elm Street and 348-354 Yonge Street for Streetscape Improvements on Elm Street in the Downtown Yonge Business Improvement Area - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations
brief: The item asks council to release $336,979 in Section 45 funds from the 8 Elm Street and 348-354 Yonge Street developments for streetscape improvements on Elm Street by the Downtown Yonge Business Improvement Area, following the council-approved Elm Street Streetscape Vision guidelines. The BIA has been working with the city on the Elm Street upgrades. The funds would be forwarded on a one-time basis through the 2026 operating budget once the BIA signs an undertaking on their use and reporting.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Toronto Community Housing for Cooling Upgrades at 275 Shuter Street - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: The item asks council to release $150,000 in Section 37 funds to Toronto Community Housing for cooling infrastructure in the community room at 275 Shuter Street. After a recent community event held in an uncomfortably hot room, the motion says the upgrades would let tenants use the space year-round. The money comes from the Queen, Richmond and Ontario Street area Section 37 agreement, through the Housing Secretariat's capital budget with 2027 cash flow.

title: Improving Safety and Access from Aberfoyle Crescent to Tom Riley Park - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: The item asks council to review safety and access on the Ward 3 pathway connecting Aberfoyle Crescent, east of Islington Avenue near Bloor Street West, to the main Tom Riley Park trail, a critical link to Islington Station, schools and businesses. The connecting segment gets no winter maintenance while the main path does, and heavy daily use plus a steep grade create winter hazards for students, seniors and transit users, worsened by Islington Station construction detours. The motion asks Parks and Recreation to review options, including winter maintenance and alternative access points, and report to the November 24, 2026 Etobicoke York Community Council.

title: Holding Utility Companies Accountable for Avoidable Service Interruptions - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: construction permits (right-of-way), electric distribution utilities, utilities, utility digs; curb cut permits; driveway paving permits; driveway resurfacing permits; driveway widening permits; landscaping permits (right-if way), electricity distribution utilities; electricity retailers, hard surface cuts; utility cuts, power utilties
brief: The item asks council to investigate holding utility companies accountable for avoidable service interruptions, such as outages caused by cables buried too shallow, draped over fences or left on grass. The motion says improperly installed infrastructure leaves residents without phone, internet or cable for days, and asks Transportation Services to study a framework requiring providers to give bill reductions, refunds or other compensation when customers lose service due to shoddy installation.

title: Use of Rubber Speed Bumps on Roadways - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: road safety, speed humps, transportation (sc); sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: The item asks council to let Transportation Services use rubber speed humps on roadways beyond laneways, with locations approved by community council. The motion says speeding endangers pedestrians, cyclists and motorists, and that rubber humps, already used on Toronto laneways and other Ontario roadways, can be installed faster than permanent humps and removed if unneeded. The change would give the city flexibility while permanent traffic calming is planned.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Creation and Installation of a Plaque to Commemorate Research Enterprises Limited - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: The item asks council to release $10,000.00 ($10,000) in Section 37 funds to Heritage Toronto for a plaque commemorating Research Enterprises Limited, the short-lived Toronto Crown corporation that became Leaside's largest employer during the Second World War. At its peak the company covered 22 hectares, employed 7,500 men and women, and produced $220 million worth of radar systems and optical instruments for the Allies; its factories later housed Corning Glass, Philips Electronics and other firms. The plaque marks the company's history and the Canadian war effort in Leaside, complementing planned interpretive signs in Radar Park.

title: Securing A Permanent Facility for the Central Eglinton Community Centre - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: community centres; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes
brief: The item asks council to secure a permanent facility for the Central Eglinton Community Centre at 160 Eglinton Avenue East, which serves seniors, families and newcomers from about 16,000 square feet. The centre is one of the ten Association of Community Centres, volunteer-board-run multi-purpose facilities funded through the operating budget that strengthen civic engagement and equity-focused outcomes. The motion connects to the council-directed facilities and operations plan that will set a prioritized, citywide, multi-year framework for the centres' sustainability and growth.

title: Reimbursement for Works Associated with a New Street Connection of Olympic Garden Drive to Yonge Street - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
brief: The item asks council to authorize reimbursement for works associated with the new Olympic Garden Drive connection from Cummer Avenue to Yonge Street at Narges Drive, approved through the 5799 Yonge Street subdivision. Building the road required acquiring part of 5795 Yonge Street, with development charge credits already authorized for the land costs, and also forces relocation and reconstruction of existing access, service and utility infrastructure at 5795 Yonge. The motion says such relocation works would normally form part of road construction costs and seeks reimbursement for them.

title: Section 37 Funds for the Mural at Wilson Subway Station - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: arts and culture;
brief: The item asks council to release $75,000.00 in Section 37 funds from the 30 Tippett Road (South Lands) development for a STEPS public art mural at Wilson Subway Station. STEPS, Sustainable Thinking and Expression on Public Space, has an agreement with the TTC for the mural project, and the funds would be forwarded once STEPS signs an undertaking on their use and financial reporting. The motion is urgent because the community has waited a long time and wants it done before summer's end.

title: Granting Members of Council Access to all Toronto Parking Authority Board Meeting Materials - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: boards of management; boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: The item asks council to amend the Parking Authority by-law so members of council can access all Toronto Parking Authority board materials, including confidential attachments, on request. Since council moved the TPA board to an all-staff composition in November 2025, no councillors have access to its confidential materials. The motion says the access is needed for council to exercise oversight under the interim structure until a new board including councillors is established, and is urgent as the last regular meeting of the term.

title: Toronto Needs Container-Friendly Trees as an Option - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
brief: The item asks council to supplement the Yonge Street planter work with a study of container-friendly tree options, saying Willowdale's Yonge Street planters are mostly filled with weeds and the Transform Yonge timeline remains unclear. The motion directs Environment, Climate and Forestry to fold into the MM42.36 report-back an analysis of improving tree survivability in different street-tree infrastructure, including species beyond those the city currently plants, along Yonge from Sheppard to Finch. It is urgent because staff are already carrying out the related work.

title: Strengthening Protections for Homebuyers - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel
topics: homeowners; home owners
brief: The item asks council to strengthen homebuyer protections after reports of residents buying new builds from bad-faith developers posing as owner-builders to dodge provincial regulation, leaving people in unsafe homes facing health risks and financial hardship. The motion asks the Chief Building Official and the Chief Communications Officer, with the Home Construction Regulatory Authority and Tarion, to develop a public awareness campaign on owner-builder risks, and calls on Ontario to review the regulatory framework and close the gaps. The matter is urgent for resident health and safety.

title: Amending Item 2025.TE19.9 - 90 Eastdale Avenue and 2 Secord Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: The item asks council to amend its February 2025 zoning approval for 90 Eastdale Avenue and 2 Secord Avenue, a 41-storey development with affordable and rental housing commitments, to facilitate the delegated payment-in-lieu of bike parking program process. The amendment adds recommendations and revises the draft zoning by-law for that process. The bill was withheld pending the Section 37 agreement securing affordable housing and rental protections, rental demolition approval and servicing matters. The motion also lists $552 and $1103 as additional listed figures.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 1478 to 1496 Kingston Road for a New Public Mural in Birchcliff Village - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: urban beautification; 20-minute makeover; beautification projects; clean & beautiful city; clean and beautiful city; clean city beautiful city; community clean-up days; facade improvement; mural program; neighbourhood beautification
brief: The item asks council to release $27,000 in Section 37 funds for a new public mural in Birchcliff Village, near Birchcliff Avenue and Kingston Road. Local artists, businesses including Bodega by City Cottage, and community members have volunteered energy and resources to advance the long-standing idea of a mural creating a sense of arrival and identity for the historic village. The one-time increase goes to the 2026-2035 Transportation Services capital budget for the StreetART program, and the motion is urgent given ongoing community beautification efforts.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 and Section 42 Funds for Improvements to Thompson Dog Off-Leash Area - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: dog off-leash areas; dog parks; dogs off leash parks; dogs off-leash parks; leash free areas; leash free dog walking areas; leash free parks; leash free zones; leash-free areas; leash-free dog walking areas; leash-free zones; off leash areas; off leash parks
brief: The item asks council to release $1,046,569.72 ($1.05 million) in Section 37 and Section 42 funds to improve the Thompson Dog Off-Leash Area, replacing the pea gravel surface that has generated accessibility, maintenance, cleanliness and drainage complaints. The funding combines $400,000 in Section 37 funds with $646,569.72 ($647,000) in Section 42 funds, the latter drawn as $300,000 and $346,569.72. Artificial turf designed for off-leash use would improve durability, accessibility and year-round usability for a community that has waited years for dog park improvements.

title: Ensuring High Standard Ice Quality at City of Toronto’s Outdoor Artificial Outdoor Stand-Alone Pleasure Skating Facilities - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: ice rinks, outdoor ice rinks; airs (rinks); civic centre ice rinks; hockey rinks; ice pads; ice surfaces; natural ice rinks; nirs; rinks; skating rinks, outdoor artificial ice rinks; outdoor artificial rinks; outdoor hockey rinks; outdoor ice pads; outdoor rinks; outdoor skating rinks
brief: The item asks council to have Parks and Recreation review outdoor skate trail operations and maintenance with the goal of consistent, high-quality ice at the city's artificial stand-alone pleasure skating facilities. The motion notes the city keeps adding permit-free skate trails, which draw crowds and are harder for staff to manage than boarded rinks, and that freeze-thaw cycles from climate change hurt conditions. A timely review would let improvements take effect in the new season.

title: 743 Warden Avenue - Amending Section 37 Agreement for Blocks 6, 7 and 8 Plan 66M-2549 - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: The item asks council to amend the Section 37 agreement for Blocks 6, 7 and 8 of the 743 Warden Avenue development, a 202-residential-townhouse project with commercial buildings, public roads, a park and a stormwater pond. The blocks were sequenced as Phase 3 to coordinate municipal road infrastructure and the commercial and residential blocks, with a holding provision in place. The motion adjusts the agreement for those blocks.

title: Commemorating Former Councillor and Toronto Transit Commission Chair Howard Moscoe - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, councillors; aldermen; alderwomen; city councellors; city councillors; council members; councilors; members of council, ttc
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow is asking council to authorize the City Manager to identify, approve and implement a commemorative naming of a city asset or other public recognition for former councillor and TTC Chair Howard Moscoe, following council's earlier direction in 2026.MM42.31. Staff are assessing options and will consult the Moscoe family, the local councillor and stakeholders; the motion also seeks authority to waive any city policies or procedures that would delay the commemoration. The matter is urgent to ensure timely implementation during the council recess.

title: Celebrating the Win: Free August Ferry Rides for Kids and Seniors - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Mayor Chow
topics: ferries, ferry tickets; ferry boat tickets, ferry boats; ferryboats
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to make Toronto Island Ferry round-trip tickets free for children, youth and older adults from August 1 to 31, 2026, following the federal decision not to move forward with expanding the Island airport and in recognition of residents who spoke out. The motion waives admission for those fare categories, infants already ride free, and amends the 2026 Fleet Services capital budget by $1,389,589.69 ($1.4 million), shifting that amount from debt funding to Section 37 community benefits from the 1 to 7 Yonge Street development for shoreline infrastructure and Jack Layton Ferry Terminal improvements. The source also lists $940,000 as an additional figure connected with the fare waiver. The matter is urgent as this is the last meeting to allocate the funds.

title: Consideration of Cycling Infrastructure Opportunities within the area of the Doris Avenue Road Extension Project south of Sheppard Avenue East - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
brief: The item asks council to consider cycling infrastructure opportunities within the Doris Avenue road extension project area south of Sheppard Avenue East, the new connection extending Tradewind Avenue north to Sheppard. The 2022 environmental assessment recommended a two-phase approach with an interim offset intersection and a future realigned intersection, and the project already includes bikeways along Sheppard between Kenneth Avenue and Yonge Street. The motion asks council to look at cycling options for the extension area as the project advances.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for A New Mural for a New Bridge - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: arts and culture, budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: The item asks council to release $5,000.00 in Section 37 funds to the Riverside District Business Improvement Area for the design and installation of a new mural at the Queen Street East rail bridge underpass this fall. The Riverside BIA has long planned the mural but waited for Metrolinx to finish the Ontario Line bridge and grant approval, which it now has. The $5,000.00 comes from the 90 to 100 Broadview Avenue development at $3,970.13 and the 201 Carlaw Avenue and 66 Boston Avenue development at $1,029.87.

title: Dedicated Commercial Loading Zone at 623 Danforth Avenue - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: loading zones; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones
brief: The item asks council to give Pape Market Foodland exclusive use of the commercial loading zone beside its store at 623 Danforth Avenue, which the grocer funded when the Danforth Cycle Track was installed in 2021. The business says delivery vehicles keep facing parking enforcement penalties in the shared zone, hurting operations that depend on frequent daily deliveries. The motion says exclusive use would improve efficiency, reduce conflicts and honour the city's original permission for the zone.

title: Provision of Access to Waste Receptacles On-Site for Customer Use in Quick-Serve Restaurants - by Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Neethan Shan
topics: waste;
brief: The item asks council to have Solid Waste Management Services research regulatory, licensing, operational and legal mechanisms to require all food service establishments to provide on-site waste receptacles for customer use. The motion says some quick-serve restaurants leave customers no option but public litter bins, which are not designed to take food-service waste. The matter is urgent so staff can begin work over the summer before council's next meetings.

title: 74 Kirknewton Road - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: This is a procedural item: Authorizing the City Solicitor to appeal the Committee of Adjustment's approval at 74 Kirknewton Road, a new three-storey detached home with a rear two-storey garden suite, to the Toronto Local Appeal Body and resolve the matter for the city is up for a decision by Council. The applicant had reduced the original eight variances to six covering building height, front, side and rear setbacks and landscaping; the Toronto and East York panel approved the application on July 22, 2026. The matter is urgent because the appeal deadline is August 11, 2026.

title: Advancing Alternate Section 37 Agreement Contributions at Bloor and Dufferin - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: The item asks council to accept a cash contribution instead of the planned below-grade tunnel connection to Dufferin Station as the Section 37 community benefit for the Bloor and Dufferin development, saying that best serves the community. The cash would be redirected to affordable housing, community and cultural amenities and public realm improvements around Dufferin Station identified through resident consultation. The motion directs staff to bring a city-initiated zoning amendment exercising the cash option once Block F is conveyed to the city, and is urgent for clarity during the council recess.

title: Protecting Toronto’s Live Music Venues - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: music;
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to have planning, economic development and development review staff continue proactive work to protect Toronto's live music venues, reporting back through the Culture Connects plan. The motion notes the city's venues face rising rents, insurance and development pressures, with recent losses including Sneaky Dee's among past closures, and that many city divisions are already looking at supports. Potential steps listed include Official Plan and zoning updates, design guidelines for mixed-use developments, cultural heritage designations and land trusts.

title: Authorization to Release Section 45 Funds from the Development at 2328 to 2350 Kingston Road for a Public Art Mural - by Councilor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: The item asks council to release up to $20,521.00 in Section 45 funds from the 2328 to 2350 Kingston Road development for the design and installation of a public art mural in the local area by Cliffside Village GP Inc., the landowner. The funds would be forwarded once the contribution is paid, the mural completed, a cost schedule provided and an above-grade building permit issued. The matter is urgent because the community wants a replacement mural after longstanding ones were demolished and the developer is willing to partner now.

title: Facing the Facts: Endorsing the Findings and Warnings of the Office of the Inspector General of Policing for an Urgent Reckoning and Immediate Action Necessary to Address and Stop Rising Antisemitism and All Forms of Hate - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: public safety & protection (sc), safety; public safety
brief: The item asks council to endorse the findings and warnings of the Office of the Inspector General of Policing's July 2026 Notice of Issue on the increase in antisemitism and hate-motivated incidents, and to call for urgent action to stop rising antisemitism and all forms of hate. The motion describes the Inspector General's role in policing oversight under the Community Safety and Policing Act and says notices of issue flag emerging matters that could harm community safety or public confidence if unaddressed. It frames the endorsement as an urgent reckoning and immediate action item for the city.

title: Considering the Cumulative Impacts of Development Activity in Cliffcrest to Ensure Proper Planning and Balanced Growth - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
brief: The item asks council to consider the cumulative impacts of the unprecedented number of medium-to-large residential development applications along Kingston Road between Brimley Road and Markham Road in Cliffcrest, atop the environmentally sensitive Scarborough Bluffs. The motion says better coordination across city divisions is needed so services, infrastructure, environmental protection and the public realm keep pace as the neighbourhood grows. It proposes an ongoing process to monitor development activity and share information, while welcoming the added housing supply during the affordability crisis.

title: Revitalizing St. Patrick’s Market Square - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: redevelopment, regeneration areas; rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to support revitalizing St. Patrick's Market Square as part of CreateTO's long-term Grange Precinct real estate strategy for downtown west, covering the market, the square, Harrison Pool, University Settlement and Grange Park. The strategy aims to coordinate capital investments across divisions, maximize public value of city-owned assets, respond to community recreation and social needs, and improve the public realm. Community consultation has consistently identified the square as a valued gathering place and expressed interest in improvements.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds for a Refresh and a Water Feature for Coxwell Common - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: water parks;
brief: The item asks council to release $100,000.00 ($100,000) in Section 42 funds to refresh Coxwell Common at 1555 Danforth, which formally became a city park after 30 years as an informal green space hosting the weekly Courtyard Farmers' Market. The money would assess the long-unused irrigation infrastructure built for a planned central water feature, review feasibility and design, and renew planting beds for biodiversity and climate resilience. The official breakdown draws the $100,000.00 ($100,000) from multiple source accounts: $1.24, $151.52, $3.59, $150.42, $106.13, $98.49, $253.80, $15.28, $6.84, $8,221.70, $6.98, $4.15, $11,058.70, $5,552.57, $392.64, $546.35, $59.70, $475.10, $11.87, $9,045.41, $136.98, $96.55, $7,759.51, $8,870.72, $188.94, $167.96, $922.89, $43.76, $163.78, $14,654.02, $16,307.29, $13,107.21 and $527.85.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Locally Branded Street Signs for the Bedford Park Neighbourhood - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: roads, street name signs; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), street signs
brief: The item asks council to release $37,596.72 in Section 37 funds for locally branded Bedford Park neighbourhood street signs. The motion traces the 150-year-old neighbourhood's identity from its 19th-century farming hamlet origins through the 1890 street railway and the 1873 Bedford Park Hotel, arguing the signage would reinforce wayfinding, community pride and the area's historic character. The project is a priority of the local residents' association, and the motion is urgent to meet timing for Bedford Park residents' initiatives.

title: Exploring a Partnership with Jays Care Foundation to Establish a Jays Care Academy in Toronto - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: baseball;
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow is asking council to have staff explore a partnership with the Jays Care Foundation to establish a Jays Care Academy in Toronto, a purpose-built community recreation hub with an indoor facility and up to four baseball fields for foundation and community use. The foundation, which uses baseball to teach life skills and build community spaces and funds diamond projects through its Field of Dreams grants, wants to use part of its fundraising proceeds, after the Blue Jays' 2025 World Series run, on the hub. The motion is urgent so staff can begin work and identify suitable city-owned sites before the summer recess.

title: Malvern Area Community Facilities and Services Working Group - Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Neethan Shan
topics: community centres, public realm; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, public spaces
brief: The item asks council to create a Malvern Area Community Facilities and Services Working Group as the Malvern Town Centre and surrounding redevelopments reshape Scarborough North. The motion says planning for housing, transportation, parks, public realm and community services should be informed by the needs of Malvern's large and diverse population, including significant Black, Indigenous and newcomer communities and other equity-deserving groups, consistent with the poverty reduction strategy and the action plan against anti-Black racism. Long-standing community anchor organizations would help ground the work.

title: Amending 2022.EY30.2 - 340 Mill Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Final Report to provide for a Development Charge Credit for cycling infrastructure requested by City Staff - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The item asks council to amend the 2022 zoning approval for the 19-storey infill rental building at 340 Mill Road, with 191 rental units, to provide a development charge credit for cycling infrastructure requested by city staff. The approval had required a $1,500,000 Section 37 cash contribution for parkland improvements at Centennial Park and connecting cycling infrastructure along Burnhamthorpe Road, which the applicant paid in full on May 7, 2025. The official figures also list $95,358 in connection with the credit amendment; the source text is truncated so the figure's precise role is not fully shown.

title: 39 Norfield Crescent - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
brief: This is a procedural item: Council votes on authorizing the City Solicitor to appeal the Committee of Adjustment's approval of a second-storey addition at 39 Norfield Crescent, creating a four-unit dwelling with a front-yard setback variance, to the Toronto Local Appeal Body and to negotiate a settlement. The committee approved the application on July 16, 2026; to preserve the city's appeal rights the solicitor filed with the appeal body on July 27. The motion lets the solicitor retain an outside consultant to assess the plan and potentially recommend a solution.

title: 340 St Clements Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: This is a procedural item: Council decides whether to authorize the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body over the refused six-storey, 54-unit apartment building at 340 St Clements Avenue. The applicant sought eleven variances covering building length, setbacks, landscaping, drive aisles, parking and loading; planning staff had asked the Committee of Adjustment to defer for further discussion, and the North York panel refused the application on July 9, 2026. The applicant appealed July 29, and the motion lets the solicitor and staff, with external consultants, oppose the appeal.

title: Exploring a Long-Term Lease for Jean Augustine Centre for Young Women's Empowerment - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: The item asks council to explore a long-term home for the Jean Augustine Centre for Young Women's Empowerment, whose current Etobicoke-Lakeshore lease is ending. The motion asks Corporate Real Estate Management and Social Development, with the Toronto District School Board and other divisions, to study converting 300 Birmingham Street into a Community Hub under the Community Space Tenancy Policy once the current lease ends, reporting back in the second quarter of 2027. The centre serves hundreds of girls and young women with mentorship, education and leadership supports.

title: Support for the Establishment of a National Fire Administration - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: fire and rescue services; fire fighting; fire services; fire suppression; firefighting; rescue; rescue operations; search and rescue
brief: The item asks council to support establishing a National Fire Administration within Public Safety Canada, developed with Canada's fire chiefs and fire service organizations. The motion cites roughly 3,200 fire departments across Canada and the growing scale and complexity of emergencies, including more frequent and severe wildfires and climate-related disasters, as the case for national coordination on policy, research, training and emergency management. It says the body would help communities maintain and replenish emergency equipment while respecting provincial and territorial jurisdiction.

title: Re-Opening and Amending 2026.TE28.4 - 808 Mount Pleasant Road and 247 to 251 Roehampton Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: This is a procedural item: The item asks council to reopen its February 2026 approval for the 61-storey mixed-use building at 808 Mount Pleasant Road and 247 to 251 Roehampton Avenue, with 889 residential units, 800 square metres of non-residential space and a new 317-square-metre park including a 471.6-square-metre EarlyON Centre. The motion lets the City Solicitor introduce the zoning bills pending execution and registration of the Section 37 agreement, since the amendment already blocks new buildings relying on the height and density until the community benefits are provided.

title: Exploring Alternative Governance Models for Biidaasige Park - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: The item asks council to explore alternative governance models, such as conservancies or collaborative partnerships used by other cities, for Biidaasige Park, the large new Port Lands park created through the tri-government flood protection project. The motion cites the park's scale, ecological restoration, public art and Indigenous placekeeping as reasons to examine whether a new stewardship model could strengthen programming, operations and maintenance alongside the Waterfront Toronto-led early activation strategy. The review would be about sustaining an asset meant to serve generations.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the development at 1478 to 1496 Kingston Road for a decorative Pedestrian Crossing at Kingston Road at Eastwood Avenue - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: The item asks council to release $27,000 in Section 37 funds from the 1478 to 1496 Kingston Road development to decorate the new signalized pedestrian crossing at Kingston Road and Eastwood Avenue, in front of the Scarboro Veterans Memorial Hall and Royal Canadian Legion Branch 13. The crossing itself, approved by community and city council and being installed this fall, improves safety for seniors, veterans and people with disabilities; the decoration would honour veterans and mark a gateway to the century-old branch. The matter is urgent with installation underway.

title: Facilitating Safe Construction Access for the Development at 8 to 10 Hyde Park Circle - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: construction; building
brief: The item asks council to facilitate safe construction access for the development at 8 to 10 Hyde Park Circle, whose trucks are currently routing through the Hyde Park Circle cul-de-sac instead of the planned Post Road access because of a narrow reserve along Post Road's north side. Residents report trucks blocking the dead-end street and compromising resident and emergency vehicle access. The motion seeks an interim solution while the applicant and Corporate Real Estate Management work out a permanent fix for the reserve.

title: 59 and 60 Annie Craig Drive Paver Fee Exemption - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: exemptions; exceptions
brief: The item asks council to grant a site-specific exemption from the Paver Maintenance Fee for about 45 square metres of unit pavers at 59 and 60 Annie Craig Drive, worth about $4,122.90 plus Harmonized Sales Tax. Streetscape redesign at the developers' voluntary initiative added layby spaces with pavers matching the existing design, triggering the fee the original approved design would not have incurred. The matter is urgent because the planned work starts before council's next meeting.

title: Stopping Auto Theft Before It Starts: Requiring Stronger Anti-Theft Technologies in New Vehicles - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: automobiles, theft; cars; used automobiles; used cars
brief: The item asks council to call for stronger anti-theft technologies in new vehicles, describing auto theft as a serious public safety concern that funds organized crime and strains police resources. Toronto Police data shows reported auto thefts fell nearly 24 percent in 2025 through enforcement and intelligence work, but police say criminal networks keep exploiting vehicle security weaknesses and enforcement alone cannot fix the problem. The motion targets the design and manufacturing stage as the needed preventative step.

title: Amending Item 2022.TE34.35 - 200 Queens Quay West - Zoning By-law Amendment - Final Report - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: zoning;
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to amend the 2022 zoning approval for 200 Queens Quay West, a 59-storey mixed-use building with 997 units of which at least 76 and up to 79 are affordable rentals with a 40-year affordability period. The motion revises the Open Door program financial incentives covering fee, parkland dedication, development charge and tax exemptions for up to 79 affordable units. The official figures list $442,477, $517,990, $89,675, $607,665, $1,050,142, $17,612, $13,904 and $3,708 in connection with the incentive adjustments; the source text is truncated so the purpose of each figure is not fully shown.

title: Re-opening of Item 2026.MM42.23 - Authorization to Release Section 45 Funds and Agreement with STEPS Public Art to Advance Utility Box and Picnic Bench Beautification in Liberty Village - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: arts and culture;
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to reopen its June 2026 approval for the Liberty Village utility box and picnic bench beautification and raise the budget from $55,000 to $60,000, switching the funding from Section 45 community benefits to minor-variance funds from 125 Western Battery Road. STEPS Public Art was confirmed in June as lead for the artist-led beautification of Bell utility boxes and Liberty Village Park picnic benches, but extra liaison work with Bell has been identified. The matter is urgent so STEPS can start site preparation, engagement and artist selection immediately.

title: Assumption of Lighting Maintenance and Repair on Thomas Clark Way - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: The item asks council to have the city take on maintenance and repair of the street lighting on Thomas Clark Way, a future public street dedicated more than a decade ago but never assumed into the road network after repeated construction delays, now pushed to at least April 2027. Three streetlights there have been inoperable for more than two years, with neither the city nor Toronto Hydro accepting responsibility while the condominium corporation carries infrastructure that would normally be public. The motion says it is unreasonable to keep that on the owners given the delays are the city's.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Richmond Street East Streetscape Improvements - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: The item asks council to release $800,000 in Section 37 funds for streetscape and cycle track upgrades on Richmond Street East beside Tricon Residential's ROQ City development at 261 Queen Street East. The funds, from the Queen, Richmond and Ontario Street area agreement, go into the 2026 capital budget so Transportation Services can contract Tricon to do the work beyond the site's approved site plan, aligned with the Old Town Toronto BIA's street network master plan. The matter is urgent because the site is near completion and council has no regular meeting until 2027.

title: Addressing Moribund Development Sites - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: construction; building
brief: The item asks council to address stalled development sites where approvals were granted but construction has not started due to economic conditions, financing problems and market uncertainty. The motion says vacant and inactive properties in established neighbourhoods must be maintained to protect public safety and neighbourhood quality, noting that 2025 property-standards amendments strengthened vacant-property rules but do not cover the specific situation of development sites. It asks council to develop tools aimed at these moribund sites.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Protective Tree Fencing in Yorkville Village - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations
brief: The item asks council to release $218,906, plus Harmonized Sales Tax, in Section 37 funds earmarked for greening Yorkville to install decorative fencing around 119 street tree pits on Bellair, Cumberland, Yorkville, Hazelton, Scollard and Bay streets. The Bloor Yorkville BIA wants the fences to protect the trees from heavy foot and vehicle traffic and fix tripping hazards, and will maintain them at its own expense; the ABC and Greater Yorkville residents' associations support the request. The source also cites $247,363, consistent with the tax-inclusive total.

title: Authority to Enter into an Extended Agreement with Parkrun Canada for Nominal Permits to Hold a Community Running Program
topics: agreements, permits, running tracks; permit renewal, tenancy agreements, walking tracks
brief: City Council is asked to extend the nominal-fee licensing agreement with Parkrun Canada to keep operating its free, volunteer-led weekly 5-kilometre run/walk on the Martin Goodman Trail on Saturday mornings. The pilot showed strong participation with no operational or park impacts, and the events use low-impact signage for about two hours per event with 5 to 15 volunteers. The item affects free public recreation access. Council decides.

title: Traffic Control Signals and Turn Prohibitions - Victoria Park Avenue and Wakehood Street
topics: traffic control systems, transportation, turn prohibitions (traffic); traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment, transportation services
brief: Transportation Services is asking City Council to approve traffic signals at Victoria Park Avenue and Wakehood Street, plus prohibitions on east-west through movements between Wakehood Street and the west-side plaza and on southbound left turns from Victoria Park onto Wakehood Street, all in effect at all times. The signals and restrictions are assessed as justified to improve safety for all road users. Council decides.

title: TTC St. Clair West Station - Sanitary Sewer Structural Lining Cost Recovery Agreement
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, fire hazards, sanitary sewers; ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: Authorizing the General Manager of Toronto Water to negotiate a cost-recovery agreement with the TTC for structural lining of sanitary sewer SL50048 near St. Clair West Station — related to TTC fire ventilation upgrades under the Line One Capacity Enhancement Program — so the TTC funds all design, construction, bypass pumping, restoration, inspection, and contingency costs is up for a decision by City Council. Council decides.

title: Amendments to the Policy for Accepting Potentially Contaminated Lands to be Conveyed to the City under the Planning Act
topics: contaminated soil, environmental policies, planning & development (sc); contaminated sites; soil contamination; soil pollution, environmental policy; environmental standards; sewer use bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council votes on amending the policy for accepting potentially contaminated lands conveyed to the city as a condition of development approval — updating subdivision Record of Site Condition requirements to match Ontario Regulation 153/04, renaming the policy to reflect conveyance authority under other legislation, adding provincial stratified soil standards, and other changes. The policy affects land the city receives through the development process. Council decides.

title: Restoring Road Safety Markings After Utility Cuts
topics: road construction, road safety, utility digs; hard surface cuts; utility cuts
brief: The item asks City Council to have Transportation Services require road-cut permit holders to fully reinstate all safety markings — crosswalks, bike lane markings, and other pavement markings — within two weeks of closing an excavation, with photographic proof as a condition of permit closeout. The motion responds to utility companies and city contractors damaging markings during road cuts and paving over them without timely restoration, which the councillor says has substantially eliminated safety markings for vulnerable road users. Council decides.

title: Indigenous Women and Children’s Shelter, 68 Sheppard Avenue West
topics: urban planning, women; city planning; community planning; regional planning, shelters for women
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng (Ward 18, Willowdale) has filed an administrative inquiry about the planned Indigenous Women and Children's Shelter at 68 Sheppard Avenue West, citing public discussion and what she describes as misinformation circulating about the project. She asks the General Manager of Toronto Shelter and Support Services, the CEO of CreateTO, the President of the Toronto Parking Authority, and the Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management to provide public clarifications so residents and her office have accurate information for constituent inquiries. The item seeks staff answers rather than a council decision.

title: Endorsement of the Council of Chief Medical Officers of Health Position Statement on Digital Culture and Child and Youth Well-Being
topics: health; health coverage
brief: The Board of Health decides whether to endorse the Council of Chief Medical Officers of Health's national position statement on digital culture and child and youth well-being, which calls for a precautionary public health approach to social media, smartphones, and online platforms. The principles align with the board's 2025 direction to work with school boards on student mental health and screen time under the Toronto Healthy Schools Strategy. The endorsement affects the city's public health stance on children's digital environments. The board decides.

title: Public Health Role in Indoor Air Quality
topics: air quality;
brief: Toronto Public Health's role in indoor air quality is before the Board of Health: staff note that oversight is split across governments and that most improvement levers sit with the province, building owners, employers, and school boards, while Toronto Public Health monitors health risks, responds to complaints, and investigates hazards. The report's recommendations focus on stronger public communication in line with federal and provincial guidance, continued collaboration with partners like school boards, and asking the province for measures to reduce wildfire smoke exposure. The recommendations affect how the city handles indoor air in homes, schools, and workplaces. The board decides on next steps.

title: Updating Administrative Authorities to Support Digital Public Engagement and 311 Service Delivery
topics: [activities in community and life], information and communication technology, non emergency municipal services, programs; 3-1-1; 311; 311 calls; non-emergency city services, ict; information and communication systems; information and technology; information technology; it
brief: City Council votes on updating administrative authorities for two resident-facing programs: the Digital Public Engagement Program, which modernizes how the city runs consultations and community engagement, and the Modernized 311 Program, which covers new 311 initiatives like Closing the Loop and the 311 website redesign. The report clarifies governance by placing the engagement program under the Chief Communications Officer and 311 under the Executive Director of the Customer Experience Division. The change affects how the city organizes public feedback and service access.

title: Amendments to Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 217, Records, Corporate (City)
topics: archives (records), audits, legislation, municipal codes; acts, auditors; auditors
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council decides whether to amend the records retention by-law (Municipal Code Chapter 217) by deleting the records classification for Auditor General audit records, since replacement classifications now exist under Chapter 3 and for city divisions under Chapter 217. The change updates which retention schedule covers audit records. Council decides on the amendment.

title: Litigation Arising from Baycrest Park Revitalization Phase 1
topics: damages, insurance claims, legal matters, parks, projects; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, legal issues
brief: The city terminated its contract with Loc-Pave Construction Limited in June 2024 after the contractor stopped returning to the Baycrest Park Revitalization Phase 1 site, then submitted a bond claim to the contractor's surety, Travelers Insurance Company of Canada. The city alleges Travelers wrongfully denied the claim, forcing the city to pay for retendering and interim work while the park sat unusable for an extended period — and has now sued to recover those costs. City Council is being asked to adopt confidential legal instructions in an attachment. The litigation affects the final cost of the park project.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Contract with DocuPet Inc., for the Provision of Pet Licensing Services
topics: animal services, contracts, information and communication technology, licences, pets; animal control; animal protection; animal shelters; animal welfare; humane society; injured animals; lost pets; missing animals; missing pets; sick animals; stray animals; stray pets, domestic animals, ict; information and communication systems; information and technology; information technology; it, licenses; licensing
brief: City Council decides whether to approve changes to the non-competitive pet licensing contract with DocuPet Inc., which the city originally approved at $680,730 for five years (October 2025 to October 2030) with a potential total of $1,537,136 ($1,756,072 net of HST recoveries) including five one-year extensions. Revised contract figures cited in the report are $136,200, $434,592, $4,453,769, $1,075,342, $2,916,633, $1,786,979, and $4,532,156, with licence fee figures of $50.00, $60.00, $25.00, $30.00, $15.00, $12.50, $7.50, and $5.00. The contract followed a 2023-2025 pilot aimed at improving licensing revenue and customer experience for the city's mandatory dog and cat licences.

title: Authority to Accept Bequest Donation for Fudger House Long-Term Care Home
topics: donation, finance (sc), long term care homes, seniors housing; bequest; toy drive, homes for the aged; long term care centers; long term care centres; long term care facilities; nursing facilities; nursing homes
brief: City Council is asked to authorize accepting a bequest donation of approximately $0.800 million from the Estate of Mary Thressa Vivian Boston for residents of Fudger House Long-Term Care Home. Because the gift exceeds the $50,000 threshold in the city's Donation Policy, council approval is required. Council decides whether to accept the donation.

title: Nominal Lease with Birchmount Bluffs Neighbourhood Centre at Birchmount Community Centre
brief: Approving a five-year nominal lease with Birchmount Bluffs Neighbourhood Centre for space in Birchmount Community Centre at 93 Birchmount Road, where the non-profit has operated since 1994 serving Ward 20. The lease covers a reception office, administrative offices, and childcare programming space, supporting the centre's recreation and social programs would get City Council's approval. Council decides on the lease.

title: Community Space Tenancy Lease Agreement with WoodGreen Community Services - 90 Mill Street and 373 Front Street East
topics: community & life (sc), leasing, properties (real estate), tenants; leases, property; real estate, renters; tenancy agreements
brief: Authorizing a Community Space Tenancy sub-sublease with WoodGreen Community Services for about 5,015 square feet of community space at 90 Mill Street and 373 Front Street East, where the organization would deliver integrated services supporting healthy aging, social connection, economic stability, and newcomer and youth inclusion is up for a decision by City Council. WoodGreen was selected through a competitive expressions-of-interest process on organizational capacity, financial sustainability, and alignment with city priorities. Council decides on the lease.

title: Non-Competitive Contracts with Suppliers for the Supply of Proprietary Parts and Maintenance Services at Water and Wastewater Treatment Plants for Toronto Water
topics: contracts, sewer and water infrastructure, suppliers, water treatment plants; filtration plants; water filtration plants; water treatment and supply plants; water treatment facilities, sewer and water services; water and sewer infrastructure; water management systems
brief: The question before City Council: whether to approve two non-competitive contracts totalling $1,368,432, ($1,392,517 net of HST recoveries) — $368,432 ($374,917) with Johnson Controls Canada L.P. and $1,000,000 ($1,017,600) with Lakeside Process Controls Ltd.; the report also cites $500,000 and $1,368,432 — for proprietary parts and maintenance at water and wastewater treatment plants, to December 31, 2026 with four one-year renewal options. Each supplier is the sole manufacturer or authorized distributor of its equipment. Council decides.

title: Non-Competitive Contracts with Jenoptik Smart Mobility Solutions, LLC for Red-Light Camera Systems
topics: contracts, red light cameras, road safety, science & technology (sc); red light monitoring
brief: City Council votes on approving two non-competitive bridge contracts with Jenoptik Smart Mobility Solutions totalling $8,312,151 ($8,458,445 net of HST recoveries) — $4,183,865 ($4,257,501) and $4,128,286 ($4,200,944); the report also cites $500,000 — to keep operating the city's 299 red-light cameras. The current contracts expire December 31, 2026 and May 7, 2027, and with the October municipal election recess, council couldn't award the planned single replacement contract in time. The bridge deals keep the Vision Zero camera program running without interruption.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Leitner-Poma Canada Inc., for the Supply and Maintenance of the Ski Lifts at Earl Bales Ski and Snowboard Centre and Rope Tow Lift at Don Valley Golf Course for Parks and Recreation
topics: contracts, golf courses, parks, ski centres, suppliers; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, golf centers; golf centres; golf facilities; public golf, ski centers; ski facilities; ski hills; ski trails; skiing centres; snow centres
brief: City Council decides whether to approve a non-competitive contract with Leitner-Poma Canada Inc. worth $418,363 ($425,726 net of HST recoveries) — the report also cites $500,000 — for proprietary parts and maintenance for the ski lifts at Earl Bales Park's North York Ski and Snowboard Centre and the rope tow at Don Valley Golf Course, from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027 with three one-year renewal options. Leitner-Poma is the sole manufacturer and servicer of the lift equipment. Council decides.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Kemira Water Solutions Canada Inc., for the Supply of Iron Salts at Wastewater Treatment Plants for Toronto Water
topics: contracts, sewer and water infrastructure, suppliers, wastewater treatment plants; sewage treatment plants; treatment plants; waste water treatment plants, sewer and water services; water and sewer infrastructure; water management systems
brief: City Council is asked to approve a non-competitive one-year contract (2027, plus four one-year renewal options) with Kemira Water Solutions Canada Inc. worth $43,484,155 ($44,249,476 net of HST recoveries) — the report also cites $500,000 — for iron salts used to remove phosphorus at all four of Toronto's wastewater treatment plants. The chemicals keep the city within the phosphorus discharge limits in its operating permits, protecting lake water quality from algae growth. Council decides.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Haywood Hunt and Associates Inc.
topics: agreements, contracts, environment (sc), external services; consultants; consulting services; professional services, tenancy agreements
brief: Approving a non-competitive three-year contract (from October 6, 2026, plus two one-year options) with Haywood Hunt and Associates Inc. worth $500,000 ($508,800 net of HST recoveries) as a ceiling, with payment only for work actually performed would get City Council's approval. The Canadian surveillance services firm was selected under the compatibility exception. Council approval is needed because the cumulative commitment exceeds the Chief Procurement Officer's authority.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Comtech Solacom Technologies Inc., for the Provision of Software and Hardware, Installation and Configuration of Guardian Next Generation 9-1-1 and Related Maintenance Services
topics: contracts, emergency services, information and communication technology, technology acquisition; 9-1-1; 911; 911 calls; emergency assistance; emergency response, ict; information and communication systems; information and technology; information technology; it, information technology acquisitions; it acquisitions
brief: The city wants a non-competitive agreement with Comtech Solacom Technologies Inc. worth $3,754,157 ($3,820,230 net of HST recoveries) — the report also cites $500,000 — for software, hardware, installation, and maintenance of the Guardian Next Generation 9-1-1 call-taking console used by Toronto Paramedic Services' dispatch centre, for one year plus four one-year renewals. The system integrates phone lines, radio channels, and intercoms for emergency dispatch, and the deal includes cybersecurity enhancements against evolving threats. The relevant authority decides on the agreement.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Bloomberg Finance LP for the Provision of Continued Leasing Proprietary Software and Data Services
topics: agreements, contracts, leasing, science & technology (sc), software; computer programs, leases, tenancy agreements
brief: Approving a non-competitive one-year contract (January 8, 2027 to January 7, 2028, plus three one-year renewal options) with Bloomberg Finance LP worth $392,400 USD ($399,306 USD net of HST recoveries) — the report also cites $500,000 — for the proprietary financial market data and analytics system staff have used since 1996 to issue debentures, make investment decisions, and plan long-term capital financing is up for a decision by City Council. The exclusive-rights exception applies since only Bloomberg provides the system. Council decides.

title: Award of Doc5534207316 to Alberici Constructors Ltd., for Replacement of Raw Water Pumps and Travelling Screens at the Island Water Treatment Plant, and Amendment of Purchase Orders 7100000228 and 7100000229 with R.V. Anderson Associates Limited for Services During Construction and Post-Construction
topics: construction, purchasing, water treatment; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, building, water filtration; water purification
