brief: The question before the General Government Committee: whether to award Alberici Constructors Limited a $34,027,915 ($34,626,806 net of HST recoveries) contract to replace raw water pumps and travelling screens at the Island Water Treatment Plant, and to amend two R.V. Anderson Associates purchase orders — services during construction up $720,877 ($733,564) and post-construction services up $119,258 ($121,357) — after scope changes and a schedule extension pushed delivery dates to December 31, 2029 and December 31, 2031. The report also cites $10,070,000, $1,048,108, $1,768,985 ($1,800,119), $38,125, and $157,383 ($160,153) in related purchase order figures. The committee decides on the award and amendments.

title: Authority to Reallocate Funds for the Effluent Disinfection System Upgrades Project at Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant
topics: finance (sc), legal matters, projects, wastewater treatment plants; legal issues, sewage treatment plants; treatment plants; waste water treatment plants
brief: This is a confidential item: City Council authorizes reallocating funds for the Effluent Disinfection System Upgrades at the Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant, needed for potential resolution of project claims, and to adopt confidential staff instructions that stay sealed because they involve litigation or potential litigation and negotiating positions. No public dollar figures are given.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order Number 6050426 with Intrahealth Canada Limited for Electronic Medical Records Solution
topics: contracts, information and communication technology, public health, purchasing, records; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, ict; information and communication systems; information and technology; information technology; it
brief: City Council votes on amending the Intrahealth Canada Limited purchase order for the electronic medical records system, adding $30,885 ($31,427 net of HST recoveries) — raising it from $638,088 to $669,515 — and extending the term to January 31, 2029, to sustain hosting, maintenance, support, and software releases. Council approval is needed because the cumulative vendor commitment exceeds the Chief Procurement Officer's authority.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order 7200000116 with Medallia Inc., for Digital Data Collection and Analysis Tool
topics: contracts, digital libraries, information and communication technology, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, ict; information and communication systems; information and technology; information technology; it, online libraries
brief: City Council decides whether to amend the Medallia Inc. purchase order for the city's digital survey and data collection tool, adding $233,620 USD ($322,395 CAD) net of taxes — or $237,731 USD ($328,069 CAD) net of HST recoveries — for 2026 and 2027; the report also cites $195,364, $428,983, $1, and $1.38. The city has used the tool (formerly CheckMarket) since 2018 across more than 30 divisions for public and staff surveys, but Medallia's new 2025 licensing model made the existing authority insufficient. The amendment keeps the service running while staff plan a move to a cheaper alternative.

title: Amendment to Master Services Agreement, Amendment to Purchase Order 6053207, and Executing Various Purchase Orders with e-Builder Inc., for Subscriptions and Professional Services
topics: agreements, external services, projects, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, consultants; consulting services; professional services, tenancy agreements
brief: The city wants to extend its agreement with e-Builder Inc. for Trimble Unity Construct — the cloud platform used to plan, deliver, and report on infrastructure capital projects — for four more years (March 25, 2027 to March 24, 2031), amend Purchase Order 6053207, and create new purchase orders to bring Parks and Recreation and Transportation Services onto the platform. The figures cited are an amendment of $4,988,313 ($5,076,107 net of HST recoveries), raising the value from $5,968,061 to $10,956,374, plus new purchase orders of $2,068,401 ($2,104,805) and $1,049,928 ($1,068,407). The request is for ceiling authority only, with no commitment to spend it all.

title: Amendment to Blanket Contract 47022313 with Beanfield Metroconnect for Wide Area Network Services
topics: computer networks, contracts, information and communication technology, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, ict; information and communication systems; information and technology; information technology; it
brief: The city wants to amend its wide-area network contract with Toronto-based Beanfield Metroconnect by up to $14,000,000 ($14,246,400 net of HST recoveries), raising the contract from $23,490,110 ($23,903,536) to $37,490,110 ($38,149,936), and extend it five years (plus two one-year options) past its April 16, 2027 expiry. The network is the digital backbone connecting City Hall, emergency services, libraries, community centres, water facilities, and traffic systems into one secure network with redundancy. Continuity of the connection is what's at stake.

title: Annual Update on OMERS Related to the City's Employer Contributions
topics: annual reports, employees, employment & labour (sc), retirement; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, staff
brief: This is an information item: the General Government Committee receives the annual summary of the city's 2025 employer contributions to OMERS, the Ontario Municipal Employees' Retirement System, with information on the city's members and contributions relative to the overall plan. No decision is attached.

title: 1151 Weston Road - Alterations to and Removal of an Attribute of a Designated Heritage Property under Part IV, Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: easements, heritage designation;
brief: Approving alterations to — and removal of a heritage attribute of — the designated 1949 Scotiabank building at 1151 Weston Road (northeast corner of Weston Road and Eglinton Avenue West), in connection with the proposed 46-storey development on the site, and authorizing a Heritage Easement Agreement is up for a decision by City Council. The modernist bank building by architect Gordon S. Adamson, with its limestone cladding, bas-relief panels, and projecting roof entrance, would be conserved as part of the project under conditions. This heritage decision runs alongside the zoning decision for the tower.

title: 1151 Weston Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The question before City Council: whether to approve Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments for a 46-storey mixed-use tower at 1151 Weston Road containing 509 homes and about 296 square metres of ground-floor commercial space, on a Part IV-designated heritage property. The plan conserves the single-storey 1949 Scotiabank building by reorienting and relocating it within the site and integrating it with the new development, next to a transit station. A companion heritage report covers the alterations under the Ontario Heritage Act.

title: 4686 and 4690 Dundas Street West and 56 Nottingham Drive - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council votes on approving Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments for a 10-unit condominium townhouse development at 4686 and 4690 Dundas Street West and 56 Nottingham Drive. Staff say the infill project fits provincial policy, the city's Official Plan, and the Townhouse and Low-Rise Apartment Guidelines. Council's decision determines whether the ten townhomes can be built as proposed.

title: Mount Dennis Station Protected Major Transit Station Area - Official Plan Amendment - Final Report
topics: official plan amendments, planning;
brief: City Council decides whether to approve a city-initiated Official Plan Amendment creating a Protected Major Transit Station Area around Mount Dennis Station — the interchange of TTC Line 5 Eglinton LRT, the GO Kitchener line, and UP Express near Eglinton Avenue West and Weston Road. The new policy (Site and Area Specific Policy 671) would set the station area boundaries, permitted land uses, minimum building densities, and a target of 160 residents and jobs combined per hectare. The amendment goes to the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing for final approval with no appeal. It will shape how densely the Mount Dennis station area can develop.

title: Improving Traffic Safety on St. Phillips Road
topics: road safety, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: A petition from 52 households describes a pattern of dangerous driving on St. Phillips Road — 35 motor vehicle collisions recorded by police since 2024, including two crashes months apart in which vehicles hit the same hydro pole in front of 47 St. Phillips Road, knocking out neighbourhood power. The item asks Etobicoke York Community Council to order a formal traffic safety review, with traffic calming measures such as speed humps to be considered after Transportation Services' assessment. Families and residents along the street are the ones seeking action.

title: 5 and 43 Junction Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, mixed use areas, official plan amendments, rezoning; developing land; development (land); land development, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: City Council is asked to approve Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments for a large multi-phase development at 5 and 43 Junction Road: four mixed-use buildings with six towers of 18 to 35 storeys, 1,947 homes, a retained medical office building, affordable housing, new commercial space, a new public park, and a new public street. Staff say the proposal fits provincial policy and the city's Official Plan. The decision would bring nearly 2,000 homes plus a park and street to the Junction area.

title: Mabelle Avenue - Parking Amendments
topics: change, parking prohibitions, stopping prohibitions; amendments; conversion; modification, no parking, no stopping
brief: Most of Mabelle Avenue between Dundas Street West and Cordova Avenue would switch from no-parking-anytime to no-stopping-anytime — a stricter rule — to keep the street clear for transit and traffic, while the existing $1.50 paid parking areas stay and a small paid-parking section is added on the west side south of Dundas. City Council decides because the TTC operates on Mabelle Avenue. Drivers who park on Mabelle would face tighter restrictions.

title: St Albans Road - Heavy Vehicles
topics: heavy truck prohibitions, heavy trucks;
brief: Prohibiting heavy vehicles at all times on St Albans Road between Kipling Avenue and Aukland Road, following a staff review of the need for a full-time ban would get City Council's approval. City Council decides because the TTC operates transit service on St Albans Road. Truck drivers using St Albans as a route and nearby residents would feel the change.

title: Royal York Road and Royal York Court - Traffic Control Signals
topics: traffic, traffic control systems; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Installing traffic control signals at Royal York Road and Royal York Court, which staff say are justified by their assessment and would improve safety for all road users is up for a decision by City Council. City Council decides because the TTC operates service on Royal York Road. The signals would change how vehicles and pedestrians move through the intersection.

title: Park Lawn Road - U-turn Prohibition
topics: [rules in transportation], turn prohibitions (traffic);
brief: The question before City Council: whether to prohibit northbound U-turns at all times on Park Lawn Road between the Gardiner Expressway westbound on-ramp and The Queensway. City Council decides because the TTC operates transit service on Park Lawn Road. Drivers heading north on Park Lawn would lose the option to make U-turns on this stretch.

title: 1025 The Queensway - Draft Plan of Subdivision Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, subdivision (land); subdivision of land
brief: City Council is being told that the Executive Director of Development Review intends to approve a draft plan subdividing 1025 The Queensway into eight development blocks, two park blocks, three new public streets, two landscape areas, two privately owned public spaces, and a private driveway — the next step for a mixed-use project whose zoning was approved in June 2025 but whose by-law can't be enacted until this subdivision approval and a Section 37 agreement securing a childcare facility are in place. This is largely an information item for council under delegated approval rules. The subdivision sets the physical framework for the future development of the site.

title: Corrective By-law for the Permanent Closure of Portions of Dundas Street West, Kipling Avenue and Bloor Street West
topics: road closures; street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council decides whether to pass a corrective by-law fixing legal descriptions for the permanent closure of portions of Dundas Street West, Kipling Avenue, and Bloor Street West in the Six Points area. The original by-law (503-2021) was enacted but never registered on title, and one parcel (Part 4 on Plan 66R-31942) was included in error. The correction changes no policy or redevelopment plans — it just makes the legal paperwork match the intended closure before registration.

title: Wright Avenue - Traffic Calming (Speed Cushions)
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: One speed cushion is proposed for Wright Avenue between Jane Street and Plainfield Road, paired with parking changes including a new no-standing zone on the north side near Jane Street and adjusted parking prohibitions on the south side. City Council decides because the TTC runs buses on Wright Avenue. Drivers and transit riders on this stretch would both be affected.

title: Brown's Line and Jellicoe Avenue - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: pedestrian crossovers, road safety; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo
brief: City Council decides whether to install traffic control signals at Brown's Line and Jellicoe Avenue, where Transportation Services says crossing protection is needed for pedestrians and other vulnerable road users. City Council decides because the TTC operates service on Brown's Line. The signals would change how pedestrians cross and how drivers move through the intersection.

title: Lake Shore Boulevard West - City-initiated Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendments - Final Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A two-and-a-half-year study of Lake Shore Boulevard West is coming to City Council with final recommendations: an Official Plan Amendment (No. 951), new zoning by-law amendments, and Urban Design and Streetscape Guidelines that set the vision for building heights and public space along the avenue. The study involved residents, the local Councillor, businesses, BIAs, Humber College, and landowners. What council adopts will shape future development along Lake Shore Boulevard West for years.

title: Kipling Avenue and Firwood Crescent - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: pedestrian crossovers, road safety; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo
brief: City Council is asked to approve installing traffic control signals at Kipling Avenue and Firwood Crescent to make the crossing safer for pedestrians, and to prohibit pedestrian crossings on Kipling Avenue within 30.5 metres of the intersection once the signals go in. The change would affect pedestrians crossing Kipling and drivers using the intersection.

title: 4975 Dundas Street West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A developer wants to build a 44-storey tower on a four-storey base with 563 homes at 4975 Dundas Street West, plus ground-floor commercial space. Council is asked to change the Official Plan and zoning to allow it.

title: Ryding Lands Study - Directions Report
topics: [actions of government], development, policy development; developing land; development (land); land development, policy making
brief: Staff have drafted emerging directions for the Ryding Lands study, which envisions shifting the area south of St Clair Avenue from low-scale industrial uses to a mix of new development with streets and public spaces. Council is asked to endorse the directions.

title: 175 and 185 Eileen Avenue - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: part lot control, planning;
brief: This is a procedural item: Council is asked to exempt 175 and 185 Eileen Avenue from the Planning Act's part-lot-control rules for two years, so the lots can be divided to create 58 freehold townhouse units.

title: 1233 to 1255 The Queensway - Official Plan Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: mixed use areas, official plan amendments;
brief: A developer wants to build a mixed-use project on six blocks at 1233 to 1255 The Queensway, including two new parks, two new streets, and a secured childcare facility. Council is asked to change the Official Plan to set the planning framework.

title: Operating Variance Report for the Four Months Ended April 30, 2026
brief: The call on whether to approve amendments to the 2026 approved operating budget with no impact on the City's net operating budget belongs to Council. For the four months ended April 30, tax-supported operations showed an unfavourable net variance of $4.6 million, with an unfavourable $97.4 million variance projected at year-end. The report's figures also include $27.7 million and $32.7 million.

title: Capital Variance Report for the Four Months Ended April 30, 2026
topics: financial reports; annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: The decision on whether to approve in-year budget adjustments to the 2026-2035 capital budget and plan, alongside a report showing 2026 capital spending of $1.106 billion in the first four months, 18.4 per cent of the budget and above the five-year historical average of 14.0 per cent rests with Council. City divisions and agencies are projected to spend $5.417 billion by year-end, 89.9 per cent of the 2026 approved capital budget.

title: Operating Variance Report for the Year Ended December 31, 2025
topics: annual reports; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards
brief: Approving amendments to the 2025 approved operating budget with no impact on the City's net budget goes to Council for a decision. Tax-supported operations ended 2025 with a favourable net variance of $108.2 million, and rate-supported programs reported a favourable $66.1 million variance.

title: Capital Variance Report for the Twelve Months Ended December 31, 2025
topics: capital budgets;
brief: Approving in-year adjustments to the 2025-2034 capital budget and plan to align with year-end funding needs, after 2025 capital spending of $5.603 billion came in at an 83.7 per cent spending rate, up from $4.740 billion and 73.8 per cent in 2024 goes to Council for a decision. One attachment stays confidential for reasons including a pending land transaction.

title: Toronto Water 2026 Capital Budget and 2027 to 2035 Capital Plan Adjustments
topics: budgets, capital budgets, environment (sc), water; budgets and accounts
brief: The decision on whether to authorize reallocating $32.683 million in cash flows within Toronto Water's 2026 capital budget and 2027-2035 capital plan for project accelerations and deferrals, with zero overall budget impact rests with Council. The adjustments also convert approved future-year estimates and increase total project costs by $245.294 million for two approved projects to allow contract awards ahead of schedule in late 2026 or early 2027, with added cash flow commitments of $4.764 million, $8.197 million, $10.121 million, $7.756 million, and $17.306 million.

title: Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation Annual General Meeting and 2025 Audited Financial Statements
topics: annual reports, finance (sc); annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards
brief: This is a procedural item: Council is asked to treat part of its meeting as the Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation's annual shareholder meeting and to receive its 2025 annual report and audited financial statements. No policy change is proposed.

title: Making Grocery Prices Fair: Banning Surveillance Pricing in Toronto
topics: costs, economic development, food; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing, menus
brief: Mayor Chow and Councillor Bravo are asking Council to have staff identify ways the City could ban and regulate surveillance pricing, where personal data is used to change grocery prices based on who or where the customer is, and report back in the first quarter of 2027 with options. The motion notes school food program expansion is saving families with two children $900 a year on groceries, and that Manitoba has legislated against the practice.

title: Good Roads Board of Directors Meeting, Chatham-Kent, June 11 - June 12, 2026
topics: governance; governance structure; municipal governance
brief: This is an information item: Council receives an update on the June 11-12, 2026 Good Roads board of directors meeting in Chatham-Kent on municipal transportation advocacy and governance. No policy change is proposed.

title: Report on Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) Annual General Meeting - June 4-7, 2026
topics: governance; governance structure; municipal governance
brief: This is an information item: Council receives an update on the June 4-7, 2026 Federation of Canadian Municipalities annual conference in Edmonton, covering housing, infrastructure, public safety, and municipal finance. No policy change is proposed.

title: Toronto Community Housing Corporation - Annual General Meeting and 2025 Audited Consolidated Financial Statements
topics: financial reports, governance; annual financial reports; financial statements, governance structure; municipal governance
brief: Council treated part of its meeting as Toronto Community Housing Corporation's annual shareholder meeting, received its 2025 annual report and audited consolidated financial statements, and appointed KPMG as its 2026 auditor. Council also asked the Toronto Community Housing board to work with the City Manager on a plan to expand deep building retrofits — prioritizing projects that revitalize and expand the housing stock, cut operating costs, and better protect tenants from extreme heat — and to report on the plan as part of the 2027 budget process. The retrofit plan matters to social housing tenants facing extreme heat and aging buildings.

title: Advancing More Supportive Housing to Address Homelessness and Create Pathways to Long-Term Housing Stability
topics: homelessness;
brief: The Housing Rights Advisory Committee is asking Council to call on the Ontario and federal governments for coordinated, sustained investment in supportive housing for people exiting homelessness, including more federal capital funding for rapid construction. The committee points to a gap in supportive housing for people with complex mental health and addiction challenges and backs modular units with wrap-around supports as a scalable model.

title: Toronto Port Lands Company - Annual General Meeting and 2025 Audited Financial Statements
topics: finance (sc), governance; governance structure; municipal governance
brief: This is a procedural item: Council is asked to treat part of its meeting as the Toronto Port Lands Company's annual shareholder meeting, receive its 2025 audited financial statements and annual report, and appoint KPMG as its 2026 auditor. No policy change is proposed.

title: Amending the Composition of the City's Appointments to the Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre Board of Directors
topics: boards of management, public appointments, special purpose bodies; abccs; abcds; agencies; boards; commissions; committees of management; local boards, boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: Adjusting the makeup of its five appointments to the Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre board: the General Manager of Parks and Recreation's designate would become the Director of Community Recreation, and the Director's seat would shift to the Manager of Community Recreation heads to Council for a decision. The change keeps the board at five City-appointed members and aligns board decisions with City recreation priorities.

title: Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre Annual General Meeting and 2025 Audited Financial Statements
topics: audits, city-operated sports facilities; auditors; auditors
brief: This is a procedural item: Council, as a shareholder, is asked to adopt resolutions receiving the Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre's 2025 audited financial statements and reappointing Welch LLP as auditor. No policy change is proposed.

title: Lakeshore Arena Corporation - Annual General Meeting and 2025 Audited Financial Statements
brief: This is a procedural item: Council is asked to treat part of its meeting as Lakeshore Arena Corporation's annual shareholder meeting, receive its 2025 annual report and audited financial statements, and appoint Welch LLP as its 2026 auditor. No policy change is proposed.

title: Build Toronto Inc. 2025 Annual General Meeting and Audited Financial Statements
topics: financial reports, governance; annual financial reports; financial statements, governance structure; municipal governance
brief: This is a procedural item: Council is asked to treat part of its meeting as Build Toronto Inc.'s annual shareholder meeting, receive its 2025 audited financial statements and annual report, and appoint KPMG as its 2026 auditor. No policy change is proposed.

title: Establishing Limited Legal Services at The 519 Church Street Community Centre
topics: community centres, legal aid, legal matters; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, legal assistance, legal issues
brief: Whether to authorize The 519 Church Street Community Centre's board to offer limited, direct legal advice to eligible members of the 2SLGBTQ+ community, with risk mitigation and accountability conditions including eligibility criteria now sits with Council. The authorization would amend the centre's approved program scope, and staff lawyers and a paralegal would provide the advice to clients who fall outside existing legal aid, pro bono, and clinic services.

title: Arena Boards of Management Settlement of Operating Results for the Year Ended 2024
topics: arenas; indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: Up for a decision before Council: direct that 2024 operating surpluses totalling $204,163 from three arenas (George Bell, William H. Bolton, Forest Hill) be paid to the City to partly fund $201,746 in deficits at four other arenas (McCormick, Moss Park, Ted Reeve, North Toronto), leaving a net surplus of $2,417 to the City. The report's figures also include $210,055.

title: Association of Community Centres Settlement of Operating Results for Year Ended 2024 and 2025
topics: annual reports; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards
brief: Council is set to decide whether to settle the Association of Community Centres' operating results: 2024 surpluses totalling $118,971 from four centres (Applegrove, Ralph Thornton, Central Eglinton, Swansea Town Hall) would be paid to the City to partly fund $406,589 in deficits at six other centres. The report's figures also include $287,618, $203,621, $105,737, and $97,884.

title: 2026 Levy on Railway Roadways and Rights-of-Way and on Power Utility Transmission and Distribution Corridors
brief: Council has the final say on whether to authorize the 2026 tax levy on railway roadways and rights-of-way and power utility transmission and distribution corridors, totalling about $6,993,742, with a $6,484,859 municipal share and a $508,883 provincial education share, at rates unchanged from the 2025 total of $6,992,485 ($6,483,956 municipal, $508,529 education). Staff note that had rates been indexed to inflation since 2005, the levy would generate an additional $3,891,024 in 2026; the report's figures also include $3,601,155.

title: 2026 Heads and Beds Levy on Institutions
topics: finance (sc), institutional levies; heads and beds; institutional taxes
brief: Before Council for a decision: authorize the 2026 heads and beds levy of $75 per provincially rated hospital bed, full-time student, or resident place on colleges, universities, public hospitals, and correctional facilities, expected to raise about $20.6 million. The $75 rate has been unchanged since 1987; had it been indexed to inflation it would be $186.08, which staff estimate would bring in an additional $30.6 million in 2026.

title: Obligatory Reserve Funds, Reserves and Discretionary Reserve Funds as at December 31, 2025
topics: budgets, finance (sc), reserve funds; budgets and accounts, reserves and reserve funds
brief: The City's obligatory reserve funds fell from $6,726.4 million to $6,597.5 million in 2025, a $128.9 million decrease driven by development charges, the Ontario-Toronto New Deal, and water and wastewater funds. Development charge balances fell from $2,840.2 to $2,466.5 million, a $373.7 million decrease. The report's other figures are $5,612.8 million, $5,471.2 million, $141.6 million, $5,131.6 million, $339.6 million, $18,863.7 million, $44,349.1 million, $12,068.7 million, and $12.6 million. The report also serves as the required 2025 statement of development charge balances, and Council is asked to establish a Vehicle Reserve for Environment, Climate and Forestry.

title: Property Taxes: 2027 Interim Levy By-Law
topics: property taxes, taxes; levies, municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: Council decides whether to adopt the 2027 interim property tax levy of about $3.13 billion, based on 50 per cent of 2026 taxes billed, to cover the City's cash needs until the 2027 operating budget and final levy are approved. Interim due dates run from February to June 2027 depending on the payment plan.

title: 701 Fleet Street - Authorization to Enter into a Long-term Lease and Community Access Agreement with Tempo Basketball Club Inc.
brief: Leasing City-owned land at 701 Fleet Street to Tempo Basketball Club Inc. for a new Women's National Basketball Association practice facility of about 60,000 square feet, with a 40-year initial term and two 20-year renewal options would get the City's approval. The deal would secure year-round public recreation access plus a new public park with outdoor basketball courts, washrooms, and public realm improvements; the report cites $0.8 million. It is the first agreement of its kind for a WNBA practice facility.

title: Considerations for Toronto Membership in the Association francophone des Municipalités de l'Ontario
topics: bilingual status, municipal associations; bilingualism; services in french
brief: Staff are recommending the City join the Association francophone des municipalites de l'Ontario as an Individual Member for the rest of 2026 and 2027, with a review of outcomes before considering a Corporate Membership in 2028. Council is asked to direct the City Manager to register one staff member for individual membership for the remainder of 2026 and up to four memberships for 2027, and to have the City Clerk canvass councillors for interest in appointment. It affects the City's francophone municipal advocacy ties.

title: Improving the Usability of Old City Hall as a Filming Location
topics: film and television industry, film permits; cinema industry; film and television cluster; film production; movie industry; television industry, film production; film shoots; filming; filming permits; location filming permits
brief: The Film, Television and Digital Media Advisory Board is asking the committee to have staff review fees, accessibility, and operating conditions for film and TV production at Old City Hall, consult industry stakeholders on barriers, and report in 2027 on actions to reduce costs and improve usability. No changes are proposed yet; this is a study request.

title: Follow Up on 2026.EC27.1: Refining the Definition of an Entertainment Establishment/Nightclub in Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 545, Licensing
topics: business licences, entertainment establishments, municipal codes, nightclubs; business licensing; business permits; municipal licenses, dance clubs; dance halls; discos; night clubs, entertainment facilities
brief: Council will weigh whether to amend the licensing by-law so venues with a capacity under 151 people are not classified as nightclubs and are instead licensed based on their actual operations. Staff identified the change after a year of implementing 2025's modernized bar, restaurant, and entertainment-venue licensing rules, and a broader implementation review continues with a report back in 2027. It affects how small venues are licensed and where enforcement focuses.

title: Changes to Business Improvement Area Boards of Management
topics: boards of management, business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations, boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is an administrative item: Council is asked to appoint Alexis Berger to the Upper Village Business Improvement Area board of management and to remove Haris Kayani as a director of the Little Jamaica BIA board of management. No other changes are proposed.

title: Lower Don Parkland Indigenous Naming - Progress Update
topics: First Nations, parkland dedication; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples
brief: The City has been studying an Indigenous name for the Lower Don parkland system and trail, including the proposed name Wonscotonach, but engagement since 2018 found no consensus on its accuracy, spelling, or interpretation. Council is asked to authorize staff to continue an Indigenous-led process with the Mississaugas of the Credit First Nation, including a land-based site visit, and report back in the second quarter of 2027 with a chosen Anishinaabemowin name and an interpretive narrative. No name is being chosen at this meeting.

title: Follow-up on Item 2026.MM42.61: Suitability of the Standard Theatre as a Live Music Venue
topics: entertainment establishments, music, theatres (facilities); auditorium; performance spaces; performing arts centres; performing arts facilities, entertainment facilities
brief: This is an information item: Council receives a report finding that converting the vacant Standard Theatre at 285 Spadina Avenue, which opened in 1921 as a Yiddish theatre, into a live music venue would be a permitted use. Further restoration work would depend on the property owner and potential tenants. No policy change is proposed.

title: Exploring Options to Recoup City Enforcement Costs for Challenging Properties
topics: costs, enforcement;
brief: The privately owned property at 92 Lappin Avenue in Ward 9 - Davenport has been the subject of City enforcement since 2009, and was closed in August 2025 after Toronto Fire Services and Toronto Building found serious fire and life-safety risks. City costs for the property from 2021 through 2026 total $306,000, of which $236,000 has been recovered. The item asks Council to have City divisions and the City Solicitor explore options to recover enforcement costs for challenging properties like this one.

title: Toronto Fire Services 2025 Annual Report
topics: annual reports, fire and rescue services; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, fire fighting; fire services; fire suppression; firefighting; rescue; rescue operations; search and rescue
brief: Council received the Toronto Fire Services 2025 annual report on fire protection service levels and performance, which the municipal code requires the Fire Chief to present each year. Council asked the Fire Chief to analyze the financial impacts of provincial legislation and regulation changes on Fire Services workforce costs, directed the City Manager to negotiate with the Province of Ontario to recover those costs, and requested report-backs ahead of the 2027 budget on improving fire response times in Etobicoke, Scarborough, and Don Valley, including new or accelerated fire stations. The outcome affects how the City recovers fire-service costs from the province and where new fire stations may go.

title: Ombudsman Toronto Report - No Refunds for Discontinued TTC Tickets and Tokens: An Investigation Behind How the Decision was Made
topics: public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: Toronto's Ombudsman has finished investigating how the TTC decided not to refund or credit discontinued legacy tickets and tokens, and his June 17, 2026 report makes eight recommendations that TTC leadership and the board have agreed to implement. He asks Council to receive the report for information. The item matters to anyone who held old TTC tickets or tokens when they were discontinued.

title: Implementation of the Development Charges Reduction Program
topics: by-laws, legislation; acts, bylaws
brief: The question before Council: whether to amend the Development Charges By-law to implement the Development Charges Reduction Program, which would introduce time-limited residential rate decreases of 40 to 60 percent and suspend annual indexing through 2029 so rates stay flat during the program. The changes are backed by $1.5 billion in confirmed federal and provincial funding over 10 years, announced in June 2026 as part of the Canada-Ontario Partnership to Build, to support housing-enabling infrastructure already in the City's 10-Year Capital Plan. To qualify for the reduced rates, a development's first building permit would need to be issued during the program period. This matters to residents because lower development charges are intended to reduce the cost of building homes and speed up housing supply.

title: Ward-Based Maintenance Team Pilot - Response to Council Direction
brief: This is a procedural item: Council is asked to receive a report responding to its direction to establish a ward-based maintenance team pilot. The report describes the City's current interdivisional model, where public realm maintenance is organized by geographic operating areas rather than by ward, with staff, equipment and contractors deployed by service demand and local conditions, and says further analysis would be needed to define the model and assess feasibility before any pilot. No decision is required.

title: Update on Implementation of the Community Mailbox Conversion Program in Toronto
topics: mail services; courier services; mail rooms; mailrooms
brief: This is a procedural item: Council is asked to receive a status update on Canada Post's community mailbox conversion program in Toronto, which includes Canada Post's May 14, 2026 responses to Council's questions from its April 2026 motions. Discussions continue on proposed mailbox sites in Ward 1 Etobicoke North, the overall conversion timeline and a city-wide implementation plan, and staff will report back once full details are provided. No decision is required.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Early Outcomes from the Hosting of the FIFA World Cup 2026
topics: soccer, sporting events, tourism; championships
brief: Council received a supplementary report on early outcomes from Toronto's hosting of the FIFA World Cup 2026, and directed staff to review the tournament's Mobility Plan and make the measures that worked permanent — including keeping the traffic cameras added for the tournament, expanding transit signal priority, and keeping parking and turn restrictions that helped congestion. Council also asked the Auditor General to conduct a value-for-money audit of Toronto's hosting of the tournament, and directed that the final post-tournament report analyze whether incidents of intimate partner and gender-based violence changed between June 11 and July 19, 2026, compared with the same period in 2025. The financial impact statement puts the cost at $9.0 million, covering FIFA Fan Festival costs that Council wants offset with new revenue streams.

title: Delegation of Authority for the 2026 Council Recess Period
topics: council meetings, delegation of authority; signing authorities
brief: As it does before every municipal election, Council votes on giving senior City staff time-limited decision-making authority for the 2026 election recess, so that City business, contracts and capital work can continue after the 2022 to 2026 Council term ends with the July 29 to 31, 2026 meeting. The delegated authorities would run until the first regular business meeting of the new Council term in December 2026, be used only when needed to keep City operations running, and be reported back on by the City Manager at that first meeting. The delegation covers authority thresholds of $5 million, $10 million, $2 million, $50,000, $500,000, $100,000 and $50 million, alongside the authorities already delegated under the procurement and financial control by-laws.

title: Appointment of Interim City Solicitor
topics: municipal officials, public appointments; city officials
brief: Council decides whether to appoint an Interim City Solicitor effective September 8, 2026, to serve until a permanent City Solicitor is appointed. The candidate's identity and curriculum vitae summary are in a confidential attachment, which Council is asked to release publicly once the appointment is adopted. This keeps the City's top legal office filled through the transition into the election period and the new council term.

title: 353 to 357 College Street - Sewer By-law Requirements Under Site Plan Application 18111118STE20SA
topics: by-laws, municipal codes; bylaws
brief: Council grants a one-time exceptional exemption to the Sewers By-law for the development at 353 to 357 College Street under Site Plan Application 18111118STE20SA, allowing the property's control maintenance access holes to be located on the municipal right-of-way. The recommendation follows Council's direction in June 2026 to report back on compliance with the by-law's requirements, and the detailed reasons are in a confidential attachment that would stay private as solicitor-client privileged advice.

title: 835 to 839 Yonge Street - Alterations to Designated Heritage Properties and Demolition of Heritage Attributes on Designated Heritage Properties under Sections 33 and 34(1)1 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Approving alterations to and demolition of specified heritage attributes at the designated properties at 835 to 839 Yonge Street, at the corner of Yonge Street and Davenport Road, to allow a mixed-use development with 41- and 49-storey towers containing 922 residential units and at least 750 square metres of non-residential space would get Council's approval. The site includes surviving elements of the former Grand Central Market, a 1935 Spanish Colonial Revival building acquired by the Canadian Tire Corporation in 1936, and now holds a Canadian Tire gas bar and surface parking lot. A heritage easement agreement would be registered to ensure long-term conservation of what remains of the heritage property.

title: Stotts’ Bridge, Twyn Rivers Drive Over the Rouge River - Demolition of a Designated Heritage Structure, Approval with Conditions
topics: bridges, demolitions, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Approving the demolition of Stotts' Bridge on Twyn Rivers Drive over the Rouge River, a heritage-designated 1915 Warren pony truss bridge with a 22.1-metre single span and a narrow 4.1-metre deck limited to one lane of traffic is up for a decision by Council. The bridge, designed by civil engineer Frank Barber and considered a Scarborough landmark, was closed after safety concerns found in routine inspections, and the road is an evacuation route in the event of a Pickering nuclear station evacuation. The plan is an emergency replacement: demolish the bridge, install a temporary bridge, and then build a permanent truss bridge, with heritage conditions attached. The bridge sits within the federally owned Rouge National Urban Park, and its loss removes a rural landmark even as it restores a safe crossing.

title: 6 Whitney Avenue - Application to Demolish a Structure and Erect a New Structure on a Designated Heritage Property in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District
topics: heritage conservation districts, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, heritage districts; historic areas
brief: The question before Council: whether to approve demolishing a garage at the rear of 6 Whitney Avenue, a C-rated property in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District, and building a new carport connected to the existing dwelling. Heritage Planning staff find the proposal complies with the North Rosedale District Plan, the national conservation standards and the Official Plan, and recommend approval subject to conditions, including the applicant obtaining the needed planning variances.

title: 2 Whitney Avenue - Application to Erect a Structure in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District
topics: heritage conservation districts; heritage districts; historic areas
brief: Council votes on approving the retention and completion of a partially built masonry wall on City-owned land adjacent to 2 Whitney Avenue, a B-rated property in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District, under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The wall was erected without a heritage permit, but the applicant has revised the design since an earlier refusal, and staff now find it complies with the North Rosedale District Plan, the national conservation standards and the Official Plan. The recommendation is to approve it subject to conditions, including an encroachment agreement for the City land involved.

title: Report on the Investigation into the Disclosure of Confidential Information from Audit Committee Item AU11.3
topics: confidentiality, disclosure, investigation; additional disclosure; request for disclosure, investigators
brief: This is a procedural item: Council is asked to receive the Integrity Commissioner's report on the investigation into the unauthorized disclosure of confidential information from an attachment to the February 12, 2026 Audit Committee agenda, some of which appeared in a media article before it became public. The disclosure was found to be deliberate, but there was not enough evidence to identify who was responsible or to conclude that a council member or political staff member breached the Code of Conduct. The Integrity Commissioner will work with the City Clerk and City Solicitor on guidance about handling confidential information in members' offices. No decision beyond receiving the report is required.

title: 87 Highland Avenue - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District
topics: heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Council decides whether to refuse a heritage permit for alterations the owner of 87 Highland Avenue, a C-rated property in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District, made without a permit. The owner removed the dentils on the east gable, the brackets on the north gable and the Tudor detailing on both gables, built a new front porch, installed new windows on the front and side, and applied a white coating to the masonry on the dwelling and a new front brick wall. Staff found the changes incompatible with the North Rosedale District Plan, the national conservation standards and the Official Plan, and will keep working with the owners toward restoring the property's historic character if Council refuses.

title: 8 Lowther Avenue - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property Under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Approval
topics: heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Council approves a rooftop addition with a roof deck at 8 Lowther Avenue, a three-storey semi-detached home in the East Annex Heritage Conservation District between Bedford Road and Avenue Road. Although the addition would be higher than the existing roof ridge and therefore conflicts with the district's guidelines, staff support it because it is set back 6.48 metres from the street, sits behind the roof ridge, and would be minimally visible from the street without harming the district's heritage character.

title: 2125 Lawrence Avenue West - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Stating its intention to designate the City-owned Weston Lions Arena at 2125 Lawrence Avenue West in Lions Park, near the Humber River in the Weston neighbourhood, under the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value would get Council's approval. The ice-skating arena, built around 1948 to 1949 of concrete block with a rugged-brick and simulated-stone facade, was listed on the City's Heritage Register in March 2026, and the City took over the facility in April 2026 while it reviews the building's condition. Staff found it meets three of the nine provincial criteria for designation, which would let Council review future alterations or demolition. This matters to residents because designation gives the City a say over changes to a neighbourhood recreation landmark.

title: 19 to 37 Queens Quay East (Pier 27, Phase 3) - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: appeals, by-laws, planning & development (sc), zoning; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor seeks Council's directions for an Ontario Land Tribunal hearing about the official plan and zoning amendments for 19 to 37 Queens Quay East, the third phase of the Pier 27 waterfront development. The proposal is for a 45-storey residential building and an 11-storey mixed-use residential building with at-grade retail. Council refused the applications and the applicant appealed to the Tribunal in October 2025; a hearing is scheduled for March 2027, and the recommendations are confidential legal advice.

title: 245 to 251 Marlee Avenue, 1 to 7 Romar Crescent and 16 Stayner Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor seeks Council's directions for an ongoing Ontario Land Tribunal appeal about the official plan and zoning amendments for 245 to 251 Marlee Avenue, 1 to 7 Romar Crescent and 16 Stayner Avenue, where a 37- and 35-storey mixed-use building is proposed. The applicant appealed after Council failed to decide in time, and Council has directed the City Solicitor to oppose the application at the Tribunal. No hearing dates are scheduled, though appearances could occur during Council's election break, and the recommendations are confidential legal advice.

title: 30 to 36 Hendon Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor seeks Council's directions for an Ontario Land Tribunal hearing about the official plan and zoning amendments for 30 to 36 Hendon Avenue, where a 46-storey purpose-built rental residential building is proposed. Council refused the applications and the applicant appealed to the Tribunal in August 2025; no hearing has been scheduled yet, and the City Solicitor requires further directions. The recommendations are confidential legal advice.

title: 27, 31 and 51 Tapscott Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor seeks Council's directions for an Ontario Land Tribunal hearing about the Malvern Town Centre redevelopment at 27, 31 and 51 Tapscott Road. The 2022 master-plan proposal called for 15 tall buildings in phases, with phase one seeking two mixed-use towers of 32 and 39 storeys with 877 units, 62,387 square metres of residential space, 2,039 square metres of non-residential space and 319 parking spaces; the April 2025 resubmission revised phase one to 42- and 43-storey towers with 894 units, 69,620 square metres of residential space, 1,975 square metres of non-residential space and 349 parking spaces. The applicant appealed after Council failed to decide in time, with a case management conference set for August 2026, and the recommendations are confidential legal advice.

title: 237 Victoria Street - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor seeks Council's instructions for the Ontario Land Tribunal proceedings on 237 Victoria Street. The 2022 applications proposed a 24-storey mixed-use building with 416 square metres of ground-floor non-residential space and 256 dwelling units, appealed in June 2023 after Council failed to decide in time; a separate 2026 official plan amendment for 237, 249 and 251 to 253 Victoria Street would set a site-specific policy for those lands and is covered by a related planning report to be considered at the same Council meeting. The instructions are confidential legal advice.

title: 2915, 2917, 2939, 2941 and 2943 Bloor Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application- Request for Directions Report
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor seeks Council's directions for the Ontario Land Tribunal proceedings on 2915, 2917, 2939, 2941 and 2943 Bloor Street West. The October 2025 zoning application proposed a 29-storey mixed-use building with 423 dwelling units, including 7 rental replacement units, and 1,024 square metres of non-residential space; the applicant appealed in February 2026 after Council failed to decide in time, and a first case management conference was held in April 2026 with no hearing date set. The instructions are confidential legal advice.

title: 147 to 151 Liberty Street and 54 to 68 Fraser Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project

brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor seeks Council's directions for the remaining appeals of Official Plan Amendment 778, which Council adopted in February 2025 to revise Avenues policies and designate 283 kilometres of new Avenues. title: Status Update Report on Official Plan Amendment 804 - Request for Directions
topics: appeals, planning;
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor seeks Council's directions on the status of Official Plan Amendment 804, which Council adopted in May 2025 to align the Official Plan's employment-area definitions with provincial legislation (Bill 97) and the 2024 Provincial Planning Statement, barring institutional, commercial, retail and office uses in Employment Areas except with the primary employment use. The amendment went to the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing in June 2025 and is still awaiting a decision; meanwhile the City has received 47 site-specific applications to redesignate employment lands and faces 10 active Tribunal appeals seeking employment-land conversions, with hearings starting as early as November 2026. The recommendations are confidential legal advice. The outcome affects where housing and other uses can replace job lands across the city.

The owner has also applied under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act, and council is being asked for directions on how to handle the heritage side of the file. The directions will shape the City's position as the tribunal case moves forward.

brief: City staff want council to refuse retroactive approval for work already done at 87 Highland Avenue in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District. The owner removed architectural elements, including dentils on the east gable, brackets on the north gable, and Tudor detailing, installed replacements, built a new front porch, and put in new windows along the front. Staff say the alterations do not meet the district's standards, and council will decide whether the changes can stay.

title: 8 Lowther Avenue - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property Under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Approval

City Council is asked to approve the alterations under Part V, Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The property sits on the north side of Lowther Avenue between Bedford Road and Avenue Road.

topics: heritage designation, heritage properties, planning; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Garibaldi House at 302 King Street East in Corktown, on the northeast corner of King Street East and Berkeley Street, is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The designation would legally protect the property's cultural heritage value.

topics: heritage designation, heritage properties, planning; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties

City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The designation would protect two of the St. George campus's defining historic buildings.

topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Kimbark House at 43 Kimbark Boulevard, an early-20th-century Arts and Crafts two-storey home in Lawrence Park South, is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The property sits southwest of Avenue Road and Lawrence Avenue.

title: Stotts’ Bridge, Twyn Rivers Drive over the Rouge River - Demolition of a Designated Heritage Structure, Approval with Conditions
topics: demolitions, heritage properties, planning; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Stotts' Bridge on Twyn Rivers Drive over the Rouge River, a designated heritage structure, is slated for demolition as part of its emergency replacement. City Council is asked to approve the demolition with conditions under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act. The 22.1-metre bridge has a narrow 4.1-metre deck that limits traffic to a single lane, and Twyn Rivers Drive is an identified evacuation route, so the decision weighs heritage protection against the need for a safe, functioning crossing between Sheppard Avenue East and the city limits.

topics: demolitions, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties

City Council is asked to approve the demolition and construction under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act. Heritage staff say the plan complies with the district plan and recommend approval.

topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The former Weston Lions Arena at 2125 Lawrence Avenue West, a City-owned ice-skating arena in Lions Park near the Humber River, is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The designation would protect the arena's cultural heritage value in the Weston neighbourhood.

title: Fare Collection System Update
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, fare media, fares; air fares; airline fares; rail fares; taxi fares; transportation fares, transit tickets; transit tokens, ttc
brief: TTC staff update the Board on the fare collection system, the 2012 TTC-Metrolinx agreement expiring November 28, 2027, whose automatic renewal no longer applies after Metrolinx opted out in May 2025. Following the Board's April 2026 direction, staff posted a public request for information on May 27, 2026, with submissions due July 17, 2026, to understand value for money in automated fare collection offerings. The Board is asked to adopt the recommendations in the confidential attachment. The decision shapes how fare collection is managed after 2027.

title: Update on City of Toronto-Toronto Transit Commission Relationship Framework
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, agreements, local government structure; city council structure; committee structure; council committee structure; council structure; council-committee structure; governance structure, tenancy agreements, ttc
brief: TTC staff present a plan to develop a comprehensive relationship framework between the City of Toronto and the TTC, following direction from the TTC Board and City Council to strengthen the accountable and transparent relationship. As a city agency, the TTC works with the city to deliver safe, reliable and accessible transit, and the framework would complement the City of Toronto Act, the TTC chapter of the Municipal Code and the financial control by-law. The Board is asked to receive the plan.

title: 2200 Yonge Street Reconfigured Entrance Connection to Eglinton Station
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, commercial properties, properties (real estate); office real estate; retail space, property; real estate, ttc
brief: The TTC Board will consider the reconfigured entrance connection to Eglinton Station as part of the Phase One redevelopment of the southwest corner of Yonge Street and Eglinton Avenue. The owner is renovating the 17-storey building at 2200 Yonge Street and demolishing the Bank of Montreal glass pavilion at 2210 Yonge Street, including a new integrated accessible entrance with an elevator linking street level, the station concourse and the platform, plus two new fare lines and a new stairway. The Board's decision determines the station entrance arrangement for the redevelopment.

brief: Declaring a roughly 320-square-metre portion of 6 Spadina Road, including the existing entrance building, surplus to the TTC's operating needs goes to the TTC Board. The surplus land would be released to the City of Toronto for sale to the developer, on condition the owner builds a new integrated accessible entrance connection, the Spadina capacity improvements and a future pedestrian right-of-way between Spadina Road and Walmer Road; demolition of the existing entrance building is anticipated. The decision enables the accessible entrance and capacity work at Spadina station.

The Board is asked to receive the update for information.

The Board directed staff in June 2026 to develop commemoration options in consultation with Mr. Moscoe's family and local stakeholders; the Yorkdale atrium, which will again house Michael Hayden's Arc en Ciel light installation, was chosen for its visibility. The TTC Board is asked to approve the commemorative naming. The commemorative naming is estimated to cost $6,000 for new signage and installation.

The report fulfills the provincial requirement under the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act to report annually on implementation, and includes updates on the Wheel-Trans Transformation Program and the Easier Access Program. title: Exploring Weekly Fare Capping - by Commissioner Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Chair Jamaal Myers
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, fare media, transit fares, transit passes; electronic fare cards; fare cards; metropasses; passes; transit smart cards, transit tickets; transit tokens, ttc
brief: Commissioner Alejandra Bravo is bringing a motion, seconded by Chair Jamaal Myers, to explore weekly fare capping. Fare capping is a pay-as-you-go model that guarantees riders pay for no more than a maximum number of trips, and the Strategic Planning Committee has prioritized it among cost-effective ridership measures; the motion says a weekly cap should be urgently studied before fare capping is implemented. The TTC Board is asked to direct the study so the board can maximize the goal of attracting new and returning riders.

title: Speeding up the College Streetcar Study - by Commissioner Dianne Saxe, seconded by Chair Jamaal Myers
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, streetcar routes, streetcars; street-cars, ttc
brief: Commissioner Dianne Saxe is bringing a motion, seconded by Chair Jamaal Myers, to speed up a study of transit priority on the College streetcar line. The motion notes that more than half of Ward 11 residents depend on transit and active transportation, that Toronto's streetcars are among the slowest in the world because they are stuck in mixed traffic, and that priority measures already rolled out on Spadina, Bathurst and Dundas have shown considerable improvements. The TTC Board is asked to direct staff, with the General Manager of Transportation Services, to study what is possible and achievable on College Street.

title: Protecting Tenants from Fraudulent Evictions
topics: eviction, fraud, tenants; renters; tenancy agreements, waste (fraud)
brief: Tenants hit with fraudulent evictions are left to investigate on their own, gather their own evidence, and hire their own lawyers. A councillor is asking the Planning and Housing Committee to have staff study whether RentSafe officers could be empowered to spot rental fraud and compile evidence for criminal investigations, with a feasibility report due by mid-2027. The motion cites an example of tenants paying $525 more per month in rent following a fraudulent eviction.

title: Our Plan Toronto: Recommendations on the East Harbour Employment Area Conversion Request - Final Report
topics: development, land use, official plan amendments; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Staff recommendations are back before council on the request to convert East Harbour employment lands to non-employment uses, the fourth in a series of final reports under the Our Plan Toronto municipal comprehensive review. Council referred the item back to the Planning and Housing Committee in October 2023. About 150 conversion requests were received during the review of employment-designated lands, and the provincial Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing is the final approval authority for the Official Plan amendment.

brief: The item asks the Infrastructure and Environment Committee to have the General Manager of Transportation Services — with the TTC CEO and community consultation — report back in Q1 2027 with recommendations to improve the College streetcar's speed and reliability through transit priority measures within the city's control, such as signal changes and parking and turn restrictions. The motion notes over half of Ward 11 residents don't own cars and cites transit priority gains on Spadina, Bathurst, and Dundas. The item affects College streetcar riders. The committee decides.

brief: The item asks the Infrastructure and Environment Committee to have the General Manager of Transportation Services report back at the first 2027 meeting with recommendations for snow clearing that would give pedestrian access to lawfully built laneway homes in Ward 11 — starting with Shaftesbury Court and Croft Street — whose only road access is via public lanes the city doesn't plow. The motion follows staff declining to recommend snow removal for the city's 2,744 public laneways. The item affects laneway homeowners' winter access. The committee decides.

title: Utility Construction Photo Documentation
brief: This is a procedural item: the Audit Committee asks City Council to have the General Manager of Transportation Services provide permits, timing, and sequencing for utility work on four Ward 14 (Toronto-Danforth) streets — Woodfield Road, Riverdale Avenue, Grant Street, and Danforth Avenue — and to report on pylon removal after construction. Council decides on the direction.

title: Implementation Strategy for a Modern Utility Billing System
topics: solid waste management fees, utilities, water meters; power utilties, remote water meters
brief: This is a procedural item: the committee is receiving the implementation strategy for a modern utility billing system, developed after council's November 2025 direction for Toronto Water — with solid waste, revenue services, finance, and technology officials — to hire a billing-systems expert, set up governance, and report back in Q2 2026 with a recommendation, plan, and funding needs. The strategy affects how residents are billed for water and other utilities. The committee receives the report.

title: Road Construction on Keele South of Sheppard
topics: construction, road restrictions, sanitary sewers; building, lane restrictions; road information; traffic restrictions; trip info; tripinfo
brief: A member motion raises resident complaints about third-party construction on Keele Street north and south of Sheppard Avenue — managed by Canada Lands Corporation and its partners for sanitary sewer work connecting to the Black Creek Tunnel Project starting in 2027 — citing lane closures with no visible work, no construction notice to residents, no central contact point, and a timeline running into the school year on an arterial serving York University and Highway 401 access. The motion asks the committee to act on the disruption. The item affects Keele Street traffic and residents. The committee decides on direction.

title: Options to Provide an Inexpensive, Non-polluting Power Supply for Mobile Food Vendors
topics: electricity, greenhouse effect, vendors; electric power; electricity usage, greenhouse gas emissions
brief: The item asks the Infrastructure and Environment Committee to have the Executive Director of Environment, Climate and Forestry — with Toronto Hydro, Municipal Licensing and Standards, and Transportation Services — evaluate New York City's pilot letting mobile food cart vendors rent clean, swappable rechargeable batteries instead of running noisy, polluting gas or diesel generators. The motion notes most Toronto food vendors rely on generators, whose cumulative noise and air pollution affect nearby residents and workers, and whose fuel cost burdens vendors. The committee decides on the request.

title: Options for Connecting the Loop Trail to The Meadoway

brief: The committee is receiving an overview of options for connecting the Loop Trail to The Meadoway — part of the Ravine Strategy's vision of a continuous citywide trail and greenspace network — with coordinated work by the city, the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority, and community and funding partners. New sections opened in summer 2026, and the safe, accessible connection is expected to be complete by the end of 2027. The report affects ravine access and active transportation. The committee receives the report.

No policy change is proposed.

brief: After a fatal attack at the Salsa on St. Clair festival that killed two people, Councillors Bravo and Matlow are asking the committee to have staff include festival and large-gathering safety work in the next Festival Strategy update. The work would engage police, paramedics, fire, and emergency management on planning coordination for large events. The motion asks for a plan, not new spending.

No change to Toronto's last-call rules is proposed yet.

brief: The Francophone Affairs Advisory Committee is asking the committee to have staff study whether the City could help fund a permanent venue for Theatre francais de Toronto, the city's only professional French-language theatre, which has operated for nearly 60 years without a permanent home. The study would also examine collaboration options. Seventy-one Franco-Ontarian organizations have signed letters supporting the project.

topics: boards of management, committee meetings, investment; boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: The Direct Investment Committee is asking the Toronto Atmospheric Fund board to approve an investment of up to $400,000 in preferred shares of a Canadian electric vehicle charging enablement company, as part of a $2,000,000 seed financing round. The company's AI-enabled power management systems support Level 2 EV charging in buildings with limited electrical capacity and in fleet applications, reducing the need for costly electrical upgrades. The investment fits the fund's clean transportation and retrofit goals.

The fund finances high-growth, sustainability-focused companies in clean energy, agriculture, and health, and performance so far has met expectations. The commitment fits the fund's investment policy and target allocation.

topics: boards of management, funding, investment; boards of directors; boards of governors, financing
brief: The Direct Investment Committee is asking the Toronto Atmospheric Fund board to amend the existing 2025 Credit Agreement for its $4.5 million revolving working-capital facility with a company that provides integrated electric vehicle fast-charging and battery energy storage solutions. The Vice President of Impact Investing recommends the amendment.

title: Declaring the Drug Toxicity Crisis an Epidemic
topics: health; health coverage
brief: The Board of Health is considering a proposal to declare the drug toxicity crisis an epidemic, brought forward in the context of April data showing 485 non-fatal suspected opioid overdoses attended by Paramedic Services — the highest monthly prevalence since 2021 — and four public drug alerts issued so far this year compared to one in 2025. The proposal's framing attributes the figures to an unregulated toxic drug supply and the closure of nearly all supervised consumption sites, and cites burnout among front-line workers responding to multiple overdoses daily. The declaration would affect the city's public health posture on the overdose crisis. The board decides.

title: Investigating the Increased Risk of Heart Disease, Lung Cancer, and Tumours from Bringing Jets to Toronto’s Waterfront Communities
topics: health; health coverage
brief: City Council has asked the Board of Health to direct the Medical Officer of Health to gather all available data on the health impacts of transportation emissions — including ultrafine particles — and noise from jets near residential communities, in the context of Billy Bishop Airport specifically, Pearson International Airport, and international examples. The request also includes working with Health Canada on a comprehensive study of jets near Billy Bishop, including healthcare costs and burdens and a comparison with Pearson. The item stems from a May 2026 council decision. The board decides on the request.

The response includes programming to advance Indigenous data sovereignty and health outcomes through Toronto Public Health's Indigenous Health Strategy. The board decides on sharing the report.
