title: Mount Pleasant Sidewalk Study
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: pedestrian walkways, road safety, sidewalks; footpaths; pedestrian ways; walking paths; walkways
brief: A study is proposed for pedestrian safety on Mount Pleasant Road, where there is no sidewalk on the west side between Crescent Road and Roxborough Drive. Pedestrians walking north from Roxborough Street East to reach the park, Yellow Creek or the signalized crossing to the east side face what the ward councillor calls a dangerous situation. The item asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to direct staff to report back in the first quarter of 2027 with recommendations on adding the sidewalk.

title: Re-appointment of Board Members on the Cecil Community Centre Board of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: appointments, boards of management, community centres; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to reappoint Laura Mandelbaum, Ryan Patrick Northfield, Hadi Damani and Andrea Wan to the Cecil Community Centre board of management, for terms beginning June 30, 2026 and ending June 30, 2028. The reappointments follow the board's June 24, 2026 membership election, and current member Corals Zheng has chosen not to renew. No policy change is proposed.

title: Annex Intersections Safety Study
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: pedestrians, safety, schools; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums, pedestrianization, public safety
brief: A safety study is proposed for two wide, non-standard, offset intersections in the Annex: St. George Street at Bernard Avenue, and Kendal Avenue at Walmer Road. The Annex Residents' Association asked for the study, saying both intersections pose chronic dangers for pedestrians, including many children walking to school, and suggesting fixes like bump-outs to narrow traffic lanes and encourage drivers to stop. The item asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to direct staff to report back with recommendations at the first 2027 meeting.

title: Adding Seating on Streetscapes in Ward 11
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: [activities in transportation], pedestrians, transportation; pedestrianization, transportation services
brief: Transportation Services, in consultation with the TTC, would report back in the first quarter of 2027 on adding seating along streetscapes in Ward 11. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to direct the report. Councillor Dianne Saxe notes that more than half of Ward 11 residents do not own cars and rely on walking and transit, including many seniors, and that streetscapes lack seating even where local businesses want to encourage foot traffic. The report would prioritize locations with the greatest need.

title: Traffic Calming - Scadding Avenue, between Princess Street and Hahn Place, and Speed Limit Reduction on Scadding Avenue, between Lower Sherbourne Street and Hahn Place
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: pedestrians, safety, traffic calming, traffic calming measures; pedestrianization, public safety, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Traffic calming is proposed for Scadding Avenue between Princess Street and Hahn Place, along with a lower speed limit on Scadding Avenue between Lower Sherbourne Street and Hahn Place. Residents and the St Lawrence Neighbourhood Association report speeding and cut-through driving to bypass The Esplanade in an area with heavy pedestrian traffic from Parliament Square Park, Princess Street Park and David Crombie Park, plus a school, daycare, community centre and seniors' building; staff also found a discrepancy between the posted and by-lawed speed rules. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the measures.

title: Traffic Calming - Denison Avenue, between Queen Street West and Wolseley Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: pedestrians, safety, traffic calming, traffic calming measures; pedestrianization, public safety, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: One speed hump is proposed for Denison Avenue between Queen Street West and Wolseley Street, after the Queen Street West BIA reported motorists speeding as they leave the neighbourhood onto Queen Street West. The area has heavy pedestrian and cyclist activity, with nearby destinations including St. Stanislaus Kostka Church, Randy Padmore Park and Queen Street West businesses. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is bringing the proposal to the Toronto and East York Community Council for a decision.

title: Ordnance Street, Between Strachan Avenue and the South End of Ordnance Street - Traffic Calming
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: public safety & protection (sc), traffic calming, traffic calming measures; traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Three speed humps are proposed for Ordnance Street between Strachan Avenue and the street's south end, following a resident request and an online survey of local condo residents that drew over 100 responses, a majority in favour. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik says the humps would improve safety at a key downtown intersection. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the installation.

title: Advancing Parking and Traffic Amendments, Speed Reduction and Allowing for Future Speed Humps on Iannuzzi Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: on-street parking, parking prohibitions, speed humps, speed limits; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, no parking, sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Parking and traffic changes are proposed for Iannuzzi Street, where residents and the Fort York Neighbourhood Association raised concerns about speeding and parked vehicles blocking sightlines for drivers exiting a nearby condo complex. Engineering staff determined the street has not yet been assumed or classified by the city, so speed humps cannot be physically installed yet; approving (bylawying) two speed humps now would let the city install them quickly once the road is assumed. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the package.
address: Toronto Ontario Iannuzzi Street Fort York Boulevard

title: Advancing Parking and Traffic Amendments, Speed Reduction and Allowing for Future Speed Humps on Bruyeres Mews
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking prohibitions, speed humps, speed limits; no parking, sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: A package of parking and traffic changes is proposed for Bruyeres Mews in the Fort York area, developed with local residents, the Fort York Neighbourhood Association and city staff. Residents raised concerns about vehicles parking in a no-standing area on the north side near Bathurst Street, causing congestion, honking and poor visibility for pedestrians and cyclists; crosswalk lines and a yellow divider line at Iannuzzi Street are already being installed, and the changes would also lower speeds and allow future speed humps. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the amendments.

title: Safer Streets for Davenport: Reducing Speed Limits
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: road safety, safety, speed limits; public safety
brief: Speed limits would be lowered on several collector roads across Davenport under this proposal from Councillor Alejandra Bravo. The councillor says the streets function more like local streets, linking residents to schools, parks and everyday destinations used by hundreds of pedestrians, and that higher vehicle speeds are creating safety risks as more people walk, cycle and take transit. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the reductions.

title: Re-opening and Amending 2025.TE25.42 - Accessible Parking Spaces
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: accessibility, parking, parking regulations; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: This item re-opens the September 2025 decision (2025.TE25.42) that approved accessible parking spaces on Chudleigh Road and Morrison Avenue. The Chudleigh Road space is not long enough for the original applicant's vehicle and is no longer needed, while the Morrison Avenue space would be relocated to better meet the applicant's needs. The item asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to rescind the old approvals and approve the relocated Morrison Avenue space.

title: Parking Amendments on Wade Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: A no-standing regulation is proposed for the west side of Wade Avenue, south of Paton Road, beside the entrance and exit of a business's paid boulevard parking area. The business owner reported that vehicles routinely block the boulevard parking, causing delays for employees, deliveries and guests, and staff found extra measures are needed even though city rules already prohibit parking in front of a legal boulevard. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the change, which is aimed at discouraging the blocking.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Rochdale Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming, traffic calming measures; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Speed humps are proposed for Rochdale Avenue between Ennerdale Road and Harvie Avenue, in the heart of Caledonia-Fairbank, connecting residents to local shops, schools, parks and transit. Residents reported frequent speeding and near misses, and overwhelmingly supported the humps in a neighbourhood survey as the area continues to grow. Councillor Alejandra Bravo is bringing the proposal to the Toronto and East York Community Council for a decision.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Pelham Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming, traffic calming measures; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Speed humps are proposed to close a gap on Pelham Avenue left by the 2018 approval, which only covered the section from Uxbridge Avenue to Laughton Avenue. The remaining block is used by young students walking to Charles-Sauriol Elementary School and families visiting Pelham Avenue Playground, and residents say drivers speed toward the existing humps; a neighbourhood survey found unanimous support for the new humps. Councillor Alejandra Bravo is bringing the proposal to the Toronto and East York Community Council for a decision.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Muir Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: road safety, speed humps, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Speed humps are proposed for Muir Avenue, a local route south of Dufferin Mall running west from Dufferin Street, where residents reported speeding and dangerous driving. Residents voted in support of traffic calming in a hand-delivered neighbourhood survey, and the new humps would build on measures already in place on nearby streets. Councillor Alejandra Bravo is bringing the proposal to the Toronto and East York Community Council for a decision.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Margueretta Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic calming, traffic calming measures, traffic regulations; traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Speed humps are proposed for Margueretta Street between College Street and Dundas Street West, a block between two busy arterials that draws heavy pedestrian activity and cut-through traffic avoiding nearby intersections. Residents told Councillor Alejandra Bravo's office that speeding is a daily problem, with near-accidents reported, and strongly supported the humps in a neighbourhood survey. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the installation.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Kirknewton Road
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic, traffic calming, traffic calming measures; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Speed humps are proposed for Kirknewton Road, a residential street running south from Eglinton Avenue West that people use to walk and cycle to nearby schools, businesses and parks. Residents contacted Councillor Alejandra Bravo's office about excessive speeds and dangerous driving, and a hand-delivered survey confirmed strong neighbourhood support for the humps. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the installation.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Greenlaw Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming, traffic calming measures; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Speed humps are proposed for Greenlaw Avenue, which runs south from a busy section of St. Clair Avenue West and connects the neighbourhood to schools, small businesses and parks. Residents reported drivers speeding to avoid nearby major intersections, running stop signs and driving aggressively in an area where many young children live and walk, and voted strongly in favour of the humps in a neighbourhood survey. Councillor Alejandra Bravo is bringing the proposal to the Toronto and East York Community Council for a decision.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Gilbert Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking prohibitions, traffic calming, traffic calming measures, traffic regulations; no parking, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Speed humps are proposed for Gilbert Avenue between Kitchener Avenue and Eglinton Avenue West, completing a traffic calming network already in place on other sections of the street. Residents reported near accidents involving themselves and their children walking the street, which draws drivers bypassing traffic on busy roads, and strongly supported the humps in a hand-delivered survey. Councillor Alejandra Bravo is bringing the proposal to the Toronto and East York Community Council for a decision.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Ennerdale Road
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming, traffic calming measures; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Two speed humps are proposed for Ennerdale Road between Rochdale Avenue and Chudleigh Road, on a stretch residents say lacks the traffic calming found further south toward Dynevor Road. Ennerdale runs south from Eglinton Avenue West and is a busy route to nearby destinations; a neighbourhood survey confirmed strong support for the humps. Councillor Alejandra Bravo is bringing the proposal to the Toronto and East York Community Council for a decision.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Earlscourt Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming, traffic calming measures; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Speed humps are proposed for Earlscourt Avenue just south of Rogers Road, to fill a gap in the street's existing network of humps that residents say encourages speeding and dangerous driving. Residents reported near accidents and, in a neighbourhood survey, voted strongly in favour of the humps to slow traffic and reduce cut-through driving. Councillor Alejandra Bravo is bringing the proposal to the Toronto and East York Community Council for a decision.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Concord Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: safety, speed humps, traffic calming, traffic calming measures; public safety, sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Speed humps are proposed for Concord Avenue between Bloor Street West and College Street, a block between two major arterials that residents say is used by drivers cutting through to avoid congestion. Residents have reported excessive speeds and near-collisions and raised concerns for children travelling to and from Dewson Street Junior Public School; a neighbourhood survey backed traffic calming. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the installation.

title: Improving Traffic Calming Measures on Blackthorn Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking regulations, speed humps, traffic calming, traffic calming measures; parking by-laws; parking bylaws, sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: A gap in traffic calming on Blackthorn Avenue between Rogers Road and Rowntree Avenue would be closed with new speed humps, about 100 metres south of the southernmost existing hump near Rockwell Avenue. The five original humps date to 2000, and residents say the gap left after the street was converted to one-way southbound through the Silverthorn Cycling Connections project encourages speeding on a street used by many families and young children. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the additional humps.

title: Improving Permit Parking on Delaware Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking regulations, permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Permit parking rules would be aligned along Delaware Avenue between Shanly Street and Hallam Street, where residents say the shorter parking period pushes drivers to leave cars there to dodge the longer overnight-until-10:00-a.m. restriction in effect south of Shanly Street. A survey hand-delivered by Councillor Alejandra Bravo's office found support for standardizing the block with the rules south of Shanly. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the change.

title: Improving Permit Parking on Conway Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking regulations, permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Residents on Conway Avenue asked Councillor Alejandra Bravo's office to fix permit parking rules that they say are confusing, with switchover days cutting parking availability and posted signs that do not match other sections of the street. A neighbourhood survey showed strong support for removing the switchover days and keeping parking on the north side, which has far more spaces, to standardize the rules. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the amendments.

title: Improving Permit Parking on Concord Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Parking rules on Concord Avenue between College Street and Dewson Street would be cleaned up under this proposal, after residents told Councillor Alejandra Bravo's office that inconsistent and confusing regulations leave too few spaces for permit holders on weekday afternoons and evenings. The changes align school bus loading and short-term parking restrictions with Dewson Street Junior Public School's operating hours and standardize the street's posted rules, with a $3.25 parking-machine charge. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the amendments.

title: Improving Pedestrian Safety at Turnberry Avenue and Alentejo Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: community safety, parking prohibitions, traffic speed; no parking
brief: An all-way stop is proposed for the intersection of Turnberry Avenue and Alentejo Street, along with parking restrictions to clear sightlines for drivers. The intersection sits in a residential area near General Mercer Junior Public School and several parks, and residents say it remains dangerously unsafe despite traffic calming installed on Turnberry Avenue in 2023. Councillor Alejandra Bravo is bringing the measures to the Toronto and East York Community Council for a decision.

title: Davenport Village Traffic Safety Plan: Additional Improvements
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking prohibitions, stopping prohibitions, traffic regulations; no parking, no stopping
brief: Following last year's Davenport Village Traffic Safety Plan, residents have raised new concerns about unsafe parking and blocked sightlines at intersections in the area. Transportation staff found that Brandon Avenue, west of Lansdowne Avenue, has no signed parking regulations, so three-hour unsigned parking on both sides narrows the road and reduces visibility for pedestrians, cyclists and drivers. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to add parking restrictions to fix the problem.

title: Accessible Loading Zone Mavety Street south of Dundas Street West
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: accessibility, loading zones, transportation; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, transportation services
brief: Transportation Services wants to install a designated on-street accessible parking space on Mavety Street, south of Dundas Street West, to serve a resident with mobility needs. The spot is being placed on Mavety Street rather than Dundas Street West to avoid that street's parking restrictions; it replaces one pay-and-display space, which staff say will have minimal impact on local parking demand. City Council is asked to approve the change, which also cleans up inconsistencies in the traffic by-law for the surrounding signed parking.

title: Naming of an Existing Public Lane Located West of Vaughan Road, North of Ellsworth Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: lanes, naming, street names; renaming; road names; street naming, traffic lanes; turn lanes; turning lanes
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the name “Aren Levy Lane” for an existing public lane west of Vaughan Road, north of Ellsworth Avenue. Staff say the proposal complies with the city's street naming policy and its principles for commemoration in the public realm. No policy change is proposed.

title: Shaftesbury Avenue - Parking Amendment
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, parking, parking regulations, transportation; parking by-laws; parking bylaws, transportation services, ttc
brief: Parking signs on Shaftesbury Avenue were removed years ago for the TTC's elevator project at Summerhill station, and residents have been pressing to have the original signs restored ever since the TTC gave the road space back. A by-law conflict is blocking the restoration, so The item asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to rescind the current one-hour parking rule (9:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday to Saturday) on the north side between Summerhill Avenue and a point 91.4 metres east of Yonge Street.

title: Re-open Items TE27.50, Roxborough Street West (Phase 2) - Construction Staging Area - Amendments and  TE33.70, Improving Pedestrian Safety on Roxborough Road
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: pedestrian crossovers, safety, sidewalks, transportation; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, public safety, transportation services
brief: Two earlier decisions are being reopened so the construction staging area at 1 Roxborough Street West can be adjusted and extended. Transportation Services now advises it is safer and more feasible to put the temporary pedestrian crossover 40 metres west of Paul Hahn Lane instead of 100 metres, and the current staging permit expires before the next community council meeting. The item asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to re-open the items and approve the changes, which affect pedestrians' access to the remaining sidewalk during construction of the new multi-unit building.

title: Euclid Avenue direction change
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: roads, traffic direction; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), one way operations; one way streets; one way traffic; two way operations; two way streets; two way traffic
brief: Euclid Avenue residents are asking that the block between Ulster Street and Harbord Street be flipped from one-way northbound to one-way southbound. The street, the closest continuous northbound route west of Bathurst, has been overwhelmed by cut-through traffic including chronic illegal use by heavy trucks, which residents say police have not had the resources to enforce against. Councillor Dianne Saxe is bringing the change to the Toronto and East York Community Council for a decision.

title: Improving Pedestrian Safety on Crescent Road - Delegated
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: road safety, safety; public safety
brief: Residents on Crescent Road between Cluny Drive and South Drive report that cut-through drivers, guided by wayfinding apps, are driving onto the sidewalk to get around TTC buses, trucks and parked cars, which is especially dangerous for children walking to and from school. Transportation staff visited the site and confirmed both the safety problem and delays to the Rosedale 82 bus caused by the narrow road and parked vehicles. This delegated motion, before the Toronto and East York Community Council for a final decision, covers the measures within community council's authority; a companion motion handles the parking changes that need City Council.

title: Appointment to the Community Centre 55 Board of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: appointments, board members, boards of management, community centres, public appointments; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to appoint Pauline Grant and Patrick Sweeney to the Community Centre 55 board of management, for terms ending June 30, 2030. The board has confirmed both nominees are qualified. No policy change is proposed.

title: Appointment of Community Members to the Eastview Neighbourhood Community Centre Board of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council

brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to appoint Bilaal Bana, Rizwan Desai and Julia Porter to the Eastview Neighbourhood Community Centre board of management (terms ending June 30, 2027) and to reappoint Farhan Chaudhary, Claire Lukka, Dalreen Fobler, Mubarak Baker and Lauren Lee (terms ending June 30, 2028). The board has confirmed all nominees are qualified. No policy change is proposed.

title: Appointment of Community Members to the Applegrove Community Complex Board of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: appointments, boards of management, community centres, public appointments; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to appoint five nominees to the Applegrove Community Complex board of management: Kathryn Edgett-Emirzian (term ending June 30, 2027) and Jean Lim O-Brien, Kirstin Vanderpark, Pat Jordan and Lesley Nilsson (terms ending June 30, 2028). The appointments follow the end of Brian Wood's term and the resignation of Juanita Morris, and the board has confirmed all nominees are qualified. No policy change is proposed.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Moss Park Arena Board
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: appointments, arenas, boards of management, public appointments; boards of directors; boards of governors, indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to appoint Pui See Ho as a public member of the Moss Park Arena Board, for a term ending April 2, 2030. The City Clerk shortlisted and interviewed candidates and recommends the appointment, with confidential attachments on the candidate kept private. No policy change is proposed.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the William H. (Bill) Bolton Arena Board
body: Toronto and East York Community Council

brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to appoint Ashley Winberg as a public member of the William H. (Bill) Bolton Arena Board, for a term ending October 23, 2029. The City Clerk shortlisted and interviewed candidates and recommends the appointment, with confidential attachments on the candidate kept private. No policy change is proposed.

title: Appointments to the Board of Management of the Waterfront Neighbourhood Centre
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: appointments, boards of management, nomination, public appointments; boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to appoint Tina Szeto, Claudia Huerta and Devyaani Bhardwaj to the Waterfront Neighbourhood Centre board of management, for terms ending July 8, 2030. The board has confirmed the nominees are qualified, and the appointment follows the end of Carole Therriault's term on June 23, 2026. No policy change is proposed.

title: St. John's Road - Additional Speed Humps
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic, transportation; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, transportation services
brief: Six additional speed humps are proposed for St. John's Road between Jane Street and Beresford Avenue, on top of two humps approved in 2003, following continued complaints about drivers travelling at high speeds. Staff say the street does not meet the usual numerical warrant for traffic calming, but lower thresholds can be used in Community Safety Zones to protect vulnerable road users. The Toronto and East York Community Council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: Traffic Calming (Speed Humps) - Various Streets in Ward 4
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming, transportation; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, transportation services
brief: Transportation Services is recommending speed humps on five streets in Ward 4: Armadale Avenue (Colbeck to Ardagh), Beresford Avenue (Annette to Dundas West, and Colbeck to Ardagh), Pacific Avenue (Humberside to Dundas West) and Parkway Avenue (Grenadier to Dundas West). Staff say the streets meet the city's traffic calming criteria. The Toronto and East York Community Council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: Castle Frank Road and South Drive (Non-Delegated) - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: pedestrian crossovers, pedestrians, road safety, safety; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, pedestrianization, public safety
brief: City Council is asked not to authorize pedestrian crossovers at two spots on South Drive — at Craigleigh Gardens and the Milkman's Lane access point — after a staff review found the technical warrant criteria were not met and the road geometry made them unsuitable. A companion delegated report covers the Castle Frank Road crossing. Council approval is required because the TTC runs transit on South Drive.

title: Castle Frank Road and South Drive - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: pedestrian crossovers, pedestrians, safety; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, pedestrianization, public safety
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked not to install a pedestrian crossover at 36 Castle Frank Road, after a staff review found the technical warrant criteria were not met and the road geometry made it unsuitable. A companion non-delegated report covers the two requested South Drive crossings. Staff do recommend pavement marking improvements at the Elm Avenue and Castle Frank Road/Nanton Avenue intersection to improve sightlines and stop compliance.

title: Pedestrian Crosswalks on Winona Drive between Holland Park Avenue and Glenhurst Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council

brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to receive a report for information summarizing where new marked crosswalks could go on Winona Drive between Holland Park Avenue and Glenhurst Avenue. No policy change is proposed.

title: 227 Gerrard Street East - Proposed Traffic and Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, traffic, transportation; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, transportation services
brief: A portion of Ontario Street south of Gerrard Street East would convert from one-way southbound to two-way traffic, with updated parking rules, to give drivers proper access to the new seven-storey mixed-use building at 227 Gerrard Street East. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the changes, which address the site plan agreement; all costs fall to the developer.

title: Cooper Street, Downes Street, and John M Tinsley Street - Traffic Regulations and Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, traffic regulations, transportation; transportation services
brief: Traffic and parking rules on Cooper Street, Downes Street, and John M Tinsley Street would be set for the new public streets in the former LCBO lands development at 55 Lake Shore Boulevard East — including more overnight permit parking on Cooper Street for nearby residents, plus pickup and drop-off and short-term visitor parking. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the regulations for the streets, which have been newly conveyed to the city as part of Phase 1.

title: Temporary Adjustments to Traffic and Parking Regulations for 2026 Distillery Winter Village (Delegated)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking regulations, traffic, transportation; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, parking by-laws; parking bylaws, transportation services
brief: Whether to approve temporary traffic and parking rules around the Distillery District from November 12, 2026 to January 3, 2027, to manage visitors and protect nearby residents' streets during the Distillery Winter Village event now sits with the community council. The measures would limit traffic infiltration into local streets and prioritize access for residents. A companion report covers the streets that need City Council approval.

title: Temporary Adjustments to Traffic and Parking Regulations for the 2026 Canadian National Exhibition (Delegated)

topics: change, parking prohibitions; amendments; conversion; modification, no parking
brief: Parking would be banned at all times on the west side of Stephen Drive along a roughly 23-metre stretch starting 62 metres south of the street's north end. Etobicoke York Community Council has the final decision. Anyone parking on that side of Stephen Drive would need to find another spot.

title: Cliveden Avenue - Parking Amendments
topics: parking, parking regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Parking rules on the west side of Cliveden Avenue near Bloor Street West would be updated to match what's actually signed on the street — including shifting the angle-parking zone, adding a small angle-parking section, adjusting the $4.50 parking machine zone, and creating a no-stopping area at the curb depression about 37 metres south of Bloor so the accessible parking ramp stays clear. The item also corrects misspellings of "Cliveden Avenue" in existing regulations. Etobicoke York Community Council has the final say on these parking tweaks.

title: Evans Avenue - Heavy Vehicles
topics: heavy truck prohibitions, heavy trucks;
brief: Transportation Services studied whether to extend the overnight heavy-truck ban on Evans Avenue (between Islington Avenue and Royal York Road) to a full 24-hour ban, and is reporting the results back to Etobicoke York Community Council for information — no decision on a ban is attached to this item. Truck operators and residents along Evans Avenue are the ones watching this one.

title: Maple Leaf Drive and Jane Street - Investigation of Turn Prohibition
topics: traffic, turn prohibitions (traffic); motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: Staff investigated a possible peak-period left-turn ban from Jane Street onto Maple Leaf Drive, as directed by the community council in May 2026, and found it would not work because of negative impacts on the Maple Leaf and Rustic neighbourhoods. The recommendation is simply that Etobicoke York Community Council receive the report for information — no ban is being proposed. Drivers on Jane Street and residents of the surrounding neighbourhoods are the ones affected.

title: The Kingsway and Lambeth Road - Turn Prohibition
topics: traffic, turn prohibitions (traffic); motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: The southbound left-turn prohibition at The Kingsway and Lambeth Road would be removed, since the intersection has been rebuilt and now handles all turning movements safely — the ban is no longer needed. Etobicoke York Community Council makes the final decision. Drivers at this intersection would gain back the left-turn option.

title: Toledo Road - U-turn Prohibition

brief: Transportation Services wants to extend the existing U-turn prohibition on Toledo Road, moving its boundary from between Mills Road and Renforth Drive to between Renforth Drive and a point 200 metres west. Etobicoke York Community Council has the final decision. Drivers on Toledo Road would face U-turn restrictions on a different stretch of the road.

title: Berry Road - Traffic Calming (Speed Cushions)

brief: Berry Road between Prince Edward Drive South and Park Lawn Road would get four speed cushions (a transit-friendly version of speed humps) and a speed limit drop from 40 km/h to 30 km/h, with staff saying the street meets the Traffic Calming Policy criteria. Etobicoke York Community Council decides. Drivers on Berry Road would see both a lower speed limit and physical traffic calming.

Staff say the streets meet the updated Traffic Calming Policy, and Etobicoke York Community Council makes the final call. The goal is slower vehicle speeds, especially for pedestrian safety.

Staff say all three streets meet the Traffic Calming Policy criteria, and Etobicoke York Community Council has the final say. Drivers on these streets would face new physical speed controls.
address: Dales Road Toronto Ontario; Mendota Toronto Ontario; Wesley Toronto Ontario

The plan followed a study of road safety in the area, and the community council has the final say. Residents on these streets would see slower vehicle speeds as a result.

brief: This is a procedural item: the Infrastructure and Sustainability Working Group's chair and a member will give the Film, Television and Digital Media Advisory Board a verbal update on a recent meeting held after the Film Strategic Plan was adopted. No decision is attached.

brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee will hear the property owner's appeal of a property standards order issued April 20, 2026 for 3434 Eglinton Avenue East, unit 1208 (file 26 144634 PRS 00 IV). The committee can confirm, change, or cancel the order. The hearing gives the owner a chance to challenge the city's maintenance or repair requirements.

title: 85 Silver Springs Boulevard - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number 26 139792 PRS 00 IV
topics: municipal codes, parking facilities, property standards;
brief: This is a procedural item: an appeal of the property standards order for 85 Silver Springs Boulevard goes before the Property Standards Committee. The order was issued April 9, 2026 (file 26 139792 PRS 00 IV). The committee will decide whether the order stands, changes, or is cancelled.

title: 143-147 Main Street - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, demolitions, rental housing; application process, rental properties; rental units
brief: It's City Council's call whether to approve demolishing 7 rental homes at 143 and 147 Main Street for the proposed 10-storey, 56-unit building, on the condition that the owner replaces them with 7 new rental units and provides tenants with a compensation and right-to-return plan. The tenant assistance plan would give existing tenants the right to return at similar rents plus financial compensation. The approval also recommends a residential demolition permit with a $20,000.00 financial condition.

title: 143, 145 and 147 Main Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning; bylaws, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: A 10-storey mixed-use building with 56 homes — including 7 replacement rental units — and 98 square metres of commercial space is proposed for 143, 145, and 147 Main Street, and City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments. The plan is described as appropriate intensification within a protected major transit station area. The bills would be withheld until the rental housing demolition application is approved.

title: Renaming Tichester Park in Honour of Hedy Bohm
topics: naming, roads, street names; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), renaming; road names; street naming
brief: Tichester Park at 27 Tichester Road would be renamed Hedy Bohm Park, honouring the Holocaust survivor — born in Romania in 1926, imprisoned at Auschwitz, immigrated to Toronto in 1949 — and longtime Tichester Road resident known for Holocaust education and community work. Councillor Josh Matlow's motion asks City Council to approve the renaming despite the city's naming policy provisions; the sign costs would come from the 2026 Parks and Recreation operating budget.

title: 6-8 and 10-12 Sumach Street - Alterations to Designated Heritage Properties Under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The decision on whether to approve alterations to the heritage-designated Victorian terrace houses at 6-8 and 10-12 Sumach Street — built in 1886-1888 as late-Victorian workers' housing — and to enter into a heritage easement agreement rests with City Council. The plan would relocate the two heritage buildings on the development site so two new mixed-use and residential towers can be built; heritage staff are satisfied the proposal conserves the properties. Designation by-law 90-2026 was enacted in February 2026.

title: High Park Avenue - Parking Amendments
topics: parking, parking regulations, permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Parking rules on High Park Avenue would change so permit holders can no longer park in the daycare's short-term pickup zone at the High Park Early Learning Centre between 3 and 3:15 p.m. on weekdays, after complaints that parked vehicles are disrupting afternoon pickup. City Council is asked to approve the 15-minute parking prohibition and to fix discrepancies between the by-lawed regulations and posted signage on the street. Council approval is required because the TTC runs transit on High Park Avenue.

title: Accessible Parking Space - Davenport Road (Non-Delegated)
topics: accessibility, parking, transportation; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, transportation services
brief: City Council is set to decide whether to designate a new on-street accessible parking space on the south side of Davenport Road, east of Dufferin Street, and to remove an older by-lawed space near Bartlett Avenue North that no longer has signage and is no longer needed. Council approval is required because the TTC runs transit on Davenport Road.

title: 1, 2A and 4-16 Sumach Street and 90 Eastern Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning & development (sc), residential properties, zoning bylaws; residential real estate, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Two tall towers are proposed for 1, 2A and 4-16 Sumach Street and 90 Eastern Avenue — a 59-storey mixed-use building and a 55-storey residential building with 1,276 homes and at least 1,200 square metres of commercial space — and City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments with a holding provision. The Official Plan change is needed to permit the scale of development in the Corktown part of the King-Parliament Secondary Plan area. The plan includes demolishing 11 homes, three of them rentals, with a separate heritage report on the designated properties at 6-12 Sumach Street considered alongside.

title: Temporary Adjustments to Permit Parking Relocation on Mathersfield Drive and Chestnut Park
topics: construction, parking, permit parking; building, on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: The decision on whether to allow temporary permit parking on Mathersfield Drive and Chestnut Park for about a year starting June 2026, making up for on-street parking lost to a watermain replacement project on Rowanwood Avenue, Cluny Drive, Pricefield Road, and Thornwood Road rests with City Council. The work replaces a 900mm transmission watermain with a new 1200mm one, with shaft construction, tunnelling, and truck haul routes that will displace existing permit holders.

title: Realignment of Permit Parking Area 1E to Exclude the Development Located at 3459 and 3461 Dundas Street West
topics: parking, permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: The decision on removing the development at 3459 and 3461 Dundas Street West from Permit Parking Area 1E, so residents and visitors there would no longer qualify for the city's on-street overnight permit parking program rests with City Council. Staff say the realignment of the area map is feasible and raise no objections. Council approval is required because the TTC runs transit on Dundas Street West.

title: Transit Priority Measures to Support Transit Diversions during the College Street / Carlton Street Closure Between Bay Street and Church Street
topics: road closures, traffic regulations, transportation, turn prohibitions (traffic); street closures; temporary highway closings, transportation services
brief: A decision on temporary transit priority measures — parking and traffic changes — so the 506 Carlton streetcar can be rerouted while College Street and Carlton Street close for sewer and track work from late July to December 2026 goes to City Council. Regular streetcar operations through the area would be suspended during the project, with the 506 diverted around the construction zone and replacement bus service added. The measures include exempting TTC vehicles from left-turn restrictions and extending no-stopping and no-parking rules along diversion routes.

title: Ossington Avenue Safety and Streetscape Improvements
topics: lanes, road safety, sidewalks; traffic lanes; turn lanes; turning lanes
brief: City Council is set to decide whether to approve a redesign of Ossington Avenue between Dundas Street West and Queen Street West — bringing vehicle lane widths to current standards, expanding sidewalks and pedestrian space, and providing full-time parking. Staff say the narrow lanes fall short of minimum standards for emergency vehicles and buses, with high rates of improper passing and sideswiping, while the busy commercial strip's narrow sidewalks lack space for its high pedestrian volumes. The 2028 road resurfacing from Dundas to Argyle is the window to make the changes.

title: Oakwood Village Streets Plan - Non-Delegated Road Safety Improvements
topics: improvement, roads, safety; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), enhancement; rehabilitation (property), public safety
brief: The decision on whether to approve the road safety changes in the Oakwood Village Streets Plan that the community council cannot approve on its own, because Oakwood Avenue carries TTC service rests with City Council. The changes include a new pedestrian signal at Oakwood and Clovelly avenues, removal of an existing pedestrian crossover, and weekday morning and afternoon turn bans at Oakwood and Earnscliffe Road.

title: 564-576 Sherbourne Street and 29-37 Linden Street - Rental Housing Demolition - Amending Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, development, rental housing, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, developing land; development (land); land development, rental properties; rental units
brief: A decision on a revised rental housing demolition plan for 564-576 Sherbourne Street and 29-37 Linden Street: 23 rental units would be demolished and replaced with 25 rental units, and 23 existing rental rooms would be replaced with 20 studio units goes to City Council. The revision folds in 564 Sherbourne Street, with four more rental units and one room, following a minor variance application; the updated recommendations would replace the 2024 approval. The redevelopment would contain 716 residential units including the 45 replacement units. The approval carries a $20,000.00 financial condition.

title: 1095-1111 Danforth Avenue and 1117 Danforth Avenue - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, rental housing, road closures; building, rental properties; rental units, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: City Council decides whether to approve closing part of the south sidewalk, the eastbound bike lane, and the parking lane on Danforth Avenue for 35 months — from June 25, 2026 to April 30, 2029 — to build a 14-storey rental apartment at 1095-1111 and 1117 Danforth Avenue, with temporary pedestrian and bike lanes. Council approval is required because Danforth Avenue is a major arterial street. Six parking machine spaces on the south side, which charge $3.25 per hour, would be temporarily removed.

title: 307 Sherbourne Street - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
topics: community safety, construction, sidewalks, traffic regulations; building
brief: The decision on extending the construction-staging closure of the east sidewalk and cycle track on Sherbourne Street for eight more months — from June 25, 2026 to January 31, 2027 — for the 18-storey student residence at 307 Sherbourne Street rests with City Council. Only eight months were granted initially because a watermain replacement project was planned nearby; that project has now been delayed to March 2027.

title: 50 Richmond Street East - Construction Staging Area
topics: buildings, construction, road closures; building, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Approving closing the north sidewalk on Richmond Street East for 14 months — from June 25, 2026 to July 31, 2027 — for interior alterations at 50 Richmond Street East, with a temporary shared pedestrian and bike lane set up in the existing cycle track goes to City Council for a decision. Council approval is required because the TTC runs transit on Richmond Street East.

title: 374-390 Dupont Street - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning; bylaws, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: A decision on approving growing the approved project at 374-390 Dupont Street from 12 to 16 storeys, while reducing the commercial floor space from 1,000 to 810 square metres sits with City Council. An Official Plan change is needed for the extra height and the decrease in non-residential floor area. The owner would also be asked to make reasonable commercial efforts to find a suitable off-site parkland dedication as a substitute for the on-site requirement.

title: 914 Bathurst Street - Construction Staging Area
topics: condominium housing, construction, road closures; building, condominiums; condos, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: The decision on whether to let SD Bathurst Inc. close the west sidewalk and southbound curb lane on Bathurst Street, plus the north sidewalk on Barton Avenue, for 30 months — from May 31, 2026 to November 30, 2028 — to build a 12-storey condo at 914 Bathurst Street, with a temporary pedestrian walkway in the closed lane rests with City Council. Council approval is required because the TTC runs transit on Bathurst Street. The report also references a $2.00 fee amount.

title: Use of Nathan Phillips Square for Various Events - October 1, 2026 - April 30, 2027
topics: [activities in culture], [events in culture], development; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Eight event organizers — including city cultural productions, Breakthrough T1D, the Canada Running Series, and others — would get exemptions from the public square rules to use Nathan Phillips Square from October 2026 to April 2027, and to serve alcohol through Vintners Quality Alliance gardens under set conditions. City Council is asked to grant the permissions, contingent on approval from the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario and the Medical Officer of Health and compliance with the city's municipal alcohol policy.

title: 20 Gerrard Street East - Alterations of a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Whether to approve altering and removing some heritage features of the former Willard Hall building at 20 Gerrard Street East — owned by Covenant House Toronto and used as a social service facility for vulnerable populations — to allow a seven-storey building, and to enter into a heritage easement agreement now sits with City Council. The new building would support the site's ongoing use for transitional housing, wellness, education, employment, and community programs. Heritage staff are satisfied the proposal conserves the heritage properties.

title: 153 and 185 Eastern Avenue - Alterations to Designated Heritage Properties Under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: agreements, heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation, tenancy agreements
brief: City Council decides whether to approve alterations to two heritage-designated industrial buildings — the Cleaning Room building at 153 Eastern Avenue and the Machine Shop building at 185 Eastern Avenue, parts of the former Dominion Wheel and Foundries complex — and to enter into a heritage easement agreement. The alterations would support a development plan with three new residential towers plus commercial and community space. Heritage staff are satisfied the proposal conserves the properties.

title: 170 Merton Street - Demolition of a Heritage Attribute under Section 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: demolitions, development, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, developing land; development (land); land development, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Before City Council for a decision: approve removing the terrace of the heritage-designated former Visiting Homemakers Association building at 170 Merton Street — by careful deconstruction and salvage — and to amend the heritage easement agreement. The 1969 Late Modern building's terrace, a heritage attribute previously slated for in-situ conservation, would be demolished, reconstructed, and extended as part of the site's proposed 45-storey mixed-use redevelopment. Staff say the revised proposal continues to conserve the heritage property.

title: 291 Lake Shore Boulevard East, 2 Small Street and 200 Queens Quay East (Quayside Blocks 1B, 1C and 2) - City-initiated Zoning By-law Amendments - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, rezoning, zoning; bylaws, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Approving city-initiated zoning changes for Quayside Blocks 1B, 1C, and 2 to allow a new Toronto Public Library branch in the waterfront neighbourhood goes to City Council for a decision. The item also makes small technical fixes to elevator overrun and amenity space rules. The library zoning should only be enacted after City Council approves the related Executive Committee report on June 16, 2026.

title: 50 Park Road - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Refusal
topics: heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: City Council will weigh whether to refuse the heritage permit application for alterations to the heritage-designated 1954 building at 50 Park Road — the former Ontario Association of Architects headquarters, designed by John B. Parkin — for a proposed 31-storey mixed-use tower. The related planning application for 38, 40, and 50 Park Road is already before the Ontario Land Tribunal, and the city's solicitor would oppose any appeal of the refusal.

title: 150 College Street (Medical Sciences Building - 1 King's College Circle) - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter Into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: agreements, heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation, tenancy agreements
brief: City Council decides whether to approve alterations to the heritage-designated University of Toronto Medical Sciences Building at 150 College Street — constructed between 1966 and 1970 — in connection with rehabilitating the complex to support a nine-storey multipurpose building. The report also seeks approval to enter into a heritage easement agreement to ensure the long-term conservation of the designated property, which houses the Temerty Faculty of Medicine.

title: 81 Chestnut Park - Application to Erect a Structure in the South Rosedale Heritage Conservation District
topics: heritage conservation districts, structures; heritage districts; historic areas
brief: A new coach house-style dwelling would be built at 81 Chestnut Park in the South Rosedale Heritage Conservation District, and City Council is asked to approve the structure under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act. Heritage staff recommend approval: the design complements the larger home at 77 Chestnut Park that was once part of the same property, and its setback, height, and scale are compatible with the district's heritage buildings.

title: 40 Wabash Avenue - Alterations to and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Designated Heritage Property under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: demolitions, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Approving altering and removing some heritage features of the former Canada Linseed Oil Mills factory at 40 Wabash Avenue — a city-owned site built in phases from 1910 to the 1940s — to build a new community recreation centre, with a conservation plan to protect the heritage features comes before City Council. The vacant factory, featuring a prominent chimney stack visible from Dundas Street West, was approved for adaptive reuse in 2016 and sits beside Sorauren Avenue Park.

title: 1337 Queen Street West - Demolition and New Construction on a Designated Heritage Property under Part V, Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Approval
topics: demolitions, development, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Approving demolishing a non-contributing building at 1337 Queen Street West in the Parkdale Main Street Heritage Conservation District and building a 16-storey mixed-use replacement, under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act is on City Council's agenda. The work is the West Block of the city-led Parkdale Hub project, which is revitalizing city-owned facilities and expanding community services at Queen Street West and Cowan Avenue, including the Parkdale library branch and the Masaryk-Cowan Community Recreation Centre.

title: 257, 259 and 291 Lake Shore Boulevard East, 2 Small Street and 200 Queens Quay East (Quayside Blocks 1 and 2) - Urban Design Guidelines - Final Report
topics: building plans, urban design, zoning bylaws; building records, civic improvements, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Endorsing the urban design guidelines for Quayside Blocks 1 and 2 — at 257, 259, and 291 Lake Shore Boulevard East, 2 Small Street, and 200 Queens Quay East — on the waterfront heads to City Council for a decision. Endorsing the guidelines is required before site plan approval can proceed for the first development on the site, under the Section 37 agreement; the guidelines were developed by the applicant and accepted by staff.

title: 110-114 Maitland Street and 440 Jarvis Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, rental housing, residential properties, zoning bylaws; rental properties; rental units, residential real estate, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The applicant for a 56-storey mixed-use building at 110-114 Maitland Street and 440 Jarvis Street — 579 homes including 36 replacement rentals, plus 4,739 square metres of non-residential space — appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on March 30, 2026 after council missed its decision deadline. City Council is asked to direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose the application in its current form at the tribunal while continuing to negotiate with the applicant. A rental housing demolition application for the 36 existing rentals is also filed.

title: 206 Russell Hill Road - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, exemptions, part lot control; application process, exceptions
brief: The property at 206 Russell Hill Road would be split into four residential lots sharing a common-elements condominium with underground parking, and City Council is asked to exempt the lands from the Planning Act's part lot control rules for three years. The exemption would let the owner create the lots as parcels of tied land; proof of property tax payment and a no-transfer restriction are required before the by-law is introduced.

title: Liberty For All Regeneration Area Study - Final Report
topics: community development, employment opportunities, housing, official plan amendments; careers; employment; job applications; job boards; job openings; job opportunities; job postings; job vacancies; jobs; vacancies (jobs), community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development, homes; residences
brief: It's City Council's call whether to adopt Official Plan Amendment 914, a new vision for Liberty Village's growth as a transit-oriented complete community with both housing and jobs, consistent with provincial directives and the Official Plan. The plan addresses traffic congestion, requires new developments to increase the tree canopy and soft landscaping, and expands the area's road network with new public streets and wider landscaped sidewalks. It would require affordable housing in both condo and purpose-built rental projects, conserve heritage resources, and strongly discourage private vehicle travel while prioritizing transit and active transportation.

title: 1 to 7 Yonge Street, South Block - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The existing 25-storey office building at 1 to 7 Yonge Street would be converted into a hotel with 487 suites, and City Council is asked to approve the zoning amendment for the south block of the property. Staff describe the adaptive reuse of the building as an appropriate and efficient use of land that fits provincial policy and the Official Plan.

title: 221, 225 and 227 Sterling Road - Community Benefits Charge In-Kind Contribution
topics: community & life (sc), community benefits, donation; bequest; toy drive
brief: The developer of 221, 225, and 227 Sterling Road would hand over a 465-square-metre ground-floor community agency space to the city as its in-kind community benefits contribution. City Council is asked to accept the space, which represents 100 percent of the site's four-percent community benefits charge value under the city's by-law; the developer would design, build, and finish it to the city's satisfaction before the first condo registration.

title: 221, 225 and 227 Sterling Road - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, planning, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: City Council is set to decide whether to approve demolishing 56 rental units at 221, 225, and 227 Sterling Road. The owner must provide 58 replacement rental units — including 47 live-work units — protected for 20 years, with a tenant assistance plan for affected renters. The zoning for the site's three buildings (27, 24, and 21 storeys with 851 units total) was already approved by the Ontario Land Tribunal in 2023, and the approval carries a $20,000.00 financial condition.

title: 9 Drumsnab Road - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property in the South Rosedale Heritage Conservation District - Refusal
topics: community councils, heritage preservation, heritage properties, planning; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff are asking City Council to refuse a request to replace the original windows and enlarge the entryway of the heritage-designated home at 9 Drumsnab Road, a 'B-rated' property in the South Rosedale Heritage Conservation District. The proposal — new windows plus larger sidelights, transom window, and door opening — does not comply with the district plan, national conservation standards, or the Official Plan, according to the report. If the owner appeals, council would send the City Solicitor to oppose the appeal at the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: 136 St Germain Ave - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 26 142355 PRS 00 IV
topics: downspouts, municipal codes, property standards;
brief: This is a procedural item: an appeal of the property standards order for 136 St Germain Avenue goes before the Property Standards Committee. The order was issued April 10, 2026 (file 26 142355 PRS 00 IV). The committee will decide whether the order stands, changes, or is cancelled.

title: 75 Havenbrook Blvd- Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 26 129063 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee will hear the property owner's appeal of a property standards order issued March 17, 2026 for 75 Havenbrook Boulevard (file 26 129063 PRS 00 IV). The committee can confirm, change, or cancel the order. The hearing gives the owner a chance to challenge the city's maintenance or repair requirements.

title: 31-35 St. Dennis Drive - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 26 109199 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the owner of 31-35 St. Dennis Drive is appealing a property standards order issued March 30, 2026 (file 26 109199 PRS 00 IV) to the Property Standards Committee. The committee hears the appeal and can uphold, amend, or rescind the order.

title: 27 Pondsview Drive - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number:  26 138402 PRS 00 IV
topics: catchbasins, municipal codes, property standards; catch basins; catch-basins
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee received an appeal letter dated April 15, 2026 for 27 Pondsview Drive (file 26 138402 PRS 00 IV). The committee will hear the owner's appeal of the property standards order and can uphold, amend, or rescind it.

title: 25 Pondsview Drive - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 26 138055 PRS 00 IV
topics: catchbasins, municipal codes, property standards; catch basins; catch-basins
brief: This is a procedural item: an appeal of the property standards order for 25 Pondsview Drive goes before the Property Standards Committee. The order was issued April 1, 2026 (file 26 138055 PRS 00 IV). The committee will decide whether the order stands, changes, or is cancelled.

title: 18 Cameron Avenue  - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 26 136821 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee will hear the property owner's appeal of a property standards order issued April 1, 2026 for 18 Cameron Avenue (file 26 136821 PRS 00 IV). The committee can confirm, change, or cancel the order. The hearing gives the owner a chance to challenge the city's maintenance or repair requirements.

title: Guildwood Village Neighbourhood Character Guidelines
topics: community development, zoning designations; community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development, permitted use requests; permitted uses
brief: Guildwood Village Neighbourhood Character Guidelines, which set out the desired architectural character and design principles for development in the Guildwood community, go to City Council for adoption. The guidelines follow a December 17, 2024 council direction to review development rules in the area. If adopted, they would shape how future buildings in Guildwood Village look.

title: 1215 to 1255 McCowan Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend refusing a proposal for three residential towers of 25, 45, and 55 storeys with 1,412 homes and ground-floor retail at 1215 to 1255 McCowan Road. The proposal covers 117,913 square metres of floor area (including 4,810 square metres of retail), a floor space index of 6.42, and 1,446 parking spaces mostly in a three-level underground garage. City Council will decide whether the application is refused.

title: Formerly 95 Pidgeon Street (Blocks 1-3 of Plan 66M-2562) - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: exemptions, part lot control, townhouses; exceptions
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is asked to exempt Blocks 1, 2, and 3 of Plan 66M-2562 (95 Pidgeon Street) from the Planning Act's part lot control rules, which would allow the creation of 26 three-storey townhouse units, eight of them as parcels of tied land in a common elements condominium. Staff call the exemption appropriate for the orderly development of the lands. It is a legal step that lets the townhouse lots be created.

title: Renaming of a Portion of Zoo Road
topics: naming, street names; renaming; road names; street naming
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie is asking City Council to waive Section 6 of the Street Naming Policy and approve 'Rouge National Urban Park Road' as the name for a portion of Zoo Road. The proposal is tied to Rouge National Urban Park's growth, including its upcoming $20 million Visitor, Learning and Community Centre, set to open in 2027.

title: Bellamy Road North and Danforth Road - Traffic Safety Improvements
topics: safety, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, public safety
brief: Safety improvements are proposed for Bellamy Road North and Danforth Road as part of the Eglinton-Bendale South Neighbourhood Streets Plan, which studied speeding and the safety of pedestrians and other vulnerable road users after community consultation. A May 11, 2026 report outlines the recommended changes. Because the TTC operates on both roads, City Council must vote on it.

title: 468 to 480 Danforth Road and 509 Birchmount Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, mixed use areas, rezoning; developing land; development (land); land development, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: A 14-storey mixed-use building with 526 homes and 1,563 square metres of ground-floor retail is proposed for 468 to 480 Danforth Road and 509 Birchmount Road. Staff recommend approval, noting about 754 square metres of on-site parkland dedication that would expand the adjacent Sadler Parkette. City Council will decide, and the project would add significant new housing near Danforth Road.

title: Orton Park Road - Parking and Traffic Amendments
topics: change, parking, traffic; amendments; conversion; modification, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: Several turn restrictions are proposed in front of George B. Little Public School on Orton Park Road at Brimorton Drive: no northbound or southbound U-turns on Orton Park Road in front of the school, and no westbound left turns or through moves from the school's driveway just north of Brimorton Drive. Staff say the changes would improve traffic flow and safety for students and other road users. Because the TTC operates on Orton Park Road, City Council must vote on it.

title: Ellesmere Road and Crocus Drive/Dewey Drive - Traffic Control Signals
topics: assessment, traffic control systems; traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: No traffic signals are recommended for Ellesmere Road at Crocus Drive and Dewey Drive, because the assessment found the city's warrant criteria were not met. Staff ask City Council not to authorize the installation. Because the TTC operates on Ellesmere Road, City Council's approval is required for any change at this intersection.

title: Kingston Road and Blantyre Avenue - Traffic Control Signals and Parking Amendments
topics: change, traffic control systems, traffic signals; amendments; conversion; modification, fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Traffic signals are proposed for the intersection of Kingston Road and Blantyre Avenue, replacing the existing pedestrian refuge island about 95 metres west of the intersection. Staff acknowledge the usual traffic-volume warrants were not met but say signals would protect pedestrians better, since the island does not give them enough protection. Because the TTC runs transit on Kingston Road, City Council must vote on the change, and a related parking amendment adjusts the pay-and-display machine rules that charge $3.25 per hour on Kingston Road.

title: 1650 Military Trail (Phase 1) - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, rental housing, students; building, rental properties; rental units
brief: City Council will decide whether to authorize boulevard and lane closures on Morrish Road for Phase 1 of construction at 1650 Military Trail, where Altree Developments is building an 8-storey purpose-built student rental at the northwest corner of Military Trail and Morrish Road. Phase 1 covers shoring and excavation, with building construction to follow in Phase 2. Because Morrish Road is a collector street, City Council approval is required. The closures would support construction of student rental housing.

title: 777 Victoria Park Avenue - Construction Staging Area
topics: [activities in property], affordable housing, construction, rental housing; affordable homes; housing projects, building, rental properties; rental units
brief: City Council will decide whether to authorize temporary road and sidewalk closures on Victoria Park Avenue for construction staging at 777 Victoria Park Avenue, where a 36-storey rental tower and a 12-storey affordable housing tower are being built at the northeast corner of Victoria Park and Denton Avenues. Transportation Services wants to temporarily close the east sidewalk and part of the northbound lane, plus the north sidewalk and part of an adjacent roadway. Because the TTC operates on Victoria Park Avenue, City Council approval is required. The closures would support construction of rental and affordable homes.
