title: 5, 7, 9 and 11 Bellamy Road South - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, townhouses; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: City Council votes on approving a zoning amendment for 5, 7, 9, and 11 Bellamy Road South that would allow three blocks of four-storey stacked and back-to-back townhouses with 110 homes. The mix includes 3 two-bedroom, 60 three-bedroom, and 47 four-bedroom units, with 14,100 square metres of floor area for a density of 1.85 times the site area. The project would add family-sized townhouse homes in the area.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council reviews the Order Paper, the list of business before it. No decision is involved beyond organizing the meeting's work.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions, and announcements are made at the council meeting. No decision is involved.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: council members may file petitions at the meeting. No decision is involved.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: council members declare any interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act before business begins. No policy decision is involved.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports, New Business and Business Previously Requested from City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council formally introduces the committee reports coming forward to this meeting, including reports from the Executive Committee, Board of Health, Civic Appointments Committee, Economic and Community Development Committee, and General Government Committee. The item sets the agenda for what council will consider. No decision is made at this step.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council confirms the minutes from its regular meeting of May 20 and 21, 2026. No policy decision is involved.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council opens its meeting with O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is involved.

title: Authority to Enter into Municipal Housing Project Facility Agreements with Community Housing Providers
topics: housing providers, supportive housing; alternative housing; special needs housing; supported housing, community housing corporations
brief: Property tax exemptions are proposed for affordable homes at three co-operative housing sites and two Toronto Community Housing properties. City Council is asked to authorize municipal housing project facility agreements with the community housing providers, which would help keep rents affordable. The move advances the city's HousingTO plan and the community housing modernization strategy council adopted in June 2024.

title: Preserving Affordable Homes at 38 Abell Street and 210 Simcoe Streets
topics: affordable housing, housing; affordable homes; housing projects, homes; residences
brief: Affordable homes and arts spaces at 38 Abell Street and 210 Simcoe Street are being secured after the insolvency of non-profit operator Artscape, which announced in August 2023 that its assets would be sold by a court-appointed receiver. City Council is asked to approve long-term nominal leases with a new operator so the city-owned affordable housing units are preserved. The move follows council's direction to protect the city's affordable housing interests in the receivership.

title: Toronto Local Appeal Body - Chair's 2025 Annual Report
topics: appeals, courts;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Planning and Housing Committee is asked to receive the Toronto Local Appeal Body Chair's 2025 annual report for information. The TLAB is the independent tribunal that hears appeals of Committee of Adjustment decisions on minor variances and consents. No policy change is proposed.

title: Amendment to Municipal Code Chapter 27 (Council Procedures) and Municipal Code Chapter 925 (Permit Parking): Streamlining Permit Parking Exclusions for New Developments
topics: municipal codes, permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: New developments would be shut out of on-street permit parking under a rule change implementing council's 2021 direction. City Council is asked to amend the Council Procedures and Permit Parking chapters so residents, visitors, and tradespeople at new developments are excluded from residential on-street permit parking eligibility. The change would also keep decisions on these exclusions with full council rather than community councils.

title: Toronto Builds: 40 Bushby Drive - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Three residential towers of 44 to 59 storeys are proposed at 40 Bushby Drive in Scarborough, with at least 1,000 square metres of non-residential space. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes, which would remove the requirement for a public street in the Scarborough Secondary Plan and protect for outcomes of the Scarborough Rapid Transit Future Use Initiative.

title: Housing Action Plan: Incorporating Low-rise Residential Lands into Zoning By-law 569-2013 -   Scarborough District - Final Report
topics: low rise buildings, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Scarborough's low-rise residential lands would be folded into the city-wide Zoning By-law 569-2013 in the fourth phase of a cleanup project. City Council is asked to approve the zoning amendment, aligning local standards with former municipal rules and recent city-wide changes. Staff say the move removes barriers, simplifies administration, and supports more housing under the Housing Action Plan.

title: Zoning for Low-Carbon Technologies - Final Report
topics: [activities in science and technology], rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Installing heat pumps, solar panels, energy storage, and electric vehicle chargers could get easier under proposed zoning changes. City Council is asked to approve the Zoning for Low-Carbon Technologies final report, which modernizes the city-wide zoning by-law to support the Official Plan and the TransformTO climate strategy. The changes contribute to the city's goal of net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2040.

title: 328 Bellamy Road North - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The John Perryman (J.P.) Wheler House at 328 Bellamy Road North in Scarborough's Golfdale-Cedarbrae-Woburn area is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The house sits on the west side of Bellamy Road North, south of Lawrence Avenue East.

title: 34 Jason Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The Elm Bank Piggery property at 34 Jason Road in Etobicoke's Thistletown community is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The property sits on the north side of Jason Road at Riverdale Drive and traces its roots to a 19th-century farm property.

title: 4150 Yonge Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The John Street Workers Cottages at 4150 Yonge Street in North York's Bedford Park-Nortown neighbourhood are proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The cottages sit on the west side of Yonge Street north of Wilson Avenue.

title: 339 Queen Street East - Proposed Amendment to Designating By-law under Part IV, Section 30.1 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The heritage designation for 339 Queen Street East would be updated to say more about why the building matters. City Council is asked to amend the reasons for designation in the 2017 designating by-law to reference Cecil B. Tadman's nearly 50-year ownership through the Home Furniture Company Limited, to clarify its value as a Chicago School style example, and to note its historic post-and-beam timber frame. The change enriches the record without altering the property's protected status.

title: Humber Bay Shores, Christie's Redevelopment and Park Lawn GO Station
topics: public transit, transit networks; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is asked to receive for information a report on tools to support Humber Bay Shores as a complete community with access to higher-order transit. The report follows council's November 2025 direction and covers options including holding provisions, plus planned community facilities such as a recreation centre, library, childcare, agency space, and schools tied to the Christie's redevelopment and Park Lawn GO Station. No policy change is proposed.

title: 2600 Don Mills Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal Report
topics: construction, demolitions, planning & development (sc), residential properties, zoning bylaws; building, residential real estate, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Applications for four residential buildings at 2600 Don Mills Road — three at 42 storeys (140.50 metres) and one at 47 storeys (155.25 metres), with 1,814 units in a two-phase plan — were deemed complete in August 2025; a related rental demolition application would remove a 19-storey building with 226 rental units. The applications were appealed on February 27, 2026, and staff's appeal report sets out the City's position for the decision-maker.

title: 844 Don Mills Road and 1150 Eglinton Avenue East (Block 8) - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, exemptions, planning approvals, properties (real estate), townhouses; developing land; development (land); land development, development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals, exceptions, property; real estate
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve exempting 844 Don Mills Road and 1150 Eglinton Avenue East (Block 8) from part-lot-control rules so eighty townhouse units can be created as conveyable lots, with a 6.40-metre private laneway as the common-elements parcel. The exemption is the legal step that lets each townhouse be sold separately.

title: 2673-2675 Bayview Avenue - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: construction, exemptions, planning, properties (real estate), townhouses; building, exceptions, property; real estate
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve exempting 2673-2675 Bayview Avenue from part-lot-control rules so ten townhouse units — eight townhouse units and two detached dwellings — can be created as conveyable lots, along with a private driveway, mail box, water and stormwater parcels. The exemption is the legal step that lets each home be sold separately.

title: 235 Wicksteed Avenue - Temporary Use Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: approval, offices, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a temporary zoning change to allow a portable concrete batching plant and office trailer at 235 Wicksteed Avenue for up to three years. The Director of Community Planning for North York District recommends amending Zoning By-law 569-2013 for the site. The temporary use supports nearby construction activity.

title: 7 St. Dennis Drive - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction permits (right-of-way), permits, road closures, street occupation permits; curb cut permits; driveway paving permits; driveway resurfacing permits; driveway widening permits; landscaping permits (right-if way), curblane permits; road use permits; street closure permits; streets and sidewalks, permit renewal, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Osmington Gerofsky Development Corp, is building a 37-storey residential building at 7 St. Dennis Drive, between Don Mills Road and Deauville Lane. Transportation Services wants authorization to temporarily close the south sidewalk, part of the eastbound bicycle lane and part of the eastbound traffic lane for 25 months — September 1, 2026 to September 30, 2028 — for construction. Because St. Dennis Drive is a collector street, City Council must vote on it. The closure affects pedestrians, cyclists and drivers on the street for over two years.

title: Don Mills Regeneration Area Study - Final Report
topics: avenue study, planning, urban design, urban form, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, civic improvements, streetscapes; urban landscape
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve two Official Plan Amendments setting a renewed vision for the Don Mills Regeneration Areas — the Leslie Site (1121 and 1123 Leslie Street) and the Wynford-Gervais Site (15 Gervais Drive, 39 Wynford Drive and 1200 Eglinton Avenue East) — shifting them from employment uses to new mixed-use communities. The frameworks support transit-oriented communities leveraging the Eglinton Crosstown LRT. The amendments shape future housing and jobs on both sites.

title: Hollyhock Court, Mattamy (North York) Limited - Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2567
topics: assumption of services, municipal services, properties (real estate), subdivision (land); city services, property; real estate, subdivision of land
brief: Staff recommend City Council assume the municipal services installed by Mattamy (North York) Limited under a July 9, 2019 subdivision agreement for Plan of Subdivision 66M-2567 at Hollyhock Court, and release the performance guarantee held for those services. Assumption means the City takes over maintenance of the infrastructure.

title: 80 Carl Hall Road, North York -  Assumption of Services, Registered Plans 66M-2520, Stanley Greene Subdivision
topics: agreements, assumption of services, development review process; development control; development reviews, tenancy agreements
brief: Staff recommend City Council assume the municipal services installed by Parc Downsview Park Inc. under a January 13, 2015 subdivision agreement for Plan of Subdivision 66M-2520 at 80 Carl Hall Road — including about 117 metres of 450-millimetre sanitary sewer outside the plan — and release the performance guarantee. Assumption means the City takes over maintenance of the infrastructure.

title: 75-81 Billy Bishop Way - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal Report
topics: Official Plans, appeals, official plan amendments, planning, rezoning, urban planning, zoning bylaws; city planning; community planning; regional planning, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff have prepared an appeal report on the application for five tall buildings ranging from 21 to 49 storeys (83.6 to 164.1 metres) with 2,055 dwelling units at 75-81 Billy Bishop Way — deemed complete in July 2025, with about 149,161 square metres of residential space and 2,493 square metres of non-residential space in three blocks with 6-storey base buildings. The report sets out the City's position on the appealed application for the decision-maker.

title: Expanding Recreational Programming for Toronto’s Seniors  - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: seniors; elderly; geriatric; older adults; senior citizens
brief: The item asks council to have Parks and Recreation review demand for free and low-cost older adult recreation programs and report back in the second quarter of 2027 with opportunities to add or enhance offerings like yoga, aquafit and art classes. The motion says demand for senior recreation spots far exceeds supply and that expanding programs supports aging in place with dignity as Toronto's population ages. No dollar figure is attached.

title: First Impressions Matter: Exploring Opportunities to Improve Grass Cutting in the City - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
topics: turf maintenance; grass cutting; grass repairs
brief: The item asks council to have Transportation Services review grass-cutting schedules in existing contracts and adjust them where feasible for varying growth through spring, summer and fall. The motion argues that overgrown boulevards and main-road green spaces detract from the city's appearance for residents and the millions of tourists Toronto receives, especially during the April-to-June peak growing season. No dollar figure is attached.

title: Authority to Accept an In-Kind Donation and Enter into an Agreement for Baseball Diamond Improvements at Stan Wadlow Park - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: baseball diamonds, donation, recreation & tourism (sc); ball diamonds; baseball fields; hardball diamonds, bequest; toy drive
brief: The item asks council to accept an in-kind donation worth up to $100,000 ($0.100 million) from the East York Baseball Association, funded by the Jays Care Foundation, for improvements at Stan Wadlow Park's baseball diamonds at 888 Cosburn Avenue. The work covers lighting upgrades for Diamonds 1 and 2 and infield grading and restoration at Diamond 2 to support children's community baseball. Council authority is required because the donation exceeds the $50,000 threshold in the city's Donation Policy.

title: Advancing Planting and Sand Renourishment at Hanlan’s Point Beach and Surrounding Area - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to direct Parks and Recreation and Environment, Climate and Forestry to carry out the immediate actions of the Hanlan's Point Landscape Plan by October 2026: at least 10,000 square metres of planting and naturalization, with analysis toward up to 20,000 square metres, plus sand renourishment. The motion notes Hanlan's Point Beach is Canada's oldest surviving queer space and the site of Canada's first Gay Pride gathering, and that erosion, dune degradation and beach loss threaten its cultural and ecological value. The source lists a $400,000 figure in connection with the work.

title: Advancing Work on the Wellington Destructor - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to advance work on the Wellington Destructor, the former incinerator identified as a city-building opportunity for the growing Niagara neighbourhood alongside two forthcoming parks at 801 Wellington Street West and 10 Ordnance Street. Community engagement since 2017 envisioned non-profit programming and market activations, and CreateTO has since assessed the building's condition and explored temporary uses after a contract termination. The motion directs Corporate Real Estate Management to complete redevelopment analysis and plan the next round of community engagement.

title: Sewer Access Hole for 353 to 357 College Street - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
brief: The item asks council to have Toronto Water report directly to the July 29-31, 2026 meeting on sewer access compliance for the hostel expansion at 353 to 357 College Street. A city error meant the zoning and site plan approvals let the hostel's small business expand into an adjacent vacant lot without the necessary sewer access hole, so the approved building can only proceed if the access hole is placed in the sidewalk, normally contrary to the Municipal Code. The matter is urgent because the small-business redevelopment of the derelict lot is ready but blocked.

title: Can the Standard Theatre be Restored to Use as a Music Venue? - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: redevelopment; rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: The item asks council to have staff report by July 29-31, 2026 on whether the vacant Standard Theatre at 285 Spadina Avenue, at Dundas Street, could be restored as a live music venue. The 1921 theatre, built for live Yiddish theatre and designed by Benjamin Brown, one of Toronto's first Jewish architects, has sat vacant since 1975 and may still have good acoustics. The motion notes Toronto is short of live music venues and says there may be a short-term chance to relocate an existing cultural venue there at a reasonable price.

title: Advancing a Redevelopment Strategy for the Toronto Builds site at 770 Don Mills Road - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: light rail transit, redevelopment; lrt, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow is asking council to direct CreateTO to advance a redevelopment strategy for the city-owned Toronto Builds site at 770 Don Mills Road, a surface parking lot steps from the Crosstown's new Don Valley Station and the Ontario Line. CreateTO has begun early planning for a transit-oriented, mixed-income development including an elementary school, park space, retail, childcare and market and affordable housing, with possible additions like community space or a long-term care home. The motion is urgent to get direction before the council recess.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Macklin Garden Project - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: gardens, improvement; enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: The item asks council to release $9,000.00 ($9,000) in Section 37 community benefits for a small garden project, Macklin Garden, in Ward 16, Don Valley East. The money comes from the development at 39 Green Belt Drive, collected for neighbourhood park improvements. The motion creates a new capital sub-project at $9,000 gross and $0 debt in 2026.

title: Temporary Delegation of Authorities Required for the Church Street Pedestrianization Pilot - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: pedestrian infrastructure, pedestrian walkways; footpaths; pedestrian ways; walking paths; walkways, pedestrian network
brief: This is a procedural item: The item asks council to temporarily delegate traffic-management authority to the General Manager of Transportation Services for the Church Street Pedestrianization Pilot, running June 26 to August 22. The pilot closes Church Street to vehicles with an unobstructed central emergency lane and businesses extending patios into the curb lane with one-metre clearance zones for mobility devices and wheelchairs. Delegation would let staff make real-time adjustments to optimize an accessible streetscape while the pilot is underway.

title: Yonge North Subway Extension Steeles Station Design and Construction Impact Mitigation: Passenger Pick-Up and Drop-Off and Pest Management - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: subway trains;
brief: The item asks council to press for better design and construction-impact handling around the Yonge North Subway Extension's future Steeles Station. The motion seeks dedicated passenger pick-up and drop-off infrastructure in the station design to avoid the congestion seen around Sheppard Station, and asks Metrolinx to develop a comprehensive pest management plan for the construction period, including supports for residents affected by rodent activity near the works. It frames both as matters of long-term functionality and community wellbeing.

title: Amending Item 2022.CC39.7 - 10-32 Raglan Avenue - Amendment of Section 37 Agreement to Facilitate a Seniors’ Housing Facility - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: agreements, seniors housing; tenancy agreements
brief: This is a procedural item: The item asks council to amend the 2022 Section 37 agreement for 10-32 Raglan Avenue, a 97.5-metre, 28-storey mixed-use building, to facilitate a seniors' housing facility. The existing agreement secured a community agency space, a new on-site public park, roadway and bike share funds, laneway lighting, micro retail, live/work units and at least ten percent three-bedroom units. The motion adjusts those community benefits to accommodate the seniors' housing use. The motion also lists $1 as an additional listed figure.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2025.TE24.2 340 to 376R Dufferin Street and 2 Melbourne Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: The item asks council to reopen its July 2025 approval for the development at 340 to 376R Dufferin Street and 2 Melbourne Avenue so the zoning by-law can be adjusted for minor owner-requested changes enabling phased delivery. The preconditions for introducing the bills have been met, and the motion swaps the referenced attachment in the earlier decision. The matter is urgent because bills delivered in June keep the adjustment within one year of the July 2025 decision and add flexibility for housing delivery.

title: Recognition, Restoration, and Expansion of The AIDS Memorial (Toronto) - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: Human Papillomavirus, memorials; hpv; papillomavirus infections, monuments; permanent memorials
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow is asking council to recognize, restore and expand The AIDS Memorial (Toronto) in Barbara Hall Park in Church-Wellesley Village, a living memorial established in 1988 and made permanent in 1993 that centres the names of people who died of AIDS. More than 21,000 Canadians have died of AIDS-related illness and more than 65,000 people in Canada are living with HIV, with the impact borne especially by communities facing stigma including gay and bisexual men, trans people, African, Caribbean and Black, Indigenous, sex worker, drug user, incarcerated, newcomer and migrant communities. The motion treats the memorial as a civic site of national significance whose grief, history and activism span every ward.

title: Extending the Permit for a Seasonal Outdoor Patio at 460 Adelaide Street East - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: The item asks council to extend the seasonal outdoor patio at 460 Adelaide Street East, operating on a portion of the privately owned publicly-accessible space at 424-460 Adelaide Street East, until October 15, 2027. Council granted the temporary patio in 2024 with an expiry of October 15, 2025 to test the impacts, and staff report no observed negative effects. The extension is urgent because the 2026 patio season is already underway.

title: Improving Public Access at Birchmount Stadium - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: stadiums; sports stadiums
brief: The item asks council to have staff explore expanding public access to Birchmount Stadium, the premier publicly funded track-and-field facility in Scarborough upgraded as part of a $206 million sport infrastructure investment for the 2015 Pan Am Games. Use is currently limited to school students on weekday school hours, heavy athletic-group permits evenings and weekends, and summer-only weekday-morning drop-in, with residents and clubs saying the permit structure leaves the track underused. The motion asks staff to review the Toronto District School Board agreement, introduce a multi-use permitting model and expand drop-in windows beyond summer.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Investing in Birch Cliff Village with a Review of Streetscape Enhancements - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: The item asks council to release $30,000 in Section 37 funds to review streetscape enhancements for Birch Cliff Village, the historic Scarborough main street along Kingston Road between Warden Avenue and Birchmount Road. Recent infrastructure and roadwork have strained local businesses, and the motion says strategic investment in gateway and placemaking features would strengthen the corridor's identity and support recovery. The item is urgent to align with current and planned Transportation Services work in the area.

title: Partial Reimbursement of Permit Fees for Toronto Music, Arts and Nature Alliance - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: cultural facilities; art centres; arts centres; cultural attractions; cultural centres
brief: The item asks council to approve a further partial reimbursement of permit fees for the Toronto Music, Arts and Nature Alliance, the non-profit behind the 25-year Promise Cherry Beach summer event series. In 2024 the emergency closure of the Cherry Street bridge cut attendance roughly in half, and council already refunded 25 percent of that year's $60,150.66 in fees, totalling $13,319.51, leaving $46,831.15 outstanding. This motion seeks an additional reimbursement, with the source listing $28,098.69 as the figure for the further payment. The source also lists $1,000 as an additional listed figure.

title: Support for Théâtre français de Toronto - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: theatres (facilities); auditorium; performance spaces; performing arts centres; performing arts facilities
brief: The item asks council to explore how the city can support Théâtre français de Toronto's long-standing project to build a permanent venue for French-language theatre, with construction scheduled to begin within weeks. The company has been a pillar of Toronto's Francophone cultural life for nearly 60 years as the city's only professional French-language theatre, drawing nearly 12,000 audience members a season with surtitles for non-Francophones; 71 Franco-Ontarian organizations have backed the need for a permanent home. Federal support has been secured but is not enough to complete the project. The source cites $3 million in connection with the support request.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Mallow Park Lighting Improvements - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: improvement, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: The item asks council to release $150,000 in Section 37 community benefits for the design and installation of park lighting and associated infrastructure at Mallow Park in Ward 16, Don Valley East. The money is drawn from two source accounts: $60,072 from the 15 Mallow Road development fund and $89,928 from the 905 Don Mills Road development fund. The motion creates a new Mallow Park Lighting Improvements capital sub-project at $150,000 gross and $0 debt in 2026.

title: 447 Horsham Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: appeals;
brief: This is a procedural item: Council authorizes the City Solicitor to appeal the Committee of Adjustment's approval of a three-storey, six-unit apartment building at 447 Horsham Avenue to the Toronto Local Appeal Body and resolve the matter for the city. The applicant had originally also sought a two-storey rear garden suite but removed it before the June 4, 2026 hearing, reducing the variances to six covering setbacks, height and platform encroachments. The motion is urgent because the appeal deadline of June 24, 2026 required the solicitor to file to preserve the city's rights.

title: Referral of Urgent Laneway Naming to the Toronto and East York Community Council: Public Lane South of St. Clair Avenue West - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: The item asks council to refer the urgent naming of the public lane south of St. Clair Avenue West, off Ellsworth Avenue, to the July 8 and 9, 2026 Toronto and East York Community Council meeting as Aren Levy Lane. The lane honours Aren Levy, who owned and operated the Levy's family clothing store at 541 St. Clair West for over 30 years, with the lane as his primary shipments access; the store once grew to three locations and was cited in media as a competitor to major retailers. His son consented and a community petition shows support; the motion is urgent because the submission deadline has passed and this is the last opportunity in the current council term.

title: Authority to Enter into Agreements to Facilitate the Implementation of FIFA World Cup 2026 Indigenous Legacy Initiatives - by Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: recreation & tourism (sc), soccer;
brief: The item asks council to authorize the FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto executive director to negotiate and enter agreements so the approved Indigenous Legacy Initiatives can be implemented immediately. An Indigenous Advisory Body was established in line with Call to Action 91, with funding set aside within the Secretariat's budget and no impact on the $380.0 million gross budget for the tournament. The initiatives aim to make sure hosting benefits reach Indigenous communities across the city.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2026.TE32.25 - Spadina Road, between Lowther Avenue and Kendal Avenue - Toronto Transit Commission Subway Ventilation Equipment Replacement - Construction Staging Area - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: public transit, transit networks; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: This is a procedural item: reopening and amending its May 2026 approval for the TTC's Spadina Road subway ventilation equipment replacement between Lowther Avenue and Kendal Avenue, adopting a revised construction staging area and schedule, would get Council's approval. The TTC needs temporary street-level access to the centre-of-road ventilation shafts at Spadina Station on Line 1 to replace end-of-life equipment, in a corridor already disrupted for years by the station's accessibility construction. The previously approved single-phase plan closed northbound and southbound through lanes; the motion revises the staging approach. The motion also lists $2.00, $5.75 and $5 as additional listed figures.

title: Supporting Local Arts and Culture Organizations in Ward 10 - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: art programs, arts and culture; art classes; art workshops; arts programs
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to support local arts and culture organizations in Ward 10 that are being displaced or need affordable, accessible space. The motion notes groups like Bygone Theatre and On Task Studios have lost their homes, Cinecycle needs accessibility work for its laneway venue, and IATSE Local 58 seeks downtown training space for live-performance workers. Engagement since 2022 fed into the Culture Connects Plan in 2024, and the motion aims to secure space, leverage opportunities and investigate support for underserved sectors.

title: Reducing Development Charges in Partnership with the Provincial and Federal Governments - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: funding, intergovernmental relations; federal-municipal relations; governmental relations; inter-governmental relations; intergovernmental cooperation; provincial-municipal relations, financing
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow is asking council to endorse the deal announced June 23, 2026 in which the province provides $1.5 billion over ten years through the Development Charge Reduction Program, funded via the Canada-Ontario Partnership to Build, to pay for major infrastructure in the city's 10-year capital plan instead of collecting it from residential homebuyers. The program would cut residential development charges by 40 to 60 percent for three years, with deeper 60 percent discounts for two-bedroom-plus units to encourage family housing. The city says the investments would generate an estimated 143,000 jobs, and the source also cites $1.2 billion in additional financial contributions.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds for Advancing Playground Improvements at Trinity Bellwoods Park - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: improvement, playgrounds; adventure playgrounds; indoor playgrounds; playground structures, enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to release $1,100,000 ($1.1 million) in Section 42 funds for playground replacement and improvements at Trinity Bellwoods Park, following community consultation that found new equipment, surfacing, added features and repairs are needed. The money comes from developments at 107 Bathurst Street, 431 Richmond Street West and 621 King Street West in Ward 10, split as $459,989, $465,600 and $174,410 across three source accounts. The motion is urgent so design consultations can start this summer.

title: 537 Kennedy Road - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza
topics: appeals, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This is a procedural item: Authorizing the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body over the refused garden suite variances at 537 Kennedy Road is up for a decision by Council. The structure was built without permits in 2014, and the applicant has repeatedly revised the application since 2021; the Scarborough Committee of Adjustment panel refused the variances on April 14, 2026 over setbacks, height and gross floor area. Planning staff concluded the proposal does not meet the intent of the city's garden suite framework.

title: Safer Access to Transit: Building a Pedestrian Connection from Stephenson Avenue to the Danforth GO Platform - Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Study and Design - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: trains;
brief: The item asks council to release $250,000 in Section 37 funds to study and design a safer, direct pedestrian connection from Stephenson Avenue to the Danforth GO platform, where west-side access currently means multiple stairs, poor lighting and busy traffic on Main Street's east side. The motion directs Transportation Services, with Metrolinx and adjacent landowners, to complete a feasibility study and initial design for the walkway. The $250,000 is drawn from three source accounts: $76,668.18, $76,408.29 and $96,923.53.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2026.PH30.2 Toronto Builds: 970 Kipling Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: The item asks council to reopen and amend its May 2026 approval for the Toronto Builds housing project at 970 Kipling Avenue so the developer can be credited for above-base park improvements. The selected proponent will deliver a 2,193-square-metre portion of the site in base park condition for Parks and Recreation to maintain, and wants to complete the above-base improvements before the first building occupancy since some units will front onto the parkland. The motion would authorize a development-charge credit for the parks component covering that design and construction work, ahead of finalizing the ground lease and project agreement.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds to the Gulliver Park Play Enhancement Project - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: improvement, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: The item asks council to release $40,000 in Section 42 funds, secured from the 2175 Keele Street development in Ward 5, to the Gulliver Park Play Enhancement project. The motion amends the 2026-2035 parks capital budget on a one-time basis by $40,000 gross and $0 debt in 2026 for park improvements at Gulliver Park. The funds come from source account XR2213-4201601.

title: Creating a Pedestrian Streets Program for Toronto - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: pedestrian infrastructure, pedestrians, walking; pedestrian network, pedestrianization
brief: The item asks council to create a citywide Pedestrian Streets Program identifying candidate streets for seasonal and year-round pedestrianization next year, building on the Church Street pilot council approved in May 2026. The motion cites the popularity of Toronto street festivals and an April 2026 destination master plan finding that Toronto lags peer cities in walkability, while noting Transportation Services' pedestrian streets policy work has slipped past its original December 2025 target. Staff would broaden the scope and accelerate the policy into a program.

title: North York Pedestrian Tunnel - Request for Safety and Accessibility Review - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: accessibility, pedestrian infrastructure, safety; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, pedestrian network, public safety
brief: The item asks council to order a safety and accessibility review of the North York Pedestrian Tunnel, the city-owned underground link between Yonge Sheppard Centre at 4841 Yonge Street and the Service Canada building at 4900 Yonge Street. Local residents, including seniors who rely on the tunnel, have raised concerns about safety and accessibility. The motion asks Corporate Real Estate Management, with Transportation Services, to report before the 2027 budget process on a workplan and budget covering structural findings, state of good repair, accessibility compliance and safety.

title: Revitalizing Toronto’s Peace Garden - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: gardens;
brief: The item asks council to revitalize Toronto's Peace Garden, established in 1984 as the city's physical commitment to peace and opposition to nuclear warfare, with its gazebo, incomplete roof, and an eternal flame kindled in Hiroshima surrounded by waters from Nagasaki. The garden's creation drew Pierre Trudeau turning the first sod, Pope John Paul II lighting the flame, and Queen Elizabeth II's dedication; more than 40 years on, engaged community groups want its message renewed as global conflicts drive division at home. The motion asks council to support the revitalization effort.

title: Public Realm Planters on Yonge Street: Interim Management and Long-Term Governance - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: benches (street furniture), city-owned trees; city owned trees; public owned trees; publicly owned trees; trees on public property
brief: The item asks council to set up interim care and long-term governance for the neglected public planters along Yonge Street through North York Centre, citing vacant tree pits, overgrown weeds and litter on a corridor home to Mel Lastman Square and the North York Civic Centre. With the full Transform Yonge rebuild years away, the motion asks staff to address the immediate disrepair and establish clear maintenance responsibilities so future public realm investments stay well maintained and accountable. Yonge through North York Centre is the largest concentration of office space outside downtown.

title: Allocating Community Benefit Charges from 2810 to 2816 Bayview Avenue Development to Improve Sheppard East Park - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
topics: community benefits, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: The item asks council to direct 100 percent of the Community Benefits Charges from the 2810 to 2816 Bayview Avenue development toward improvements at Sheppard East Park, at 229 Glendora Avenue, through the 2027 budget process. The park serves a growing neighbourhood, and the motion argues the charges should flow to the park given the development's added demand for green space. Possible upgrades include amenities, accessibility features, landscaping, pathways, seating and playground work, identified through the parks planning process with the local councillor. No dollar figure is attached.

title: Request to Accept In-Kind Community Benefits for 1243 Islington Avenue - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: The item asks council to accept 21 affordable rental housing units as an in-kind community benefits charge from the owner of 1243 Islington Avenue, a 61-storey mixed-use building with about 702 units and a privately owned publicly-accessible space. The offer covers 3 percent of the building's residential units, with a 25-year affordability period, a unit mix matching the building overall, full integration, and rents under the Official Plan definition. Planning staff have reviewed the proposal and support accepting it.

title: Ensuring Safety and Accessibility in Local Parks - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: accessibility, parks, safety; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, public safety
brief: The item asks council to act on park safety and accessibility in Ward 3, where residents report more illegal bonfires and dogs off-leash outside designated areas as the busy park season arrives. The motion also flags new pressure on Marie Curtis Park, now the only access route to the newly opened Jim Tovey Lakeview Conservation Area in Mississauga, straining trails and limited parking. It asks Parks and Recreation and Municipal Licensing and Standards to review education and by-law compliance for off-leash dogs and related park pressures.

title: Establishing a Public Art Program for New Transit Stations - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: arts and culture, stations;
brief: The item asks council to request that Metrolinx work with the TTC to create a public art program for new transit stations, matching the TTC's existing program. There is currently no comparable program for Metrolinx-owned stations on Lines 5 and 6 or the future Ontario Line, though the TTC program has beautified stations and reduced vandalism through juried art selected with local representatives and the public. The motion would extend community-engaged public art to the new lines.

title: Commemorating Former Councillor and Toronto Transit Commission Chair Howard Moscoe - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: memorials; monuments; permanent memorials
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow is asking council to commemorate former councillor and TTC Chair Howard Moscoe, who served on Toronto, Metro and North York councils for 32 years, including Toronto City Council from 1998 to 2010. He chaired the TTC from 1998 to 2000 and 2003 to 2006, promoted a municipal housing corporation for rent-geared-to-income housing in North York, and ran three times provincially in Wilson Heights. His career began as a high school art teacher before entering municipal politics in 1978.

title: Advancing the Redevelopment of Scadding Court Community Centre - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: community centres; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to advance the long-planned redevelopment of Scadding Court Community Centre, which also houses the Sanderson library branch, an alternative school, and an indoor pool. Council endorsed redevelopment principles in 2012 and an interdivisional working group has explored scenarios since; in April 2025 council redesignated the lands from Parks to Mixed Use Areas. The centre serves the downtown community with recreation, child and family supports, an EarlyON centre, food security and urban agriculture, seniors and newcomer programming.

title: Planning for the Centennial Celebration of Guild Park and Gardens (2032) - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
topics: gardens, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: The item asks council to start planning now for Guild Park and Gardens' centennial in 2032, a milestone for the 88-acre Scarborough Bluffs site known for its open-air collection of salvaged architectural fragments. The motion traces the site from the 1914 Bickford estate through the 1932 Guild of All Arts to today's public park and Clark Centre for the Arts. Early coordination between city divisions and community stakeholders would shape a commemoration of the park's cultural, historical and natural heritage.

title: Authorization to Amend Section 37 Agreement for 5800 Yonge Development Application - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
topics: development, funding; developing land; development (land); land development, financing
brief: The item asks council to amend the Section 37 agreement for the 5800 Yonge Street redevelopment, approved in 2022 with a required child care facility and 4,291.6 square metres of parkland dedication. The owner now proposes a revised framework keeping the fully fitted-out standalone child care facility, with furnishings and equipment, plus a $500,000 child care facility capital contribution. The motion notes Bill 23 has limited the city's community-benefit tools, making the retained child care commitment significant.

title: Commemorating the Life and Work of Rabbi Arthur Bielfeld - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: commemorative benches, memorials; monuments; permanent memorials
brief: The item asks council to commemorate Rabbi Arthur Bielfeld, who served Temple Emanu-El as Rabbi and Rabbi Emeritus for 58 years and was awarded the Order of Canada in 2013. Remembered for social justice advocacy on poverty, hunger and peace and for interfaith community building, he helped found the Leo Baeck Day School, MAZON Canada, KOLEL and the Campaign Against Child Poverty. The motion asks the City Manager to identify commemoration opportunities in Ward 15, Don Valley West, in consultation with his community, after his passing earlier this year.

title: Aligning the City’s Response on Sites Under Active Litigation - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: building codes;
brief: The item asks council to align the city's response when illegal work, from heritage destruction to unauthorized tree removal, clears the way for construction on a site under active litigation. Toronto Building must issue permits under the Ontario Building Code where no applicable-law violation exists, even while the city is suing and a court could order the site restored, effectively pre-empting that outcome. The motion asks council to address the disconnect between the litigation and permitting processes.

title: Celebrating Bastille Day on the French Mile - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: signs; signage
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow is asking council to mark Bastille Day with temporary honorary sign toppers on Bloor Street West between Avenue Road and Yonge Street on July 14, 2026, celebrating the French community's contributions to Toronto. The motion directs Transportation Services to install one topper per intersection at Avenue Road, St. Thomas Street, Bay Street and Yonge Street, and to negotiate an agreement with the France Canada Chamber of Commerce covering fabrication, installation, removal and reimbursement. The French Mile partnership formally recognizes Toronto's bonds with France.

title: Authority to Enter into a Nominal Fee Licence Agreement with Jumblies Theatre and Elder Duke Redbird - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: fees, licences, theatres (facilities); administrative fees; admission fees; admission prices; rates; service charges; user charges; user fees, auditorium; performance spaces; performing arts centres; performing arts facilities, licenses; licensing
brief: Councillor approval is being sought for a new nominal-fee licence agreement with Jumblies Theatre and Elder Duke Redbird for Indigenous cultural programming on about 3,000 square feet of Toronto Island Park near Blockhouse Bay. The 2023 agreement, which expired after a successful three-year seasonal run of knowledge sharing, storytelling, performances, ask-an-Elder drop-ins and school tours around a teepee, is up for renewal. The program was supported by the Wigwam Chi-Chemung, Elder Redbird's floating art installation and interpretive learning centre telling the story of Indigenous presence on the waterfront.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Recognize and Commemorate the Cabbagetown Group Softball League - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: sports clubs; badminton clubs; baseball associations; baseball leagues; bowling clubs; cross-country ski clubs; curling clubs; gymnastic clubs; hockey associations; hockey leagues; karate clubs; lacrosse clubs; lawn bowling clubs; ride clubs; rifle clubs; slo-pitch leagues; soccer clubs; soccer leagues; softball associations; softball leagues; swim clubs; tennis clubs; volleyball clubs
brief: The item asks council to release $10,000.00 in Section 37 funds to formally recognize the Cabbagetown Group Softball League with a commemorative plaque. The league has given queer and trans people a safe place to play softball for more than 50 years, starting as Sunday pickup games in 1975, formalizing in 1977, playing the first international queer softball game that year, and co-founding what is now International Pride Softball in 1979. Its current home is McCleary Park.

title: Authorization to Release Section 45 Funds and Agreement with STEPS Public Art to Advance Utility Box and Picnic Bench Beautification in Liberty Village - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: funding, urban beautification; 20-minute makeover; beautification projects; clean & beautiful city; clean and beautiful city; clean city beautiful city; community clean-up days; facade improvement; mural program; neighbourhood beautification, financing
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to release $55,000.00 in Section 45 funds and confirm STEPS Public Art as the lead organization to beautify Bell utility boxes and picnic benches in Liberty Village Park, to be completed in fall 2026. The work grew out of the Liberty for All neighbourhood study and FIFA World Cup legacy efforts; earlier plans with the Box Murals program stalled when that organization went on hiatus, and the BIA lacked capacity. STEPS would run artist calls for the box and bench art.

title: Request to include the Third-Party Sign Tax Structure in the City’s current Sign By-law review - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: by-laws, signs; bylaws, signage
brief: The item asks council to include the Third-Party Sign Tax in the city's ongoing Sign By-law review, saying the 2010 tax has not been examined for whether it still works amid new sign types, technologies and advertising models. The motion asks the Chief Building Official to run the tax review as part of the broader by-law modernization so affected businesses are engaged once, identifying ways to keep the tax fair, transparent and supportive of city revenues.

title: Improving Access to Space for Community Programs Across Scarborough - by Councillor Neethan Shan, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: recreational programs; community programs; recreation programs; recreation registration
brief: The item asks council to improve equity-deserving and diverse Scarborough communities' access to city-owned spaces for community programming and gatherings. The motion asks Corporate Real Estate Management and Economic Development and Culture to review booking barriers and take action, including extended hours, activating more community-accessible spaces, and better awareness of what is available and how to book it. It frames the work as affirming that culture belongs in Torontonians' daily lives.

title: Identifying How to Improve Access to Space for Faith Communities Across Toronto - by Councillor Neethan Shan, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: accessibility, faith communities; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, faith based groups; faith groups; religious communities
brief: The item asks council to identify how to improve faith communities' access to city space, saying growing religious communities face challenges with limited worship space, permits, parking and transportation. The motion asks the City Manager to explore better information on booking city-owned spaces, permit processes, parking exemptions and transportation access, and asks senior staff to review community safety and inclusion supports. Toronto is home to more than 3.2 million people of wide-ranging religious affiliations.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds for Various Park Improvement Projects - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: improvement, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: The item asks council to allocate Section 42 parkland funds from multiple developments to capital improvements at five Ward 11 parks: David Balfour Park, Christie Pits Park, Vermont Square Playground, Ramsden Park and Taddle Creek Park. The official figures list $300,000 for converting the David Balfour Park washroom to year-round use plus planting improvements, and $150,000 for Christie Pits baseball field improvements, with $35,000 and $250,000 also listed for the remaining projects. The investments target washrooms, play equipment, pathways, lighting, safety and accessibility.

title: Honouring Constable Marc Pinizzotto - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: condolences, police officers;
brief: The item asks council to commemorate Constable Marc Pinizzotto, the 18-year Toronto Police Service member and Emergency Task Force officer killed in the line of duty on June 11, 2026 while executing a search warrant in a major shootings investigation. The motion describes an outpouring of grief from residents, officials and police services across Canada, and asks the city to honour his service and sacrifice so future generations remember his dedication. He is survived by his family, remembered as a husband, father, son, coach and mentor.

title: Hitting the Right Notes in Downsview: Supporting Toronto’s Music Industry While Considering Local Residents - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: music, noise control; noise barriers; sound barriers
brief: Rogers Stadium, the open-air venue on the old Downsview runway that opened in June 2025, drew about 700,000 visitors last year and expects over a million in 2026 with more than 1,000 part-time jobs, but residents in York Centre, Willowdale and Vaughan report serious concert-night noise concerns. Councillor James Pasternak's motion asks council to balance support for Toronto's music industry with residents' concerns by exploring capital improvements and operational measures at the stadium; operator Live Nation has already added soundproof cladding with mixed results. The motion also notes the lack of a city noise-response process for the venue.

title: Exemption from Permit Parking Polling Requirements for Old Weston Road, between Davenport Road and St. Clair Avenue West - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Residents of Old Weston Road between Davenport Road and St. Clair Avenue West have historically parked overnight in front of their homes, but the stretch is not in a permit parking zone and several residents recently received overnight tickets. Councillor Alejandra Bravo's motion asks council to exempt the street from the by-law's city-managed polling requirement so it can be added to permit parking area 3D at the July community council meeting, if a neighbourhood survey of residents shows support. Many households lack private parking and already hold 3D permits.

title: Closing the Gap Between Provincial Funding and Rising Public Health Costs - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: funding, public health; financing
brief: The item asks council to press the province to close the gap between public health funding and rising costs. Toronto Public Health's mandatory programs face inflationary pressure plus a ratified Local 79 agreement bringing a cumulative 16.4 percent salary and benefit increase over four years, 17.9 percent for public health nurses, against a provincial commitment of roughly 1 percent annual increases through 2026-27. The motion says inflation-adjusted provincial funding is needed to deliver mandatory programs for a growing population. No dollar figure is attached.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to the Chinese Cultural Centre of Greater Toronto to Facilitate Construction of the Asian Garden at Cynthia Lai Park - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: construction, cultural facilities, gardens; art centres; arts centres; cultural attractions; cultural centres, building
brief: The item asks council to release $11,499.28 in Section 37 funds to the Chinese Cultural Centre of Greater Toronto for construction of the Asian Garden at Cynthia Lai Park, a community-led project reflecting Scarborough's diversity. The funds come from the 1088 Progress Avenue development across the street, where contributions sat unused for more than three years and became eligible for redirection under a 2025 by-law. The reallocation was made at the Chief Planner's discretion in consultation with the local councillor.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Ward 18 Participatory Budgeting Projects - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: improvement, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: Through Ward 18's participatory budgeting process, residents chose park improvements for the West Lansing and Avondale neighbourhoods: new seating, picnic tables, a gazebo, playground and adult fitness equipment, and ping pong tables. Councillor Lily Cheng's motion asks council to release $500,000 in Section 37 funds, from the 4841 to 4881 Yonge Street, Sheppard Avenue East and Forest Laneway developments, to create the capital sub-projects so work at Franklin, Gwendolen, Glendora and Avondale parks can proceed. The cash flow is $250,000 in 2026 and $250,000 in 2027.

title: Authorization to Enter into a Land Exchange at Donalda Club (12 Bushbury Drive, 1413 Don Mills Road and Don Valley Parkway W/S) for the Future Expansion of the East Don Trail Network - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: trail systems; footpaths; multi-pupose trails; multi-purpose paths; multi-use pathways; multi-use trails; pedestrian trails; recreational trails; trail networks; trails; walking paths; waterfront trail
brief: The item asks council to authorize a land exchange with the Donalda Club so the city receives ravine land for a future East Don Trail expansion, while the club gains ownership of parts of its golf course it currently leases from the city. The club has operated at 12 Bushbury Drive, 1413 Don Mills Road and the Don Valley Parkway since 1960, with three parcels under a city lease dating to 1986 and expiring in 2035. The source lists a $96,740 figure in connection with the exchange, and staff say the terms meet Official Plan rules for parkland exchanges.

title: Amending Part Lot Control Exemption By-Law for 276-294 Main Street - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: exemptions, part lot control; exceptions
brief: This is a procedural item: Council votes on repealing the Part Lot Control Exemption By-law for 276-294 Main Street because the developer has chosen a different land-division method. Council enacted the exemption by-law in 2023, extended in 2025, to divide the site into four stratified lots, but the applicant will now proceed through a Plan of Condominium application instead. Repealing the by-law lets the draft-approved condominium advance so the land division happens through one controlled process.

title: 35 to 37 Baseball Place - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: appeals;
brief: This is a procedural item: Council decides whether to authorize the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose the owner's appeal of the Committee of Adjustment's refusal at 35 to 37 Baseball Place. The owner had sought a variance to allow a vehicle dealership where zoning does not permit one; the committee refused it on May 21, 2026, and the owner appealed June 1. The motion lets the solicitor retain an outside consultant and resolve the matter for the city, and is time-sensitive.

title: 2 Blaketon Road - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: appeals, tree protection, tree removal;
brief: This is a procedural item: Council authorizes the City Solicitor to respond to the owner's appeal of the Committee of Adjustment's refusal at 2 Blaketon Road, where the owner sought variances to build eight back-to-back townhouses on a corner lot. The committee refused the application on May 28, 2026 over zoning variances including gross floor area, floor space index, lot coverage and setbacks under both the city-wide by-law and the Major Streets intensification by-law. Planning staff had found the application consistent with the Major Streets policies, while Urban Forestry raised concerns. The motion lets the solicitor retain experts for the city's case.

title: (Removed)
topics: safety, workplaces; job sites; telework; work from home; worksites, public safety
brief: This item was added to the council agenda in error and has been removed by the City Clerk. There is no motion, no decision and no action attached to it.

title: Queen's Park North Donation - Concept Plan Update Report
topics: donation, funding, landscape design, planning, urban design, urban planning; bequest; toy drive, city planning; community planning; regional planning, civic improvements, financing, landscape architecture; landscape projects
brief: The committee is receiving an update on the planned revitalization of Queen's Park North — Canada's oldest municipal park — with a revised Concept Plan responding to March council direction, including an urban forest management plan, heritage emphasis, a food-and-beverage feasibility study, and a time-limited design working group. The figures cited are $50.0 million, $8.7 million, $16.5 million, $21.0 million, and $3.8 million. Council approval of the Concept Plan would guide detailed design and project agreements. Council decides.

title: Concerns and Considerations raised by the Province of Ontario and Energy Utilities regarding Development in Proximity to the Hearn Switching Station
topics: controller cabinets (traffic), official plan amendments, utilities; power utilties
brief: This is an information item: staff present the province's and energy utilities' concerns about development near the Hearn Switching Station in the Port Lands, as requested after council's March 2026 direction on the Official Plan Amendment appeal for 402 and 440 Unwin Avenue, which proposes residential uses where only port industrial, energy, and city-serving uses are permitted south of the Ship Channel. The item affects future Port Lands energy infrastructure and development. No decision is attached.

title: Right-Turn-on-Red Prohibition - Victoria Park Avenue and Kingston Road
topics: streetcars, traffic signals, transportation; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, street-cars, transportation services
brief: Transportation Services is asking City Council to prohibit southbound right turns on red at all times at Victoria Park Avenue and Kingston Road, because TTC streetcar tracks on Kingston Road encroach into the path of turning vehicles at the constrained intersection, creating a conflict point. Council decides.

title: Metrolinx Eglinton Crosstown LRT - At-grade Segment and Tunnel Section - Traffic and Parking By-law Amendments and Road Dedication
topics: light rail transit, municipal codes, parking regulations; lrt, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Approving the remaining traffic and parking by-law amendments for the Eglinton Crosstown LRT corridor — both the at-grade and tunnelled sections, between Kennedy Road and Weston Road — and dedicating newly built roadway lands as public highway, after the line entered revenue service on February 8, 2026, is up for a decision by City Council. Council decides.

title: Western Beaches Public Realm Plan
topics: beaches, parks and open space areas, public realm, waterfronts; green spaces; open spaces, lakefronts; waterfront trail, public spaces
brief: This is an information item: the committee receives the Western Beaches Public Realm Plan updating the 2009 Western Waterfront Master Plan for the beaches between the Humber River and Ontario Place — covering breakwaters, shoreline erosion, water quality, and visitor experience — shaped by community and Indigenous engagement, to be implemented incrementally as funding is identified. The committee receives the report.

title: Updates on Vision Zero Road Safety Initiatives: Enhancing Safety in School Zones, Permanent Roadside Memorials, Changes to Parking Regulations for Intersection Pedestrian Signals, and Road Safety Improvement Projects
topics: memorials, parking, parking regulations, pedestrian signals, road safety, safety, schools, traffic control systems; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums, crosswalk lights; pedestrian displays, monuments; permanent memorials, parking by-laws; parking bylaws, public safety, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: The committee is receiving a Vision Zero update covering school-zone safety — with plans for additional Toronto Police enforcement after the province ended automated speed enforcement — the provincial Road Safety Improvement Fund, enhanced School Safety Zone plans, a permanent roadside memorial program for fatal collisions, parking regulation changes near intersection pedestrian signals, and new road safety improvement projects requiring no lane removals. The update affects child pedestrian safety and road design citywide. The committee or council decides on next steps. The Vision Zero road safety improvement and cycling enhancement projects recommended in the report are estimated to cost $6,193,000 to install, with funding already included in the capital budget.

title: Improvement of Tactile Wayfinding in Line 5 Stations
topics: accessibility, persons with a disability, subway stations; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, disabled; disabled persons; handicapped persons; people with disabilities; persons with disabilities; persons with special needs; physical disabilities; physically challenged; physically disabled; physically impaired; special needs; the physically disabled
brief: The item asks City Council to request the TTC Board work with Metrolinx, consulting the Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee, to improve tactile wayfinding for visually impaired riders in Line 5 (Eglinton Crosstown) stations — where floor tiles currently guide only to elevators, not stairs or escalators — and to set that as the standard for future and refurbished stations. The item affects accessible transit navigation. Council decides.

title: Expansion of Ontario’s Deposit Return Program
topics: bottle deposit return programs, recycling, waste diversion, waste management infrastructure; 3 rs; reduce reuse recycle, beverage container returns; bottle deposits; bottle returns
brief: The item asks City Council to have the City Manager send a letter to Ontario — addressed to the Premier and the Minister — asking the province to immediately implement a deposit-return program for non-alcoholic beverage containers. The motion notes Ontario's alcohol deposit system returns about 75 per cent of empties, Ontario is one of few provinces without a non-alcoholic deposit program with a roughly 50 per cent recovery rate, and peers including Peel Region, Waterloo, the Association of Municipalities of Ontario, and the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative have made the same ask. The item affects beverage container recycling. Council decides.

title: Update on MM40.20 - Reinstating Paddle the Don for 2027
topics: conservation, rivers, watersheds; environmental conservation; environmental improvements; environmental management; environmental protection; environmental stewardship; greening, subwatersheds
brief: This is an information item: staff report on reinstating the Paddle the Don canoe event — run by the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority from 1993 to 2019 with about 500 participants annually — for 2027, noting coordination with ongoing Lower Don construction, staffing, and financial considerations must be resolved first. The committee is asked to receive the report.

title: Achieving Universal Student Nutrition - 2026 Service Subsidies
topics: health; health coverage
brief: Authorizing the Medical Officer of Health to transfer 2026 municipal student nutrition funding — $31.170 million combined: $7.216 million to the Angel Foundation for Learning and $23.954 million to the Toronto Foundation for Student Success, including $0.518 million held in reserve for remaining Phase 4 applications, fall applications, and appeals — would get City Council's approval. Implementing these allocations would complete the city's goal of a universal morning meal program across all public school communities by the 2026-2027 school year. The funding affects food access for children and youth in schools citywide. Council decides.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order 6049718 with Veolia Water Canada Inc., for Critical Capital Improvements and Maintenance at the Disco Organics Processing Facility
topics: agreements, contracts, organics processing facilities, water; tenancy agreements
brief: The city wants to amend its purchase order with Veolia Water Canada Inc. to fund critical capital improvements and maintenance at the Disco Road organics processing facility, which has operated since 2014 and needs urgent infrastructure work. Some of the work is being accelerated to line up with the council-approved facility expansion so the site is ready and downtime is minimized. No dollar figures are provided in the agenda text; the purchase order was originally authorized under 2019.IE5.11 for operating and improving the organics facility.

title: Animate Nathan Phillips Square
topics: benches (street furniture), park benches, public realm, purchasing, squares; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, civic squares; public squares, public spaces
brief: The item asks the General Government Committee to have staff study the feasibility and costs of adding bench seating at Nathan Phillips Square for the summer 2026 season — similar to benches used at the University of Toronto Scarborough campus — and report back to the June 24-26 council meeting with recommendations. The motion frames seating as a way to make the square more welcoming and usable, while noting operational, security, and cost considerations. The committee decides whether to order the study.

title: Occupational Health and Safety Report: End of Year 2025
topics: employment & labour (sc), health (sc), injuries, working conditions; collective agreements; employment contracts; workplace policies
brief: This is an information item: City Council is asked to receive the city's 2025 occupational health and safety report. Lost-time injuries rose 7.5 per cent over 2024, recurrences rose 10.4 per cent, and medical-aid injuries rose 8.9 per cent, while invoiced Workplace Safety and Insurance Board costs fell from $65.95 million in 2024 to $64.06 million in 2025 — driven mainly by mental and emotional illness claims, followed by firefighter cancers and musculoskeletal disorders. The report also sets out 2026 priorities for addressing identified hazards.

title: 1652 Keele Street - Community Space Tenancy Lease Agreement with The Black Women's Institute for Health and Municipal Capital Facility Designation
topics: city-owned properties, community associations, community centres, leasing; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, city owned properties; city properties, leases
brief: Signing a Community Space Tenancy lease with The Black Women's Institute for Health for about 2,017 square feet in the city-owned Keele Community Hub at 1652 Keele Street, and designating the space as a municipal capital facility, is up for a decision by City Council. The organization was selected through a 2025 competitive process and would join five existing tenants delivering integrated services focused on youth, newcomers, and families. Council decides on the lease and designation.

title: 1141 Bloor Street West and 980 Dufferin Street - Community Space Tenancy Lease Agreements and Municipal Capital Facility Designations for Five Tenant Agencies in the Bloor-Dufferin Community Hub
topics: city-owned properties, community centres, leasing, municipal facilities, non-profit organizations; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, city facilities; municipal buildings, city owned properties; city properties, leases, non profit; nonprofit; not-for-profit organizations
