brief: The question before City Council: whether to sign Community Space Tenancy leases with five non-profit organizations to occupy about 19,132 square feet in the city-owned Bloor-Dufferin Community Hub at 1141 Bloor Street West and 980 Dufferin Street, and to designate each tenancy as a municipal capital facility. The tenants were chosen through competitive expressions of interest in 2021 and 2025 on merit, capacity, and alignment with city priorities, and would deliver integrated family, settlement, mental health, and culturally responsive services from the shared hub. Council decides on the leases and designations.

title: Delegation of Authority for Licence Agreements to Facilitate the use of Published Sound Recordings in Recreation Facilities
topics: audio recording, licences, music, recreational facilities; audio; audio tapes, licenses; licensing, recreation facilities; recreational amenities
brief: City Council votes on giving the General Manager of Parks and Recreation standing authority to sign music licensing agreements with Re:Sound and the Society of Composers, Authors and Music Publishers of Canada (SOCAN), the two bodies authorized under federal copyright law to collect royalties for playing recorded music in public. The report cites $80,000 in licensing costs. The delegation lets recreation facilities and programs keep playing music legally without coming back to council for each agreement.

title: Litigation Arising from the Replacement of the Watermain at the Kipling Avenue Bridge over the Humber River
topics: bridges, construction, legal matters, projects, watermains; building, legal issues, mains; water mains
brief: The city hired Parsons Inc. to design a new 400 mm watermain across the Humber River at the Kipling Avenue Bridge and support construction, but the city alleges errors in the design and construction administration made it impossible to finish the project as designed — work was interrupted, then completed at greater cost after Parsons re-did the design. The city has sued Parsons to recover the extra costs it attributes to the errors. City Council is being asked to adopt confidential legal instructions in an attachment and to authorize their public release. The litigation affects the final cost of the bridge watermain project.

title: Non-Competitive Procurement Contract with SmartSimple Software Inc., for New Configuration of the Toronto Grants, Rebates and Incentives Portal for Housing Secretariat
topics: affordable housing, contracts, purchasing, software, subsidies and grants; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, affordable homes; housing projects, computer programs, financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs
brief: City Council decides whether to approve a non-competitive two-year contract with SmartSimple Software Inc. worth up to $300,000 ($305,280 net of HST recoveries) — the report also cites $27 million, $100 million, and $500,000 in program and procurement figures — to reconfigure the Housing Secretariat's grant application portal. The portal is the central hub where non-profits apply for city grants, but new and expanded housing and tenant grant programs can't be supported by the current setup and are being run on paper outside the system. The contract would bring those programs into the portal.

title: Non-Competitive Contracts for the Provision of the City’s Traffic Electrical Maintenance and Emergency Services, and Traffic Electrical Planned Capital Works Roster
topics: agreements, contracts, electric distribution utilities, electricity, traffic; electric power; electricity usage, electricity distribution utilities; electricity retailers, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, tenancy agreements
brief: City Council is asked to approve non-competitive one-year contracts (August 1, 2026 to July 31, 2027) with Black & McDonald Ltd. ($17,745,351, or $18,057,669 net of HST recoveries) for Service Area A and TM3 Inc. ($5,851,671, or $5,954,660 net of HST recoveries) for Service Area B to maintain the city's traffic signals and electrical infrastructure with 24/7 emergency response, plus a planned capital works roster; the report also cites $19,894,553 ($20,244,697), $500,000, $16,027,600 ($16,309,686), and $4,552,388 ($4,632,510). The current contracts expire July 31, 2026, and the new deals keep the same scope and pricing with only a contract-permitted inflation increase.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with ServiceNow Canada Inc., for Licenses and Professional Services
topics: agreements, contracts, government services, licences; licenses; licensing, tenancy agreements
brief: Approving a non-competitive three-year contract (plus two one-year options) directly with ServiceNow Canada Inc. worth $13,508,403 ($13,746,151 net of HST recoveries) — the report also cites $500,000 — for licences and professional services, as a ceiling with no commitment to spend it all would get City Council's approval. ServiceNow is the city's enterprise IT platform for service desk tickets, projects, assets, and technology requests; the current reseller agreement expires December 3, 2026, and staff say a direct deal gets better pricing. The platform supports compliance with audit recommendations on IT asset management.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with RouteSmart Technologies Inc., for the Continued Use of Collection Route Management and Service Planning Software for Solid Waste Management Services
topics: contracts, science & technology (sc), software, solid waste management; computer programs, solid waste management planning; swm; waste management
brief: Approving a non-competitive agreement with RouteSmart Technologies Inc. worth up to $850,000 ($864,960 net of HST recoveries) for up to five years to move Solid Waste Management's garbage collection route-planning software to the cloud-based RouteSmart Online is up for a decision by City Council. The vendor ended support for the current on-premises version in March 2026, even though the city was authorized to use it through 2030, and the software is critical for designing collection routes and day-to-day operations. The deal covers the same period with a city opt-out option.

title: Non-Competitive Bridge Contract with Arcadis Professional Services (Canada) Inc., for the Provision of the City’s Congestion Management Centre Operations Services
topics: agreements, congestion, contracts, road operations; gridlock, road services, tenancy agreements
brief: The question before City Council: whether to approve a non-competitive one-year bridge contract (October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027) with Arcadis Professional Services (Canada) Inc. worth $4,512,329 ($4,591,746 net of HST recoveries) — the report also cites $500,000 — to keep operating the city's Congestion Management Centre (formerly the RESCU Traffic Operations Centre). The centre runs 24/7 traffic operations across 2,500 traffic signals and 385 monitoring cameras, dispatching emergency transportation maintenance and managing incidents. Arcadis (formerly IBI Group) has held the contract since 2021, and the bridge deal keeps service running under the same terms until a new procurement is done.

title: Award of Doc5398199635 to Alberici Constructors Ltd., for the New Ultraviolet Disinfection and Residuals Management Facility at the Island Water Treatment Plant, and Amendment to Purchase Orders 6056811 and 6057463 with AECOM Canada ULC for Contract Administration and Post-Construction Services
topics: contracts, projects, purchasing, wastewater treatment plants; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, sewage treatment plants; treatment plants; waste water treatment plants
brief: The city wants to award Alberici Constructors Ltd. a $333,856,566 contract ($339,732,442 net of HST recoveries; the report states the net figure as $333,856,56) for a new ultraviolet disinfection and residuals management facility at the Island Water Treatment Plant, reallocate $99,966,862 within Toronto Water's capital budget and plan, and amend two AECOM Canada ULC purchase orders — $16,368,760 ($16,656,850) for construction administration and $64,359 ($65,492) for post-construction services — after scope changes and a major schedule extension. Additional figures cited are $3,724,823 ($3,790,380), $20,093,583 ($20,447,230), $275,435 ($280,283), and $339,794 ($345,775) in revised purchase order values. The project affects drinking water treatment infrastructure on the Toronto Islands.

title: Administrative Penalty Tribunal - Chair's 2025 Annual Report

brief: This is an information item: City Council is asked to receive the 2025 annual report from the Chair of the Administrative Penalty Tribunal, the independent body of 25 council-appointed hearing officers who provide the final, unappealable review of parking violation disputes after screening. (A matching item went to the General Government Committee as GG29.21.)

title: 555 Rexdale Boulevard - Woodbine Secondary Plan Study, Infrastructure Master Plan and Transportation Master Plan - Interim Report
topics: Master Plans, Secondary Plans, infrastructure, transportation; transportation services
brief: This is an interim report: staff summarize the Woodbine Secondary Plan study so far, which sets a vision and planning rules for the southeast Woodbine lands. Council is asked to endorse the emerging directions before further study and public engagement.

brief: A developer proposed three four-storey residential buildings with about 125 homes at 3100 Weston Road, keeping the community centre and heritage structures, then appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal after council missed the deadline. Staff want the city's lawyers to oppose the current version.

title: 1243 Islington Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: mixed use areas, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A developer wants to build a 61-storey mixed-use tower with about 702 homes at 1243 Islington Avenue, plus a small public plaza and a mid-block pedestrian connection. Council is asked to change the zoning to allow it.

title: 5500 Dundas Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: mixed use areas, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: A developer wants to build two mixed-use towers of 14 and 16 storeys with about 560 homes at 5500 Dundas Street West, plus ground-floor commercial space and a publicly accessible plaza. Council is asked to change the zoning to allow it.

title: Review of Parking and Transit Related Requests for Etobicoke York District
topics: parking, transit networks;
brief: Councillor Holyday asks city planners to review the removal of minimum parking requirements for new developments in Etobicoke York, and to report on whether pausing the change is feasible until transit service improves.

topics: buildings, official plan amendments, residential properties, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: A developer wants to build two 43-storey and one 39-storey towers with about 1,579 homes at 39 Newcastle Street, plus a public plaza and some non-residential space. Council is asked to change the Official Plan and zoning to allow it.

title: Lake Shore Boulevard West at Silver Moon Drive - Lane Designation
topics: [activities in transportation], [attributes in transportation];
brief: Staff want the southerly eastbound lane on Lake Shore Boulevard West near Silver Moon Drive designated as right-turn only, to make lane use clear and reduce conflicts between drivers.

brief: Staff recommend adding two pedestrian crossovers at the right-turn lanes where Black Creek Drive meets Weston Road, plus yield controls for drivers. The changes aim to make crossing safer for people on foot.

brief: Staff recommend installing traffic lights at Humberline Drive and Claireville Drive (south intersection) to make crossing safer for pedestrians. Pedestrian crossings on Humberline Drive just north of the intersection would also be prohibited.

topics: by-laws, change, road closures, temporary signs, traffic, urban transit systems; amendments; conversion; modification, bylaws, local transit authorities; municipal transit authorities; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; transit agencies; transit operating agencies, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: To allow construction of the Eglinton Crosstown West light-rail extension's Renforth, Kipling, and Scarlett stations, Council is asked to approve long-term lane closures, temporary traffic signals, and detours for pedestrians and cyclists.

title: 2686 and 2688 Lake Shore Boulevard West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: apartment neighbourhoods, official plan amendments, residential properties, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: A developer wants to build a 12-storey residential building with about 172 homes, including four live-work units, at 2686 and 2688 Lake Shore Boulevard West. Council is asked to change the Official Plan and zoning to allow it.

title: Annual Review of the City of Toronto’s Asset Management Planning Progress
topics: annual reports, assets, finance (sc); annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards
brief: Adopting the City's first annual asset management progress report, required under provincial regulation, covering progress on the Corporate Asset Management Plan across 26 City divisions, agencies, and corporations heads to Council for a decision. Technical amendments would be delegated to the Chief Financial Officer.

title: Annual Report on City Loans and Loan Guarantees
topics: annual reports, finance (sc), financial reports, loans; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: The call on whether to approve refinancing the City's $4.048 million ($4,047,660) interest-only capital loan to Lakeshore Arena Corporation over a 17-year term starting June 30, 2026, renew a $175,000 line-of-credit guarantee for Young People's Theatre for three years, and continue a letter-of-credit guarantee for Canadian Stage's $820,000 line of credit belongs to Council. The report notes the City's loan portfolio as of December 31, 2025: about $5.995 million in line-of-credit guarantees, $34.46 million in capital loan guarantees, $36.845 million in outstanding direct capital loans, and one $600,000 direct line of credit.

title: City of Toronto Investment Report for the Year 2025
topics: annual reports, financial reports, investment; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: This is an information item: Council receives the City's 2025 investment report. The General Fund had a book return of 3.6 per cent and generated $391.0 million for the year, while the Sinking Fund portfolio had a market return of 2.7 per cent and generated approximately $85 million. No policy change is proposed.

title: Toronto Hydro Corporation Annual General Meeting and 2025 Audited Financial Statements
topics: annual reports, meetings; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards
brief: Council treated part of its meeting as Toronto Hydro Corporation's annual shareholder meeting, reappointed the corporation's auditor, and received and approved the financial documents, which are confidential. Council also affirmed that Toronto Hydro is and should remain solely owned by the City of Toronto, and amended the Toronto Hydro Shareholder Direction so that, unless Council directs otherwise, the corporation cannot raise capital by selling shares or equity investments to anyone other than the City. The decision locks in the City's sole ownership of Toronto Hydro.

title: 2025 Annual General Meeting and Wind-Up of Casa Loma Corporation
topics: annual reports, corporations, culture (sc), economic development, financial reports, meetings; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, annual financial reports; financial statements, business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing
brief: Council, as sole shareholder, is asked to receive Casa Loma Corporation's 2025 annual report and audited financial statements and to approve the voluntary wind-up of the corporation, with the City taking direct oversight of Casa Loma through the Economic Development and Culture Division. Net future lease revenues would go to the Casa Loma Reserve Fund, and the existing lease with Liberty Entertainment Group runs to January 2034. No net financial impact is expected.

title: Quayside Development Project Update
topics: development, library branches, public libraries; branches, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Up for a decision before Council: grant authorities to advance the first phase of the Quayside waterfront development at Queens Quay East and Parliament Street, a 4.9-hectare mixed-use community led by Waterfront Toronto with Dream Unlimited and Great Gulf, and to endorse a new Toronto Public Library neighbourhood branch in the central waterfront. The report's figures are $4,000,000, $2,500,000, $500,000, $2,000,000, $375,000, $381,600, $750,000, $763,200, $1,125,000, and $1,144,800.

title: Expanding the Rain Barrel Program

brief: The subsidized rain barrel pilot proved extremely popular, selling out its first allocation in 9 hours. Mayor Chow is asking Council to add $238,249 to the 2026 operating budget, fully recovered from Toronto Water at no net cost, to buy more barrels, and to limit the program to one barrel per household so more residents can take part. It affects homeowners looking to cut stormwater runoff and water use.

title: Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative's 2026 Annual Conference, May 6-8, 2026
topics: annual reports, city initiatives, conferences, economic development; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing, city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives, conference travel
brief: This is an information item: Council receives an update on the May 6-8, 2026 Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative annual conference on economic resilience, trade, and infrastructure. The report notes the region generates approximately $9.3 trillion USD in annual economic output. No policy change is proposed.

title: 2026 Sociable City Summit and Academy April 12-15, 2026, Nashville, Tennessee
topics: community development, economic development, municipal associations, stakeholders; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing, community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development
brief: This is an information item: Council receives an update on the April 12-15, 2026 Sociable City Summit in Nashville on nighttime economy best practices, attended by Toronto's Night Economy Champion. No policy change is proposed.

title: 2026 Good Roads Conference March 29 - April 1, 2026
topics: annual reports, conferences, infrastructure, transportation; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, conference travel, transportation services
brief: This is an information item: Council receives an update on the March 29-April 1, 2026 Good Roads conference on municipal transportation and infrastructure, where the reporting member was named President of the Good Roads Association. No policy change is proposed.

title: Simplifying the 311 Intake Experience
topics: non emergency municipal services, public inquiries; 3-1-1; 311; 311 calls; non-emergency city services, judicial inquries
brief: The Service Excellence Committee is asking the Executive Committee to have the Customer Experience division report to the June 2026 Council meeting with a plan to simplify the 311 intake process and clearer public messaging about how requests are prioritized. The work covers a redesigned web and mobile front end and better tracking of service requests.

title: Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal 2025 Annual Report
topics: animals, dogs; fauna
brief: This is an information item: the committee receives the Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal's 2025 annual report, covering the tribunal's independent review of appeals to dangerous dog orders. No policy change is proposed.

title: Proposed Humber Bay Shores Business Improvement Area Poll Results
topics: business improvement areas, polling; bia; business improvement associations
brief: A City Clerk-run poll found the required number of valid ballots and a majority in favour of establishing a Humber Bay Shores Business Improvement Area, covering the area southeast from the CN Rail Corridor from Mimico Creek to the Humber Bay River and Humber Bay Park. Council is asked to designate the area as a new BIA and have the City Solicitor prepare the designation by-law. The decision affects local businesses in the Humber Bay Shores area.

title: Changes to Business Improvement Area Board of Management
topics: [activities in management], business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations
brief: This is an administrative item: Council is asked to remove Tara Longo as a director of The Eglinton Way Business Improvement Area board of management. No other changes are proposed.

title: Establishing Toronto's Cultural Districts Program
topics: [locations in culture], neighbourhoods; cultural neighbourhoods; ethnic neighbourhoods; neighborhoods
brief: Directing staff to implement a Cultural Districts Program in phases, starting with formal recognition of Little Jamaica, Church-Wellesley Village, West Chinatown, Little Iran, and Banglatown as the City's first Cultural Districts comes before Council. The program would celebrate culturally distinct areas and respond to commercial displacement threatening their businesses and landmarks. Future districts could be added through an application process.

title: Authority to Enter Agreement with the Ministry of Long-Term Care for the Funding and Development of 4610 Finch Avenue East Long-Term Care Home
topics: development, funding, long term care homes; developing land; development (land); land development, financing, homes for the aged; long term care centers; long term care centres; long term care facilities; nursing facilities; nursing homes
brief: The City wants to build a new 378-bed long-term care home at 4610 Finch Avenue East, expected to be completed in 2030, replacing City-run beds that do not meet provincial design standards. Council is asked to authorize the City Manager to negotiate and enter a development agreement with Ontario's Ministry of Long-Term Care so the City can access provincial capital funding. The agreement carries multi-year financial and legal obligations for the City.

title: Establishing the Lawrence Heights Neighbourhood Centre in the Association of Community Centres
topics: community centres, neighbourhoods; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, cultural neighbourhoods; ethnic neighbourhoods; neighborhoods
brief: A decision on establishing the Lawrence Heights Neighbourhood Centre as a new Association of Community Centres board of management, the first expansion of the AOCC model in over 30 years sits with Council. The 12-member board would include 11 public members and the Ward 8 councillor, and early approval gives time to form the board, hire an executive director, and set up governance before opening. It affects community programming in Lawrence Heights.

title: Improving Access to Toronto Island Park - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: accessibility, parks; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Toronto Island draws 1.5 million visitors a year, and two new faster, higher-capacity ferries arrive in 2027. This motion asks Council to direct staff to examine a fairer ferry fare structure, including discounted fares like the TTC's and removing extra passenger fees, and to report back through the 2027 budget process. The motion affects what Torontonians pay to visit the Island.

title: 396 to 398 Church Street, 73 to 77 McGill Street and 50 Gerrard Street East - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor seeks Council's instructions for the Ontario Land Tribunal proceedings on 396 to 398 Church Street, 73 to 77 McGill Street and 50 Gerrard Street East. The 2022 proposal was a 43-storey mixed-use building with 463 residential units, 216 square metres of ground-floor retail and 28,782 square metres of total floor area, appealed after Council failed to decide in time; in July 2026 Council accepted a without-prejudice settlement offer for a revised 37-storey building with 425 units, 241 square metres of retail and 24,815 square metres of floor area, but that settlement did not proceed to a hearing and is not under Tribunal order. The instructions are confidential legal advice.

title: 2650 Lawrence Avenue East - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor seeks Council's directions for an Ontario Land Tribunal hearing about the development at 2650 Lawrence Avenue East. The August 2025 applications proposed a 33-storey residential building and a 43-storey mixed-use building; the applicant appealed both the zoning and official plan amendments after Council failed to decide in time. The hearing starts in November 2026, and the recommendations are confidential legal advice.

title: 2 Sandfield Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Consent to Review Tribunal Decision
topics: appeals;
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor seeks Council's directions on the owner's request for Council's consent to file a review request with the Ontario Land Tribunal over its decision on 2 Sandfield Road. The Tribunal had allowed the owner's appeals of Council's refusal of official plan and zoning amendments and withheld its final order pending conditions; the owner now wants Council's consent to seek a review of the Tribunal's earlier decision so it can proceed with a revised proposal. The recommendations are confidential legal advice.

title: 650 Parliament Street - City’s Claim for Recovery of Costs
topics: costs, emergency services; 9-1-1; 911; 911 calls; emergency assistance; emergency response
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor seeks Council's adoption of confidential recommendations about the City's claim to recover the costs of emergency services provided after the August 2018 fire at 650 Parliament Street, a 22-storey building with 570 apartments owned by Parwell Investments Inc. and Bleeman Holdings Ltd. About 1,500 residents were displaced, and the City paid for shelter, food, clothing, medical aid and transportation after the owner said it was not immediately equipped to respond; the owner's president agreed to make the City whole, and the City sued in 2020 and has since resolved its claim. The recommendations are confidential legal advice. The outcome affects how much of the public cost of the emergency response the City recovers from the property owner.

title: 257, 259 and 291 Lake Shore Boulevard East, 2 Small Street and 200 Queens Quay East - Minutes of Settlement with Redpath Sugar Ltd.
topics: environment (sc);
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor seeks Council's adoption of confidential recommendations on minutes of settlement with Redpath Sugar Ltd. concerning Quayside Blocks 1 and 2 at 257, 259 and 291 Lake Shore Boulevard East, 2 Small Street and 200 Queens Quay East. The settlement updates 2011 minutes that bound the City, Redpath and the former Toronto Waterfront Revitalization Corporation to assess and mitigate the environmental impacts of Redpath's sugar refining facility at 95 Queens Quay East, including its electrical co-generation system, since provincial noise guidelines and air assessment rules have changed since 2011. The recommendations are confidential legal advice. This matters to future residents of the Quayside waterfront development, whose homes would sit near an operating industrial refinery.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Compliance Audit Committee
brief: Appointing Sara Gelgor as Chair, along with Ramin Faraji and Catherine Syms, to the Compliance Audit Committee, with two alternate members, for a term matching the council term that follows the 2026 municipal election is up for a decision by Council. The panel that interviewed candidates made the recommendations. The committee oversees compliance audits of election campaign finances, so its makeup matters to the integrity of the 2026 election's aftermath.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Local Appeal Body
topics: public appointments;
brief: The question before Council: whether to appoint Ron Kanter, Trevor Kezwer and Gerald Swinkin to the Toronto Local Appeal Body, which decides appeals on certain land-use planning matters, for a term from July 17, 2026 to July 17, 2030. The appointments were recommended by the Nominating Panel after interviews, and Council is also asked to keep the panel's confidential attachment private because it contains personal matters about identifiable individuals. This matters because the Appeal Body decides planning disputes that affect neighbourhoods.

title: Ontario-Toronto New Deal - Advancing the Upload of the Don Valley Parkway and Frederick G. Gardiner Expressway to the Province
topics: highways; freeways; motorways; parkways
brief: Council approved the Interim Funding Approach and Framework and the Provincial Terms and Conditions for uploading the Gardiner Expressway and the Don Valley Parkway to the province, and approved the Provincial Term Sheet in principle, authorizing the City Manager to negotiate a Transfer Payment Agreement and continue negotiations with the Ministry of Transportation on implementing the upload. Council also directed staff to develop a framework for continuing public space improvements, including the Under Gardiner Public Realm Plan, as part of the negotiations. The upload would shift the cost and control of two major expressways from the City to the province.

title: Follow Up on 2026.EX31.2: Framework for Implementing a Maximum Indoor Temperature By-law
topics: temperature; heat
brief: Council received a report setting out a proposed framework for a maximum indoor temperature by-law, and directed the City Manager to report back by June 2027 with the by-law for Council approval, along with an implementation plan covering research, stakeholder engagement, key by-law components, and enforcement costs. Council also asked the Ontario government to amend the Residential Tenancies Act to prohibit above-guideline rent increases for by-law compliance costs, to introduce a 26 degrees Celsius maximum temperature standard for rental units and add cooling to the definition of ‘vital services,’ and to amend the Ontario Building Code — and asked for National Building Code changes too — to address overheating in new homes. This matters to tenants and vulnerable residents exposed to extreme heat in their homes.

title: Enhancing the City’s Approach to Reporting, Tracking and Communicating Odour Issues at the Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant
topics: wastewater; sanitary sewage; sewage; waste water
brief: This is a procedural item: Council is asked to receive a report on steps to improve how the City handles odour from the Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant after an odour event in April 2026. The actions include a new 311 service request for plant- or wastewater-related odour concerns, a new communications strategy with clearer trigger criteria for notifying the community, stronger internal incident escalation and councillor notification at Toronto Water, and capital investments including primary tank refurbishments and a future odour control facility on Coxwell Avenue. No decision is required. This matters to residents near the plant who are affected by its odour.

title: 690 to 720 Sheppard Avenue East - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor seeks Council's directions for an Ontario Land Tribunal hearing about the redevelopment at 690 to 720 Sheppard Avenue East. The 2022 applications sought two mixed-use buildings of 32 and 28 storeys; the applicant appealed in February 2025 after Council failed to decide in time, filed revised plans in June 2026, and the hearing is set to begin October 20, 2026. The recommendations are confidential legal advice, and the matter is described as urgent.

title: Ombudsman Toronto Report - No Refunds for Discontinued TTC Tickets and Tokens: An Investigation Behind How the Decision was Made
topics: public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is asked to receive the Ombudsman's report on the TTC's decision not to refund or credit discontinued tickets and tokens. The report makes eight recommendations, which TTC leadership and the Board have agreed to implement. No decision is required.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Lakeshore Arena Corporation Board
topics: arenas, board members; indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: Appointing two public members and one tenant representative to the Lakeshore Arena Corporation Board for terms ending June 26, 2028 (and until successors are appointed), goes to City Council for approval. The nominees' details stay confidential as they concern identifiable individuals.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Heritage Toronto Board of Directors
topics: board members, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Appointing eight public members to the Heritage Toronto Board of Directors — including one member from the Indigenous community — for terms ending June 26, 2030 (and until successors are appointed), goes to City Council for approval. The nominees' details stay confidential as they concern identifiable individuals.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will introduce general bills and confirming bills, which formally turn Council's decisions into by-laws. The source material gives no further detail.

title: Long-Term Care Annual Performance Report
topics: annual reports, long term care homes; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, homes for the aged; long term care centers; long term care centres; long term care facilities; nursing facilities; nursing homes
brief: This is an information item: the General Manager of Seniors Services and Long-Term Care presents the annual performance report for the city's ten long-term care homes — covering compliance with the Fixing Long-Term Care Act, ministry key performance indicators, resident and family satisfaction, and waitlist data — noting the homes outperform provincial benchmarks on clinical indicators, have more waitlisted applications, and show improved resident and family experience. The committee is asked to receive the report.

title: 2025 Draft Financial Statements and Audit Results Report
topics: annual reports, audits, financial reports, zoos; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, annual financial reports; financial statements, auditors; auditors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will consider approving the 2025 draft financial statements and audit results report. The Policy and Finance Committee reviewed the statements and the audit results report on May 1, 2026 and recommended them for board approval; the board is also asked to recommend that City Council receive the statements for information. The decision finalizes the zoo's audited financial reporting for the year ended December 31, 2025.

title: Appointment of Representative to the Canadian National Exhibition Association Membership
topics: Canadian National Exhibition, boards of management, zoos; boards of directors; boards of governors, cne; the ex
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will receive a letter providing information about appointment and membership to the Canadian National Exhibition Association. No decision is described in the source text.

title: Policy and Finance Committee Appointments
topics: appointments, zoos;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management is asked to appoint two board members to the Toronto Zoo Policy and Finance Committee. The Chief Transformation Officer recommends the board appoint two new members to the committee. The decision determines who sits on the committee that oversees the zoo's policy and finance work.

title: Election of Vice-Chair
topics: advisory committees, appointments, delegation of authority, governance; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups, governance structure; municipal governance, signing authorities
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will elect a Vice-Chair, following the vacancy left when Dr. Cynthia Holmes' term ended on April 23, 2026. Under the board's procedural by-law, the board elects a Vice-Chair at its first meeting after a vacancy; the term is two years and all members are eligible. The decision determines who will serve as the zoo board's Vice-Chair.

title: Attendance and Revenue Report - May 2026
topics: financial reports, zoos; annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will receive the attendance and revenue report for May 2026, with visitor statistics and revenue results for January 1 through May 31, 2026 and a dashboard of key metrics. The Chief Transformation Officer recommends the board receive the report for information.

title: Endangered Species Reserve Fund - 2026 Budget
topics: animals, budgets, zoos; budgets and accounts, fauna
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will receive the proposed 2026 budget for the Endangered Species Reserve Fund, which supports conservation, research and education initiatives for the protection and recovery of endangered and threatened species in Canada and globally. The Chief Science Officer recommends the board receive the report for information.

title: 2025 Conservation Impact Report
topics: conservation, zoos; environmental conservation; environmental improvements; environmental management; environmental protection; environmental stewardship; greening
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will receive the 2025 Conservation Impact Report, an annual summary of the zoo's conservation science research, community engagement, partnerships, publications, national and international outreach and conservation programs. The Chief Science Officer recommends the board receive and review the report for information.

title: Toronto Zoo Operational Update
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will receive a verbal update on zoo operations from Dolf DeJong, Chief Executive Officer of the Toronto Zoo. No recommendation is attached.

title: 2026 Exempt Staff Compensation
topics: employees, human resources, labour force, zoos; labor force; workforce, staff
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will consider a merit and cost-of-living adjustment for the zoo's exempt (non-union) staff in 2026. The CEO recommends the board approve the recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 and keep the information confidential as it concerns labour relations and employee negotiations. The decision sets the 2026 compensation adjustment for exempt zoo staff.

title: Potential Development Opportunity
topics: development, zoos; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will consider pursuing a potential development opportunity on the southeast portion of Parking Lot 1, in collaboration with the City of Toronto and a community partner. The CEO recommends the board endorse the repurposing in principle, subject to planning reviews, impact studies and engagement with the city, and direct zoo staff to advance discussions through City Corporate Real Estate Management and in collaboration with CreateTO. The decision determines whether the zoo moves forward with development talks on part of its parking lands.

title: Food Services Management Agreement
topics: agreements, contracts, zoos; tenancy agreements
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will consider authorizing negotiation of an extension to the agreement with the zoo's current vendor for food services. The CEO recommends authorizing the Chief Transformation Officer to negotiate and execute the extension on the recommended terms in Confidential Attachment 1, keep that information confidential, and incorporate any resulting budgetary changes into the 2027 budget process. The decision determines who runs the zoo's food services next.

title: Net Zero Transition Project - Scope A RFP Award
topics: agreements, renewable energy, zoos; green energy; green power, tenancy agreements
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will consider awarding RFP-01 for the Net Zero Transition Project Scope A to Ecosystem Energy Services Inc. in the amount of $45,037,625 excluding applicable taxes. The project supports the zoo's TZNet0 Environmental Sustainability Plan and the City of Toronto's TransformTO objectives through phased decarbonization, electrification, renewable energy, water conservation, infrastructure renewal and waste diversion across the zoo campus. The Director of Capital Programs and Sustainability recommends the board express support for the project and authorize the CEO to negotiate and execute the agreement.

title: Construction of Concrete Walkway and Steps at Savanna Herd Barn Project - Additional Scope
topics: agreements, construction, zoos; building, tenancy agreements
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will consider amending the construction agreement for RFQ 43, the concrete walkway and steps at the Savanna Herd Barn project, to complete additional work. The Director of Capital Program and Sustainability recommends amending the agreement up to $327,295.20, from $249,774.57, excluding applicable taxes. The decision sets the walkway project's amended commitment at $327,295.20.

title: Summer/Fall Celebrations
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will receive a PowerPoint presentation on summer and fall celebrations from Adam Huston, Director of Guest Experience. No recommendation is attached.

title: Reopening Item IB15.9: Review of the Global Equity Mandates - Revisiting the Implementation Rationale
topics: economic development, investment; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing
brief: This is a procedural item: the board chair asks the Toronto Investment Board to reopen item IB15.9 at its June 22, 2026 meeting to discuss the active-versus-passive split of the global equity portfolio and the stylistic tilt (value versus growth) of the active component. The board decides whether to reopen the item.

title: Real Assets Update - Infrastructure
topics: investment;
brief: This is a procedural item: Shortlisting potential investment managers for infrastructure under the real assets category, with the search process and firms listed in a confidential attachment to protect competitive negotiations is up for a decision by the Toronto Investment Board. Staff would then interview the shortlisted firms and report back with recommendations. The board decides on the shortlist.

title: Environmental, Social, and Governance Reporting Update
topics: economic development, investment; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing
brief: This is an information item: the Toronto Investment Board receives an ESG ratings update from MSCI on the Long Term Fund and Sinking Fund portfolios, based on March 31, 2026 holdings. Detailed reports stay confidential; only summary data is public. No decision is attached.

title: Investment Manager and Other Updates
topics: economic development, investment; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing
brief: This is an information item: the Interim Director of Capital Markets and Treasury updates the Toronto Investment Board on investment manager activities — real asset fund expense ratios, ESG reporting, the transition to a new multifactor index manager, and fund balances as of April 30, 2026. Details are in confidential attachments. The board is asked to keep them confidential.

title: Presentations from Investment Managers
topics: economic development, investment; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing
brief: This is an information item: the Toronto Investment Board hears presentations from Connor, Clark & Lunn Investment Management (active fixed income) and Leith Wheeler Investment Counsel (active fixed income). No decision is attached.

title: Sinking Fund and Long Term Fund - Performance and Compliance Update for the First Quarter of 2026
topics: economic development, investment; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing
brief: This is an information item: the Director of Capital Markets and Treasury presents the Sinking Fund and Long Term Fund performance and investment-policy compliance check for Q1 2026. The board is asked to receive the report.

title: New Appointment to the Toronto Investment Board
topics: appointments, public appointments;
brief: This is an information item: City Council appointed Lovisa McCallum to the Toronto Investment Board for a term from March 28, 2026 to March 28, 2030, filling the seat left by Kevin Adolphe.

title: Advancing More Supportive Housing to Address Homelessness and Create Pathways to Long-Term Housing Stability
topics: homelessness, housing, persons who are homeless; homeless; homeless individuals, homes; residences
brief: An item before the Housing Rights Advisory Committee proposes the city advance permanent supportive housing built rapidly with prefabricated modular units paired with wrap-around supports, targeted at people exiting homelessness — particularly those with complex mental health and addiction challenges — with intergovernmental funding and inclusive planning. The item's framing says the approach would reduce evictions, returns to homelessness, and shelter strain. The item affects how the city addresses encampments, shelter overcapacity, and rent-geared-to-income demand. Any direction would flow through the committee.

title: First Term Accomplishments and Key Priorities of the City’s Housing Rights Advisory Committee
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: This is a procedural item: the Housing Rights Advisory Committee chair highlights the committee's first-term accomplishments and summarizes priorities identified if the committee is re-established in the next council term. No decision is attached.

title: Ombudsman Toronto’s Housing Unit Three Years In: Lessons Learned and the Road Ahead
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: This is an information item: Deputy Ombudsman Reema Patel presents a reflection on the first three years of Ombudsman Toronto's Housing Unit, covering lessons learned and the road ahead. No decision is attached.

title: Overview of 2025.EX28.2 - Implementation of Ombudsman’s Recommendations and City Council Directives on the City’s Response to a Vital Services Outage in a Multi-Tenant Home
topics: housing, rental housing; homes; residences, rental properties; rental units
brief: This is an information item: Municipal Licensing and Standards updates the Housing Rights Advisory Committee on actions under council direction 2025.EX28.2 — strengthening enforcement, staff training, and interdivisional coordination to protect tenants affected by vital services outages in multi-tenant homes. No decision is attached.

title: Introduction of By-laws
topics: bonds, draft by-laws; debentures; notes, draft bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Debenture Committee will introduce a general bill and a confirming bill to enact the June debenture decisions. No policy change is proposed.

title: Authority to Issue a Debenture
topics: bonds, financial reports; annual financial reports; financial statements, debentures; notes
brief: Toronto is set to borrow $300 million through a 30-year debenture led by BMO, sold June 9, 2026, and delivered to investors June 24, 2026. The Debenture Committee is asked to approve the borrowing and introduce the enabling by-law so the proceeds can finance approved capital projects, with all costs already in the 2026 tax-supported operating budget. The decision adds $300 million of long-term debt for City infrastructure.

title: Appeal of the Chief Building Official's Decision for a Sign Variance Application for Two First Party Wall Signs at 15-35 Mercer Street
topics: sign permits, signs; billboard permits; permanent sign permits; sign variances; street banner permits; temporary sign permits, signage
brief: The Sign Variance Committee will hear an appeal of the Chief Building Official's decision on a sign variance for two illuminated first-party wall signs showing static copy at 15-35 Mercer Street. The applicant is Madison Group; the signs would sit on the uppermost storey of the west tower. The committee will decide whether to grant the variance.

title: Application for Five Variances, Each Subject to Three Conditions, Respecting One Third Party Electronic Ground Sign - 825 Milner Avenue
topics: electronic signs, signs; changeable message signs; electronic billboard signs; electronic overhead message signs, signage
brief: The Sign Variance Committee will decide on five variances that would let the Chief Building Official issue a permit for a single-faced third-party electronic ground sign at 825 Milner Avenue in Ward 25 - Scarborough Rouge Park. The applicant, Pattison Outdoor Advertising, proposes a sign up to 10.0 metres high with one rectangular face measuring 5.76 metres by 2.88 metres showing static electronic copy. Each variance would be subject to three conditions.

title: Application for One Variance, Subject to Two Conditions, Respecting One Third Party Electronic Ground Sign - 4925 Steeles Avenue West
topics: electronic signs, signs; changeable message signs; electronic billboard signs; electronic overhead message signs, signage
brief: The Sign Variance Committee will decide on one variance that would let the Chief Building Official issue a permit for a third-party electronic ground sign with two faces at 4925 Steeles Avenue West. The applicant, Permit World Consulting Services Inc, proposes a sign up to 10.0 metres high with two back-to-back faces showing static electronic copy. The variance would be subject to two conditions.

title: Housing Benchmark Report: Affordable Housing Development and Construction Costs on City-owned Sites and Comparable Sites Across Canada
topics: affordable housing, construction, costs; affordable homes; housing projects, building
brief: CreateTO's board is getting a benchmark report comparing affordable housing development and construction costs in Toronto with comparable sites in major Canadian cities. The board ordered the report in January 2026 to support city decisions on building technologies for affordable housing projects. The report includes a dataset on development and construction costs.

title: Housing Progress Update
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: CreateTO's board is getting its regular update on 2026 housing priority work: six sites under construction, four with secured proponents, one in a market offering process, eight with initial planning approvals, four undergoing initial approvals, and two managed by other city partners. The board is asked to receive the update for information.

title: Building Toronto's Housing Future - Housing Development Office 2026 Annual Toronto Builds Update and Three-Year Work Plan
topics: affordable housing, annual reports; affordable homes; housing projects, annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council has forwarded the Housing Development Office's 2026 Toronto Builds update and three-year work plan to the CreateTO board, which is asked to keep two confidential attachments private since they contain negotiating positions. No policy change is proposed.

title: Housing Development Office 2026 Annual Toronto Builds Update and Three-Year Work Plan
topics: affordable housing, annual reports; affordable homes; housing projects, annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards
brief: This is a procedural item: Housing Development Office staff will present the 2026 annual Toronto Builds update and three-year work plan, adopted by City Council on May 21, 2026, to the CreateTO board. The presentation covers directed activities and initiatives to support new homes. No decision is being asked for.

title: North York at the Centre: Directions Report for an Updated Secondary Plan
topics: Official Plans, emergency services; 9-1-1; 911; 911 calls; emergency assistance; emergency response
brief: Following council's adoption of the North York at the Centre directions in March 2026, the CreateTO board is asked to direct its CEO to assess whether emergency services facilities in the area need to be replaced or expanded. The assessment would be done with the Fire Chief, Toronto Paramedics, Toronto Police, and Corporate Real Estate Management. The request links the area's growth plan to its emergency infrastructure.

title: 2026 Annual Objectives - Chief Executive Officer - Update
topics: employees; staff
brief: This is a procedural item: the CreateTO board is asked to approve updated 2026 annual objectives for the Chief Executive Officer, now with targets, timelines, and metrics, and to keep the details confidential. No public policy decision is involved.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item RA25.4 to Give Direction on Confidential Attachments
topics: committee meetings, employees; staff
brief: This is a procedural item: the CreateTO board is asked to re-open its earlier decision on the CEO's 2025 performance appraisal to give direction on how the confidential attachments should be handled. No public policy decision is involved.

title: Chief Executive Officer's Report - June 2026
topics: advisory committees; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups
brief: This is a procedural item: CreateTO's Chief Executive Officer is reporting to the board on intergovernmental announcements, the agency's three lines of business, operational updates, and the 2026 municipal election period. The board is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Théâtre français de Toronto
brief: Member Hélène Grégoire is asking the Toronto Francophone Affairs Advisory Committee to support Théâtre français de Toronto's decades-long project to build a permanent French-language theatre venue, proposing the committee request that the City explore what it can do to help. The company, operating for nearly 60 years as Toronto's only professional French-language theatre, draws about 12,000 audience members a season and has letters of support from 71 Franco-Ontarian organizations. The committee decides whether to advance the request to the City.

title: Request for the Re-establishment of the Toronto Francophone Affairs Advisory Committee Following the 2026 Municipal Election
brief: With the committee's term ending, member Christine Michaud is asking the Toronto Francophone Affairs Advisory Committee to request that the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture take steps to re-establish the committee for the municipal term following the 2026 election, and to keep an official mechanism for dialogue between the City, Francophone organizations, and the Francophone community. The committee decides whether to make the request; continuity of its initiatives is at stake.

title: Bureau du Québec à Toronto
topics: culture (sc), ergonomics, information & communication (sc);
brief: This is an information item: the Government of Québec's Public Affairs and Francophonie Attachée will present to the committee on the Bureau du Québec à Toronto. No decision is attached — the committee simply receives the presentation.

title: Considerations for Toronto Membership in the Association Francophone des Municipalités de l'Ontario
brief: Toronto joining the Association francophone des municipalités de l'Ontario as an Individual Member for the rest of 2026 and 2027 — one staff membership for 2026 and up to four in 2027 — with the Clerk canvassing councillors interested in appointment for 2027 and a review in the third quarter of 2027 on whether to pursue a corporate membership in 2028, is up for a decision by City Council. City Council makes the final decision on membership.

title: Analysis of City Services Delivered in French
brief: This is an information item: the committee will receive the results of a city-wide survey assessing which City services are available to the public in French. No decision is attached — the findings are presented for the committee's information.

title: Toronto Francophone Affairs Advisory Committee End-of-Term Progress Report
brief: This is an information item: the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture will present the Toronto Francophone Affairs Advisory Committee's end-of-term progress report. No decision is attached — the committee simply receives the presentation.

title: Concrete Replacement at Coca-Cola Coliseum
topics: Exhibition Place, concrete, contracts, replacement;
brief: Approving a $484,000.00 contract (excluding HST, including a $20,000.00 cash allowance) with Clifford Restoration Limited for concrete replacement outside the Coca-Cola Coliseum comes before the board. The project is time-sensitive given the event and game schedule. It was the lowest compliant bid.

title: Princes' Gates Lighting Project Receives Award from the Toronto Illuminating Engineers Society
topics: Exhibition Place, awards, engineering;
brief: This is an information item: the board receives a report recognizing that the Princes' Gates lighting revitalization won the 2026 Illumination Section Award for Outdoor Lighting Design from the Toronto Illuminating Engineers Society. No policy change is proposed.

title: Agreement with the Festival Management Committee for the Toronto Caribbean Carnival 2026
topics: Exhibition Place, agreements, festivals and special events; community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals, tenancy agreements
brief: The board is set to decide whether to approve a one-year agreement with the Festival Management Committee for the 2026 Toronto Caribbean Carnival Grande Parade at Exhibition Place on Saturday, August 1, 2026, on the same terms and conditions as 2025.

title: Parking Lot CP853 Rehabilitation
topics: Exhibition Place, contracts, parking, restoration; rehabilitation (property)
brief: The decision on approving a $2,039,985.00 contract (excluding HST, including a $50,000.00 cash allowance) with Tony Battista Paving Inc. to rehabilitate Parking Lot CP853 rests with the board. The project is time-sensitive due to seasonal weather and to prevent disruptions during major events. It was the lowest compliant bid.

title: Exhibition Place Position on New Requests for Casino License
topics: Exhibition Place, casinos, gambling; bingo; lotteries; raffles
brief: Whether to grandfather the historical temporary casino operated by the Canadian National Exhibition Association during the annual fair, and to require that any new requests for casino licences at Exhibition Place come to the board for approval now sits with the board. The report cites public health evidence on the impacts of gambling expansion, and notes Council's history of opposing permanent casinos in Toronto.

title: Exhibition Place Management Report - First Quarter March 31, 2026
topics: Exhibition Place, management (activity);
brief: This is an information item: the Exhibition Place board receives the first-quarter 2026 management report from its chief executive. No policy change is proposed.

title: Exhibition Place Financial Report - First Quarter March 31, 2026
topics: Exhibition Place, financial reports; annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: This is an information item: the board receives the first-quarter 2026 financial report for all Exhibition Place program areas, with one attachment kept confidential because it contains the board's financial information. No policy change is proposed.

title: 2027 Electrical and Mechanical Services Price List - ShowTech Power and Lighting (SPL)
topics: Exhibition Place, fees, rentals; administrative fees; admission fees; admission prices; rates; service charges; user charges; user fees
brief: It's the board's call whether to approve ShowTech Power and Lighting's 2027 price list for electrical and mechanical services at events, effective January 1, 2027, with the detailed pricing kept confidential. ShowTech has been the exclusive provider of these services at Exhibition Place since 2015.

title: Public Appointment to the Board
topics: Exhibition Place, public appointments;
brief: This is an information item: City Council appointed Bhutila Karpoche to the Exhibition Place Board of Governors for a term from April 24, 2026, to March 28, 2030, with Howard Lichtman's term ending April 23, 2026. No decision is proposed.

title: Security System Upgrades Grounds-wide
topics: Exhibition Place, awards, security;
brief: The board has the final say on whether to approve a $10,084,218.70 contract (excluding HST) with Ainsworth Inc. for grounds-wide security system upgrades including CCTV cameras and card access, because the existing system needs significant upgrades and is no longer viable to maintain. The amount includes an additional price of $49,803.76 and a $200,000.00 cash allowance. It was the lowest compliant bid; deferring risks security and safety vulnerabilities.

title: Draft Financial Statements and Audit Results for the Year Ended December 31, 2025
topics: Exhibition Place, audits, financial reports; annual financial reports; financial statements, auditors; auditors
brief: KPMG is presenting the board with Exhibition Place's draft 2025 audited financial statements, a management representation letter, and an audit findings report, with an unqualified audit opinion and no significant internal control issues. The board is asked to approve the statements and related transfers, including a $0.450 million operating budget deficit subsidy received from the City of Toronto and a $2.538 million transfer payable to the City.

title: Election-Related Activities
topics: communication, elections, municipal elections; communicating; communications, polls (elections); voting
brief: This is an information item: members of the City's adjudicative boards will get a bulletin explaining their code-of-conduct obligations if they campaign or take part in the upcoming provincial or municipal elections. title: 3044 Dundas Street West - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council include 3044 Dundas Street West (including 3046 and 3048) in the Junction on the City's Heritage Register. The circa-1908 red-brick commercial main street building — with Romanesque Revival architecture and ground-level storefronts — contributes to the Dundas streetscape and the early development history of the West Toronto Junction near the railway corridor. It sits within the West Toronto Junction Heritage Conservation District study area. Listing recognizes its cultural heritage value; designation is a separate, stronger step.

title: 328 Bellamy Road North - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate 328 Bellamy Road North — the J.P. Wheler House — in Scarborough's Golfdale-Cedarbrae-Woburn neighbourhood under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The two-and-a-half-storey brick 'bank' house, built in 1867 into a hillside above West Highland Creek with Gothic elements, belonged to local agriculturalist, mill owner and politician J.P. Wheler, who served as reeve 18 times between 1851 and 1875. Designation is the first legal step toward protecting the property's heritage attributes.

title: 4150 Yonge Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate 4150 Yonge Street — the John Street Workers Cottages — in Bedford Park-Nortown under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The two single-storey Ontario Cottage-style houses, built in 1860 by carpenter Robert Gray and relocated here in the 1980s from John Street, housed tradespeople and millworkers' families until the area's late-20th-century redevelopment. Designation is the first legal step toward protecting the properties' heritage attributes.

title: 34 Jason Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate 34 Jason Road — the Elm Bank Piggery — in Etobicoke's Thistletown community under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The single-family house-form building from about 1921 (with a 1926–1933 extension atop mid-19th-century foundations that once supported the Grubb family piggery) was listed on the Heritage Register in 2006 and is one of eighteen pre-1870 listed properties identified for designation under the City's Bill 23 implementation. It was later owned by photographer Bruce Metcalfe and family. Designation is the first legal step toward protecting the property's heritage attributes.
