The update is subsequently consolidated into the city's variance reporting to City Council.

title: Fare Collection Update
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, fare media, fares; air fares; airline fares; rail fares; taxi fares; transportation fares, transit tickets; transit tokens, ttc
brief: TTC staff update the Board on the TTC-Metrolinx Master E-Fare Collection Outsourcing Agreement, the 2012 deal expiring November 28, 2027, whose automatic five-year renewal no longer applies after Metrolinx opted out in May 2025 to negotiate a new contract. At its April 16, 2026 meeting the Board directed staff to run a public market sounding on value for money in automated fare collection offerings. The Board is asked to adopt the recommendations in the confidential attachment. The decision shapes how fare collection is managed after 2027.

title: Bloor-Yonge Capacity Improvements Project - Platform Edge Doors and Net Zero
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, infrastructure, projects, subway stations; ttc
brief: Including Net Zero requirements and platform edge doors in the Bloor-Yonge Capacity Improvements project, along with the infrastructure to enable the doors as part of the system-wide platform protection program, goes to the TTC Board for endorsement. The report assesses the impacts of both additions, following the February 2025 board report that awarded the progressive design-build development phase to Kenaidan Murphy Joint Venture and committed to reporting back by the second quarter of 2026; the assessment puts the cost at $6.35 million. The Board's endorsement determines whether the features are built into the project.

title: Advancing Safety on the TTC: 2026 Focus Areas
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, infrastructure, safety, subway stations; public safety, ttc
brief: TTC staff present the 2026 focus areas plan for advancing safety on the TTC, building on the Community Safety, Security, and Well-Being Plan 2024-2028. The focus areas are visible and mobile staff deployment including in-vehicle presence; technology, station and system enhancements; and continued coordinated response connecting people to supports; an attached update also assesses platform protection technologies. The plan frames safety as both incident reduction and how customers experience the system daily. The Board is asked to receive the plan.

title: Presentation: Indigenous Wayfinding on the TTC
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, wayfinding; ttc
brief: Cameron Stewart will present to the TTC Board on Indigenous wayfinding on the TTC. The presentation explores an Indigenous perspective on transit wayfinding, using Queen Station as a case study for how Indigenous knowledge systems, principles, narratives and spatial understandings can be integrated into the TTC's wayfinding framework for clearer, more inclusive and culturally responsive navigation. The Board is asked to receive the presentation for information.

title: Approved Minutes of the Advisory Committee on Accessible Transit (ACAT) General Monthly Meeting of March 26, 2026
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, accessibility, advisory committees, specialized paratransit services; accessible public transportation; accessible transit; accessible transit service; door to door service; special mobility services; wheel trans; wheel-trans; wheeltrans, ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups, barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the TTC Board will receive the approved minutes of the Advisory Committee on Accessible Transit (ACAT) general monthly meeting of March 26, 2026. The meeting covered the TTC's accessibility plans for the FIFA World Cup, including communication about Wheel-Trans pick-up and drop-off locations, training for escorting people with accessibility needs, website improvements for screen readers, and Line 5 and Line 6 station descriptions. The Board is asked to receive the minutes for information.

title: Coordination of Closures - by Chair Jamaal Myers, seconded by Commissioner Ausma Malik
topics: Toronto Transit Commission; ttc
brief: Chair Jamaal Myers is bringing a motion, seconded by Commissioner Ausma Malik, to improve coordination of transit closures with other construction and events. Each year the TTC adopts a subway and streetcar closures forecast for infrastructure and state-of-good-repair work, but it is developed with limited formal coordination with city divisions and regional agencies responsible for roads, major events and parallel transit. The motion directs TTC leadership to expand collaboration on the 2027 and future forecasts to avoid overlapping impacts where possible.

title: Commemorating Former TTC Chair Howard Moscoe - by Chair Jamaal Myers, seconded by Vice-Chair Joe Mihevc
topics: Toronto Transit Commission; ttc
brief: Chair Jamaal Myers is bringing a motion, seconded by Vice-Chair Joe Mihevc, to commemorate former TTC Chair Howard Moscoe. Mr. Moscoe served on Toronto-area councils for 32 years, including Toronto City Council from 1998 to 2010, and served on the TTC Board from 1992 to 2006, as Chair from 1998 to 2000 and also as Commissioner and Vice Chair. The TTC Board is asked to approve the commemoration.

title: Chief Executive Officer’s Report - May 2026
topics: Toronto Transit Commission; ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the TTC Board will receive the CEO's Report for May 2026, the monthly performance overview. This edition focuses on subway service, with key performance indicators through the end of March 2026 and a comparison to the November 2025 results; copies also go to City Council members, the City Manager and the CFO and are posted publicly. The Board is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Confidential Ombudsman Toronto Report
topics: Toronto Transit Commission; ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: Ombudsman Toronto has submitted a report for the TTC Board's consideration, but the investigation is not complete. The Board is asked to keep the information confidential under section 173(1) of the City of Toronto Act, 2006, which covers ongoing Ombudsman investigations.

title: TTC Pension Plan Bylaw Amendments
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, pensions; ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the TTC Board is asked to note bylaw amendments approved by the TTC Pension Fund Society board. The changes update the base year period used to calculate retiring employees' pensions to include 2025, provide a 2.00 percent increase to pensioners currently receiving a pension (both provided annually since 2011 given the plan's strong financial position), rename board positions from President and Vice President to Chair and Vice Chair, and make administrative changes to meeting and officer rules.

title: Requesting a 7 Bathurst Express Bus - by Commissioner Josh Matlow, seconded by Commissioner Dianne Saxe
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, bus routes, express bus routes; express routes; limited-stop rocket services, ttc
brief: Commissioner Josh Matlow is bringing a motion, seconded by Commissioner Dianne Saxe, requesting a 7 Bathurst Express Bus. About 35,000 people rely on the 7 Bathurst bus daily, and the motion notes persistent congestion on Bathurst Street causing speed, reliability, bunching and gapping problems; Council approved speed and reliability measures for the route in October 2025. The TTC Board is asked to direct staff on establishing the express service.

title: Review of Subway Capacity Constraints and Infrastructure Readiness for Protected/Major Transit Station Areas Compliance and Provincial Densification Mandates - by Commissioner Liane Kim, seconded by Commissioner Josh Matlow
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, legislation, planning & development (sc); acts, ttc
brief: Commissioner Liane Kim is bringing a motion, seconded by Commissioner Josh Matlow, for a review of subway capacity constraints and infrastructure readiness in light of provincial densification mandates and Protected/Major Transit Station Area requirements. The motion notes that Ontario's Bill 23 aims for 1.5 million homes by 2031, that high-density growth near subway stations will strain TTC infrastructure and finances, and references $2.3 billion. The TTC Board is asked to approve the review.

title: MM39.50 Safer Subways: Making Public Safety a Priority and Restoring Confidence to Toronto Transit Commission Riders Across Toronto
topics: Toronto Transit Commission; ttc
brief: City Council's March 2026 item MM39.50, Safer Subways, asked the TTC Board to act on public safety and rider confidence. Council requested a funded 10-year plan for platform edge doors (including a multi-station pilot, Line 1 high-priority stations and the Bloor-Yonge capacity project) reported back through the 2027 budget process, plus published cleanliness standards for all subway stations with public station-level performance reporting no later than the first quarter of 2027. The TTC Board is asked to direct the CEO, in partnership with the City Manager, to develop the plan.

title: Honouring Frederick Langdon Hubbard
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, facility naming; park naming, ttc
brief: TTC staff recommend renaming the Subway Operations Building at the Hillcrest Complex the Frederick Hubbard Building, to honour Frederick Langdon Hubbard, the first Black Canadian appointed Chair of the TTC Board, on the 100-year anniversary of his 1930 appointment. The site was chosen for its visibility, connection to Hubbard's life and work and feasibility, following consultation with TTC employees including the ATU 113 Black Caucus and Black employees across roles, and endorsement by the TTC's employee inclusion and belonging committee. The TTC Board is asked to approve the renaming. The renaming is estimated to cost $6,000 for new signage and installation, with funding to be requested in the 2027 operating budget.

title: Draft Consolidated Financial Statements of Toronto Transit Commission for the Year Ended December 31, 2025
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, financial reports; annual financial reports; financial statements, ttc
brief: The draft consolidated financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025 go to the TTC Board for approval, before they go to City Council for information through the City's Audit Committee. The statements show an accounting surplus of $758.1 million, an increase of $254.9 million over the 2024 surplus; the TTC also adopted amended public-sector accounting rules for leased assets effective January 1, 2025, which staff determined had no impact on the reported amounts.

title: KPMG LLP Audit Findings Report on the Toronto Transit Commission Consolidated Financial Statements for the Year Ended December 31, 2025
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, financial reports; annual financial reports; financial statements, ttc
brief: KPMG's findings report on its audit of the TTC's consolidated financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025, goes to the TTC Board for approval, before it is forwarded to the City Clerk for the next City Audit Committee meeting. The report details key audit risks, the testing performed and the conclusions, and KPMG proposes to issue an unqualified (clean) independent auditor's report on the statements. The Board's approval moves the audited statements toward City Council.

title: Toronto Transit Commission - 2026 Follow-up - Status of Previous Auditor General’s Recommendations
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, audits, buses, finance (sc), information and communication technology; auditors; auditors, city buses; coaches (buses), ict; information and communication systems; information and technology; information technology; it, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item for the TTC Board: the Auditor General's 2026 follow-up on the status of her earlier recommendations. The follow-up reviewed 41 of 45 recommendations that management reported as fully implemented or no longer applicable, drawn from nine reports covering TTC bus maintenance, non-revenue fleet management, accounts payable, a 2016 briefing-note complaint review and others. The Board is asked to receive the follow-up, which verifies whether the recommendations were fully implemented and their intended benefits achieved.

title: Chief Executive Officer Performance and Objectives
brief: This is a procedural item: the TTC Board will receive information on the Chief Executive Officer's performance and objectives. The Board is asked to keep the information in Confidential Attachment 1 private in its entirety, as it concerns personal matters about an identifiable individual.

title: Administrative Inquiry - Community Bus Routes
brief: Chair Jamaal Myers has submitted an administrative inquiry for the June 3, 2026 TTC Board meeting seeking clarity on the Community Bus program's ridership, the cost of continuing the service and the per-ride subsidy. Under the board's proceedings by-law, the Board can receive the inquiry or refer it to the appropriate TTC official or department. The inquiry would put the program's ridership and costs on the public record.

title: Exploring opportunities related to the Spirit Garden in Nathan Phillips Square
topics: aboriginal services;
brief: The Aboriginal Affairs Advisory Committee discussed opportunities around the Spirit Garden in Nathan Phillips Square, including possibly transferring ownership to an Indigenous non-profit organization. The committee recommended that the Executive Committee direct the City Manager to report back in the second quarter of 2027 on transferring ownership of the Spirit Garden site to the Council of Fire, an Indigenous non-profit organization, which would conclude the external discussions on the site's ownership.

title: Exploring opportunities to Convey City-owned Lands Operated by Indigenous non-profit organizations for Housing or Shelter Purposes
topics: aboriginal services;
brief: The Aboriginal Affairs Advisory Committee discussed exploring ways to transfer City-owned land that is or could be operated by an Indigenous non-profit organization for housing or shelter purposes. The committee recommended that the Executive Committee have the Deputy City Manager for Community Development and Social Services, working with the Housing Secretariat and Shelter and Support Services, review opportunities to convey city land to Indigenous non-profit operators for a nominal amount and report back by the second quarter of 2027.

title: Update from the Aboriginal Affairs Advisory Committee Indigenous Identity Vetting Working Group
topics: aboriginal services;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Aboriginal Affairs Advisory Committee's Indigenous Identity Vetting Working Group will provide an update on its progress to date. The source material gives no further detail. No decision is required.

title: Terms of Reference Review
topics: aboriginal services;
brief: This is a procedural item: the committee will discuss recommendations from the Toronto Aboriginal Support Services Council on updating its Terms of Reference. No decision is required.

title: Purchase Order Amendment for General Contracting Services Number 6056841 with Pomerleau Inc., for General Contracting Services for Toronto Paramedic Services Multi-Function Station at 300 Progress Avenue
topics: builders, construction, emergency medical services stations, paramedics, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, ambulance stations; ems stations, building, contractors; renovators
brief: The city wants to amend Pomerleau Inc.'s general contracting purchase order for the Toronto Paramedic Services multi-function station at 300 Progress Avenue, extending the completion date from April 30, 2028 to September 30, 2029 after unforeseen site conditions and design coordination issues hit the schedule. The station is meant to handle growing paramedic call demand with more targeted crew deployment across the city.

title: Award of Negotiated Request for Proposals Doc4711617964 to CTI Working Environments for the Supply, Delivery and Installation of Office Furniture
topics: city-owned properties, contracts, employees, offices, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, city owned properties; city properties, staff
brief: The city wants to award CTI Working Environments a three-year blanket contract (plus two one-year options) worth up to $75,900,905 ($77,236,761 net of HST recoveries) — the report also cites $9,114,652 and $16.7 million — for the non-exclusive supply, delivery, and installation of office furniture and task chairs, coordinated with construction work. The furniture supports the council-approved touch-it-once program of repairs, accessibility upgrades, and net-zero work at City Hall, Metro Hall, and the new Etobicoke Civic Centre. The city only pays for goods actually ordered and delivered.

title: Award of Doc5491818166 to Pomerleau Inc., for Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant Digester Gas Compressors, Dryers and Chillers Installation and Amendment to Purchase Order 6052432 for Associated Engineering (Ont.) Ltd for Construction Administration Services
topics: construction, contracts, purchasing, wastewater treatment plants; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, building, sewage treatment plants; treatment plants; waste water treatment plants
brief: The city wants to award Pomerleau Inc. a $55,637,202 ($56,616,416 net of HST recoveries) contract to install digester gas compressors, dryers, and chillers at the Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant — including a novated $8,755 ($8,909,468 including HST recoveries) amount from pre-purchase vendor Aerzen Canada Inc. — and to add $4,086,496, ($4,158,419 net of HST recoveries) to Associated Engineering (Ont.) Ltd.'s construction administration purchase order, raising it from $1,548,956 ($1,576,218) to $5,635,452 ($5,734,636). The figures reflect the base work, provisional items, and contingency for the plant upgrade.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order Number 6055184 with Hariri Pontarini Architects for the Enhanced State of Good Repair, Accessibility and Net Zero Project at St. Lawrence Centre for Performing Arts
topics: city-owned properties, contracts, cultural facilities, projects, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, art centres; arts centres; cultural attractions; cultural centres, city owned properties; city properties
brief: The city wants to add $8,821,675 ($8,976,936 net of HST recoveries) to Hariri Pontarini Architects' purchase order for the St. Lawrence Centre for the Performing Arts, raising it from $5,515,438 ($5,612,510) to $14,337,113 ($14,589,446) — the report also cites $34 million, $3 million, $5.5 million, and $84.5 million in related program figures. Council previously cancelled the centre's redevelopment project and redirected the contract to an enhanced state-of-good-repair program with accessibility upgrades and net-zero objectives. The amendment funds the revised consulting scope.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order 6054643 with AECOM Canada ULC for Engineering Design Services at the Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant for the Old Primary Sedimentation Tanks Upgrades Project
topics: construction, contracts, engineering, purchasing, wastewater treatment plants; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, building, sewage treatment plants; treatment plants; waste water treatment plants
brief: The General Government Committee is asked to add $884,434 ($900,000 net of HST recoveries) to AECOM Canada ULC's purchase order for engineering design of the Old Primary Sedimentation Tanks upgrades at the Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant, raising it from $3,050,880 ($3,104,575) to $3,935,314 ($4,004,575). The increase funds additional design services for scope changes tied to the project's original objectives. The committee decides on the amendment.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order 6053845 with Maple Reinders Constructors Limited for the Biosolids Master Plan Implementation Project and South Facility Upgrades Project at Highland Creek Treatment Plant
topics: construction, contracts, projects, purchasing, wastewater treatment plants; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, building, sewage treatment plants; treatment plants; waste water treatment plants
brief: Adding $9,827,044 ($10,000,000 net of HST recoveries) to Maple Reinders Constructors Limited's purchase order for the Biosolids Master Plan and South Facility upgrades at the Highland Creek Treatment Plant, raising it from $267,115,742 ($271,816,979) to $276,942,786 ($281,816,979) would get the General Government Committee's approval. The increase pays for extra work found during construction — ventilation and process mechanical changes, electrical cable removals, and unforeseen site conditions. The committee decides on the amendment.

title: Non-Union Separation Costs for 2025
topics: employees, employment termination, labour relations, severance pay; collective bargaining; employee relations; labor relations; union-management relations, employee exit; layoff; termination of employment, severance payment, staff
brief: This is an information item: the General Government Committee receives the 2025 report on separation costs for non-union employees the city terminated without just cause, as required after a 2014 Auditor General review. Separation payments are decided case by case under provincial legislation and court-considered factors, and three 2025 matters remain outstanding with possible further financial implications. No decision is attached.

title: Toronto Fire Department Superannuation and Benefit Fund - Funding Valuation Report as at December 31, 2025
topics: benefits, costs, employment & labour (sc), fire and rescue services, pensions; fire fighting; fire services; fire suppression; firefighting; rescue; rescue operations; search and rescue
brief: This is an information item: the General Government Committee receives the December 31, 2025 funding valuation of the Toronto Fire Department Superannuation and Benefit Fund, prepared by RSM Canada LLP. The valuation confirms a 1.10 per cent automatic cost-of-living increase in pensioner benefits effective January 1, 2026, paid from fund surpluses under the plan's by-law — council doesn't vote on the increase itself. Cited valuation figures are $159.3, $160.7, $99.3, $112.8, $60.0, $47.9, $159.1, $160.5, $97.5, $106.1, $61.6, and $54.4.

title: Amendment to Blanket Contract 47025022 with Wintergreen Learning Materials for the Supply and Delivery of Children's Furniture, Toys and Manipulatives for various Children's Services locations
topics: child care facilities, contracts, early childhood education, education (sc), purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, child care agencies; child care centres; day cares; day nurseries; home care agencies; home child care providers; nursery schools, early education; ece; kindergartens; pre-school education; preschool education; preschool learning
brief: The city wants to add $900,000 ($915,840 net of HST recoveries) to the Wintergreen Learning Materials contract for children's furniture, toys, and learning materials for Children's Services locations, raising it from $5,600,000 ($5,698,560) to $6,500,000 ($6,614,400). The increase uses part of $4.18 million in provincial Professional Learning funding that wasn't known when the contract was sourced, mainly to buy resource kits for licensed childcare and EarlyON programs supporting inclusive early learning. The General Government Committee decides on the amendment.

title: Implementation of Construction Management at Risk Delivery Model for Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant Integrated Pumping Station Construction Contract 3
topics: construction, contracts, projects, sewer and water infrastructure, wastewater treatment plants; building, sewage treatment plants; treatment plants; waste water treatment plants, sewer and water services; water and sewer infrastructure; water management systems
brief: This is an information item: staff are telling the General Government Committee about the plan to use a Construction Management at Risk delivery model — where a construction manager advises during design and then acts as general contractor — for the Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant Integrated Pumping Station Construction Contract 3. The model is described as increasingly used in Ontario for large complex municipal infrastructure. The committee is asked only to receive the report.

title: Summary of Open Competitive Awards Made by the Chief Procurement Officer from April 11 to May 12, 2026
topics: awards, contracts, funding, projects, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, financing
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Procurement Officer reports to the General Government Committee on competitive contracts awarded from April 11 to May 12, 2026, under the officer's authority to award solicitations up to $30 million with terms up to five years. The committee is asked only to receive the report.

title: Implementation of a Food Safety Management Plan for Special Events
topics: health; health coverage
brief: Toronto Public Health developed an online Food Safety Management Plan that walks special-event organizers through safe food handling, risk assessment, vendor oversight, and emergency planning — launched voluntarily in January 2025 after the board directed it, with early users reportedly giving strong support. The item affects the thousands of street festivals, farmers' markets, and other events each year, many concentrated on summer weekends. Any direction on the plan's next steps would come from the board.

title: 2026 and 2027 Toronto Urban Health Fund Allocations and Review Process
topics: health; health coverage
brief: The Board of Health is asked to authorize the Medical Officer of Health to allocate $2.157 million in 2026 and $1.051 million in 2027 from the public health operating budget to the Toronto Urban Health Fund, renewing grants to 21 previously approved community projects for HIV and substance-use prevention, plus up to $0.900 million in each of 2026 and 2027 to the Ontario HIV Treatment Network for a pilot aligning the fund with the Toronto to Zero initiative. The interim renewal process streamlines reporting to reduce administrative burden on community organizations. The board decides on the allocations.

title: Toronto Public Health's Nursing Recruitment and Retention Strategy
topics: health, nurses; health coverage
brief: The Board of Health keeps pushing Toronto Public Health's nursing recruitment and retention strategy and has the Medical Officer of Health report back on it. Nurses — public health nurses and registered practical nurses — are the division's largest regulated workforce and deliver programs across communities. The strategy addresses workforce trends, recruitment, retention, and workplace culture. The board decides on the direction.

title: Election-Related Activities
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee is circulating a bulletin to help members of the city's adjudicative boards who plan to take part in the upcoming provincial general election or municipal election understand their obligations. The bulletin covers the Code of Conduct for Members of Adjudicative Boards. It is guidance, not a decision.

title: 3434 Eglinton Ave East, 904 - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 26 131475 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee will hear the property owner's appeal of a property standards order issued March 19, 2026 for 3434 Eglinton Avenue East, unit 904 (file 26 131475 PRS 00 IV). The committee can confirm, change, or cancel the order. The hearing gives the owner a chance to challenge the city's maintenance or repair requirements.

title: 3434 Eglinton Ave East, 701 - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 26 133902 PRS 00 IV
topics: draft by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; draft bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the owner of 3434 Eglinton Avenue East, unit 701 is appealing a property standards order issued March 25, 2026 (file 26 133902 PRS 00 IV) to the Property Standards Committee. The committee hears the appeal and can uphold, amend, or rescind the order.

title: 3434 Eglinton Ave East, 601 - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 26 124536 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: an appeal of the property standards order for 3434 Eglinton Avenue East, unit 601 goes before the Property Standards Committee. The order was issued March 6, 2026 (file 26 124536 PRS 00 IV). The committee will decide whether the order stands, changes, or is cancelled.

title: 3131 Eglinton Avenue East - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number 25 256381 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal law, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee will hear the property owner's appeal of a property standards order issued November 25, 2025 for 3131 Eglinton Avenue East (file 25 256381 PRS 00 IV). The committee can confirm, change, or cancel the order. The hearing gives the owner a chance to challenge the city's maintenance or repair requirements.

title: Contract Award for SAP Third Party Support and Enhancement Services
topics: contracts;
brief: The Toronto Parking Authority asks its board to award Deloitte Canada a five-year contract of approximately $1,206,002.76, excluding HST, for SAP third-party support and enhancement services following a competitive RFP. SAP is the organization's system of record for financial management, procurement, asset and maintenance operations and human resources.

title: Contract Award for Broadband and Managed Network Services
topics: contracts;
brief: The Toronto Parking Authority asks its board to authorize using the Province of Ontario's Vendor of Record arrangement to contract Bell Canada for broadband and managed network (SD-WAN/SASE) services — approximately $7,109,302, ($7,109,302,) excluding HST over five years — replacing end-of-life network infrastructure that no longer meets performance, security and reliability needs.

title: Contract Award for Microsoft Cloud Subscriptions
topics: contracts;
brief: The Toronto Parking Authority asks its board to authorize a three-year Enterprise Subscription Agreement with Microsoft Canada Ltd., not to exceed $3,850,060, ($3,850,060,) excluding HST, making Microsoft its enterprise technology partner across productivity, customer engagement, data and analytics, AI and cloud hosting for its parking, Bike Share and EV operations.

title: Delegation of Authority Update: February 1, 2026 - April 30, 2026
topics: delegation of authority; signing authorities
brief: This is a procedural item: the board receives the delegation-of-authority update for February 1, 2026 to April 30, 2026, covering commitments made under the President's authority — up to $500,000 per commitment, raised from $250,000 in 2021. The update reports how the President used the delegated spending authority.

title: Summary of Legal Disputes Update - May 2026
topics: legal matters; legal issues
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Parking Authority updates its board on legal disputes — supplier disputes, personal injuries, commercial tenancy disputes and trademark protection — noting it carries general liability insurance and has assigned counsel and adjusters. Details are in a confidential attachment. The board is asked to receive the update.

title: Toronto Parking Authority - 2026 March 31 Year-to-Date Financial Performance (First Three Months Results)
topics: finance (sc);
brief: The Toronto Parking Authority's operating income for the first three months of 2026 was $11.2 million — $1.4 million below plan and $0.9 million below 2025. Total revenue was $37.6 million, $2.4 million below plan and $1.4 million below the prior year, on 5.7 million trips — 0.9 million below plan and 0.6 million below prior year. On-street revenue was $13.8 million, $2.6 million below plan on 0.8 million fewer trips after winter storm closures. The report also cites $26.4 million, $3.9 million, $34.2 million, $42.5 million and $1.5 million. The board is asked to receive the results.

title: Toronto Parking Authority - 2025 Annual Report
topics: annual reports; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards
brief: The Toronto Parking Authority asks its board to receive its 2025 annual report, summarizing key accomplishments: 32.3 million trips, North America's largest municipal parking operator, North America's third-largest bike share program and Canada's largest municipal EV charging network. The report cites $893,000, $14.6 million, $48.4 million, $3.6 million, $174.8 million and $11.5 million.

title: Toronto Parking Authority - 2026 Follow-up Status of Previous Auditor General’s Recommendations
topics: audits; auditors; auditors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Auditor General's follow-up on outstanding recommendations reviews seven recommendations reported as fully implemented, from three reports — the 2016 audit of revenue operations at off-street facilities, observations on a land acquisition at Finch Avenue West and Arrow Road, and a third report. The board is asked to receive the follow-up verifying implementation.

title: On Street Parking Rate Increases in Ward 18
topics: parking;
brief: This is a procedural item: after the board adopted 2026 on-street parking rate changes, the local councillor raised concerns about rates in Willowdale (Ward 18). The board is asked to refer Councillor Lily Cheng's request to the President for consideration in future budget years.

title: Protecting Chinatown as a Cultural District - Chinatown (Larch Street) parking garage
topics: parking;
brief: This is a procedural item: following City Council's March 2026 adoption of Item MM39.53, the Toronto Parking Authority board is asked to give high priority to completing planned safety and other upgrades to the Chinatown (Larch Street) parking garage in 2026. The upgrades affect safety for garage users.

title: Short Term Parking at the Price Street Green P Lot
topics: parking;
brief: This is a procedural item: following City Council's March 2026 adoption of Item MM39.7, the Toronto Parking Authority board is asked to designate at least 20 spots in the Price Street Green P lot as non-renewable short-term parking (maximum three hours) for customers of local restaurants and businesses. The change affects parking turnover near the businesses.

title: 10-Year Toronto Parking Authority Fleet Replacement and Decarbonization Program (2026 to 2035) Phase One
topics: city vehicles, city vehicles; city owned vehicles; city-owned vehicles; corporate fleet, city owned vehicles; city-owned vehicles; corporate fleet
brief: The Toronto Parking Authority asks its board to approve Phase One (2026–2028) of a 10-year fleet replacement and decarbonization program, with spending authority of $3,300,000 ($3,300,000,) excluding HST to replace 30 end-of-life vehicles and procure fleet vehicles and related equipment. The phase starts the organization's shift to a more sustainable fleet.

title: Contract Award - 2026-CS-VAR-E1030 Security Enhancements - Pedestrian Access Controls Implementation Retainer
topics: contracts;
brief: The Toronto Parking Authority asks its board to award a $1,200,000 contract to Smith and Andersen Consulting Engineering for design support and construction oversight for security upgrades — pedestrian access controls — at twelve car parks, following the board's May 15, 2025 security framework discussion. The report also cites $500,000 and $600,000. The upgrades affect safety for customers using the twelve facilities.

title: Contract Award - 2026-CON-CP404-C10 Systems Operations Centre Construction
topics: contracts, contracts;
brief: The Toronto Parking Authority asks its board to award a $5,344,982.72 construction contract (excluding HST) for Phase Two of the Systems Operations Centre at 95 Beecroft Road (Car Park 404), and to amend the consulting contract with Barry Bryan Associates to $847,500 (excluding HST) for expanded construction-phase services. title: 390, 394, 396 and 398 Spadina Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 14-storey mixed-use building with 54 homes and ground-floor commercial space is proposed for 390 to 398 Spadina Road, and City Council is asked to approve the zoning amendment. The owner must provide a tenant assistance plan for the five existing rental units that would be demolished, backed by a lawyer's undertaking to the city. The building would stand 49.2 metres tall with 9,430 square metres of floor area.

title: 1233 Yonge Street and 9 Woodlawn Avenue East - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, rental housing, tenants; rental properties; rental units, renters; tenancy agreements
brief: Forty rental units at 1233 Yonge Street and 9 Woodlawn Avenue East would be demolished for the proposed 47-storey, 730-unit building, and City Council is asked to approve the rental housing demolition application. The owner must replace all 40 rentals, protect them for 20 years, and provide a tenant assistance plan giving existing tenants the right to return at similar rents plus financial compensation. The report also recommends a residential demolition permit with a $20,000.00 financial condition.

title: Ontario Place Event - RBC Amphitheatre 2026 Traffic Management Strategy
topics: concerts, entertainment establishments, traffic management; entertainment facilities, traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations
brief: The decision on letting Live Nation Canada put up temporary fencing on the Lake Shore Boulevard West boulevard between Ontario Drive and Strachan Avenue, from May 21 to October 9, 2026, as part of its traffic management plan for concerts at the Ontario Place RBC Amphitheatre rests with City Council. The fencing is meant to discourage illegal stopping along Lake Shore during concerts, which has created traffic and pedestrian safety problems. Council approval is required because Transportation Services cannot issue a street event permit longer than four consecutive days.

title: 1233 Yonge Street and 9 Woodlawn Avenue East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council is set to decide whether to approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments for a 47-storey mixed-use building at 1233 Yonge Street and 9 Woodlawn Avenue East, with 730 homes including 40 replacement rental units. The Official Plan amendment is needed to permit the 155-metre height. A related rental demolition application is being considered at the same community council meeting.

title: Pedestrianizing Church Street Pilot
topics: community development, development, pedestrians, transportation; community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development, developing land; development (land); land development, pedestrianization, transportation services
brief: Councillor Chris Moise is asking City Council to close Church Street to vehicles between Wellesley Street East and Alexander Street from June 19 to August 21, 2026 for a pedestrianization pilot run with the Church-Wellesley Village BIA, with east-west streets staying open. The stretch was chosen because it has hosted large festivals like Pride and Halloween on Church and has no dedicated bus or streetcar routes, limiting disruption to TTC service. Results would be evaluated after the pilot.

title: Improving Traffic and Pedestrian Safety on Lansdowne Avenue
topics: pedestrians, safety, traffic, traffic regulations; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, pedestrianization, public safety
brief: Approving parking changes on Lansdowne Avenue north of Davenport Road — banning standing on the west side and stopping on part of the east side — after residents reported speeding, poor sightlines on the curve, and conflicts with cyclists and pedestrians near Earlscourt Park is on City Council's agenda. Councillor Alejandra Bravo's motion follows a neighbourhood walk with residents and city staff; Transportation Services recommends the changes as urgent.

title: Establishing an Accessible Loading Zone on Oakwood Avenue
topics: accessibility, loading zones, parking, parking regulations; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: A resident on Oakwood Avenue who uses TTC Wheel-Trans would get an accessible loading zone on the east side of the street, between Glenhurst Avenue and St. Clair Avenue West, in effect 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily. City Council is asked to designate the zone, which would remove two daytime parking spaces but give the resident — and neighbours with mobility needs — a reliable pickup and drop-off spot.

title: Traffic Improvements: Left Turn Prohibition-Bathurst Street and Albert Wiggan Lane
topics: traffic, traffic regulations, turn prohibitions (traffic); motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: The call on whether to ban northbound left turns at all times at Bathurst Street and Albert Wiggan Lane, with displaced left turns made at St. Clair Avenue West and Raglan Avenue, about 150 metres away belongs to City Council. The report follows the 2026 St. Clair and Bathurst planning framework, whose transportation assessment identified ways to improve safety and traffic flow; council approval is required because the TTC runs transit on Bathurst Street.

title: 83-97 River Street and 2-4 Labatt Avenue - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
topics: condominium housing, construction, road closures; building, condominiums; condos, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: City Council has the final say on whether to extend construction-staging closures around 83-97 River Street and 2-4 Labatt Avenue for another 44 months — May 21, 2026 to December 31, 2029 — covering the east sidewalk, northbound bike lane, and parking lay-by on River Street, plus parts of Labatt Avenue and Carfrae Lane. The project was paused after 2022 because of market conditions and has been repositioned from a 34-storey condo to a purpose-built rental building. The parking machines in the staging area charge $3.25 per hour.

title: Spadina Road, between Lowther Avenue and Kendal Avenue - Toronto Transit Commission Subway Ventilation Equipment Replacement - Construction Staging Area
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, construction, heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems, replacement; air conditioning; air conditioning systems; boilers; climate control systems; cooling systems; furnaces; heat; heating systems; hvac; ventilation; ventilation systems, building, ttc
brief: The TTC plans to replace end-of-life subway ventilation equipment in Spadina Station's Line 1 shafts, and City Council is asked to approve temporary lane closures and turn bans on Spadina Road between Lowther and Kendal Avenues for 15 months, from October 2026 to December 2027. The northbound and southbound through lanes would close, with one curb lane kept open each way to maintain two-way traffic; eastbound and westbound left turns would be banned at all times at Lowther. The report also references a $2.00 fee amount.

title: 54 - 66 Fraser Avenue and 68 Fraser Avenue (147 Liberty Street) - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property, Demolition of Heritage Attributes and the Demolition of a Building under Sections 33, 34(1)1 and 34(1)2 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Refusal
topics: demolitions, heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff want City Council to refuse heritage alterations and the demolition of heritage features at the designated factory buildings at 54-66 Fraser Avenue and 68 Fraser Avenue (entered at 147 Liberty Street) — an early-20th-century industrial complex — tied to a proposed 55-storey mixed-use tower whose planning application is already before the Ontario Land Tribunal. The proposal would fully retain and restore the building at 68 Fraser and the street-facing façades at 54-66 Fraser while demolishing the rest. Staff recommend refusal of the heritage application.

title: 257, 259 and 291 Lake Shore Boulevard East, 2 Small Street and 200 Queens Quay East - Class 4 Noise Area Classification (NPC-300)
topics: land use, noise, noise control; amplified music; construction noise; loud music; noise pollution; traffic noise, noise barriers; sound barriers
brief: Before City Council for a decision: classify the Quayside development blocks at 257, 259, and 291 Lake Shore Boulevard East, 2 Small Street, and 200 Queens Quay East as a Class 4 noise area under the provincial noise guideline. The classification allows higher permitted sound levels for the new homes than would otherwise apply near existing industry — here, Redpath Sugar and Amrize — with noise control measures required through site plan approval before the holding provision can be lifted and development proceeds. Studies by RWDI, peer-reviewed by Arcadis, conclude the classification is appropriate.

title: 26 to 36 Mountview Avenue and 21 to 29 Oakmount Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The developer of two towers — 41 and 39 storeys with 873 homes — at 26-36 Mountview Avenue and 21-29 Oakmount Road appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on March 27, 2026 after City Council missed its decision deadline. Council is now asked to direct the City Solicitor to oppose the application in its current form at the tribunal while staff keep negotiating with the applicant. The proposal would redesignate the site from Neighbourhoods to Apartment Neighbourhoods and includes 11 rental replacement units, with a separate rental demolition application also filed.

title: 958 Broadview Avenue - Alterations to a Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: agreements, heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation, tenancy agreements
brief: The heritage-designated former Chester Public School at 958 Broadview Avenue — now Estonian House, an 1891 late-19th-century school in Richardsonian Romanesque and Queen Anne styles — would be altered to allow the proposed 26-storey residential tower. City Council is asked to approve the alterations under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and to amend the existing heritage easement agreement, registered in 2022. Council approved earlier alterations for a 14-storey tower in 2022; the revised proposal grows the tower to 26 storeys.

title: 954, 956 and 958 Broadview Avenue and 72 Chester Hill Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The approved 14-storey project at 954, 956, and 958 Broadview Avenue and 72 Chester Hill Road would grow to 26 storeys with 309 homes, including eight affordable units, and City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments. The proposal keeps the previously approved elements: restoration of the heritage building, a new public park next to Broadview Avenue, eight affordable ownership homes, and naturalizing and conveying rear lands to the Toronto Region Conservation Authority. The site sits in a protected major transit station area; the recommendations also include a $200,000 cash payment from the developer toward capital improvements in the ward near the site, on top of the previously secured contributions.

title: 17-19, 23 and 25 Toronto Street and 55 Adelaide Street East - Alterations to Heritage Properties, Demolition of a Building within the St. Lawrence Neighbourhood Heritage Conservation District, Approval of a Replacement Building and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: demolitions, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Heritage-designated buildings at 17-19 and 25 Toronto Street and 55 Adelaide Street East would be altered, and the non-contributing building at 23 Toronto Street demolished, to make way for the proposed 91-storey mixed-use tower. City Council is asked to approve the changes under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act and to enter into a heritage easement agreement. Heritage staff support the plan, which fully retains 17-19 Toronto Street and 57 Adelaide Street, keeps the façades of 25 Toronto and 55 Adelaide in place, and adds a low-rise building that complies with the St. Lawrence Heritage Conservation District plan.

title: 17-19, 23 and 25 Toronto Street and 55 and 57 Adelaide Street East - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: building plans, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; building records, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 91-storey mixed-use tower with 840 homes and 7,920 square metres of commercial and office space is proposed for 17-25 Toronto Street and 55-57 Adelaide Street East, and City Council is asked to approve the zoning amendment with a holding provision. A separate heritage report on the designated properties on the site — including the demolition and replacement of 23 Toronto Street within the St. Lawrence Neighbourhood Heritage Conservation District — comes to council alongside this item. The development would also be excluded from on-street permit parking.

title: 614 Danforth Road - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council decides whether to refuse a zoning amendment that would allow a 33-storey mixed-use building at 614 Danforth Road. The proposal has 26,016 square metres of floor area with 380 homes, 322 square metres of non-residential space, and 82 parking spaces across three underground levels, for a density of 12.1 times the lot area. Staff say the application is not consistent with the Provincial Planning Statement. A refusal would block the proposal.

title: 3130 Danforth Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item that also carries an approval: the report corrects the address of the zoning amendment application site from 3130 and 3150 Danforth Avenue to 3130 Danforth Avenue only, clarifying that 3150 Danforth Avenue is not part of the site. City Council is being asked to approve the zoning amendment for the corrected site.

title: 3000, 3004, 3008, 3012 and 3020 Kennedy Road - Draft Plan of Subdivision Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, subdivision (land); subdivision of land
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is being advised that the Executive Director, Development Review intends to approve the draft plan of subdivision for 3000 to 3020 Kennedy Road, after outstanding matters are addressed. The plan would create three blocks — two residential development blocks and one 20-metre-wide new public road extending Fort Dearborn Drive eastward to Kennedy Road. No council decision is required.

title: 1710 and 1712 Ellesmere Road - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment and Draft Plan of Subdivision Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council approves an Official Plan amendment, zoning amendment, and subdivision for 1710 and 1712 Ellesmere Road that would allow 2,328 homes in five tall buildings from 29 to 55 storeys, plus 2,595 square metres of non-residential space. The total floor area of 169,273 square metres equates to a density of about eight times the lot area. The project would add significant housing density in the area.

title: 3718 and 3730 Kingston Road - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Approving a zoning amendment for 3718 and 3730 Kingston Road that would allow a 24-storey mixed-use building on a 7-storey podium would get City Council's approval. The proposal has 30,905 square metres of floor area, with 419 homes and 672 square metres of non-residential space, for a floor space index of 5.25 times the lot area. The project would add housing density along Kingston Road.

title: Review of Parking and Transit Related Requests for Scarborough
topics: parking, public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie is asking City Council to have staff study parking pressures in Scarborough: City Council would request the Chief Planner to review the removal of minimum parking requirements for new developments in Scarborough and report back on whether pausing the removal is feasible until transit service improves, and to request Transportation Services to report on blocking new condo, townhome, and multiplex developments from getting on-street residential parking permits. The motion cites Scarborough's transit gaps and car dependence, and warns that losing minimum parking rules in poorly served areas could push more parking onto residential streets.

title: Metrolinx GO Expansion Program - Reconstruction of Birchmount Road Bridge - Temporary Road Closures and Transportation Impacts
topics: road closures, transportation; street closures; temporary highway closings, transportation services
brief: City Council is getting an overview of Metrolinx's planned reconstruction of the Birchmount Road bridge over the GO Lakeshore East rail corridor, part of the GO Expansion Program. The report sets out construction stages, timelines, and long-term temporary lane closures, turning restrictions, and impacts on pedestrians, cyclists, transit, and on-street parking. The reconstruction will affect travel along Birchmount Road for an extended period.

title: Metrolinx Scarborough Subway Extension - Temporary Traffic Modifications and Public Highway Dedications - Kennedy Station Connection, Emergency Exit Building-3, and Scarborough Centre Station
topics: regional transportation agencies, traffic regulations; commuter rail systems; go transit; intercity transportation; interregional public transit systems; interregional transit systems; interurban transit organizations; metrolinx; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; regional transit authorities; regional transportation authorities; transit agencies; transit operating agencies
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve changes to the timelines of previously approved temporary road closures and related traffic by-laws, plus temporary public highway designations, to support the next phase of Metrolinx's Scarborough Subway Extension construction. The changes cover the Stations, Rail and Systems contract work at the Kennedy Station connection, Emergency Exit Building 3, and Scarborough Centre Station. Construction staging and schedules were refined as the design progressed. The closures affect roads near the subway construction zones.

title: 3307 and 3313 Ellesmere Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: mixed use areas, official plan amendments, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Approving an Official Plan amendment and zoning amendment for 3307 and 3313 Ellesmere Road that would allow an 11-storey mixed-use building of 18,049 square metres is up for a decision by City Council. The Official Plan amendment would redesignate the property from Neighbourhoods to Mixed Use Areas and add a new site-specific policy in the Highland Creek Community Secondary Plan. The project would add mixed-use density in the area.

title: 2026 Toronto Heritage Grant Awards - Second Round
topics: awards, heritage preservation, subsidies and grants; financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Five heritage conservation grants totalling $207,000.00 are up for approval in a second round of the 2026 Toronto Heritage Grant Awards, expected to unlock about $347,584.78 in private spending. The matching grants cover up to half of eligible restoration work at designated heritage properties: up to $10,000.00 for house-form buildings, or up to $20,000.00 every ten years for a full cedar or slate roof replacement. The program's 2026 budget is $317,000.00, and City Council will decide whether to award the grants.

title: Building Toronto's Housing Future - Housing Development Office 2026 Annual Toronto Builds Update and Three-Year Work Plan
topics: affordable housing, housing; affordable homes; housing projects, homes; residences
brief: The City's housing delivery arm is reporting on a year of work speeding up homebuilding on public and supported lands. The Housing Development Office's 2026 annual Toronto Builds update and three-year work plan goes to City Council, which is asked to forward it to the CreateTO board while keeping some attachments confidential for negotiations. Council is also asked to request $557.5 million in federal Build Canada Homes funding to support about 4,000 rental homes in the next 12 to 18 months, to allocate up to $217.5 million to prioritized Toronto Builds projects in the 2026-2035 capital plan, and to authorize up to $34.6 million under the Rental Housing Supply Program. The city has also secured $21.6 million in federal Build Canada Homes funding for city-led projects so far, which council is asked to endorse pursuing further.

title: 65 Heward Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The property at 65 Heward Avenue, including 87 Heward Avenue, is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The owner has agreed to extend the timeline for council's decision, which faces a deadline under the act.

title: 65-87 Heward Avenue - Official Plan Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments;
brief: The owner of 65-87 Heward Avenue wants to redesignate the site from Core Employment Areas to Mixed Use Areas, with no new buildings proposed, and appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in February 2026 after council missed its deadline; a case management conference is set for May 29, 2026. City staff recommend the City Solicitor and planners oppose the conversion in its current form at the hearing while continuing talks with the applicant. City Council will decide whether to adopt that position.

title: 3838 Bloor Street West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: homelessness, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A four-storey city-run shelter with about 60 beds is proposed at 3838 Bloor Street West under the Homelessness Services Capital Infrastructure Strategy. City Council is asked to approve Official Plan and zoning amendments: the Official Plan change would remove the requirement for retail at grade along Bloor Street West, and the zoning change would bring the site into the city-wide by-law. The changes also leave open the option of supportive or affordable housing on the site in the future. These planning approvals carry no immediate cost, but the city-wide shelter strategy they belong to is estimated to cost about $674.5 million over the ten-year capital plan (2024-2033).

title: Toronto Builds: 970 Kipling Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, housing, zoning bylaws; developing land; development (land); land development, homes; residences, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Two repositioned towers of 94.7 and 140.3 metres are proposed for 970 Kipling Avenue on city-owned land, taller than the previously approved 42 and 91 metres. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change for the Toronto Builds project, with larger tower floor plates and a reduced podium. The site is being developed through the city's affordable housing program on public land. About $9.2 million in financial incentives for this site were previously authorized through the 2019 Housing Now initiative (item EX1.1).

title: Property Included on the City's Heritage Register - Consideration of Objection for 1767 Bayview Avenue, 1773 Bayview Avenue and 73 Niagara Street
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Three property owners at 1767 and 1773 Bayview Avenue and 73 Niagara Street have objected to their buildings being listed on the City's Heritage Register. City staff are recommending council keep all three properties on the register despite the objections, which owners may file at any time under the Ontario Heritage Act. City Council will decide whether the listings stand.

title: 30-32 and 38-40 Huntley Street and 122-124 Isabella Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Three properties at 30-32 Huntley Street, 38-40 Huntley Street, and 122-124 Isabella Street in the North St. James Town neighbourhood are proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The designation would protect the cultural heritage value of the properties at the northwest quadrant of Huntley and Isabella Streets.

title: Ookwemin Minising - City-Initiated Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment, and Precinct Plan Update - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, official plan amendments; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Ookwemin Minising is in line for another round of added density. City Council is asked to approve updated Official Plan and zoning amendments and a precinct plan update that would allow more homes, including affordable housing, on public lands in the walkable waterfront neighbourhood. The changes build on a 2024 update that already increased densities, following a renewed $975 million funding commitment from all three governments in January 2025 for the area's enabling infrastructure.

title: Advancing the City’s Affordable Housing Access System
topics: affordable housing, rental housing; affordable homes; housing projects, rental properties; rental units
brief: Applying for affordable housing could get simpler through a single central access point instead of separate draws run by each housing provider. City Council is asked to advance the centralized system for affordable, deeply affordable, and rent-geared-to-income rentals, which would also give the city better oversight and data. New units entering the system would be allocated by a full random draw.

title: 3180 Dufferin Street - Class 4 Noise Area Classification (NPC-300) - Final Report
topics: buildings, development, residential properties; developing land; development (land); land development, residential real estate
brief: Staff recommend City Council classify the lands at 3180 Dufferin Street as a Class 4 noise area under provincial guidelines, to implement an approved mixed-use development of two buildings with four residential towers and ground-floor non-residential space. Class 4 allows higher daytime and nighttime sound limits, offset by specified noise-control measures — affecting how much nearby noise future residents must tolerate.

title: 3140, 3150 and 3170 Dufferin Street and 60 and 68 Apex Road - Class 4 Noise Area Classification (NPC-300) - Final Report
topics: development, environmentally sensitive areas, noise; amplified music; construction noise; loud music; noise pollution; traffic noise, developing land; development (land); land development, environmental sensitivity; environmentally sensitive lands; environmentally-sensitive areas
brief: Staff recommend City Council classify the lands at 3140, 3150 and 3170 Dufferin Street and 60 and 68 Apex Road as a Class 4 noise area under provincial guidelines, to implement an approved mixed-use development of two buildings with four residential towers and ground-floor non-residential space. Class 4 allows higher daytime and nighttime sound limits, offset by specified noise-control measures — affecting how much nearby noise future residents must tolerate.

title: Yonge North Subway Extension and Ontario Line City-initiated Zoning By-law Amendments to Implement - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, service delivery, subways; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, underground
brief: Staff propose City-initiated zoning changes to let Metrolinx build Yonge North Subway Extension and Ontario Line facilities — traction power substations, station entrance buildings and temporary construction facilities — on lands Metrolinx will acquire, where current zoning does not permit transit uses. City Council is asked to approve the amendments so the transit projects can proceed.

title: 179 and 181 Finch Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Application - Approval
topics: applications, official plan amendments, zoning; application process
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a 7-storey (24 metres) mixed-use building at 179-181 Finch Avenue East with 40 residential units, 40 square metres of retail space, 22 parking spaces and indoor and outdoor amenity space. Staff say the proposal is consistent with the Provincial Planning Statement and provides appropriate housing in the area.

title: Wynford - Concorde Focused Area Study - Final Report
topics: development, official plan amendments, policies and procedures; developing land; development (land); land development, guidelines; policies
brief: Staff recommend City Council adopt Official Plan Amendment 902 (SASP 932) from the Wynford-Concorde Focused Area Study, launched in 2023, to set a planning framework for the area around higher-order transit — an enhanced public realm and streetscape with a multi-modal transportation network serving current and future residents and workers. The amendment shapes how the Wynford-Concorde area grows.

title: Lawrence Avenue West - Road Alterations, Parking Amendments and TTC Queue-jump Lane
topics: road reconstruction, road repairs, transportation (sc); crack repairs; cut repairs; fixing potholes; pothole repairs, road alterations; road narrowing; road widening
brief: Transportation Services recommends an eastbound queue-jump lane — letting buses bypass queued traffic at a congested intersection — on Lawrence Avenue West, along with road alterations and parking amendments. The Marlee-Glencairn study team reviewed the proposal against future congestion plans, including a possible closure of the southbound Allen Road on-ramp, and found it would improve operational efficiency without harming future plans. Community council is asked to approve. The change affects bus riders, drivers and parked cars on Lawrence West.

title: 8 Parmbelle Crescent - Zoning Amendment Application - Final Report - Refusal
topics: land use, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council refuse a zoning change to allow four three-storey (11.5-metre) townhouses with one garage parking space each at 8 Parmbelle Crescent, saying the proposal does not conform with the Official Plan because it fails to respect and reinforce the existing character of the Neighbourhoods designation. Refusal would stop the four-townhouse project.

title: The Peanut Streets Plan - Protected Pedestrian Crossings
topics: pedestrians, roads, transportation; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), pedestrianization, transportation services
brief: As part of The Peanut Streets Plan, staff recommend protected pedestrian crossings at two locations on Don Mills Road and one on Van Horne Avenue. Because the TTC operates transit service on both roads, City Council — not community council — must vote on it. The crossings would make it safer for pedestrians to cross two busy roads.

title: Strengthening the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement to Support Economic Prosperity in Toronto and the Great Lakes Region - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: international alliances; city twinning; city-to-city relationships; friendship cities; partnership cities; sister city relationships; twin cities; twin city alliances
brief: The item asks council to formally support the City of St. Catharines' resolution, adopted by the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative in May 2026, on strengthening the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement ahead of its July 1, 2026 six-year joint review. The motion asks council to urge the federal government to preserve the agreement and prioritize supply-chain resiliency and competitiveness provisions. The motion notes the agreement underpins about $2.7 trillion in annual trilateral trade, with the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence region generating 30 percent of economic activity in both Canada and the United States.

title: Strengthening Compliance and Coordination Across Multiplex Development-Related Enforcement Processes - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: The item asks council to strengthen compliance and coordination across multiplex-related enforcement, after neighbourhood complaints about repeated by-law violations, tree protection breaches, construction without permits and work outside permitted hours at several multiplex sites. The motion asks Environment, Climate and Forestry to report on tree by-law enforcement deterrence in the 2027 Tree By-law Report, and Toronto Building and Municipal Licensing to tighten coordination. It builds on current enforcement initiatives to deter future violations.

title: Request for Federal Proclamation of February as Chinese Canadian Heritage Month - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: culture (sc);
brief: The item asks council to request that the federal government proclaim February as Chinese Canadian Heritage Month, recognizing a community present in Canada since the 1800s. The motion cites contributions from the Canadian Pacific Railway to today's neighbourhoods, from the historic Chinatowns to North York and the suburbs, alongside the history of exclusion including the Head Tax and the 1923 Chinese Immigration Act. Toronto is home to one of the largest Chinese populations outside Asia.

title: 5 Sulkara Court - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
brief: This is a procedural item: Authorizing the City Solicitor to respond to the owner's appeal of the Committee of Adjustment's refusal at 5 Sulkara Court, where the owner sought variances for a new detached one-storey dwelling with a basement walkout would get Council's approval. The committee refused the application in April 2026 over lot coverage, building length and depth, with issues around garage compatibility and neighbour impacts; planning staff had supported it with modifications. The motion lets the solicitor retain experts to advance the city's case.

title: Improving Training of City Enforcement Staff - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: government (sc);
brief: The item asks council to have the City Manager review and update training for by-law enforcement officers and special constables, who are scattered across divisions with highly variable training. The motion covers powers of entry and inspection, laying charges under the Provincial Offences Act, remedial action, and policies on extenuating and aggravating circumstances. It says better-trained enforcement staff will be more efficient amid limited resources, turnover, population growth and court backlogs.

title: Supporting the 140 Merton Street Development Project - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: The 29-storey, 294-unit development at 140 Merton Street, with about 30 percent affordable units plus community agency space, pedestrian connections, open space and heritage conservation, is a city-owned Housing Now site being built with the Missanabie Cree First Nation. Councillor Josh Matlow's motion asks council to allocate up to $1.4 million in additional city-led rental development capital funds to cover cost escalations so the project is not delayed. The motion is urgent as construction is imminent.

title: Metrolinx Ontario Line - Temporary Lane Closures on the Don Valley Parkway and Frederick Goldwin Gardiner Expressway and Temporary Delegation of Authority - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: This is a procedural item: Approving temporary nightly lane closures on the Don Valley Parkway and the Gardiner Expressway from May 30 to June 30, 2026, to remove the temporary support structure of the Ontario Line's Lower Don Bridge is up for a decision by Council. The bridge's main structure has been under construction since May 2025, and the staged removal involves loosening bolts and plates and controlled cable tensioning. Closures will be coordinated with FIFA World Cup 2026 and other construction to limit disruption, and approval is needed now to hold the schedule.

title: Authorization to Deem the Untravelled Portion of Montesson Street as a Right-of-Way for Purposes of a Construction Staging Agreement - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: construction; building
brief: The developer of a 41-storey mixed-use rental building at 5238 Dundas Street West wants to use about 360 square metres of adjacent city-owned land, the closed untravelled portion of Montesson Street, for construction staging instead of occupying Dundas Street West. Councillor Amber Morley's motion asks council to deem the lands a right-of-way for calculating the licence fee for the staging agreement. The city lands are planned as a future park but are not currently in use, and the motion is urgent with construction crews on standby since May 1, 2026.

title: Authority to Enter into a Non-Competitive Agreement with Municipal VU Consulting Inc. for Procurement Development Consulting Services - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: purchasing, road maintenance; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, roads maintenance; sidewalk maintenance; sidewalks maintenance; summer maintenance; winter maintenance
brief: With the city's winter maintenance contracts expiring in 2029 and a competitive procurement launching in March 2027, Councillor Paul Ainslie's motion asks council to authorize Transportation Services to enter a non-competitive agreement with Municipal VU Consulting Inc. for procurement development consulting on the 2029-2036 contracts. The work covers the procurement and contract framework plus ongoing advisory support, under a senior Executive Steering Committee chaired by the Deputy City Manager for Infrastructure Services. The source lists $550,000 and $559,680.00 in connection with the agreement.

title: Enabling Shelter Allowance Savings for Individuals Experiencing Homelessness - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Neethan Shan
topics: subsidies and grants; financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs
brief: The item asks council to request that Ontario change Ontario Works and Ontario Disability Support Program rules so people without a fixed address can keep and save their shelter allowance toward securing housing. Under current rules, unhoused recipients do not get the shelter portion, so they cannot accumulate first and last month's rent and stay stuck in shelters. The motion says the change would remove a barrier to exiting homelessness without new funding, complementing the city's shelter and housing investments.

title: Protecting Hanlan's Point Beach - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: beaches, clothing optional beaches; naturists; nude beaches; nudist beaches
brief: High Lake Ontario water levels have closed some access points to Hanlan's Point Beach, and erosion has made the recently expanded beach area critical community space in the busy season. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik's motion asks council to direct Parks and Recreation, with the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority, to work with the local councillor and the Hanlan's Point Beach Working Group on urgent development and implementation of a beach access plan for the south portion. The beach is described as one of the world's oldest surviving queer spaces, and a renourishment study is already underway.

title: Stabilization Support for Alumnae Theatre Company - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: theatres (facilities); auditorium; performance spaces; performing arts centres; performing arts facilities
