brief: The item asks council to approve a one-time $151,100 stabilization grant for the Alumnae Theatre Company, the volunteer-run women's theatre organization dating to 1918 that operates from the city-owned heritage property at 70 Berkeley Street. Like many performing arts groups, Alumnae has faced operational and financial strain, and the grant would provide immediate relief to stabilize operations while longer-term conditions improve. The motion is urgent as funding is needed as soon as possible.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds to the Oak St. Park Playground Enhancement Project - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: The item asks council to release $289,960.00 ($289,960) in Section 42 funds, from the 227 Gerrard Street East development, for the Oak St. Park playground enhancement project. The money would be added to the Parks and Recreation 2026-2035 capital budget with no debt. The motion is urgent so the contract can be awarded in time for a summer 2026 opening.

title: Authority to Accept Health Canada Funding to Advance Training and Curriculum Development for the Toronto Community Crisis Service - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: community crisis response, funding; crisis response, financing
brief: The item asks council to accept a one-year $700,000 grant from Health Canada to develop equity-focused training curriculum for the Toronto Community Crisis Service, the city's fourth emergency service. The money supports a dedicated Training Centre now under development, funding community engagement on barriers and stigma, co-developed modular training with community partners, training for community organizations, and evaluation. The city's contribution is mainly in-kind staff time, and the initiative targets culturally safe crisis response for equity-deserving communities.

title: Improving In-Station Displays on Line 5 - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: light rail transit; lrt
brief: Since the Eglinton Crosstown opened earlier this year, in-station display screens on Line 5 have consistently shown arrival estimates with no relation to actual train times, undermining riders' ability to plan trips. Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin's motion asks council to press for accurate in-station displays on the line, noting Metrolinx owns the assets. The motion says reliable arrival information is critical to making transit a dependable alternative to driving and easing congestion.

title: Creating the City of Toronto Bi-Annual Affordable Housing Awards of Excellence - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: affordable housing, municipal awards; affordable homes; housing projects, book awards; civic awards; civilian citations; community service volunteers awards; human rights awards; urban design awards
brief: The item asks council to create a City of Toronto Bi-Annual Affordable Housing Awards of Excellence recognizing the co-operative, non-profit and private partners who take the financial risk to build and manage new rental homes. The motion asks the Housing Development Office and Housing Secretariat to help the Mayor's Office set up a nomination process. It frames the awards as celebrating proponents of affordable rental housing amid the housing crisis.

title: Request the Ontario Line Station at Pape and Cosburn to be Named East York Station - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: railway stations, trains; railroad stations; train stations
brief: The item asks council to recommend to Metrolinx and the provincial transportation ministry that the Ontario Line station at Pape Avenue and Cosburn Avenue be named East York Station. The motion traces East York from its 1924 incorporation as a township through its 1967 borough status to 1997 amalgamation, and notes the East York Foundation and Hall of Fame have already asked Metrolinx for the name. It points to existing station names honouring former municipalities, including North York Centre, Scarborough Centre, Forest Hill and Leaside.

title: Cuts Hurt Kids: Speaking Out Against Cuts to Our Schools - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: education (sc);
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to speak out against cuts announced by the Toronto District School Board under provincial supervision, including shuttered outdoor education sites, discontinued family engagement programs, eliminated behaviour-management and crisis-intervention staff roles, and reduced library and equity supports. The motion asks council to express support for continuing the programs and services youth and families rely on, saying the cuts affect youth safety and development, particularly in high-needs communities. The motion is urgent as the board advances the decisions.

title: Addressing Toronto’s Female Ginkgo Trees - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: by-laws, trees; ash trees, bylaws
brief: Residents have increasingly complained about city-owned female ginkgo trees, whose fruit produces a noxious smell and hazardous rotting residue that blocks maintenance and creates safety hazards. Councillor Josh Matlow's motion asks council to direct Environment, Climate and Forestry staff to bring recommendations on the female ginkgo population, focused on community health and safety, as part of the ongoing Tree By-Law Review reporting in 2027. The city does not intentionally plant female ginkgos but has no policy for trees that fruit later in life.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for a new Bad Dog Theatre at Mirvish Village - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: arts and culture, funding, theatres (facilities); auditorium; performance spaces; performing arts centres; performing arts facilities, financing
brief: Bad Dog Theatre Company, the nonprofit improv theatre founded in 1982 that lost its home during the pandemic, has been offered a long-term lease for basement space at 588 to 590 Markham Street in the new Mirvish Village for two small theatres and workshop space. Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion asks council to release $440,000 in Section 37 developer funds for a new Bad Dog Theatre there, adding to Ward 11's culture corridor of small theatres. The accessible space sits near other Bloor Street cultural venues with strong transit service.

title: Improving Cricket Facilities, Maintenance, and Enforcement Across Toronto - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: cricket;
brief: Cricket is one of Toronto's fastest-growing sports, but city-owned facilities are falling behind on basics like seating, washrooms and field conditions, and unauthorized use keeps damaging prepared pitches. Councillor Paul Ainslie's motion asks council to have Parks and Recreation review all city cricket facilities and report back by the first quarter of 2027 with a prioritized action plan, including cost estimates, plus stronger enforcement to protect permitted users. The motion carries no dollar figure yet; the costed plan comes with the report.

title: 9 Hertford Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: appeals;
brief: This is a procedural item: Council votes on authorizing the City Solicitor to appear before the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose the appeal of the Committee of Adjustment's refusal at 9 Hertford Avenue. The applicant proposed severing the lot into two undersized lots for two semi-detached fourplexes with rear-yard garden suites, plus a pedestrian easement; planning staff recommended approval with conditions, but Urban Forestry staff recommended deferral and refusal over tree impacts. The motion also lets the solicitor retain outside consultants and settle the matter.

title: Incorporating Pedestrian and Cyclist Safety into End of School Year Public Education Campaigns - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: cyclists, pedestrians, safety; pedestrianization, public safety
brief: With summer approaching and more children out in streets and parks, the item asks council to fold pedestrian, cyclist and active-travel safety messaging into end-of-school-year public education campaigns. The motion covers phone use while crossing, noise-cancelling earbuds, and e-scooter and e-bike rules, and asks the Chief Communications Officer to coordinate with the Toronto Police. The motion is urgent so the messaging lands in this year's campaigns.

title: Planning for the Future of Bluffer's Park: Parking, Access, and Neighbourhood Protection - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: parking, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Bluffer's Park's lots fill early on warm weekends, pushing visitors onto residential streets along Brimley Road with no beach access and prompting calls for better signage. Councillor Parthi Kandavel's motion asks council to plan for the park's growth: exploring expanded parking, including at the top of the hill, and protecting surrounding neighbourhoods, ahead of a new multi-use trail along Brimley Road that will bring even more pedestrians and cyclists. The motion is urgent with summer approaching.

title: Review of Public Parking Access at Scarborough GO Station - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: parking, regional transportation agencies; commuter rail systems; go transit; intercity transportation; interregional public transit systems; interregional transit systems; interurban transit organizations; metrolinx; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; regional transit authorities; regional transportation authorities; transit agencies; transit operating agencies
brief: The item asks council to review public parking access at Scarborough GO Station, where residents report commuter parking spilling onto residential streets with illegal parking, long-term vehicle storage and congestion. The motion notes Scarborough's thinner rapid-transit network leaves many residents driving, dropping off or park-and-riding to the Lakeshore East corridor, and points to potentially underused Metrolinx lands near Natal Park and the GO maintenance yard at 3620 St. Clair Avenue East. A coordinated review by Transit Expansion and Corporate Real Estate Management would look for better use of nearby lands.

title: Dedicating June 4 as Tom Longboat Day in Toronto - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: memorials; monuments; permanent memorials
brief: The item asks council to dedicate June 4 as Tom Longboat Day in Toronto, matching the provincial day proclaimed in 2008. Thomas Charles Longboat, an Onondaga runner from Six Nations, won the 1907 Boston Marathon, represented Canada at the 1908 London Olympics, served as a dispatch carrier in the First World War, and worked 17 years in the city's street cleaning department. The motion honours his athletic and public-service legacy.

title: A Voice for Torontonians on Jet Island Airport Plan - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: airports, work plans;
brief: The item asks council to give Torontonians a voice in the province's plan for jets at Billy Bishop Airport, introduced as Bill 110, the Building Billy Bishop Airport Act, 2026, on April 23. The motion lists potential impacts under discussion: multiplied flight numbers, more downtown and waterfront noise, traffic and congestion, loss of parkland at Little Norway Park, changes at Hanlan's Point and its beach and ferry dock, and health effects from air pollution for nearby residents. The motion says the exact plan remains unclear.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Allan Gardens Master Plan and Expansion - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: funding; financing
brief: The item asks council to release $100,000.00 in Section 37 funds to the Friends of Allan Gardens for architectural drawings for the Greenhouse Link Building, which would double the conservatory from 16,000 to more than 32,000 square feet. The source also lists a $10 million figure in connection with the Allan Gardens master plan and expansion. A Friends of Allan Gardens petition has gathered more than 7,000 signatures, and the motion notes private philanthropy, corporate and federal commitments alongside the proposed municipal contribution.

title: Toronto Needs Provincial Support to Enable Noise Camera Enforcement Now - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: noise control; noise barriers; sound barriers
brief: The item asks council to seek provincial support for noise camera enforcement, saying excessive noise from modified vehicle exhausts and other sources harms residents' quality of life, health and well-being. The motion notes community advocacy, including No More Noise Toronto's sound-data work, has exposed gaps in complaint-driven enforcement, and that acoustic monitoring devices have been piloted successfully in other jurisdictions. Ontario municipalities currently lack clear legislative authority to deploy automated noise enforcement, and the motion asks the province for enabling legislation with safeguards.

title: Allocating Community Benefit Charges from 41 to 47 Hendon Avenue Development to Improve Hendon Park - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
brief: The item asks council to earmark the Community Benefits Charges from the proposed 34-storey development at 41 to 47 Hendon Avenue, directly across from Hendon Park, for improvements to the park. The development will add density and park demand in the Yonge and Finch area, and the motion asks that the charges be allocated through the 2027 budget process toward amenities, accessibility, landscaping, pathways, seating and playground upgrades. The motion carries no dollar figure in the source.

title: Improving Access to Toronto Island Park - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: accessibility, parks; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: With 1.5 million annual visitors to Toronto Island and two new faster, higher-capacity ferries arriving in 2027, Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to examine a more efficient and equitable ferry fare structure. The motion directs the City Manager and senior staff to review updated ticketing options, including discounted fares like those on the TTC, and fee-free alternatives, now that ferry fleet and terminal management has moved to Fleet Services. The goal is an Island park accessible to all as it becomes a year-round destination.

title: Authorization to Reallocate Section 37 Funds from Royal Rouge Tot Lot Park Improvements to the Dogs Off-Leash Area at Lawrence Avenue East and Starspray Boulevard - by Councillor Neethan Shan, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: funding; financing
brief: The item asks council to reallocate $200,000 in Section 37 funds, from the 7437, 7439 and 7441 Kingston Road developments, from the Royal Rouge Tot Lot Park Improvements project to a new dogs off-leash area at Lawrence Avenue East and Starspray Boulevard. The reallocation addresses a funding shortfall for the new park, which follows design development and community engagement. The motion reduces the tot lot project's 2026 cash flow by $200,000 and adds the same amount to the off-leash project.

title: Investigating the Increased Risk of Heart Disease, Lung Cancer, and Tumours from Bringing Jets to Toronto’s Waterfront Communities - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: environmental assessments, investigation; ea; ecological assessment; environmental assessment; environmental evaluation, investigators
brief: The item asks council to have the Board of Health direct the Medical Officer of Health to collect and assess data on the potential health impacts of introducing jets at Billy Bishop Airport near residential communities. The motion cites a 2017 environmental assessment commissioned by the Toronto Port Authority finding jet pollution would raise risks of heart disease, lung cancer and respiratory tract tumours, and notes schools and daycares within blocks of the airport. The motion frames the request as ensuring residents are informed about the health implications.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Church Wellesley Business Improvement Area to Support Church Street Pedestrianization Pilot - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: funding; financing
brief: The item asks council to release $50,000 ($50,000.00) in Section 37 funds, from the 50 Wellesley Street East and 31 to 35 Dundonald Street developments, to the Church-Wellesley Village BIA for the Church Street Pedestrianization Pilot. The one-time funding covers permanent improvements: new planters, cigarette disposal and recycling receptacles, and pole wraps along Church Street. The BIA identified the measures to improve cleanliness and aesthetics and support the local economy.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Branded Street Name Signs for the Church Wellesley Village in Ward 13 Toronto Centre - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: funding; financing
brief: The item asks council to release $4,700 ($4,700.00) in Section 37 funds, from the 2, 6, 8 Gloucester Street and 601 to 613 Yonge Street developments, for rainbow branded street name signs marking the boundaries of the Church-Wellesley Village. The decorative signs, requested by the Church Wellesley Neighbourhood Association and commissioned with Transportation Services, would delineate one of Toronto's most iconic neighbourhoods. The money covers fabrication and installation.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds - Improving Mercer Street Streetscape - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: funding; financing
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to release $1,500,000 in Section 37 funds, from the 15 to 35 Mercer Street development, for the Mercer Street streetscape project first conceived in 2014. The final design includes new unit paving on the roadway and curb extensions with drop curbs and laybys for on-street parking and hotel and business loading zones, steel bollards separating pedestrians and vehicles, and new bike rings, with a stronger pedestrian focus. The cash flows are $375,000 in 2026 and $1,125,000 in 2027, timed after 2024 watermain work.

title: Authorization to Extend a Nominal Fee Licence Agreement with the 519 Community Centre at Barbara Hall Park - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
brief: This is a procedural item: Council decides whether to extend The 519 Church Street Community Centre's nominal-fee licence to run programs and events in Barbara Hall Park, after the agreement expired August 31, 2025. The 519 animates the park with activities like Tai Chi and self-defence classes, medicine walks, yoga, square dancing, Drag Me to the Movies and the Toronto Queer Market, plus EarlyON family and youth programming. The park, which wraps around the community centre, includes the AIDS and Trans Memorials, a splash pad, playground and off-leash dog area.

title: Recognizing the Economic Role of Strip Plazas Through Sidewalks to Skylines - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: planning;
brief: The item asks council to formally recognize the economic and community role of strip plazas, after the city's PlazaPOV study identified more than 400 strip plaza sites citywide, most in Scarborough, supporting small businesses, ethnic retail, food access and local jobs. The motion seeks coordination between the PlazaPOV findings and Sidewalks to Skylines, the city's 10-year economic action plan, to inform future policy and programs for plazas facing redevelopment pressure near higher-order transit. The aim is supporting their adaptation while limiting displacement.

title: Toronto Island Bike Share Enhancements for the 2026 Season - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: bike paths; bicycle paths; bicycle trails; bike trails; cycling paths; cycling trails; off-road paths (cycling)
brief: Bike Share Toronto's 2025 Island pilot was heavily used, with more than 216,000 trips started on Toronto Island between May and October and the Centre Island and Ward's Island ferry dock stations ranking first and third system-wide. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik's motion asks council to have the Toronto Parking Authority, with Parks and Recreation, implement enhancements for the 2026 season: clearer cyclist behaviour education, management of bike share use around the Island's residential communities, and other stakeholder feedback. The goal is a successful program in the Island's unique conditions.

title: 83 to 87 River Street and 2 to 4 Labatt Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Reallocation of Section 37 Benefit Contribution - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The developer of the approved 34-storey mixed-use building at 83 to 97 River Street and 2 to 4 Labatt Avenue wants to provide an on-site EarlyON child and family centre instead of part of the cash community-benefits contribution secured in its Section 37 agreement. Councillor Chris Moise's motion asks council to start a zoning amendment to allow the swap, with any remaining contribution directed to on-site or ward priorities, plus a public consultation and a staff report back in the second quarter of 2026.

title: Accepting an In-Kind Donation from Wanless Park Community Tennis Club to Refurbish the Tennis Courts at Wanless Park - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: donation; bequest; toy drive
brief: The Wanless Park Community Tennis Club at 250 Wanless Avenue plans to dig out and rebuild two of its five hard courts in fall 2026 and resurface all five in spring 2027, funded from the club's capital reserve. Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin's motion asks council to accept the in-kind donation valued at up to $319,000, since the city's donation policy requires council approval for gifts over $50,000. Parks and Recreation would bear no costs for the refurbishment, and staff have approved the scope.

title: Proposed Off-Leash Area Assessment at Bluffer’s Park West Beach - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: dogs, pets; domestic animals
brief: Following a community petition for seasonal off-leash dog hours at Bluffer's Park, the item asks council to have Parks and Recreation assess whether the West Beach area could safely accommodate limited off-leash use at appropriate times of year. If the location proves feasible under the city's Dog Off-Leash Area Strategy and funding is confirmed, staff would run community engagement through the Bluffer's Park Action Plan process. The motion frames it as an interim step while Scarborough awaits more formal off-leash areas.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Common Table - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: charities, funding; charitable organizations; charity, financing
brief: The Common Table Drop-In Program feeds about 500 homeless people each weekday morning in the basement of the Church of the Redeemer in Yorkville, but the only accessible route down is an unreliable freight elevator that frequently traps passengers for an hour or more. Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion asks council to release $150,000 ($150,000) in Section 37 funds, combined with church money, to upgrade the elevator to dignified, reliable access. Many volunteers and clients have mobility limitations, and food and supplies must be delivered to the basement.

title: Odour from the Ashbridges Bay Wastewater Treatment Plant
topics: wastewater, wastewater treatment, wastewater treatment plants, water odour, water quality; sanitary sewage; sewage; waste water, sewage treatment plants; treatment plants; waste water treatment plants, sewage treatment; waste water treatment; wastewater management, water odor; water smell; water that smells funny, water quality reports
brief: A member motion raises odour from the Ashbridges Bay Wastewater Treatment Plant in Ward 14, which serves upwards of 1.4 million residents: the local councillor says she received many resident complaints and 311 calls during a recent week when a mechanical breakdown in a holding tank caused odours — since repaired — and was told by Toronto Water there were only 6 area odour complaints and 3 direct complaints in 2026, noting confusion with the 311 reporting process. The motion questions why her office wasn't notified of the failure and asks for better communication around plant odour incidents. The item affects east-end residents and plant accountability. Any direction would flow from the committee.

title: Feasibility of Requiring Side Guards on Contractor Commercial Vehicles Operating in the City of Toronto
topics: commercial vehicles, motor vehicle safety regulations, suppliers; commercial motor vehicles
brief: Staff report to council on the feasibility of requiring side guards — protective bars between truck axles that prevent pedestrians and cyclists from being pulled under wheels — on contractor commercial vehicles. The city is ahead of schedule installing guards on its own fleet by end of 2026, and staff say guards are appropriate and feasible for contracted dedicated fleets (vehicles working full-time for the city) but not feasible for contracted non-dedicated fleets serving multiple clients. The item affects pedestrian and cyclist safety around city-contracted trucks. Council decides on next steps.

title: Amending the Foundation Drainage Policy and Storm Sewer Quality Limit for Manganese
topics: storm drainage systems, water treatment, water use policies; water filtration; water purification, water restrictions
brief: Effective October 1, 2026, the city is amending its Foundation Drainage Policy to let a limited amount of foundation drainage containing groundwater discharge into storm sewers, provided it meets sewer by-law quality limits and the receiving storm sewer discharges directly to water — the result of staff review into housing-servicing flexibility without compromising sewer capacity. The item also covers the storm sewer quality limit for manganese. The change affects new housing developments that need servicing. The committee or council decides on next steps.

title: 2026 Road Classification Amendments
topics: capital budgets, highways, transportation; freeways; motorways; parkways, transportation services
brief: City Council decides whether to approve reclassifying seven roadways across Wards 3, 7, 10, and 21 under the city's road classification system — covering roads newly assumed by the city since 2018 and others needing reclassification based on current conditions — to better align roadway function with service delivery. Accurate classification affects transportation planning, infrastructure design, and capital investment decisions. Council decides.

title: Supporting the Proposed Modernization of Ontario’s Framework for Power-Assisted Bicycles (E-Bikes)
topics: by-laws, environmental impacts, power-assisted bicycles; bylaws, e-bikes; electric bicycles; electric bikes; electric-assisted bikes; power assisted bicycles, environmental effects; environmental footprint; environmental impact
brief: The item asks City Council to have Transportation Services submit comments to Ontario's Environment Registry supporting the province's proposed e-bike framework — classifying power-assisted bicycles (speed limited to 32 km/h, 500 watts or less, with functional pedals) and requiring faster, heavier moped- or motorcycle-style vehicles to be licensed and insured — with the councillor noting some elements could be improved. The city has limited ability to regulate fast, heavy micromobility vehicles and police have struggled to enforce the existing bylaw. The item affects e-bike rules and road safety. Council decides.

title: SmartTrack Invoicing
topics: invoices, payment; accounts payable, paying; payment information; payment methods; payment options; pre-authorized payment plans; pre-authorized plans; preauthorized payments
brief: Councillor Jamaal Myers (Ward 23, Scarborough North) has filed an administrative inquiry about the city's SmartTrack accounting, after an Auditor General report noted that since the project's inception in 2018 the city has received no invoices from Metrolinx — which delivers SmartTrack on the city's behalf — despite approximately $184 million in costs the report says are payable from the city's dedicated project funds. The item also cites $186 million, and notes staff have requested invoices monthly since 2018 without receiving them, complicated by Metrolinx's shared contractors with GO Expansion. The item seeks clarity on the city's financial exposure and risks, not a council decision.

title: Service Agreements Awarded and Executed by the Medical Officer of Health for 2026
topics: health; health coverage
brief: This is an information item: the Medical Officer of Health reports $7 — the report shows $7.250 million — in purchase-of-service contracts awarded and executed with community agencies in 2026 for programs including Healthy Babies Healthy Children, food security, sexual health clinics, dental care for homeless youth and low-income adults, and the Ontario Seniors Dental Care program. City Council is asked to receive the report.

title: Amendment to Contract CW2310755 with Amazon Web Services Canada Inc., for Cloud Subscription Services and Support Services
topics: contracts, databases, science & technology (sc), websites;
brief: City Council votes on amending the Amazon Web Services Canada Inc. cloud contract, adding $11,159,260 ($11,355,663 net of HST recoveries) and extending it one year — raising the contract from $447,059 ($454,927) to $11,606,318 ($11,810,589) as a ceiling with no commitment to spend it all. AWS hosts public tools like Toronto.ca and the Open Data portal plus internal city systems, with 24/7 support included. The extension continues a contract first awarded competitively and extended to June 30, 2026.

title: Amendment to Blanket Contract 47025086 and Entering into Various Non-Competitive Contracts with Active Network, Ltd., for Software Subscriptions, Processing Fees, and Professional Services
topics: contracts, external services, parks, programs, software; computer programs, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, consultants; consulting services; professional services
brief: City Council decides whether to amend the ACTIVENet contract with Active Network, Ltd. — the Parks and Recreation program registration and facility booking system — and sign three non-competitive contracts letting other divisions (Corporate Real Estate Management, Revenue Services, Court Services, the City Clerk's Office) replace end-of-life booking and payment software on the same enterprise platform through December 31, 2030. The ACTIVENet amendment adds $2,175,000 ($2,213,280 net of HST recoveries), raising it from $10,695,144.45 to $12,870,144 ($13,096,659); the three new deals are $512,301 ($521,317) for Corporate Real Estate Management, $1,420,977 ($1,445,986) for Revenue Services and Court Services, and $496,313 ($505,048) for the City Clerk's Office, with $500,000 also cited. Council approval is needed because the values and durations exceed staff authority.

title: Award of Doc5308010518 to Stantec Consulting Ltd., for Professional Services for Design, Contract Administration and Post Construction Services for the High Rate Treatment Facility at Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant
topics: construction, contracts, external services, projects, water treatment plants; building, consultants; consulting services; professional services, filtration plants; water filtration plants; water treatment and supply plants; water treatment facilities
brief: City Council reallocates $6,311,273 ($6,422,352 net of HST recoveries) within Toronto Water's 2026 capital budget and 2027-2035 capital plan from projects completed under budget, and awards Stantec Consulting Ltd. a 13-year contract (plus a two-year extension option) worth $69,935,240 ($71,166,100 net of HST recoveries) for design and construction administration of a high-rate treatment facility at the Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant. The project supports the Wet Weather Flow Master Plan for managing stormwater.

title: Administrative Amendments to Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 598 and Chapter 441 (No New Fees or Fee Increases)
topics: by-laws, municipal addresses, municipal codes, property (sc), surveys (maps); addresses; house numbers; one address repository; property numbers; street numbers, bylaws, cadastral surveys; legal boundary surveys; property surveys
brief: This is a procedural item: Making administrative amendments to Municipal Code Chapter 598 (property numbering) and Chapter 441 (fees and charges) that only reword service descriptions for municipal address changes to reflect current practice — with no new fees and no fee increases would get City Council's approval. The changes clarify and harmonize the two by-laws.

title: Application for Approval to Expropriate Parts of 2 and 90 Bloor Street East for the Bloor-Yonge Capacity Improvement Project - Stage 1
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, expropriations, projects, subways, transit networks; compulsory purchase; eminent domain, ttc, underground
brief: City Council votes on starting Stage 1 of expropriating temporary easements on parts of 2 Bloor Street East and 90 Bloor Street East to expand the Bloor-Yonge interchange station. If council approves, owners get a notice of application and have 30 days to request a hearing on whether the taking is fair, sound, and reasonably necessary; a Stage 2 report with property values and any hearing results would come back to council before any expropriation is finalized. Owners would receive compensation offers based on appraisals before the city takes possession.

title: 1029 King Street West Unit 23 - Designation of a Portion of the Property Used by West Neighbourhood House as a Municipal Capital Facility
topics: city-owned properties, community & life (sc), municipal facilities, services, taxes; city facilities; municipal buildings, city owned properties; city properties, levies
brief: City Council decides whether to pass a by-law designating about 5,005 square feet at 1029 King Street West, Unit 23 — leased to the registered charity West Neighbourhood House for community programs including pre-school drop-ins and services addressing homelessness, employment, poverty, and health — as a municipal capital facility, exempting the space from municipal and school property taxes. Council decides on the designation under Section 252 of the City of Toronto Act.

title: Non-Competitive Procurement with Darch Fire Incorporated for the Supply and Delivery of E-One Incorporated Original Equipment Manufacturer Parts and Warranty for Toronto Fire Services
topics: agreements, contracts, emergency vehicles, fire and rescue services, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, fire fighting; fire services; fire suppression; firefighting; rescue; rescue operations; search and rescue, tenancy agreements
brief: Toronto Fire Services wants a five-year non-competitive contract with Darch Fire Incorporated worth $1,664,849 ($1,694,150 net of HST recoveries) — the report also cites $500,000 — for original manufacturer parts and warranty on its E-One fire apparatus, starting after the current agreement ends December 31, 2026. Darch is the exclusive Ontario supplier of E-One heavy vehicle parts and the exclusive warranty provider, so competitive bidding isn't practical. The contract keeps parts flowing for the front-line aerial fleet.

title: Non-Competitive Contracts with Various Suppliers for the Supply of Proprietary Parts and Maintenance Services at Water and Wastewater Treatment Plants for Toronto Water
topics: contracts, maintenance, sewer and water infrastructure, sewers, storm drainage systems, storm sewers, suppliers, water; sewage systems; sewerage, sewer and water services; water and sewer infrastructure; water management systems, stormwater sewers
brief: City Council is asked to approve five non-competitive contracts totalling $7,085,485 ($7,210,190 net of HST recoveries) with Toromont Power Systems, KSB Pumps Inc. (Canada), APGN Inc., John Brooks Company Limited, and Devine & Associates Limited for proprietary parts and maintenance at water and wastewater treatment plants, from issuance to December 31, 2026 with four one-year renewal options; the report also cites $500,000 and $7,085,485. The individual contract values are $2,654,568 ($2,701,288 net of HST recoveries), $1,592,741 ($1,620,773), $1,150,000 ($1,170,240), $1,141,464 ($1,161,554), and $546,713 ($556,335). Each supplier is the sole manufacturer or authorized distributor of its specialized equipment.

title: Non-Competitive Contracts with Aimsun Inc., and PTV Group for Aimsun and Vissim Transportation Modeling Software for Transportation Services
topics: contracts, software, traffic, transportation, transportation projects; computer programs, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, transportation services
brief: City Council is asked to approve non-competitive five-year contracts: with Aimsun Inc ($115,000 USD, or $117,024 USD net of HST recoveries) for five Aimsun Next licences, and with PTV Group ($219,861 USD, or $223,731 USD net of HST recoveries) for ten Vissim licences — proprietary traffic modelling software Transportation Services uses for master plans, environmental assessments, and construction traffic management; the report also cites $500,000. Both products are sold exclusively by their vendors, so competitive procurement isn't practical. The tools model how traffic responds to changes in the road and transit network.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with RideShark Corporation for the Smart Commute Online Tool
topics: contracts, public transit, transit networks; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: City Council is asked to approve a non-competitive contract with RideShark Corporation worth $75,000 ($76,320 net of HST recoveries) for up to five years to keep running the Smart Commute online tool, the region-wide platform that helps employers and commuters shift to walking, cycling, transit, carpooling, and remote work; the report also cites $500,000. The program is aimed at cutting single-occupant vehicle trips to ease congestion.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Toronto Metropolitan University for Partnerships to Address the Digital Divide
topics: computer networks, digital libraries, equity, internet, research, wireless internet; employment equity; fair wage; pay equity, online libraries, studies; surveys (research), wi fi; wifi; wireless hotspot
brief: The question before City Council: whether to approve a non-competitive contract with Toronto Metropolitan University worth $300,000 ($305,280 net of HST recoveries) as a ceiling for up to six years of digital divide research, with no commitment to spend the full amount; the report also cites $500,000 and the $115,616 spent to date. The research continues work started after council's 2021 direction to study barriers to affordable high-speed internet for vulnerable residents, and has produced three public reports so far. The findings inform the city's digital equity efforts.

title: Non-Competitive Bridge Contract with Safeguard Perimeter Inc., for Traffic Control Services to Support Major Events in 2026
topics: [events in community and life], contracts, sports tournaments, traffic management, transportation; tournaments, traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations, transportation services
brief: City Council votes on approving a non-competitive bridge contract with Safeguard Perimeter Inc. worth $800,000 ($814,080 net of HST recoveries) for delivery, installation, and removal of traffic control equipment — barricades, signs, and traffic devices — for major city events from June 9 to December 9, 2026; the report also cites $500,000. The existing traffic control contract expires June 9, 2026, and the bridge contract keeps services running until a new tender can be awarded. Transportation Services relies on these services for road closures, event traffic management, and pedestrian safety.

title: 2025 Write-off of Uncollectible Property Taxes and Accounts Receivable
topics: financial write-offs, property (sc), provincial offences, taxes; financial write offs, levies
brief: The city is writing off uncollectible accounts from 2025: $299,458.16 in property taxes across 79 accounts (tax years 1994 to 2024) where collection is considered extremely unlikely, $1,008,896 in invoiced receivables for city services deemed doubtful, and $3,019,028 across 8,022 Provincial Offences Act cases where debtors couldn't be located, had died, or had no assets. Council is asked to approve the property tax write-off; the other two were approved under delegated authority. Staff say there is no 2025 budget impact because the amounts were already accounted for as uncollectible.

title: 2915, 2917, 2939, 2941 and 2943 Bloor Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A developer proposed a 29-storey mixed-use building with 423 homes at 2915-2943 Bloor Street West, then appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal after council missed the decision deadline. Staff want the city's lawyers to oppose the current version and keep negotiating.

title: 2 to 4 Mendota Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning approvals, zoning bylaws; development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A proposal to build a 4-storey self-storage building at 2 to 4 Mendota Road, with 31 parking spaces and 3 truck loading bays. Council is asked to change the Official Plan and zoning to allow it.

title: On-Street Electric Vehicle Charging Stations on Lake Shore Boulevard West and Weston Road - Parking Amendments (Non-Delegated Locations)
topics: electricity, non-motorized vehicles; electric power; electricity usage
brief: Up for a decision before Council: add a two-space on-street EV charging area on Lake Shore Boulevard West, and to remove the parking rules for an EV charger at 2000 Weston Road that was taken out for a new transit shelter.

title: Temporary Traffic Control Signal and Compulsory Stop Control on Highway 27, Royalcrest Road, Baywood Road, and Mars Road
topics: stopping prohibitions, traffic control systems; no stopping, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: While a culvert on Royalcrest Road is replaced and the road is fully closed, staff propose a temporary traffic light at Highway 27 and Mars Road plus new turn restrictions, in effect from July 2026 to June 2027.

title: Maple Leaf Drive and Falstaff Avenue - Traffic Safety Improvements
topics: pedestrian crossovers, traffic; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: A companion to the Maple Leaf and Rustic Streets Plan, this asks Council to approve a pedestrian crossover on Maple Leaf Drive about 260 metres east of Jane Street and to designate a Community Safety Zone on Falstaff Avenue, where traffic fines are doubled.

title: 750 Queen's Plate Drive - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: [buildings by height], residential properties, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: A proposal to build a 17-storey residential building at 750 Queen's Plate Drive. Council is asked to change the zoning by-law to permit the project, after the owner completes a servicing study and any needed infrastructure upgrades.

title: Report on Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) Committee Meetings - February 2026
topics: committee meetings, policy development; policy making
brief: This is an information item: Council receives an update on the February 2026 Federation of Canadian Municipalities standing committee meetings, covering lithium-ion battery regulation, mental health and homelessness, and infrastructure funding. No policy change is proposed.

title: Amendments to the TTC Records Retention Schedule (Municipal Code Chapter 219, Records, Corporate (Local Boards))
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, records; ttc
brief: The decision on amending the municipal code to update the TTC's records retention schedule, revising retention periods, consolidating record series, and adding new record categories, as recommended by the TTC board rests with Council. It affects how the TTC keeps and disposes of its records.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Implementation of the Integrated Regional Paramedic Response model and quarterly update on the Community Benefits Plan, Social Procurement and Workforce Development, and Liberty Village and Fort York Neighbourhood Plan
topics: community benefits, development, sports tournaments; developing land; development (land); land development, tournaments
brief: Up for a decision before Council: authorize agreements with regional municipalities to implement an integrated regional paramedic response model for the FIFA World Cup 2026, when more than 230,000 additional daily visitors are expected to strain the medical emergency response system. Council is also asked to receive a quarterly update on the community benefits plan, social procurement and workforce development, and neighbourhood plans.

title: Adjustments to Capital Budget, Carry Forward Funding and Future Year Commitments
topics: budgets, capital budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: The 2026-2035 capital budget included $968.7 million in previously approved unspent funding carried forward, but final 2025 spending figures show more is needed. Council is asked to approve an additional $237.2 million in carry-forward funding from 2025 to 2026-2035 so approved capital projects can continue, bringing total carry-forward to $1.206 billion within a $5.889 billion adjusted 2026 capital budget.

title: Waterfront Dockwalls and Western Beaches Breakwaters Action Plan Update
topics: beaches, conservation, natural environment, shorelines, waterfronts; environment; natural heritage systems, environmental conservation; environmental improvements; environmental management; environmental protection; environmental stewardship; greening, lakefronts; waterfront trail, lakeshore
brief: More than 37 km of Toronto's shoreline protection and marine structures, many over 100 years old, are aging and pose growing public safety and liability risks. Council is asked to commit $6.78 million, with $2.7 million in 2026 cash flow and $4.08 million in 2027 commitments, on an exceptional basis to accelerate the Dockwall Resilience Program and develop a state-of-good-repair program. The report's figures also include $550,000, $97 million, $180 million, $2.16 million, $6, and $4.

title: 838 Broadview Development Plan Update
topics: affordable housing, development, housing, planning; affordable homes; housing projects, developing land; development (land); land development, homes; residences
brief: This is an information item: Council receives a report on development scenarios for a mixed-income affordable housing project on City-owned land at 838 Broadview Avenue, with financial details kept confidential for property negotiations. No policy change is proposed.

title: Standardizing the Air Conditioner Benefit (Pilot)
topics: benefits, heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems, pilot projects; air conditioning; air conditioning systems; boilers; climate control systems; cooling systems; furnaces; heat; heating systems; hvac; ventilation; ventilation systems
brief: Extreme heat is one of Toronto's most urgent climate hazards, and Council is asked to expand and harmonize air conditioner benefits for low-income and vulnerable residents: Hardship Fund applicants, Ontario Works and ODSP recipients, and Toronto Community Housing and Toronto Seniors Housing tenants. The expansion uses an additional $1,060,000 from the Corporate Extreme Weather Reserve and would supply and install up to 2,400 air conditioners in summer 2026. The report's figures also include $1,041,667, $1,092,200, $1,111,422, $2,133,867, and $2,171,423.

title: Report on Participation in Ontario Big City Mayors (OBCM) Meetings April 16 - 17, 2026 and Advocacy Day, April 22, 2026
topics: development, housing, meetings, public safety & protection (sc), public transit; developing land; development (land); land development, homes; residences, local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: This is an information item: Council receives an update on April 2026 Ontario's Big City Mayors meetings with provincial ministers and federal housing officials on housing, development charges, and municipal finance. No policy change is proposed.

title: Report on Ontario’s Big City Mayors (OBCM) Caucus meeting - February 6, 2026
topics: budgets, development, mayors, taxes; budgets and accounts, developing land; development (land); land development, levies
brief: This is an information item: Council receives an update on the February 6, 2026 Ontario's Big City Mayors caucus meeting, covering the 2026 provincial pre-budget submission, health care pressures, and municipal tax reform. The report notes Toronto's operating budget allocates over $1.5 billion, 27 per cent of property tax funding, to housing and social services. No policy change is proposed.

title: Report on Mayors and Regional Chairs of Ontario (MARCO) meetings in January and March 2026
topics: community development, development, mayors; community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: This is an information item: Council receives an update on the January and March 2026 meetings of the Mayors and Regional Chairs of Ontario, covering the homelessness crisis, transit funding, and the provincial Blue Box transition. The report notes AMO research showing nearly 85,000 Ontarians homeless in 2025 and a call for an $11 billion investment over 10 years for 75,000 affordable and supportive housing units. The report's figures also include $2.5 million and $100,000.

title: Report on Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative: Great Lakes Day 2026 Advocacy Meetings (Washington, D.C.) March 3 - 5, 2026
topics: economy, environment (sc), meetings;
brief: This is an information item: Council receives an update on the March 3-5, 2026 advocacy mission to Washington, D.C., urging the U.S. government to avoid new tariffs on Canadian goods and supporting Great Lakes water and infrastructure programs. No policy change is proposed.

title: Report on Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative: Confluence Forum
topics: by-laws, climate, pollution; bylaws, contamination
brief: This is an information item: Council receives an update on the January 20, 2026 Confluence Forum on climate resilience, clean energy, and plastic pollution in the Great Lakes basin, hosted at Toronto City Hall. No policy change is proposed.

title: Expanding Youth Programs to Create Safer and Stronger Neighbourhoods
topics: city initiatives, safety, youth; adolescents, city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives, public safety
brief: Mayor Chow is asking Council to expand CityServeTO, the paid work-experience program for youth most vulnerable to violence, to give 100 more young people aged 14-18 paid work experience, skills training, mentorship, and violence prevention support this summer. The expansion would add $0.615 million to the 2026 operating budget, offset by federal funds. It targets youth and communities the program identifies as most in need.

title: Exploring a Garden of Achievement with Canada’s Walk of Fame
topics: [activities in community and life], [locations in community and life];
brief: Canada's Walk of Fame wants to turn David Pecaut Square into a Garden of Achievement honouring notable Canadians. This motion asks Council to have City divisions work with Canada's Walk of Fame, Roy Thomson Hall, Mirvish Productions, the Toronto Downtown West BIA, and others to develop a concept plan for improving the public space on the block. It is a planning request, not a funding commitment.

title: Access to Outdoor Ovens in Parks: Progress Update
topics: outdoor fireplaces, parks; chimineas, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Council already directed staff to make park outdoor ovens easier to use: permit fees were dropped for Toronto residents and non-profits, insurance costs fell 30 per cent for repeat users, and ovens can now be booked online. This report asks Council to let the General Manager of Parks and Recreation set criteria for reimbursing insurance costs for the non-profits, charities, and community groups that run ovens for public programming; the report cites $10,000. It affects community groups running public oven programs.

title: Riverside District Business Improvement Area Expansion Poll Results
topics: business improvement areas, service boundaries; bia; business improvement associations, community council boundaries
brief: The Riverside District Business Improvement Area wants to expand its boundary, and a City Clerk-run poll found a majority of accepted ballots in favour. But staff found the process lacked consultation with key City divisions on issues like traffic management, so the recommended boundary has been revised to a partial expansion. Council is asked to designate the revised boundary and have staff review the BIA expansion process for better City-wide coordination.

title: Economic Development and Culture Grants - 2025 Funding Allocation and Museums and Heritage Grants
topics: economic development, subsidies and grants; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing, financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs
brief: Completing the City's multi-year culture-grant reform by establishing the Heritage Organization Operating Partnership, giving operating funding to not-for-profit heritage organizations, plus new Museums and Heritage Microgrant programs is on Council's agenda. No new funding is requested; the programs use money currently provided as directed grants. The change affects how Toronto's museums and heritage spaces get City support.

title: Sidewalks to Skylines: A 10-Year Action Plan for Toronto’s Economy (2025-2035) - Update on Implementation
topics: [actions of government], economy, taxes; levies
brief: One year into the City's 10-year Sidewalks to Skylines economic plan, staff report that over 90 per cent of its 73 actions are completed or in progress. Council is asked to adopt updates to those actions, folding in four actions from the mayor's US-tariff response plan and three new actions focused on inclusive economic development. The update shapes the City's economic strategy through 2035.

title: It’s Time to Reinstate Cummer Station for the North York Centre - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: public transit, subway stations; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: The current Yonge North Subway Extension plan skips a station at Cummer Avenue, leaving about 2 km between Finch and Steeles stations in an area slated for major growth, including 100,000 new residents under the North York Centre Secondary Plan. This motion asks Council to request federal and provincial funding to reinstate the previously dropped Cummer Station. The outcome affects transit access for one of the fastest-growing corridors in the region.

title: Towards a Vision for a Design Standard for Future Toronto Subway Stations - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: Future subway stations could be built to a new City design standard: the motion asks Council to direct the TTC, the City, and Metrolinx to study standards covering platform screen doors, public washrooms, bike parking and bike share, well-lit two-storey ceilings above platforms, and stations integrated into surrounding buildings. Citing examples like Taipei, the idea is to treat new stations on projects such as the Yonge North and Scarborough subway extensions as civic hubs with retail and community space. The outcome would shape how every new Toronto subway station is designed.

title: Responding to Bill 98, Building Homes and Improving Transportation Infrastructure Act, 2026 - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: Ontario's Bill 98 would let the provincial transportation minister set regional transit fare and service policies through a new Fare Alignment and Seamless Transit Act, with consultations possibly starting as early as May 2026. This motion asks Council to endorse the TTC board's principles for City staff taking part in those consultations. It matters because fare and service decisions are currently made by the TTC board through public plans and budgets.

title: Payment of Legal Expenses Related to an Integrity Commissioner Investigation
topics: refund; reimbursement
brief: A $20,807.61 reimbursement is on the table for Councillor Chris Moise's legal fees from an Integrity Commissioner investigation, under the members of council operations policy. Council decides whether to approve the payment.

title: 5051 to 5061 Yonge Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: buildings, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor is seeking Council's direction on the ongoing Tribunal appeal for 5051 to 5061 Yonge Street, where Council accepted a 2024 settlement for a 55-storey building with an on-site community space of at least 604 square metres, and the matter remains under appeal. The recommendations are confidential as legal advice.

title: 2912 to 2926 Sheppard Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor is seeking Council's direction on a Tribunal hearing about a proposed 50-storey mixed-use building with 590 homes at 2912 to 2926 Sheppard Avenue East, ahead of an October 20, 2026 hearing. Council directed the Solicitor to oppose the applications in February 2026; the matter is urgent. The recommendations are confidential as legal advice.

title: Leave to Intervene in Supreme Court of Canada Case addressing Municipal Powers: Westcan Recyclers Ltd. v. Calgary
topics: courts;
brief: Authorizing the City Solicitor to seek permission to intervene in a Supreme Court of Canada case — Westcan Recyclers Ltd, goes to City Council for approval. v. Calgary — about how far a municipality must distinguish its good-governance powers from its commercial powers when passing by-laws that also advance its own commercial interests. The costs of filing materials and, if leave is granted, taking part in the appeal are estimated at less than $10,000, funded through CreateTO's 2026 operating budget.

title: Implementation of New Municipal Requirements under the Buy Ontario Act, 2025
topics: intergovernmental relations, legislation, products; acts, agricultural products; goods; manufactured articles; manufactured products, federal-municipal relations; governmental relations; inter-governmental relations; intergovernmental cooperation; provincial-municipal relations
brief: Amending the City's procurement rules, effective May 25, 2026, to prefer Ontario-made goods and services first, then Canadian-made, as required by the province's Buy Ontario Act, 2025, goes to City Council for approval. The directive includes requirements for fleet vehicles — Made-in-Ontario vehicles first — and domestic supply-chain disclosure for capital infrastructure.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Licensing Tribunal
topics: nomination;
brief: Appointing Yizhe Chi and Deborah Moriah to the Toronto Licensing Tribunal for a term ending November 14, 2026 (and until successors are appointed), goes to City Council for approval. The tribunal handles licensing appeals. Remaining application details stay confidential.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Administrative Penalty Tribunal
topics: appointments, nomination;
brief: Appointing Stephen Scharbach to the Administrative Penalty Tribunal for a term ending April 25, 2030, replacing a previously recommended candidate who withdrew on April 14, 2026, goes to City Council for approval. The tribunal decides disputes over certain City penalties. Remaining application details stay confidential.

title: Update on 2026 Motorized Watercraft Exclusion Zones
topics: recreational watercraft; boat launching; boats; leisure water vehicles; pleasure boats; pleasure craft
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is asked to receive an update on the City's request that the Toronto Port Authority fund marker buoys showing the boundaries of motorized watercraft exclusion zones in the Port of Toronto. On May 20 and 21, 2026, Council adopted the plan: the Waterfront Secretariat will transfer $310,500 from the Wider Waterfront and Marine Strategy project, part of its 2026-2035 capital budget, toward buying and installing the marker buoys in 2026, and the City Manager is authorized to enter an agreement with the Toronto Port Authority to flow the funds.

title: Ombudsman Toronto 2025 Annual Report
topics: annual reports, ombudsman; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, ombudspersons
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is asked to receive the Ombudsman Toronto's 2025 annual report for information, as required by the City of Toronto Act. No decision is required.

title: Follow-Up on 2026.EC27.2 Review of Street Vending and Artists
topics: street vending; boulevard vending; curb lane vending; curblane vending; food carts; food vending carts; hot dog carts; sidewalk vending; vending
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is asked to receive a follow-up report on the 2026 review of street vending and artists by-laws, covering how to reduce amplified disturbances near residential areas and Sankofa Square. Staff will bring a supplementary report ahead of the May 2026 Council meeting. No decision is required.

title: 212 Dundas Street East - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property Under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Approving alterations to the heritage-designated properties at 212 Dundas Street East (the former Wilton Court Hotel) and 275 George Street (the Henry Tasker House), in connection with a revised proposal for a 44-storey residential building on the site, goes to City Council for approval. Council approved a 41-storey scheme in 2021; heritage staff are satisfied the revised alterations still conserve the properties.

title: 8 Arnold Avenue - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Adding 8 Arnold Avenue to the City's Heritage Register for its cultural heritage value — a red-brick one-and-one-half-storey Ontario Farmhouse-style home from the 1870s-1880s, known as the George Marshall Residence and the earliest known house in the Mount Dennis community, goes to City Council for a decision.

title: 180 Queens Drive - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Stating its intention to designate the Oliver Master House at 180 Queens Drive — a 1911 three-storey Shingle-style house in Weston — under the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value, goes to City Council for a decision. A previous intention to designate lapsed because the by-law was not passed within the 120-day window.

title: 2351 and 2355 Keele Street - Zoning By- Law Amendment Application - Request for Directions Report
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor is seeking Council's direction on a Tribunal hearing about a proposed 25-storey residential building with 311 homes at 2351 and 2355 Keele Street. The applicant appealed in June 2023 after Council failed to decide in time; no hearing date is set. The recommendations are confidential as legal advice.

title: 155 St Dennis Drive - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: buildings;
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor is seeking Council's direction on the Tribunal matter for 155 St. Dennis Drive — a proposed four-tower development with 2,170 homes, 5 percent affordable — where the Tribunal approved the applications in October 2025 after Council refused them in 2023, and Council has directed the Solicitor to seek leave to appeal to Divisional Court. The recommendations are confidential as legal advice.

title: 151 and 161 to 181 Mulock Avenue and 6 Lloyd Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Consent to Review Tribunal Decision
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor is seeking Council's consent to ask the Tribunal to review its 2024 decision on the mixed-use development at 151 and 161 to 181 Mulock Avenue and 6 Lloyd Avenue — two residential towers plus an office building, with a later settlement adding affordable housing — where pre-conditions remain outstanding. The recommendations are confidential as legal advice.

title: 1149 and 1153 Queen Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor is seeking Council's direction on a Tribunal hearing about a zoning by-law amendment application for 1149 and 1153 Queen Street West, which Council refused. The applicant appealed in April 2025. The recommendations are confidential as legal advice.

title: 2 to 4 and 80 Union Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning bylaws, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor is seeking Council's direction on a Tribunal hearing about a proposed three-building mixed-use development of 39 to 49 storeys at 2 to 4 and 80 Union Street, ahead of a ten-day hearing starting July 13, 2026. The applicant appealed in April 2025 after Council failed to decide in time; the matter is urgent. The recommendations are confidential as legal advice.

title: 112 Walmer Road - Development Charges Complaint and Parkland Levy Appeal - Request for Directions
topics: development charges;
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor is seeking Council's direction on a development-charges complaint and parkland-levy appeal for a five-unit project (a fourplex plus garden suite) at 112 Walmer Road. The matter is urgent. The recommendations are confidential as legal advice.

title: Making it Easier to Build More Housing: Extending Development Charge Incentives to Condominium Multiplexes and Engaging on the Review of the Ontario Building Code
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: Extending development charge incentives — currently waiving charges for up to six units plus a garden or laneway suite — to condominium multiplexes, making it cheaper to build missing-middle housing, goes to City Council for approval. Council is also asked to have the Chief Building Official work with the province on streamlining the Ontario Building Code, following talks with multiplex planners, architects and builders.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority Board
topics: board members, public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Civic Appointments Committee is asked to select four candidates to interview for appointment to the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority Board, then recommend one to City Council. Candidate details stay confidential.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre Board
topics: board members, public appointments;
brief: Appointing two public members to the Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre Board for a term ending May 22, 2028 (and until successors are appointed), goes to City Council for approval. The nominees' details stay confidential as they concern identifiable individuals.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Board of Directors of TO Live
topics: board members, public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Civic Appointments Committee is asked to recommend three candidates to City Council for appointment to the TO Live Board of Directors, for a term ending May 23, 2030 (and until successors are appointed). Candidate details stay confidential.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: general bills and confirming bills will come before City Council, the formal step that makes Council's decisions law. The source material gives no further detail.

title: Moss Park Arena - 2024 Audited Financial Statements
topics: arenas, audits, financial reports; annual financial reports; financial statements, auditors; auditors, indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is asked to receive for information the 2024 audited financial statements and management letter for Moss Park Arena — the last of the eight City arenas to be presented. No decision is required.

title: Cybersecurity Audit of Exhibition Place - Phase Two: Overall Network Security and Cybersecurity Assessment of Select Critical Systems
topics: Exhibition Place, [activities in science and technology], audits, security; auditors; auditors
brief: The Auditor General's phase-two cybersecurity audit of Exhibition Place covers network security and selected critical systems, following phase one's look at physical security, user access and staff training. Exhibition Place generates $595 million in annual economic impact and earned $67.3 million in revenue in 2024. City Council is asked to authorize releasing the report once the Auditor General approves it after consulting officials.

title: Investigation into the Procurement of the PayIt Platform
topics: audits, investigation, proposals, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, auditors; auditors, bids; request for proposal; rfp, investigators
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is asked to receive for information the Auditor General's investigation into the procurement of the PayIt platform. The investigation followed Council's 2024 request to look further into the scoring of the Swiss Challenge negotiated RFP, whether more City records exist on servers or private devices of senior staff, and whether a forensic investigation is needed. No policy change is proposed.

title: Audit of Corporate Real Estate Management: Strengthening Accountability and Oversight of Change Orders in Capital Projects
topics: construction, management (sc), projects, properties (real estate); building, property; real estate
brief: The Auditor General's audit of Corporate Real Estate Management found its oversight of change orders on large capital construction projects needs strengthening, since poorly managed change orders can cause delays and significant cost increases. She asks City Council to direct the division to improve and formalize its change-order policies — with clear approval authority, thresholds and documentation — applied consistently across all projects.

title: Collective Bargaining and Labour Update
body: Toronto Transit Commission - People, Culture and Governance Committee
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, [activities in employment and labour], labour relations; collective bargaining; employee relations; labor relations; union-management relations, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the People, Culture and Governance Committee will receive an in-camera (private) update on collective bargaining and labour matters. The committee is asked to keep the information in Confidential Attachment 1 private in its entirety, as it concerns labour relations and employee negotiations.

title: Application for One Variance, Subject to Four Conditions, Respecting One Third Party Electronic Ground Sign - 3493 Kingston Road
topics: electronic signs, signs; changeable message signs; electronic billboard signs; electronic overhead message signs, signage
brief: The Sign Variance Committee will decide on one variance that would let the Chief Building Official issue a permit for a double-faced third-party electronic ground sign at 3493 Kingston Road. The applicant, JOLT Charge Inc, proposes a sign up to 2.65 metres high with two back-to-back faces showing static electronic copy. The variance would be subject to four conditions.

title: Application for Five Variances, Each Subject to Three Conditions, Respecting One Third Party Electronic Ground Sign - 123 Rexdale Boulevard
topics: electronic signs, signs; changeable message signs; electronic billboard signs; electronic overhead message signs, signage
brief: The Sign Variance Committee will decide on five variances that would let the Chief Building Official issue a permit for a double-sided third-party electronic ground sign at 123 Rexdale Boulevard. The applicant, JOLT Charge Inc, proposes a sign up to 2.65 metres high with two back-to-back faces showing static electronic copy. Each variance would be subject to three conditions.

title: Appointments to the Sign Variance Committee
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council has appointed Stephen Job and Farzana Jiwani to the Sign Variance Committee for a term beginning April 24, 2026 and ending April 24, 2030, filling the seats of Janet Ross and Anne Milchberg, whose terms ended April 23, 2026. Council also appointed Derek Lett as committee Chair. The committee rules on sign variance applications across the city.

title: Using 311 and Other Data to Identify Trends and Improve Service Delivery in Parks and Recreation, Transportation Services and Municipal Licensing and Standards
topics: advisory committees, recreation policies, service delivery, service quality, transportation; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups, transportation services
brief: On March 23, 2026, the Service Excellence Committee asked Parks and Recreation, Transportation Services, and Municipal Licensing and Standards to report back on how they use 311 data and other data to spot trends and improve service. This is that report-back, outlining how 311 information supports service delivery across the three divisions. The committee will consider the findings.

title: Simplifying the 311 Intake Experience
topics: customer service, non emergency municipal services, service quality; 3-1-1; 311; 311 calls; non-emergency city services
brief: City staff are bringing the Service Excellence Committee a plan with a phased approach to simplify the 311 intake process: streamlining the public-facing service categories and consolidating service codes where it makes sense. The work also covers improvements to how people access and track city services across every 311 channel: phone, email, online, mobile app, X, and in-person counters. The goal is a clearer, more intuitive 311 experience.

title: Barbara Hall Park Revitalization Project Update
body: Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Queer Advisory Committee
topics: parkettes;
brief: The item asks for an update from Parks and Recreation on the Barbara Hall Park revitalization in the Church-Wellesley Village, with feedback from the 2SLGBTQ+ Advisory Committee. The revitalization focuses on preserving and enhancing the AIDS Memorial and Trans Memorial, two sites of deep significance to the community. The committee is asked to receive the presentation.

title: Thrive Toronto Mental Health Report Card and Toronto Public Health Action on 2SLGBTQ+ Mental Health
body: Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Queer Advisory Committee
topics: mental health care and counselling; mental health agencies; mental health centres; psychiatric treatment; pyschiatry
brief: This is a procedural item: the 2SLGBTQ+ Advisory Committee will hear findings from Toronto Public Health and the Wellesley Institute on the Thrive Toronto Mental Health Report Card and public health work supporting 2SLGBTQ+ mental health and well-being. No decision is being asked for.

title: FOCUS Toronto and WomanACT Pilot
body: Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Queer Advisory Committee
topics: safety; public safety
brief: This is a procedural item: the 2SLGBTQ+ Advisory Committee will hear a presentation on SafeTO, Toronto's 10-year community safety and well-being plan, and the FOCUS Toronto and WomanACT pilot. No decision is being asked for.

title: Initiatives to Support 2SLGBTQ+ Communities Experiencing Homelessness
