topics: advisory committees, community outreach, homelessness; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups, awareness programs; community engagement; outreach; promotion (communication); public outreach
brief: This is a procedural item: the 2SLGBTQ+ Advisory Committee will hear a presentation from Toronto Shelter and Support Services and The 519 on the homelessness system and recent initiatives to better support 2SLGBTQ+ people experiencing homelessness. The presentation covers key data, system improvements, and partnerships for more inclusive responses. No decision is being asked for.

title: Queen's Park North Revitalization Project Update
body: Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Queer Advisory Committee
topics: advisory committees; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups
brief: This is a procedural item: the 2SLGBTQ+ Advisory Committee will receive a presentation from the Queen's Park North Revitalization Project team on community engagement and design development for the park. No decision is being asked for.

title: 40 Wabash Avenue - Alterations to and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Designated Heritage Property under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: demolitions, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council approve alterations and demolitions under Sections 33 and 34(1) of the Ontario Heritage Act for 40 Wabash Avenue — the City-owned former linseed oil mill factory built in phases from 1910 into the 1940s, with its prominent chimney stack. Vacant since 1969 and acquired by the City in 2000, the property sits beside Sorauren Avenue Park; council approved a budget in 2016 for redeveloping the lands including adaptive re-use of the former factory. The approval would advance the long-planned reuse of the site.

title: 6-8 and 10-12 Sumach Street - Alterations to Designated Heritage Properties Under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: easements, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council approve alterations to the designated heritage properties at 6-8 Sumach Street and 10-12 Sumach Street under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and enter a Heritage Easement Agreement, in connection with a proposal for two new mixed-use and residential towers. The two pairs of Victorian-era terrace houses — built 1886–1888 as workers' housing and designated in 2026 — would be relocated on the development site. Staff are satisfied the proposal conserves the heritage properties.
address: 10 - 12 Sumach Toronto Ontario; 6 - 8 Sumach Toronto Ontario

title: 20 Gerrard Street East - Alterations of a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: easements, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council approve alterations and demolition of heritage attributes of the designated heritage property at 20 Gerrard Street East (the former Willard Hall building) under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and enter a Heritage Easement Agreement. The four-storey Georgian-style institutional building — owned by Covenant House Toronto and used as a social service facility for vulnerable populations — would support a new 7-storey building enhancing its ongoing use for transitional housing, wellness, education, employment and community programs. Staff are satisfied the proposal conserves the heritage properties.

title: 153 and 185 Eastern Avenue - Alterations to Designated Heritage Properties Under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: easements, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council approve alterations to the designated heritage properties at 153 Eastern Avenue (Cleaning Room building) and 185 Eastern Avenue (Machine Shop building) under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act, with authority to enter a Heritage Easement Agreement, in connection with a proposal for three new residential towers with commercial and community uses. The two buildings of the Dominion Wheel & Foundries Ltd. Complex are rare surviving examples of the industrial complex typology in the West Don Lands. Staff are satisfied the proposal conserves the heritage properties.

title: 150 College Street (Medical Sciences Building - 1 King's College Circle) - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter Into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: easements, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council approve alterations to the designated heritage property at 150 College Street (Medical Sciences Building, 1 King's College Circle) under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and enter a Heritage Easement Agreement, in connection with rehabilitating the University of Toronto's Medical Sciences Building. The 1966–1970 complex — with its sculptural precast concrete panel cladding designed by Canadian artists Robert Downing and Ted Bieler, housing the Temerty Faculty of Medicine — is a significant example of the university's post-war expansion. The easement secures long-term conservation.

title: 212 Dundas Street East - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property Under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council approve alterations to the designated heritage properties at 212 Dundas Street East (the former Wilton Court Hotel) and 275 George Street (the Henry Tasker House) under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act, in the Garden District Heritage Conservation District. The previously approved 41-storey development has been revised to 44 storeys with a revised conservation strategy; staff are satisfied the alterations continue to conserve the on-site and adjacent heritage properties.

title: 50 Park Road - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Refusal
topics: heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council refuse the heritage permit for alterations to 50 Park Road under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The 1954 building — constructed as the headquarters of the Ontario Association of Architects by John B. Parkin, acclaimed as a 'landmark modern building' for its simple low form, clean lines and exposed steel in a park setting — is part of a proposal for a 31-storey mixed-use building (with demolition of 38 and 40 Park Road) that retains and integrates the heritage building and has been appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal. Staff do not consider the alterations appropriate for the heritage property.

title: 81 Chestnut Park - Application to Erect a Structure in the South Rosedale Heritage Conservation District
topics: heritage conservation districts, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, heritage districts; historic areas
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council approve the proposal to build a new coach-house-style dwelling at 81 Chestnut Park in the South Rosedale Heritage Conservation District under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The proposed structure — designed to complement the larger home at 77 Chestnut Park, from which the property was divided, with compatible setback, height and scale — is considered to comply with the district plan, the Official Plan and the Parks Canada conservation standards.

title: 339 Queen Street East - Proposed Amendment to Designating By-law under Part IV, Section 30.1 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: by-laws, heritage properties; bylaws, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council amend the 2017 designation by-law for 339 Queen Street East to add Cecil B. Tadman's nearly 50-year ownership as the Home Furniture Company Limited, to further describe the building as a Chicago School-style example and to add the historic post-and-beam timber frame construction as a heritage attribute. The 1907 three-storey brick store and warehouse (extended 1925–1926) at Queen Street East and Parliament Street operated as a furniture store for over a century, including as the WE Global Learning Centre after a 2017 rehabilitation.

title: 170 Merton Street - Demolition of a Heritage Attribute under Section 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: easements, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council approve demolition of a heritage attribute — the original terrace — at 170 Merton Street under Section 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and amend the Heritage Easement Agreement, in connection with a proposed 45-storey mixed-use residential building. The 1969 former Visiting Homemakers Association headquarters — a Late Modern office building with octagonal towers, ribbon windows and interlocking concrete brick, the first purpose-built headquarters of the social-welfare agency founded in 1925 — would have part of its building retained, with the terrace demolished, reconstructed and extended. Staff consider the revised proposal still conserves the heritage property.

title: 1337 Queen Street West - Demolition and New Construction on a Designated Heritage Property under Part V, Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act -Approval
topics: demolitions, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council approve demolishing the existing building on the non-contributing property at 1337 Queen Street West in the Parkdale Main Street Heritage Conservation District and erect a replacement building under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The work is part of the West Block of the City-led Parkdale Hub project — a strategic city-building initiative around Queen Street West and Cowan Avenue that includes the Parkdale library branch and the Masaryk-Cowan Community Recreation Centre, with redevelopment approved by council in November 2023. The Parkdale district plan came into force in June 2025.

title: 17-19, 23 and 25 Toronto Street and 55 Adelaide Street East - Alterations to Heritage Properties, Demolition of a Building within the St. Lawrence Neighbourhood Heritage Conservation District, Approval of a Replacement Building and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: demolitions, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council approve alterations under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act to the designated heritage properties at 17-19 Toronto Street, 25 Toronto Street and 55 Adelaide Street East, approve demolition of the non-contributing 23 Toronto Street, and authorize a Heritage Easement Agreement — all in connection with a proposed 91-storey mixed-use tower in the St. Lawrence Neighbourhood Heritage Conservation District. The proposal fully retains 17-19 Toronto Street and 57 Adelaide Street East, keeps the façades of 25 Toronto Street and 55 Adelaide Street East in place, and replaces 23 Toronto Street with a compliant low-rise building.

title: 958 Broadview Avenue - Alterations to a Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage properties, planning; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council approve alterations to the former Chester Public School (now Estonian House) at 958 Broadview Avenue under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and amend the Heritage Easement Agreement. The 1891 school — a late-19th-century village school combining American Richardsonian Romanesque and British Queen Anne styles — would be incorporated into a 14-storey residential tower with ground-floor retail approved in 2022, with removal of unsympathetic 1962–1995 additions and restoration of the heritage fabric.

title: Property Included on the City's Heritage Register - Consideration of Objection for 1767 Bayview Avenue, 1773 Bayview Avenue and 73 Niagara Street
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Three owners have objected to their properties' listing on the Heritage Register — 1767 and 1773 Bayview Avenue (mid-1930s two-storey apartment buildings listed December 2024) and 73 Niagara Street (listed December 2019). Under Section 27(7) of the Ontario Heritage Act, council must now decide whether to keep or remove the listings. Heritage staff's recommendation is before council.
address: 1767 - 1773 Bayview Toronto Ontario; 73 Niagara Toronto Ontario

title: 65 Heward Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate 65 Heward Avenue (including 87 Heward) in South Riverdale under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. Completed in 1913 for the Canadian Ammonia Company to designs by Curry and Sparling Architects, the two brick factory/warehouse buildings later housed Cine Village, once one of Canada's largest all-in-one production centres. Council must decide at its May 20–22, 2026 meeting, since the owner's waiver on the Ontario Heritage Act decision timeline expires May 31, 2026.

title: 30-32 and 38-40 Huntley Street and 122-124 Isabella Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate the properties at 30-32 Huntley Street, 38-40 Huntley Street and 122-124 Isabella Street in North St. James Town under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The Huntley Street properties are two pairs of Second Empire-style semi-detached residences with buff brick cladding and mansard roofs with ornate dormers, brackets and cornice — listed on the Heritage Register since 1976 and 1991. Designation is the first legal step toward protecting the properties' heritage attributes.
address: 122 - 124 Isabella Toronto Ontario; 30 - 32 Huntley Toronto Ontario; 38 - 40 Huntley Toronto Ontario

title: 320 McCowan Road, 1311 - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number 26 121433 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal law, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the owner of 320 McCowan Road, unit 1311 is appealing a property standards order issued March 13, 2026 (file 26 121433 PRS 00 IV) to the Property Standards Committee. The committee hears the appeal and can uphold, amend, or rescind the order.

title: 3131 Eglinton Avenue East - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number 25 256381 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal law, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: an appeal of the property standards order for 3131 Eglinton Avenue East goes before the Property Standards Committee. The order was issued November 25, 2025 (file 25 256381 PRS 00 IV). The committee will decide whether the order stands, changes, or is cancelled.

title: 62 Glen Everest Road, 404 - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number 26 122468 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal law, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee will hear the property owner's appeal of a property standards order issued March 4, 2026 for 62 Glen Everest Road, unit 404 (file 26 122468 PRS 00 IV). The committee can confirm, change, or cancel the order. The hearing gives the owner a chance to challenge the city's maintenance or repair requirements.

title: 40 Aurora Court - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number 26 113492 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal law, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the owner of 40 Aurora Court is appealing a property standards order issued February 9, 2026 (file 26 113492 PRS 00 IV) to the Property Standards Committee. The committee hears the appeal and can uphold, amend, or rescind the order.

title: 3434 Eglinton Ave E, 1103 - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number 26 116645 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal law, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: an appeal of the property standards order for 3434 Eglinton Avenue East, unit 1103 goes before the Property Standards Committee. The order was issued February 13, 2026 (file 26 116645 PRS 00 IV). The committee will decide whether the order stands, changes, or is cancelled.

title: Implementation of a Commercial Loading Zone on Queen Street East
topics: loading zones, parking; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones
brief: Paid parking on the north side of Queen Street East, just east of Jones Avenue, would be temporarily converted into a commercial loading zone while the laneway behind the businesses — the primary loading area for shops on Queen east of Jones — is rebuilt starting in May. Councillor Paula Fletcher's motion asks City Council to approve the temporary zone; the street would return to its previous parking rules once construction is done. The converted pay-parking spaces charge $3.25 per hour.

title: Mirvish Village - Traffic Amendments (Non-Delegated)
topics: parking regulations, traffic, turn prohibitions (traffic); motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Up for a decision before City Council: ban northbound left turns and southbound right turns at all times at Bathurst Street and the private driveway at 758 Bathurst Street, as part of the traffic plan for the Mirvish Village redevelopment. The bans would reinforce the area's one-way operations — Markham Street running northbound between Lennox and Bloor, and the new private east-west driveway running eastbound — and are meant to deter unsafe turns around the mixed-use project.

title: Exclusion of Bloor-Dufferin from On-Street Residential Permit Parking
topics: accessible permit parking, parking, permit parking; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled), on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: City Council will weigh whether to have staff study whether the Bloor-Dufferin development at 980 Dufferin Street and 1141 Bloor Street West can be excluded from on-street permit parking. Councillor Alejandra Bravo's motion asks Transportation Services to report back on the feasibility; excluding new developments is meant to manage parking supply and encourage walking, cycling, and transit use, in line with the city's goals to reduce congestion and emissions.

title: 333 Lake Shore Boulevard East, 200 Queens Quay East, and 2, 11, and 11 R Small Street (Quayside Blocks 3, 4 and 5) - Draft Plan of Subdivision Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, applications, planning, subdivision (land); application process, subdivision of land
brief: This is a procedural item: the report advises that the Executive Director, Development Review — acting under delegated authority — intends to approve the draft plan of subdivision for Quayside Blocks 3, 4, and 5, subject to conditions. The plan would create eight blocks: an extension of Queens Quay East, two development blocks totalling 1.015 hectares, two public streets, two public parks (Silo Park and the Water's Edge Promenade), and the Parliament Slip lake fill. Conditions include transferring streets and parkland to the city, reserving a block for a school, and building municipal services.

title: Bay Street and Edward Street - Traffic Control Signals
topics: traffic control systems, traffic management; traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Traffic signals would be installed at Bay Street and Edward Street, which staff say are justified and would make the intersection safer for all road users. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates on Bay Street; the item also updates stopping and parking rules on Edward Street and fixes mismatches between the posted signs and the by-law.

title: Lake Shore Boulevard East - Mid-Block Pedestrian and Cyclist Traffic Control Signal and Public Realm Improvements
topics: cyclists, pedestrians, public realm, traffic control systems; pedestrianization, public spaces, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: A mid-block traffic signal for pedestrians and cyclists would be installed on Lake Shore Boulevard East about 180 metres east of Cherry Street, closing a gap in the trail between Cherry Street and the Don River bridge. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to authorize the signal and ban northbound left turns there at all times. The report also updates council on public realm improvement plans for Lake Shore Boulevard East between Carlaw Avenue and Leslie Street.

title: Traffic and Parking Amendments -  Toronto Transit Commission (TTC) Traction Power Upgrade Project
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, parking regulations, traffic regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws, ttc
brief: Paid parking would be temporarily removed on sections of Granby Street, McGill Street, and nearby streets from April to August 2026 to make room for the TTC's traction power upgrade — the first project in a program of critical electrical upgrades to substations and duct banks needed to support more subway service and bigger station capacity. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates on Yonge Street. The removed pay-parking spaces, where the rate is $6.75 per hour, would be restored after construction.

title: Bayview Avenue - Parking Amendments
topics: parking, parking regulations, stopping prohibitions, traffic regulations; no stopping, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: The no-stopping rule in the west-side right-turn lane on Bayview Avenue near Front Street East would be relaxed to a no-standing rule, so drivers — including TTC buses at the transit stop — can pick up and drop off passengers. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates on Bayview Avenue.

title: 1423 Dufferin Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A nine-storey mixed-use building with 60 purpose-built rental homes is proposed for 1423 Dufferin Street, and City Council is asked to approve the zoning amendment. The project includes 123 square metres of ground-floor shops along Dufferin and a small laneway widening; the building would also be excluded from overnight permit parking. Staff say it fits provincial policy and the Official Plan.

title: Accessible Parking Spaces - April 2026 (Non-Delegated)
topics: accessibility, parking, parking regulations; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: It's City Council's call whether to approve installing new on-street accessible parking spaces for people with disabilities at various locations on streets where the TTC operates transit service. Council approval is required for those streets; this is a routine adjustment of designated accessible spots.

title: Market Street - Temporary Street Closure
topics: parking regulations, road closures, traffic regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Market Street between The Esplanade and Front Street East would close to vehicles from May 10, 2026 to January 9, 2027 for the Old Town Toronto BIA's Market Street closure event. City Council approval is required because the city cannot close a road for more than four days without it; community council does not have delegated authority for this one.

title: 3459 and 3461 Dundas Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A seven-storey mixed-use building with 45 homes is proposed for 3459 and 3461 Dundas Street West, and City Council is asked to approve the zoning amendment. The 2,520-square-metre project includes 65 square metres of ground-floor retail and a mix of unit types; the development would also be excluded from Permit Parking Area 1E. Staff say it fits provincial policy and the Official Plan and improves the public realm along Dundas.

title: 53-55 Yonge Street - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
topics: construction, parking prohibitions, road closures, road restrictions, stopping prohibitions; building, lane restrictions; road information; traffic restrictions; trip info; tripinfo, no parking, no stopping, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: H&R REIT is demolishing the buildings at 53 and 55 Yonge Street ahead of a future development and needs its construction staging extended from May 1 to July 31, 2026 — on Yonge Street between Wellington Street East and Colborne Street, and on Colborne Street between Yonge and Scott Street — after delays in sorting out staging boundaries with the TTC's King Station accessibility project, which wraps up May 1, 2026. City Council approval is required because Yonge is a major arterial road. The item also touches parking-machine rules where the rate is $6.75 per hour.

title: 49 Ontario Street (Phase 1) - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, parking regulations, sidewalks, traffic regulations; building, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Two rental towers including affordable housing are planned for 49 Ontario Street, between Ontario and Berkeley Streets, and the first construction phase — below-grade work — needs 18 months of closures. City Council approval is required because Adelaide Street East is a major arterial road; staff recommend closing the north sidewalk and the northerly eastbound cycle track on Adelaide from April 23, 2026 to September 30, 2027, plus the east boulevard and full sidewalk on Ontario Street. Pedestrians would be redirected to the south side of Adelaide, with a temporary crossover on Ontario Street, and the item also touches parking-machine rules where the rate is $4.25 per hour.

title: Quayside Infrastructure and Public Realm Project (Phase 2) - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, public realm, road closures; building, public spaces, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Waterfront Toronto's Quayside infrastructure project needs the next phase of temporary closures — including part of the Martin Goodman Trail on Parliament Street and sections of Queens Quay East — from April to December 2026. City Council approval is required because Queens Quay East is a major arterial road; the closures support the project's street realignments, servicing connections, and public-realm work, which will unlock development parcels with affordable housing commitments and deliver new public spaces. Council already authorized earlier closures running to October 2026.

title: 3286-3316 Dundas Street West - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, rental housing, residential properties; rental properties; rental units, residential real estate
brief: Six rental units at 3286-3316 Dundas Street West would be demolished for the proposed 11-storey, 191-unit rental building, and City Council is asked to approve the rental housing demolition application. All six rentals would be replaced within the new development and protected for 20 years, with a tenant assistance plan giving existing tenants a right of return at similar rents plus financial compensation for hardship. The report also attaches a $20,000.00 financial condition to the approval.

title: 171 East Liberty Street - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Adding 171 East Liberty Street — the former 1942 John Inglis Company factory complex of three brick buildings, including the Bren Gun assembly and test buildings — to the city's Heritage Register is on City Council's agenda. Listing recognizes the property's cultural heritage value under the provincial criteria and is the first step toward possible future protection. The complex is part of an important collection of surviving industrial buildings in Liberty Village.

title: 699 and 707 Yonge Street - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Refusal
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff want City Council to refuse heritage alterations for the 1887 building at 699 and 707 Yonge Street — home of the Brass Rail Tavern since 1948 — tied to a proposed 64-storey mixed-use tower. The plan would keep the heritage façade within the tower's three-storey base with a three-metre stepback, but staff say the stepback and ground-floor treatment do not adequately conserve the property's cultural heritage values, and the related Official Plan and zoning amendments do not conform with policy. If the owner appeals, the City Solicitor would oppose the appeal.

title: 8 Prince Arthur Avenue - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property Under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Approval
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Three new storeys would be added to the rear half of the heritage-designated 1886 building at 8 Prince Arthur Avenue, bringing the rear to six storeys for expanded office space, under a conservation plan to protect its heritage features. City Council is asked to approve the alterations under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The addition would rise above the existing roof ridge — which the East Annex district guidelines discourage — but staff support it because the addition sits behind the ridge and has low visibility from the street.

title: Bloor - Yorkville Cultural Heritage Resource Assessment - Final Report
topics: [attributes in culture], heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The call on whether to adopt a list of Bloor-Yorkville properties identified as having potential cultural heritage value, the product of the area's Cultural Heritage Resource Assessment belongs to City Council. Council would also direct staff to study part of the Yorkville Village Core — including community consultation — to decide whether it merits a Heritage Conservation District study. The assessment documents the area's development history to identify buildings and landscapes worth conserving.

title: 55 Lake Shore Boulevard East - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: agreements, easements, heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, tenancy agreements
brief: The heritage-designated former LCBO complex at 55 Lake Shore Boulevard East would be altered under a revised plan that puts the new towers above the Warehouse Building only, rather than above both the Office and Warehouse buildings as approved in 2022. City Council is asked to approve the alterations under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and to amend the existing heritage easement agreement. A new heritage impact assessment from March 2026 accompanies the revised conservation strategy for the rare purpose-built provincial headquarters and industrial complex.

title: Chinatown Tomorrow Planning Initiative - Proposals Report
topics: culture (sc), planning;
brief: A draft West Chinatown Planning Framework — along with proposed Official Plan and zoning changes — is being put forward as the basis for public consultation on how the area should grow. City Council is asked to approve using the draft for consultation in the second quarter of 2026, with a final report expected in July 2026. The framework aims to conserve West Chinatown's built form and cultural heritage, keep its distinctive retail character, support affordable housing, and make sure parks and community services meet local needs.

title: 3286, 3290, 3296, 3298, 3300, 3308 and 3316 Dundas Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: An 11-storey mixed-use rental building with 191 homes is proposed for 3286 to 3316 Dundas Street West, and City Council is asked to approve the zoning amendment. Six rental units would be demolished and replaced with six rental replacement units, with a tenant assistance plan giving existing tenants a right of return at similar rents; the project also includes ground-floor commercial space, 99 car parking spots, and 212 bicycle spaces. A separate rental demolition report goes to community council on April 1, 2026.

title: 333 College Street and 303 Augusta Avenue - Community Benefits Charge In-kind Offer
topics: charges, community benefits;
brief: The question before City Council: whether to accept the developer's in-kind community benefits offer for the 20-storey, 638-unit student residence approved at 333 College Street and 303 Augusta Avenue: paving Ellen Avenue to city standards, doing the title research needed to bring the abutting lanes into city ownership, and adding lighting, paving, and public-realm improvements to the lanes serving Kensington Community School. The in-kind work would cover up to 40 percent of the community benefits charge value; council separately directed that 60 percent of the charge funds go to Toronto Community Housing capital upgrades in Ward 11.

title: 353 and 355 Adelaide Street West, 46 Charlotte Street and 16 Oxley Street - Community Benefits Charge In-kind Contribution
topics: charges, community benefits, development; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: The developer of a 58-storey, 557-unit mixed-use building at 353 and 355 Adelaide Street West, 46 Charlotte Street, and 16 Oxley Street is offering 10 affordable rental units for 25 years as its in-kind community benefits contribution, instead of paying part of the community benefits charge. City Council is asked to accept the offer, which staff say equals 100 percent of 4 percent of the site's value under the community benefits by-law. The zoning was settled at the Ontario Land Tribunal in 2024, with the final order issued December 3, 2025.

title: 19 to 37 Queens Quay East (Pier 27, Phase 3) - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The developer of the Pier 27 site at 19-37 Queens Quay East wants to rework its two remaining buildings — shrinking Building A at 25 Queens Quay East from 13 to 11 storeys while adding units, and growing Building F at 35 Queens Quay East from 13 to 45 storeys with 449 homes — and appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on October 27, 2025 after City Council missed its decision deadline. Council is now asked to direct the City Solicitor to oppose the application in its current form at the tribunal while staff keep negotiating with the applicant. Building A currently has site plan approval for 132 homes plus street-level retail and a childcare centre.

title: 509 Parliament Street (Carlton Theatre) - Alterations and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The 1929 Carlton Theatre at 509 Parliament Street — a one-storey brick former movie theatre designated in 2024, though the designation by-law is under appeal — would have some of its heritage features altered and removed to make way for the proposed 10-storey mixed-use building. City Council is asked to approve the changes under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and to enter into a heritage easement agreement. Heritage staff support the proposal, which keeps the theatre's west elevation along Parliament Street in place, and say the heritage impacts are appropriately handled.

title: 509 Parliament Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal
topics: community councils, planning, zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council will weigh whether to approve the zoning amendment for a 10-storey mixed-use building with 60 homes and about 278 square metres of ground-floor shops at 509 Parliament Street. The property has been identified for heritage designation, though the designation by-law is under appeal before the Ontario Land Tribunal, so the design keeps part of the front façade within the new building. A separate heritage alterations report will come to council alongside this item.

title: 1196-1210 Yonge Street and 2-8 Birch Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, rental housing, residential tenants, tenants; rental properties; rental units, renters; tenancy agreements
brief: Eight rental units at 1196-1210 Yonge Street and 2-8 Birch Avenue would be demolished for the planned high-rise development, and City Council is asked to approve the rental housing demolition application. The eight replacement rentals would be built off-site in new multiplexes at 257 and 261 Poplar Plains Road, with existing tenants able to move directly into them at similar rents plus financial compensation for hardship. The zoning for the site was settled at the Ontario Land Tribunal for a 31-storey, 122-unit mixed-use building, with council endorsing a revised 32-storey, 64-unit version subject to the tribunal's approval. The report also recommends a residential demolition permit and attaches a $20,000.00 financial condition to the approval.

title: 10 Rosehill Avenue - City-Initiated Temporary Use Zoning By-law - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The decision on approving a city-initiated temporary zoning change letting the existing building at 10 Rosehill Avenue host concert hall, place of amusement, assembly hall, or broadcasting studio uses for three years rests with City Council. The temporary-use by-law would allow these uses on a trial basis within the current building.

title: 55-77 Davisville Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 37-storey residential building is proposed for 55-77 Davisville Avenue, and City Council is asked to approve the zoning amendment. The existing 29-storey rental building at 77 Davisville, with 483 rental units, would be kept; the project would add a mid-block walkway from Davisville Avenue to Balliol Street and a new 406-square-metre park fronting Balliol. Staff say the proposal fits provincial policy, the Official Plan, and the Yonge-Eglinton Secondary Plan, and the owner would be required to develop a construction mitigation and tenant communication plan for the existing renters.

title: Nightstar Road - Traffic Calming (Speed Cushions) and Heavy Vehicle Prohibition
topics: assessment, traffic calming;
brief: City Council will decide on a report about Nightstar Road, between Morningside Avenue and Mantis Road/Knotwood Crescent/Flower Crescent, covering proposed speed cushions and a heavy vehicle prohibition. Transportation Services does not recommend the speed cushions, finding the warrant criteria were not met. Because the TTC operates on Nightstar Road and the report includes non-delegated matters, City Council approval is required.

title: 2740 Lawrence Avenue East - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: exemptions, part lot control; exceptions
brief: The question before City Council: whether to approve a Part Lot Control Exemption application for 2740 Lawrence Avenue East, following the related decision report and by-law council adopted in November 2024. The exemption would allow the creation and conveyance of 65 three-storey townhouse units with maintenance easements in Blocks 37 through 45 on Plan 66M-2589. The step advances the townhouse development already in the works.

title: Morrish Road - Traffic Calming
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: City Council will decide whether to authorize speed cushions on Morrish Road. Councillor Neethan Shan recommends the installation after the Highland Creek Community Association and surveyed residents expressed support and staff completed the drawings, as a step toward more traffic calming in the area.

title: Pharmacy Avenue and Stellarton Road/Camilla Crescent - Traffic Control Signals
topics: traffic calming, traffic control systems, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: City Council will decide whether to install traffic control signals at the intersection of Pharmacy Avenue and Stellarton Road/Camilla Crescent. Transportation Services says the signals are justified and would improve safety for all road users. Because the TTC operates on Pharmacy Avenue, City Council approval is required.

title: Kennedy Road, at a point 140 metres north of Dancy Avenue -Traffic Control Signals
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, traffic control systems; traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment, ttc
brief: City Council will decide whether to install traffic control signals on Kennedy Road, 140 metres north of Dancy Avenue, and remove the existing pedestrian refuge island about 50 metres north of Dancy. Transportation Services says the signals are justified and would improve safety for all road users. Because the TTC operates on Kennedy Road, City Council approval is required.

title: 5445 Steeles Avenue East Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: gas stations, redevelopment, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: City Council decides whether to approve a zoning amendment for 5445 Steeles Avenue East that would redevelop the existing gas station and add a vehicle washing establishment. The renovated facility would have four new gas pumps, two electric vehicle charging stations, an expanded retail store, and no drive-through restaurant. The proposal would modernize the site with EV charging while removing the restaurant.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council reviews the Order Paper, the list of business before it. No decision is involved beyond organizing the meeting's work.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions, and announcements are made at the council meeting. No decision is involved.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: council members may file petitions at the meeting. No decision is involved.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: council members declare any interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act before business begins. No policy decision is involved.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council formally introduces the committee reports coming forward to this meeting, including reports from the Executive Committee, Civic Appointments Committee, Corporations Nominating Panel, Economic and Community Development Committee, and General Government Committee. The item sets the agenda for what council will consider. No decision is made at this step.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council confirms the minutes from its regular meeting of March 25 and 26, 2026. No policy decision is involved.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council opens its meeting with O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is involved.

title: 2700 Dufferin Street - Official Plan Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments;
brief: An application to redesignate most of 2700 Dufferin Street from General Employment Areas to Mixed Use Areas, with no new buildings proposed, was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in January 2026 after council missed its decision deadline. City staff recommend the City Solicitor and planners oppose the conversion in its current form at the hearing while continuing discussions with the applicant. City Council will decide whether to take that position.

title: 110 West Toronto Street - Official Plan Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments;
brief: The owner of 110 West Toronto Street applied to redesignate the site from General Employment Areas to Mixed Use Areas, with no new buildings proposed, then appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in December 2025 after council did not decide in time. City staff recommend the City Solicitor and planners attend the hearing to oppose the application in its current form and keep talking with the applicant. City Council will decide whether to adopt that position.

title: 108-162 Vine Avenue - Official Plan Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments;
brief: An application to redesignate 108-162 Vine Avenue from Core Employment Areas to Mixed Use Areas and Parks, with no new buildings proposed, was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in February 2026 after council missed its deadline. City staff recommend the City Solicitor and planners oppose the conversion in its current form at the hearing while continuing discussions with the applicant. City Council will decide whether to back that stance.

title: 105-109 Vanderhoof Avenue and 10 Brentcliffe Road - Official Plan Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments;
brief: The owner of 105-109 Vanderhoof Avenue and 10 Brentcliffe Road wants to redesignate the site from Core Employment Areas to Mixed Use Areas, with no new buildings proposed, and appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in January 2026 after council missed its decision deadline. City staff recommend the City Solicitor and planners attend the hearing to oppose the conversion in its current form while continuing talks with the applicant. City Council will decide whether to adopt that position.

title: RentSafeTO Update
topics: enforcement, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: Landlords of large apartment buildings could face a new fee of $42.73 or $46.81 to replace their building's colour-coded RentSafeTO rating sign, waived for social housing providers, starting June 15, 2026. The update to the apartment building standards program also lists penalty-related amounts of $500, $100.00, $501, $1,000, $200.00, $1,001, $2,000, $400.00, $2,001, $5,000, $1,000.00, $5,001, $10,000, and $2,000.00. City Council will decide whether to adopt the changes, which affect maintenance and operating standards for rental buildings with three or more storeys and ten or more units.

title: Status Update Report on Transit Oriented Communities
topics: [activities in community and life], transit networks;
brief: New housing and development around GO stations is moving ahead under the province's Transit Oriented Communities program, with Guildwood GO the first Toronto project in the expanded program. City Council is asked to approve agreements with the province covering the program, alongside updates on affordable housing in the projects, community benefits, and commuter parking. The decision affects how station-area development deals are structured.

title: 817 Mount Pleasant Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The property at 817 Mount Pleasant Road, on the southeast corner of Mount Pleasant Road and Roehampton Avenue a block north of Eglinton Avenue East, is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The designation would protect the Mount Pleasant East property's cultural heritage value.

title: 601, 625, and 673 Lake Shore Boulevard East, 185 Villiers Street, and 300 Commissioners Street - City-initiated "Meanwhile Use" enabling Policy and Zoning, and Update on McCleary District Planning Work
topics: planning, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Vacant and underused land in the McCleary District along Lake Shore Boulevard East could host temporary film shoots, creative studios, sports, cultural events, entertainment, and retail under new 'meanwhile use' rules. City Council is asked to approve City-initiated Official Plan and zoning changes enabling the short-term non-residential uses at 601, 625 and 673 Lake Shore Boulevard East, 185 Villiers Street, and 300 Commissioners Street. The idea is to put idle land to work while permanent development plans take shape.

title: 52 Finch Avenue West - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, construction, multi-unit dwellings, property (sc), zoning; building, bylaws, multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a three-storey (11 metres plus 3.6-metre elevator enclosure) mixed-use building at 52 Finch Avenue West with two residential units and office uses, three vehicle parking spaces including one accessible space, and 12 bicycle parking spaces. The small-scale proposal adds homes and office space on Finch Avenue.

title: 41 to 47 Talara Drive - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: by-laws, development, multi-unit dwellings, official plan amendments, zoning; bylaws, developing land; development (land); land development, multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings
brief: Staff recommend City Council refuse a proposed 43-storey residential tower with 369 units on a 5-storey podium at 41 to 47 Talara Drive, saying it does not conform with the Official Plan and the applicable area policy. The proposal also involves demolishing eight existing residential units, five of them rental. Refusal would stop the project as proposed.

title: 1800 Sheppard Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, official plan amendments, properties (real estate), redevelopment, zoning; bylaws, property; real estate, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve redeveloping part of the Fairview Mall lands at 1800 Sheppard Avenue East with a 48-storey mixed-use building on an 8-storey podium — 585 residential units, a small amount of non-residential space and 81 parking spaces, plus a landscaped publicly accessible open space near the entrance. The approval would reshape part of the mall site with hundreds of new homes.

title: 45 Grenoble Drive - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, development, multi-residential properties, property (sc), zoning; bylaws, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a 40-storey residential building (126 metres plus 7-metre mechanical penthouse) on a 5-storey podium at 45 Grenoble Drive with 405 units, while retaining the existing 28-storey building with 217 rental units. Staff say the proposal adds to the housing stock in Flemingdon Park and conforms to the Official Plan. The decision would add hundreds of new homes while keeping existing rental units.

title: 609 Roehampton Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, by-laws, multi-residential properties, property (sc), zoning; bylaws
brief: An application to allow two 15-storey residential buildings with 209 units at 609 Roehampton Avenue — deemed complete in May 2025 — was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on December 15, 2025, after council failed to decide within the required time. Staff have prepared an appeal report setting out the City's position for the Tribunal. The Ontario Land Tribunal, not council, will now decide the application.

title: Dallimore Circle - Request for a Don Valley Parkway Sound Barrier
topics: highways, property (sc), safety barriers; freeways; motorways; parkways, suicide barriers
brief: Residents on Dallimore Circle want a sound barrier between their properties and the Don Valley Parkway, recognizing the highway is being transferred to the Province. Councillor Jon Burnside recommends City Council ask the Minister of Transportation to consider building a noise barrier along the west side of the parkway once the transfer is complete. The request matters to homeowners dealing with highway noise.

title: 93 York Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, land use, zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning change to allow six three-storey (11-metre) townhouse units at 93 York Road, describing it as appropriate infill that meets the Bayview Townhouse Design Guidelines and the Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods major-street zoning rules. The proposal is consistent with the Provincial Planning Statement and conforms to the Official Plan.

title: 4580 Dufferin Street - Turn Prohibition
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, road safety, transportation (sc), turn prohibitions (traffic); ttc
brief: Transportation Services wants to prohibit northbound left turns at all times from Dufferin Street into the private driveway at 4580 Dufferin Street, about 95 metres north of Finch Avenue West, to improve traffic flow and safety; drivers would use the property's two driveways off Finch Avenue West instead. Because the TTC operates on Dufferin Street, City Council — not community council — must vote on it. The change affects drivers accessing the property.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Hydro Board
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Corporations Nominating Panel will select six candidates to interview for the Toronto Hydro Board, then recommend three — including a Chair — to City Council for appointment. The candidate details stay confidential as personal information about identifiable individuals.

title: Cricket Day - by Councillor Neethan Shan, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: cricket;
brief: The item asks council to proclaim September 24, 2026 as Cricket Day in Toronto, the anniversary of the first international cricket match in history, played between Canada and the United States in 1844. The motion notes cricket was declared Canada's first national sport in 1867 and is now one of the city's fastest-growing sports. It also asks staff to engage cricket organizations on hosting events and to look at expanding equitable access to cricket facilities and programming.

title: Proclaiming April as Nepali Heritage Month - by Councillor Neethan Shan, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The item asks council to proclaim April as Nepali Heritage Month in Toronto for 2026 and future years, and to ask the province and federal government to do the same. April 14 marks Nepali New Year, a major cultural occasion of renewal and unity for Nepali-Canadians. The motion celebrates the community's contributions to health care, education, entrepreneurship, public service, arts, sports and volunteerism across the city.

title: Proclaiming November 19 as Early Age Onset Cancer Awareness Day - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: cancer, health; health coverage
brief: The item asks council to proclaim November 19 as Early Age Onset Cancer Awareness Day, timed to the Colorectal Cancer Resource and Action Network's sixth annual Early Age Onset Cancer Symposium on November 19 and 20, 2026. The motion cites rising cancer diagnosis rates among Canadians born after 1980 and says late diagnosis brings poorer outcomes than for patients over 50 who are screened more regularly. It also asks for a public education campaign with the Medical Officer of Health.

title: Clarifying the Distinction Between Duplexes and Secondary Suites - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: Since 2023, multiplex permissions have let duplexes, triplexes and fourplexes be built across Toronto's neighbourhoods, but the item notes the definition of duplex has a loophole: it only requires two units on separate levels, with no proportionality or minimum unit size, making it nearly indistinguishable from a secondary suite. In practice, applicants have proposed minimal basement units that effectively allow a larger house than zoning would otherwise permit, while gaining houseplex perks like relaxed height and setbacks. The motion asks council to clarify the distinction between duplexes and secondary suites.

title: Addressing Inaccurate Supporting Documentation Submitted to the Committee of Adjustment - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: public appointments;
brief: The item asks council to have Development Review staff report back in the first quarter of 2027 on how the accuracy of supporting materials filed with Committee of Adjustment applications is verified. The motion covers items like letters or petitions of support or opposition, which do not decide the Planning Act's four tests but can shape the committee's context. The report would include any recommended process improvements for handling inaccurate documentation.

title: Opposing the Provincial Land Grab at Bathurst Quay and the Island - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: land, waterfronts; lakefronts; waterfront trail, property
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow is asking council to oppose provincial legislation that would transfer City of Toronto land at Toronto Island and at Bathurst and Queen's Quay to the province. The motion cites concerns that the legislation could pave over parkland at Little Norway Park in a neighbourhood short on green space, and notes council's March vote opposing unilateral expropriation of city land and calling for Toronto's inclusion in waterfront decisions. The motion says the province has shared no concrete plans, with only media statements about the airport expansion so far.

title: Love Parade - Remembering Claude Cormier - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: waterfronts; lakefronts; waterfront trail
brief: The item asks council to recognize the five waterfront parks designed by the late landscape architect Claude Cormier (1960-2023) and his studio, HTO, Love Park, Berczy, Sugar Beach and Leslie Lookout, through a Love Parade celebration. The motion asks the Waterfront Secretariat to work with Parks and Recreation, Waterfront Toronto, CreateTO, landscape architects and local councillors on a May 2026 bike tour of the parks and related promotion. The motion is urgent so the recognition lands in the current season.

title: Ontario Land Tribunal Appeal for 4949 Bathurst Street - Request for Directions - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: Council gives the City Solicitor direction on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of the 26-storey, 92.45-metre mixed-use building approved at 4949 Bathurst Street, with 27,192 square metres of floor area including retail, office and a private daycare in the podium. The developer appealed because council approved fewer storeys than requested plus other changes, with a five-day hearing starting May 25, 2026. City planning staff are unavailable to give evidence, so the motion authorizes retaining an external planning consultant and is filed without notice as urgent.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.TE26.49 - Improving Traffic Flow on College Street, between Dufferin Street and Gladstone Avenue - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: congestion, traffic; gridlock, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: This is a procedural item: Re-opening its November 2025 decision that imposed a full-time no-stopping restriction on College Street between Dufferin Street and Gladstone Avenue, after residents and business owners reported delayed deliveries and blocked home access would get Council's approval. Councillor Alejandra Bravo's motion would narrow the restriction to morning and afternoon rush hours, which Transportation Services says preserves the original goal of faster streetcar service and less congestion. The motion is urgent so signage can be updated immediately. The motion also lists $3.25.

title: Improving the City’s Laneway Conveyance Process - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: When a developer or landowner wants to buy part of a public laneway, often to deliver laneway improvements through a rezoning, the internal city process across Transportation Services, Corporate Real Estate Management, Legal and Development Review lacks clear roles, timelines and responsibilities. Councillor Josh Matlow's motion asks council to direct those divisions to fix the laneway conveyance process, noting delays are holding up development applications including at 2010 to 2050 Yonge and 15 Lola Road. Staff in the affected divisions support the motion, described as urgent.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Midtown Yonge Business Improvement Area for Implementation Two Interactive Public Murals at 2075 Yonge Street and 1980 Yonge Street - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: The item asks council to contribute $48,000.00 ($48,000) in Section 37 funds to the Midtown Yonge BIA for two interactive public murals on the sides of 2075 Yonge Street and 1980 Yonge Street. The murals would be painted live with LiberArt Studio as part of the second annual Arraia on Yonge Festival on June 20, 2026, doubling as performance and audience engagement. The motion is urgent because the BIA needs the funding to proceed with the spring festival project.

title: Starting Construction of the Waterfront East Rapid Transit Line in 2026 - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, construction; building, ttc
brief: With $2 billion in provincial and federal funding secured in March to match the city's $1 billion contribution, Mayor Olivia Chow is asking council to authorize the funding and governance needed to start building the Waterfront East Rapid Transit Line in the 2026 construction season. The line would serve the eastern waterfront and Port Lands including Ookwemin Minising, supporting 75,000 homes and more than 150,000 people who will live and work there, with an expected 50,000 daily riders. The source also lists a $70 million figure alongside the project funding. The motion authorizes the City Manager to establish a delivery governance model with the TTC and Waterfront Toronto.

title: 1666 St. Clair Avenue West - Liquor Licence Application - Sporting Clube Portugues de Toronto - Licence 3605953 - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: The Sporting Clube Portugues de Toronto at 1666 St. Clair Avenue West has applied to the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario for a liquor licence covering indoor and outdoor areas, and nearby residents have raised concerns about noise, litter, safety and disturbances in the residential area. Councillor Alejandra Bravo's motion asks council to tell the AGCO the licence is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing those concerns are attached, and to request a review of the application. The AGCO makes the final decision.

title: Requesting an Equitable Approach to the Canada Post Community Mailbox Conversions in Ward 1 - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
topics: mail services; courier services; mail rooms; mailrooms
brief: The item asks council to seek an equitable approach to Canada Post's community mailbox conversions in Ward 1, Etobicoke North, where many residents face mobility, health and accessibility challenges and rely on door-to-door delivery for health care, income support and government services. Etobicoke North is the only Toronto community where conversions are set to begin in late 2026 and early 2027, and the motion says the city is being asked to accommodate the change without proper engagement. The motion asks for a pause to assess implications and collaborate on a plan that protects equitable access, while recognizing Canada Post's modernization goals.

title: Improving Communication for Planned Cinematic “Shock and Awe” Explosion and Fireball Effects in Movie Production near Local Neighbourhoods: Lessons Learned from Downsview - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza
topics: film and television industry; cinema industry; film and television cluster; film production; movie industry; television industry
brief: After a controlled movie-production explosion on federal lands at Downsview's Festival Terrace on April 16, 2026 sent a fireball, mushroom cloud and vibrations through the Ancaster-Downsview neighbourhoods at about 10:40 p.m., the item asks council to review notification protocols for major controlled explosions near homes. The advance notice described a one-time flash, but many residents were unaware of the shoot and feared an industrial accident or plane crash, in a neighbourhood still marked by the 2008 Sunrise Propane explosion. The motion says the film industry is valued but residents must be properly warned.

title: 109 Knox Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: appeals, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: Authorizing the City Solicitor to appear before the Toronto Local Appeal Body over the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of third and fourth-storey additions at 109 Knox Avenue, which would have created six residential units is up for a decision by Council. Planning staff had recommended conditions tying any approval to revised plans with no habitable space above the fourth storey, but the panel refused the application in January 2026 and the owner appealed. The motion is time-sensitive and lets the solicitor resolve the matter for the city.

title: Community Mailboxes: Protecting our Public Space - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: mail services; courier services; mail rooms; mailrooms
brief: The item asks council to tighten its approach to Canada Post's community mailbox rollout, adding a deadline of no later than the second quarter of 2026 to the city's request of the City Manager, and pushing to recoup the city's costs from Canada Post so residents do not pay more for reduced service. The motion says mailboxes must be safe, accessible, well-lit and secure, with waste receptacles and litter management so the program does not undermine the public realm. Canada Post is proceeding with conversions in some Toronto postal codes.

title: Amending Item 2025.TE19.8 - 1 to 19 Thelma Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: demolitions, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: This is a procedural item: Council votes on amending the 2025 rental-housing demolition approval for 1-19 Thelma Avenue so the 11 vacant rental units, described as in disrepair and a safety concern, can be demolished sooner to advance an approved seven-storey apartment building. The motion would ease requirements to register agreements at the off-site rental replacement location and adjust financial security conditions. The motion is urgent because of the health and safety risks of the vacant properties.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds for Advancing Safety Improvements Through an Upgraded Playground Structure at Canoe Landing - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: playgrounds, safety; adventure playgrounds; indoor playgrounds; playground structures, public safety
brief: After two injuries in 2025, the playground structure at Canoe Landing's shared-use space was deemed unsafe and removed, leaving Jean Lumb Public School, Bishop Macdonell Catholic School and the Canoe Landing Community Recreation Centre without play equipment. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik's motion asks council to release $450,000.00 in Section 42 funds, from the 11 Charlotte Street development, for the design and installation of a safe, creative, age-appropriate replacement. Design consultation with the Block 31 shared-use partners continues in 2026, and the motion is urgent so spring consultation can proceed.

title: State of Good Repair at the Jarvis and Sherbourne Underpasses Within the Union Station Rail Corridor - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: maintenance, stations;
brief: Metrolinx has agreed to provide up to $500,000 to the Transportation Services capital budget for maintenance and upkeep of the Lower Jarvis Street and Lower Sherbourne Street underpasses in the Union Station Rail Corridor, where the city has maintenance expertise. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik's motion asks council to authorize the General Manager of Transportation Services to negotiate and execute the agreement with Metrolinx. The source lists $280,000 and $220,000 amounts alongside the $500,000 total. The motion is urgent because the third-party funding is tied to upcoming corridor construction timelines.

title: Enforcing the Westray Amendments to Keep Workers Safe - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: emergency management, safety; crisis management; disaster planning; disaster supply kits; emergency preparedness; emergency procedures; emergency supply kits; survival kits, public safety
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow is asking council to push for enforcement of the Westray amendments, the criminal negligence provisions created after the 1992 Westray Mine explosion that killed 26 miners, which let employers be held accountable when workers are killed or injured. The motion asks council to request that the province ensure Crown attorneys and health and safety regulators are trained in the law with sufficient investigation resources, and that the Toronto Police Service Board ensure officers have the training. It cites more than 1,000 Canadian workplace deaths a year and is timed to the April 28 National Day of Mourning and the May 9 Westray anniversary.

title: Financial Assistance for Covenant House’s Redevelopment Project at 20 Gerrard Street East and 21 McGill Street - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: Covenant House Toronto, Canada's largest agency serving youth needing pathways to housing, plans to redevelop its main site at 20 Gerrard Street East and 21 McGill Street into a modern housing-focused building with about 118 supportive and transitional homes across 121,000 square feet, plus on-site health, education, housing and employment services. Councillor Chris Moise's motion asks council to provide financial assistance for the redevelopment, noting the existing buildings are at the end of their useful life while the agency has served more than 110,000 young people over 40 years. The motion carries no dollar figure in the source text; pre-application talks with staff and neighbours are underway.

title: Ward-Based Maintenance Teams Pilot - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
topics: maintenance, motions; council decisions; decisions (council)
brief: The item asks council to pilot ward-based maintenance teams of city staff handling the everyday fixes residents complain take too long: litter and illegal dumping cleanup, grass cutting, minor tree trimming, pothole and sidewalk repair, and general public-realm maintenance. The motion notes routine issues now bounce across multiple divisions through repeated service requests, and asks the City Manager to report back to the next council meeting on a pilot. Local residents, BIAs and community groups would help set neighbourhood priorities.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.NY28.10 - 2925 Keele Street (Stanley Greene Block G) Subdivision - Assumption of Services, Correction to Reference Registered Plan 66M-2554 - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: Council decides whether to re-open its December 2025 approval for the 2925 Keele Street (Stanley Greene Block G) subdivision to correct a typographical error. The decision wrongly referenced Registered Plan 66M-2520 instead of the correct 66M-2554, which is blocking Legal Services from preparing the Assumption By-law for the subdivision's municipal services, public highways and street-lighting transfer to Toronto Hydro. The motion fixes the plan number throughout.

title: Cabbagetown Cycling Connects - Ontario Street Parking By-law Amendments - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: cycling, parking; bicycling
brief: The item asks council to approve parking by-law amendments for the Ontario Street cycling connection in Cabbagetown, which council approved in 2025 and which gets built out in 2026 alongside watermain, resurfacing and public-realm work between Wellesley Street East and Carlton Street. The changes include universally accessible sidewalks, new contra-flow bike lanes, a reconfigured cycle track beside parking to preserve curbside parking, and a new loading zone near Garner Lane, with no change to motor vehicle lanes. Most residents supported the plans in consultation.

title: Direction to Finalize Section 37 Agreement for 765 Steeles Avenue West - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: agreements, by-laws; bylaws, tenancy agreements
brief: The item asks council to give the city more flexibility over community space secured through Section 37 at the 765 Steeles Avenue West infill development. The motion directs Development Review staff to bring forward a city-initiated amendment to By-laws 1089-2022 and 1090-2022 covering the use, design, finishing and equipping of the future city facility, and asks Social Development and Children's Services to explore funding to finish and furnish the space. The goal is a facility that can adapt to surrounding residents' needs.

title: Accepting a Donation from the Friends of University Avenue for the Lighting Installation at University Median Park, Between Elm Street and College Street on University Avenue - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
