topics: donation; bequest; toy drive
brief: The non-profit Friends of University Avenue is offering the city its Radiant Journey lighting and planting installation on the University Avenue median between Elm and College Streets, a 380-metre display with 20,000 lighting control points, as an in-kind donation valued at approximately $755,000.00, plus a $32,500.00 cash donation. Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion asks council to accept the donation, with $30,000.00 earmarked for maintenance and $2,500.00 for fall 2026 flower replacement, bringing the combined value to $787,500.00. The group says it cannot afford to keep maintaining the installation itself.

title: Support for Minister’s Zoning Order (MZO) to Maintain Lands in the City of Toronto as Employment Lands to Protect the Ontario Food Terminal - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: food, zoning; menus
brief: The item asks council to support, in principle, the province's proposed Minister's Zoning Order for 125 The Queensway to keep the lands as employment uses and block incompatible uses like residential. The site sits directly beside the Ontario Food Terminal, described as a key west-end employer supporting 2,500 direct jobs and about 168,000 indirect jobs including farm workers and 5,000 registered buyers, whose board requested the order with the agriculture minister's backing. A March 2025 application to redesignate the site for residential use was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal after council did not decide in time, and council backed an appeal report on the site in February 2026.

title: Community Engagement Process to Assess Local Community Support for Echoes and Nighttime Closure of Barbara Hall Park - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Barbara Hall Park in the Church-Wellesley Village, home to the AIDS Memorial and the Trans Memorial, has faced persistent health and safety concerns, intensified since the pandemic and a rise in opioid-related incidents, especially overnight, including vandalism, violence and damage around the memorials. Councillor Chris Moise's motion asks council to run a community engagement process to assess local support for options including nighttime closure of the park, alongside the existing response team, maintenance, needle collection and crisis outreach work. The motion aligns with the Downtown East Action Plan's balance of public safety and community support.

title: Urgent Action to Address Safety and Public Realm Conditions at 464-470 Queen Street West - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: public realm, safety; public safety, public spaces
brief: The future park at 464-470 Queen Street West is moving ahead on design and demolition, but the remaining land has not been conveyed to the city and the temporary fencing around the vacant site keeps getting blown or pushed over, blocking the sidewalk at a key intersection. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik's motion asks council to direct Parks and Recreation and Development Review staff to work with the developer on immediate safety fixes and ongoing fence maintenance before conveyance. The Queen West BIA has sought improvements for years, and FIFA activity this summer adds urgency.

title: Update on the Bathurst Quay Neighbourhood Transportation Study - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: This is a procedural item: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to fold a Bathurst Quay neighbourhood transportation update into the Planning and Housing Committee's second-quarter 2026 report-back on the Billy Bishop Airport flightpath expansion. The update would cover the current status of land-side transportation directions around the airport and a preliminary assessment of transportation impacts, ahead of a fuller multi-modal study of the area. Community council has already directed the multi-modal study.

title: It’s Time to Reinstate Cummer Station for the North York Centre - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: public transit, subway stations; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: The item asks council to push for reinstating Cummer Station on the Yonge North Subway Extension, which currently skips Cummer Avenue and would leave about 2 kilometres between Finch and Steeles stations. The motion cites the North York Centre Secondary Plan's expectation of 100,000 new residents and a December 2023 staff report on the station's technical implications, arguing the gap is unusually wide for a dense urban corridor compared with 500-to-700-metre downtown Line 1 spacing. The extension's design and alignment decisions are actively advancing.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Acquisition of Community Space in the Church Wellesley Village - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: The item asks council to authorize the release of Section 37 funds to buy community space in the Church-Wellesley Village, the 2SLGBTQ+ cultural hub where development pressure has shrunk the space available to community organizations. An opportunity to acquire an existing building in the Village arose in early 2025, and the councillor's office has been working with city staff, The 519 and community stakeholders on a potential city-community partnership. The motion carries no dollar figure in the source; it would draw on reallocated Ward 13 Section 37 funds approved by council in June 2025.

title: Reinstating Paddle the Don for 2027 - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: ravines, rivers, waterfronts; lakefronts; waterfront trail, ravine protection areas
brief: The item asks council to request that the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority bring back Paddle the Don in 2027. The long-running event gave residents a firsthand experience of the Don River as a living system, and its return would support city and conservation authority goals around ravine enjoyment, environmental education and stewardship of revitalized waterways. The motion also asks city divisions to discuss with the conservation authority how to support the event and report back by June 10, 2026.

title: Improving Pedestrian Safety at Ossington Avenue and Dupont Street - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: pedestrian signals, traffic; crosswalk lights; pedestrian displays, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: Residents say the Ossington Avenue and Dupont Street intersection is unsafe, with drivers speeding through turns and nearly hitting pedestrians, in a growing area of families, seniors and cyclists. Councillor Alejandra Bravo's motion asks council to advance further pedestrian safety improvements there, building on quick-build measures installed in October 2025 such as curb extensions, tighter turn radii, bright markings and bollards between St. Clarens Avenue and Manning Avenue. The broader Dupont Complete Street project is paused pending review after provincial Bill 212, making the interim intersection work the near-term focus.

title: Towards a Vision for a Design Standard for Future Toronto Subway Stations - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: With the Yonge North and Scarborough subway extensions on the horizon, the item asks council to develop a design vision for future Toronto subway stations as civic hubs rather than purely functional transit stops. The motion points to global examples like Taipei, where stations are open, well-lit, two-storey spaces with platform screen doors, retail and community space, integrated into buildings. It asks staff to explore how station design can support safety, accessibility, economic activity, housing and community life while managing city real estate assets.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds to the Dieppe Park Baseball Lighting Improvements Project - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: baseball, funding, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, financing
brief: The item asks council to release $170,000 for the Dieppe Park baseball lighting improvements project, upgrading the 'B' diamond named for the Second World War's Dieppe Raid. The official figures list the $170,000 project amount alongside source amounts of $20,000, $22,000, $18,000, $16,000, $25,000, $14,000 and $15,000. The diamond, installed in the 1950s and used by youth baseball and adult slo-pitch leagues, is already getting infield and drainage upgrades this spring through a donation from East York Baseball.

title: 171 Parkside Drive - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: Council authorizes the City Solicitor to appeal a Committee of Adjustment decision approving a second-storey addition on a rear ancillary building at 171 Parkside Drive, to be converted into a garden suite. Community Planning staff had recommended refusal over the separation distance from the main house, the added height, and reduced soft landscaping, but the Toronto and East York panel approved it on April 9, 2026; the appeal deadline is April 21, 2026. The motion also lets the solicitor retain consultants and negotiate a settlement.

title: Responding to Bill 98, Building Homes and Improving Transportation Infrastructure Act, 2026 - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: The item asks council to respond to Ontario's Bill 98, the Building Homes and Improving Transportation Infrastructure Act, 2026, introduced March 30, 2026 and through second reading April 14. The motion focuses on Schedule 4, the Fare Alignment and Seamless Transit Act, which would let the Minister of Transportation exercise broad powers over regional transit service and fare policy, with consultation possible as early as May 2026. The motion says TTC service and fare decisions, currently made by the TTC Board through public plans and budgets, are fundamental to meeting Torontonians' needs.

title: Strengthening Racial Equity in City Programs and Services - by Councillor Neethan Shan, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: equity, programs; employment equity; fair wage; pay equity
brief: The item asks council to strengthen racial equity in city programs and services, saying equity-deserving communities still report gaps in access and outcomes despite the city's commitments. The motion asks council to have Social Development staff highlight best practices and lessons from existing racial equity initiatives in a yearly public report, explore a racial justice program advisory body with membership reflecting Toronto's racial and ethnic diversity, and look at targeted ways to improve inclusive program delivery.

title: Renewing Official Recognition of Toronto as a Certified Bird Friendly City - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: bird-friendly development guidelines; lights out toronto
brief: Toronto's certification as a Bird Friendly City through Nature Canada needs a council resolution to renew, and Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik's motion asks council to provide it. Toronto was certified in 2021 after adopting bird-friendly policies, and the city points to Toronto Green Standard bird-collision measures for new developments, lights-out practices at city facilities during migration, and the Lights Out Toronto campaign. Certification requires meeting standards on reducing threats to birds, protecting habitat and engaging communities.

title: "Have Your Say" Amplified: Enhancing Public Consultations and Surveys - Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: The city runs more than 120 public consultations a year, mostly organized in divisional silos, and councillors and residents often learn about them too late to take part. Councillor Chris Moise's motion asks council to direct the Chief Communications Officer to centrally coordinate all public consultations and make listing on the Have Your Say website mandatory before any consultation can inform staff decisions, starting no later than the first quarter of 2027. The motion also asks for formal definitions of each consultation type on the site.

title: Metrolinx Accountability on Joe Shuster Way Fence Graffiti and Public Art  - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: graffiti; graffiti abatement; graffiti crime; graffiti eradication; graffiti vandalism; grafitti removal
brief: Residents of Joe Shuster Way have long complained about graffiti, sometimes offensive, on a Metrolinx-owned fence on the north side of their street, and have been cleaning it themselves after what the motion describes as a lack of sustained Metrolinx action. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik's motion asks council to request that Metrolinx provide ongoing graffiti removal on the wall and fund a community art plan for it, developed with residents, as a long-term deterrent. The motion notes community art programming is already planned at select Ontario Line sites, setting a precedent.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds to the Ferrand Park Improvements Project - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: funding; financing
brief: The item asks council to release $439,600 in Section 42 parkland dedication funds, secured from the development at 1185 Eglinton Avenue East in Ward 16, for capital improvements at Ferrand Park. The money would be added to the Parks and Recreation 2026-2035 capital budget on a one-time basis with no debt. Section 42 funds are developer contributions earmarked for local park improvements.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds to the Wigmore Park Improvements Project - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: funding; financing
brief: The item asks council to release $367,905.77 in Section 42 parkland dedication funds, secured from the development at 1648 Victoria Park Avenue in Ward 16, for capital improvements at Wigmore Park. The money would be added to the Parks and Recreation 2026-2035 capital budget on a one-time basis with no debt. Section 42 funds are developer contributions earmarked for local park improvements.

title: Prioritizing Expansion of Roseneath Park - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Roseneath Park, a 2,340-square-metre park near Oakwood Avenue and St. Clair Avenue West, serves one of the city's lowest parkland-provision areas, and the item asks council to prioritize its expansion. The Oakwood-St. Clair Parks Plan identifies it as a priority, and the city has already bought 252 Winona Drive and secured off-site parkland dedications from the 1500 St. Clair Avenue West development toward land assembly. Parks and Recreation is actively pursuing further acquisitions as residential growth continues to squeeze park space in the area.

title: Durham Boundary Facilities Agreement Renewal - Kingston Road Bridge over the Rouge River
topics: agreements, bridge maintenance, transportation infrastructure; tenancy agreements, transportation network; transportation networks
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council decides whether to renew the cost-sharing and maintenance agreement with Durham Region for the Kingston Road Bridge over the Rouge River — shared equally — plus winter maintenance of Kingston Road to Altona Road, which Durham covers fully. The previous agreement ran from January 1, 2016 to December 31, 2025; the renewal would be one year, auto-renewing annually, terminable on 60 days' notice. Council decides.

title: Community Sports Equipment Sponsorship
topics: sponsorship, sports, sports equipment; corporate sponsorship; sponsorship opportunities
brief: The Infrastructure and Environment Committee is receiving a report on Canadian Tire Jumpstart's proposal for community sports equipment lending stations in city parks — with Equip Club as delivery partner — after council directed staff to assess a one-year pilot against conditions including a Canadian vendor, at least one station in each community council area by summer 2026, data privacy, and digital access. The item affects free sports equipment access in parks. The committee receives the report.

title: Delegation of Authority for Crossing Agreements
topics: agreements, infrastructure, transportation; tenancy agreements, transportation services
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council gives the General Manager of Parks and Recreation standing authority to negotiate and sign crossing agreements or permits letting city infrastructure — parks, trails, roads, bridges, recreation facilities — cross third-party lands such as railway corridors or pipeline rights-of-way for approved capital projects, consistent with existing delegated authority held by other divisions. The change would streamline approvals for capital projects. Council decides.

title: Seeking Clarity on the City of Toronto's Application to the Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund
topics: administration, city-operated sports facilities, community centres, council items, funding, infrastructure, public inquiries, recreation centres, sports facilities; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, clauses; items (council); items before council, financing, judicial inquries, rec centers; rec centres; recreation centers, sports venues
brief: This is a procedural item: council referred Councillor James Pasternak's (Ward 6, York Centre) inquiry and the City Manager's answer about the city's application to the provincial Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee for consideration. No new decision is attached.

title: The Electrification Advantage
topics: electric distribution utilities, electricity, utilities; electric power; electricity usage, electricity distribution utilities; electricity retailers, power utilties
brief: The committee is receiving The Electrification Advantage, a report responding to the Mayor's economic action plan on U.S. tariffs and earlier climate directives, on increasing local renewable energy generation and reducing natural gas dependence at the Portlands Energy Centre. The report outlines actions within the city's authority to build on the province's 2025 Integrated Regional Resource Plan for Toronto — pursuing local energy efficiency, renewables, and storage — plus steps to improve affordability and air quality and cut climate pollution. The report affects the city's climate strategy and local energy mix. The committee receives the report.

title: Approach to Public Electric Vehicle (EV Charging) Three-Year Plan
topics: electric distribution utilities, electric scooters, electricity, parking; electric power; electricity usage, electricity distribution utilities; electricity retailers, go peds; go-peds; motorized scooters; scooters
brief: The committee is considering a three-year plan to expand public EV charging through a collaboration agreement between the city, the Toronto Parking Authority, and an experienced Canadian proponent — with the partner's estimated investment of $35.8 million and major terms in a confidential attachment — with the report also citing $1.5 billion. The model aims to deploy charging at scale on city-owned property while reducing the city's financial and operational risk, prioritizing Canadian suppliers, alongside measures to remove barriers to charging on non-city lands. The plan affects public charging access for residents and workers citywide. The committee decides.

title: Redesign Study of the Intersection of Eglinton Avenue West and the Allen Road Expressway - April 2026 Update
topics: intersections, traffic data, transportation research; cordon count programs; ridership; traffic counts; traffic information; traffic measurement; traffic studies, transportation monitoring
brief: This is an information item: the General Manager of Transportation Services reports on the redesign study for the Eglinton Avenue West and Allen Road expressway intersection — initiated by council in February 2025 after 2023 changes caused congestion spilling onto neighbourhood streets — including a progress update, work plan, and monitoring results from December 2025 traffic pattern changes. Council is asked to receive the report.

title: Watermain Cleaning and Relining on Various Streets in the Sheppard Avenue / Chesswood Drive Area
topics: contracts, stadiums, watermains; mains; water mains, sports stadiums
brief: Councillor James Pasternak (Ward 6, York Centre) is raising concerns about Toronto Water's watermain cleaning and relining contract 26TW-CPI-03CWD on Sheppard Avenue and Chesswood Drive — an area that saw major disruptive construction in 2023 — noting local businesses' fear of renewed disruption and that Sheppard Avenue is a key route to Rogers Stadium, which seats 52,200 and has 17 concerts booked in May 2026 starting May 26. The motion flags unclear information about potential lane or road closures. The item affects local employment lands businesses and concert traffic. Any direction would flow from the committee or council.

title: Repairs and Rehabilitation on Wilson Avenue Due to Contract BFPP (21 ECS-LU-04FP)
topics: business improvement areas, public realm, restoration; bia; business improvement associations, public spaces, rehabilitation (property)
brief: Councillor James Pasternak (Ward 6, York Centre) is asking City Council to direct the General Managers of Toronto Water and Transportation Services to work with the subcontractor responsible for contract BFPP (21 ECS-LU-04FP) — in consultation with the Wilson Village BIA and the local councillor — to immediately repair and restore infrastructure damaged during construction on Wilson Avenue, where garden beds, interlocking brick, and decorative sidewalks were destroyed beyond expected disruption. The councillor notes no road closures will be granted after May 26, 2026 because of the Rogers Stadium concert season. The item affects Wilson Avenue businesses and the public realm. Council decides.

title: Traffic Control Signals - Victoria Park Avenue
topics: capital budgets, pedestrians, traffic control systems; pedestrianization, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Transportation Services is asking City Council to approve traffic control signals on Victoria Park Avenue at Belmore Avenue, Sloane Avenue, and Ruscica Drive/Innismore Crescent, based on assessments showing they would improve safety for all road users. Pedestrian crossings would be prohibited on Victoria Park near Belmore Avenue (between the south curb line and a point 30.5 metres north of the north curb line) and near Ruscica Drive/Innismore Crescent (between the north curb line and 30.5 metres south of the south curb line) in conjunction with the signals. Council decides.

title: Congestion Management Plan - 2026 Spring Update
topics: congestion, traffic, traffic data, transportation research; cordon count programs; ridership; traffic counts; traffic information; traffic measurement; traffic studies, gridlock, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, transportation monitoring
brief: The committee is receiving the Congestion Management Plan 2026 spring update, including the first observations of the Chief Congestion Officer (in the role since January 5, 2026) and the approach to long-term congestion management — the report cites $299.4 million. The report attributes Toronto's congestion to car-oriented planning history, transit expansion not keeping pace with growth, extensive capital work, rapid population growth, and increased development activity. The update affects how the city manages road congestion. The committee receives the report.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Upland Software Inc., for Telecom Expense Management Service
topics: contracts, information & communication (sc), purchasing, science & technology (sc), software; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, computer programs
brief: City Council decides whether to approve a non-competitive contract with Upland Software Inc. for Cimpl, the telecom expense management platform the city uses to track network, phone, and wireless spending across all divisions, for three years plus two one-year options at $2,625,000 ($2,671,200 net of HST recoveries); the report also cites $500,000. The software was competitively procured in 2020, and the non-competitive route relies on the exclusive-rights exception since only Upland provides it. The platform is tied to compliance with an Auditor General recommendation on telecom expense controls.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Microsoft Canada Inc., for M365 Software Licenses, Cloud Subscriptions, and Support Services
topics: contracts, information and communication technology, purchasing, software licences; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, ict; information and communication systems; information and technology; information technology; it, software licenses
brief: City Council is asked to approve a non-competitive five-year contract (three years plus two one-year options) directly with Microsoft Canada Inc. for Microsoft 365 software licences, cloud subscriptions, and support for about 32,000 city staff, since the current agreement expires May 31, 2026 and staff say dealing directly secures better commercial terms than resellers. The item also extends the previously approved Microsoft Unified Support by five months at no extra cost to cover the full term. The report cites a $500,000 figure.

title: Non-Competitive Agreements Required to Support the Existing and New Electric Ferries
topics: agreements, contracts, ferries, projects, vessels; boats, ferry boats; ferryboats, tenancy agreements
brief: The city wants four non-competitive agreements to keep Toronto's ferry services running and certified — covering regulatory certification, vessel maintenance and repair, and specialized electrical support for the existing ferries and new electric ferries entering service in 2026 and 2027. Staff cite Canada Shipping Act obligations, exclusive manufacturer rights, and the critical 2026 World Cup period as reasons competitive bidding isn't practical. The report cites agreement figures of $4,060,288 ($3,990,063), $4,508,771, $17,483,958 ($17,181,562), $19,415,165, $500,000, $1,017,845 ($1,000,241), $1,130,272, $1,596,314 ($1,568,705), $1,772,637, $8,799,461 ($8,647,269), $9,771,414, $6,070,337 ($5,965,347), and $6,740,842.

title: Non-Competitive Extension with Moneris Solutions Corporation for Payment Processing Services
topics: [activities in finance], agreements, contracts, credit cards, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, credit card receipts; credit card statements, tenancy agreements
brief: Approving a non-competitive three-year extension (January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2029) with Moneris Solutions Corporation for credit and debit card payment processing, since the current contract expires December 31, 2026 and a competitive replacement procurement was paused while staff work on modernizing the city's payments landscape would get City Council's approval. Council approval is required because the cumulative commitment exceeds the Chief Procurement Officer's authority.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Blanket Contract 4300000085 with City Dispensers Inc., for the Non-Exclusive Supply and Delivery of Prescription Eyewear for Toronto Employment and Social Services
topics: contracts, employment & labour (sc), health (sc), optometry services, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, contact lenses; eye care; eye glasses; eyeglasses; eyewear; optometrists; optomology services
brief: Adding $1,500,000 to the non-competitive blanket contract with City Dispensers Inc. for prescription eyewear supplied through Toronto Employment and Social Services — raising it from $500,000 to $2,000,000 and extending it from May 31, 2026 to February 28, 2027 — is up for a decision by City Council. The contract funds glasses as a medical benefit for Ontario Works, Ontario Disability Support Program, and low-income recipients; over 8,000 clients received vision care benefits in 2025, with costs covered by the province. Staff say the extension avoids service interruption while new vision-care delivery models are explored for 2027.

title: Purchase Order Amendments for Professional Services and Non-Competitive Contract with Jordan Sook Studios Inc., for the Provision of Public Art - New Etobicoke Civic Centre
topics: civic centres, contracts, projects, public art, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, ccs, outdoor art; outdoor sculptures; outdoor statues
brief: For the new Etobicoke Civic Centre at 3755 Bloor Street West — the mixed-use building with offices, council chamber, childcare, library, health clinic, recreation centre, retail, and civic square, now in above-grade construction and described as on budget and on schedule — the city wants to amend purchase orders for contract administration and project management services and award a non-competitive public art contract to Jordan Sook Studios Inc. The report's financial figures are $1,705,928 ($1,735,952 net of HST recoveries), $20,234,075 ($20,590,194), $21,940,002 ($22,326,146), $2,310,827 ($2,351,498), $5,018,707 ($5,107,036), $7,329,534 ($7,458,533), $500,000, $514,250, and $523,301, covering the purchase order amendments and the public art contract.

title: 130 Merton Street - Designation of a Portion of the Property used by Senior Peoples' Resources in North Toronto as a Municipal Capital Facility
topics: community centres, municipal facilities, properties (real estate), seniors, taxes; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, city facilities; municipal buildings, elderly; geriatric; older adults; senior citizens, levies, property; real estate
brief: The question before City Council: whether to pass a by-law designating part of 130 Merton Street — Unit 600, about 10,295 square feet leased from Brigham Holdings Inc. and used by the non-profit Senior Peoples' Resources in North Toronto as a community centre offering home care, house calls, and transportation for seniors — as a municipal capital facility, which would exempt the space from municipal and school property taxes. Council decides on the designation under Section 252 of the City of Toronto Act.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Bramic Creative Business Products Ltd., for the Provision and Installation of Specialized Dispatch Consoles and Related Maintenance Services for Paramedic Services
topics: agreements, communication, contracts, maintenance, paramedics; communicating; communications, tenancy agreements
brief: The city wants a non-competitive agreement with Bramic Creative Business Products Ltd. worth $3,723,977 ($3,789,519 net of HST recoveries) — with a $500,000 figure also cited — for dispatch consoles and maintenance for Toronto Paramedic Services, for one year with four one-year renewal options. Bramic makes the current consoles and is the only certified servicer; the contract supports the backup ambulance communications centre's relocation and expansion to at least 40 workstations amid rising 9-1-1 call volumes. The current agreement expires December 31, 2026, and council approval is required.

title: Non-Competitive Procurement Contract with Motorola Solutions Canada Inc., for the Provision of Enhanced Radio Communications Equipment at the St. Lawrence Market North Building
topics: city-owned properties, emergency services, purchasing, telecommunications; 9-1-1; 911; 911 calls; emergency assistance; emergency response, acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, city owned properties; city properties, phone services; telephone services; voice communication; voice mail
brief: City Council votes on approving a non-competitive contract with Motorola Solutions Canada Inc. worth $887,354 ($902,971 net of HST recoveries) — with a $500,000 figure also cited — to design and install additional radio equipment extending the city's emergency radio network inside the St. Lawrence Market North building at 92 Front Street East. The building reached substantial completion in November 2024, and building staff found radio dead zones after occupancy; the system supports police, fire, and paramedic communications. Council decides on the contract.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Wajax Limited for Repairs, Maintenance, Service Calls and Authorized Warranty Work on Allison Automatic Transmissions for Toronto Fire Services
topics: contracts, external services, fire and rescue services, fire trucks, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, consultants; consulting services; professional services, fire fighting; fire services; fire suppression; firefighting; rescue; rescue operations; search and rescue
brief: The question before City Council: whether to let Toronto Fire Services negotiate a non-competitive agreement with Wajax Limited for repairs, parts, and warranty work on Allison automatic transmissions in its roughly 190 fire apparatus, capped at $1,167,038 ($1,187,578 net of HST recoveries), with the report also citing a $500,000 figure. The current Wajax agreement ends November 30, 2026, and Allison has given Wajax the exclusive right to maintain its transmissions. The deal covers work on an as-needed basis for the fire fleet.

title: 2351 and 2355 Keele Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application- Appeal Report
topics: appeals, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A developer proposed a 25-storey, 311-unit residential building at 2351 and 2355 Keele Street, then appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal after council missed the decision deadline. Staff want the city's lawyers to oppose the current version and keep negotiating with the applicant.

title: 611, 619, 623 and 623A Keele Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: high rise buildings, mixed use areas, official plan amendments, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, tall buildings
brief: A developer wants to build a 33-storey mixed-use building with about 395 homes and ground-floor shops at 611-623A Keele Street. Council is asked to change the Official Plan and zoning to allow the extra height and fewer non-residential uses.

title: 54 Atomic Avenue Driveway and North Queen Street - Turn Prohibition
topics: safety, turn prohibitions (traffic); public safety
brief: Council has the final say on whether to ban northbound left turns at all times from the private driveway at 54 Atomic Avenue onto North Queen Street, to address safety and operational concerns at the driveway.

title: Highway 27 and Rexdale Boulevard - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: highways, pedestrian crossovers; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, freeways; motorways; parkways
brief: The decision on whether to install three pedestrian crossovers and two yield controls at the right-turn channels of Highway 27 and Rexdale Boulevard, and to correct a mismatch between the posted signs and the existing yield regulations rests with Council.

title: The East Mall and West Deane Park Drive - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: pedestrian crossovers, traffic control systems; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Council will weigh whether to install traffic signals on The East Mall, about 35 metres north of West Deane Park Drive, to improve safety for all road users.

title: Grand Avenue and Algoma Street - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: assessment, pedestrian crossovers; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo
brief: Staff recommend that Council NOT install traffic signals or a pedestrian crossover at Grand Avenue and Algoma Street, since the intersection did not meet the warrant criteria.

title: 2775 Jane Street - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Approving a 27-storey residential building with about 420 homes at 2775 Jane Street, north of the existing 17-storey apartment, on condition that the applicant withdraws its Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of the Jane Finch Secondary Plan is on Council's agenda.

title: 327 Royal York Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Approving two 43-storey buildings at 327 Royal York Road with about 1,046 homes, 106 vehicle parking spaces, 795 bicycle parking spaces, and 233 square metres of non-residential space comes before Council.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto Mobility Plan: Temporary Adjustments to Traffic and Parking Regulations
topics: parking regulations, soccer, traffic regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: The decision on authorizing temporary traffic and parking by-law amendments, permit parking exemptions, delegated authority for further measures, and road closures as needed during the FIFA World Cup 2026 tournament rests with Council. The plan aims to manage increased travel demand and keep transit, emergency access, and pedestrian and cyclist movement working. It affects travel around event areas during the tournament.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: By-law Exemptions to Facilitate Planning and Delivery of the FIFA World Cup 2026 Events at Fort York and the Bentway, and at Nathan Phillips Square
topics: festivals and special events, fireworks, special occasion permits, sports tournaments; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits, community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals, firecrackers, tournaments
brief: Council has the final say on whether to authorize exemptions to certain by-laws to deliver FIFA World Cup 2026 events at Fort York, the Bentway, and Nathan Phillips Square, including an exemption allowing the sale of plastic bottled water at the FIFA Fan Festival from June 10 to July 19, 2026, alongside City water trailers. The exemptions are temporary measures to support the tournament.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026: Non-Competitive Procurement with the FIFA Fan Festival Toronto vendor
topics: international events, purchasing, sporting events; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, championships, international event bids; olympic bids
brief: The FIFA Fan Festival Toronto vendor won a $16.0 million contract in December 2025 to run site production and programming. Council is asked to authorize a non-competitive $9.0 million increase with the same vendor for additional services to improve the fan experience and safety, with all incremental costs revenue-supported or reallocated so there is no net cost to the City. The report's figures also include $380.0 million, $25.0 million, $500,000, and $7.1 million.

title: 2026 Property Tax Clawback Rate Report
topics: commercial areas, industrial properties, property tax rates, property taxes, residential properties, taxes; commercial districts; retail areas, industrial real estate, levies, municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts, residential real estate
brief: Council must adopt annual property tax by-laws, the municipal levy, the education levy, and clawback rates, before final tax bills can be issued. This report sets the 2026 clawback rates for commercial, industrial, and multi-residential properties, recovering revenue foregone from the policy capping tax increases at 10 per cent for properties with increases over $500. It affects businesses and landlords in those property classes.

title: Towards a Beautiful City: Update on Priority Items
topics: public realm; public spaces
brief: This is an information item: Council receives an update on eight priority items for improving the public realm, covering streets, parks, plazas, and the waterfront, plus the directive for graffiti removal and 1,000 new murals. No policy change is proposed.

title: Toronto Personal Watercraft Safety Plan
topics: recreational watercraft, safety, water; boat launching; boats; leisure water vehicles; pleasure boats; pleasure craft, public safety
brief: Jet skis and other personal watercraft are creating growing safety risks along the waterfront, conflicting with swimmers and paddlers, and unpermitted commercial rentals have appeared in City parks and beaches. Council is asked to adopt a Personal Watercraft Safety Plan developed with the Toronto Police Marine Unit, the Toronto Port Authority, and Transport Canada, and to thank the Port Authority for 2026 motorized watercraft exclusion zones at three beaches and request their continuation. It affects waterfront safety for swimmers, paddlers, and boaters.

title: Implementation of O.Reg 1/26 under the Liquor Licence and Control Act, 2019 in the City of Toronto
topics: by-laws, liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits, bylaws
brief: Ontario has expanded bring-your-own liquor permits to cover cultural and community outdoor events such as neighbourhood festivals, movie screenings, art exhibits, and farmer's markets, effective April 30, 2026. The item asks Council to have the City Clerk and Economic Development and Culture report to the April 22, 2026 Council meeting with the by-law or authority changes needed to create a municipal event-designation process. It affects summer event organizers and small businesses.

title: Fighting for the Scarborough East Rapid Transit Line
topics: capital budgets, public transit, transportation; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, transportation services
brief: The Mayor is asking Council to make the Scarborough East Rapid Transit Line its top unfunded transit priority and to ask the provincial and federal governments to each fund one-third of the cost, after both committed one-third shares of the Waterfront East LRT ($2 billion secured). title: Financial and Major Projects Update for the Year Ended December 31, 2025
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, capital budgets, financial reports, operating budgets, transportation infrastructure; annual financial reports; financial statements, transportation network; transportation networks, ttc
brief: The TTC Board will receive the 2025 year-end financial and major projects update for Conventional and Wheel-Trans services. Preliminary results show a net favourable operating variance of $0.1 million, with a $120.6 million (8.2 percent) revenue shortfall fully offset by $120.7 million (4.2 percent) in under-expenditures; the revenue miss was driven by lower provincial funding from the deferred opening of Lines 5 and 6, lower-than-expected ridership and smaller draws from the TTC Stabilization Reserve. Preliminary year-end capital spending reached $1.661 billion, including $20.7 million in additional approved spending. The Board is also asked to approve in-year capital budget adjustments: offsetting $61.9 million in accelerated project spending with $61.9 million from delayed projects (no debt impact), adding $0.3 million to the Equipment program from PowerON funding and $0.6 million to Bridges and Tunnels from Crosslinx funding, and including the adjustments in the capital variance report for City Council's consideration.

brief: TTC staff report back to the Board on initiatives to improve the speed and reliability of the streetcar and LRT networks, as directed through earlier board items. Compared with initial opening, average afternoon peak round-trip travel time has improved by about 10 minutes on Line 5 and about 20 minutes on Line 6, and staff are developing a surface transit priority toolkit with Toronto Metropolitan University to identify congestion points. The work supports the 2026-2028 ridership growth strategy and the TTC's core mission of reliable service. The Board is asked to direct staff to keep going — expanding transit signal priority on Lines 5 and 6 and streetcar routes, reviewing operating rules on speeds, and reviewing streetcar stop spacing — and to report back with an update in the first quarter of 2027.

The TTC Board is asked to adopt the TTC's response to the provincial legislation.

The TTC Board is asked to direct staff on identifying required capital work to improve service reliability.
