topics: Exhibition Place, audits, computer networks, internet, security; auditors; auditors
brief: Exhibition Place generates $595 million in annual economic impact and $67.3 million in 2024 revenue, making it Canada's largest convention centre and entertainment and sports venue. The Auditor General is asking the board to adopt the recommendations from phase two of her cybersecurity audit, covering overall network security and select critical systems, with the detailed findings kept in a confidential attachment. Management agrees with the recommendations.

title: Service Standard Dashboard: An Update on Static and Interactive Reporting Tools
topics: customer service, service quality;
brief: The Service Excellence Committee is asking the Executive Committee to have the City Manager report by the first quarter of 2027 on requiring City divisions to develop corrective action plans when service performance standards are missed or gaps persist. The request builds on the new Service Standard Dashboard tracking nine high-volume 311 service categories.

title: Leveraging Data to Drive Service Excellence in Parks and Recreation and Transportation Services
topics: customer service, parks, transportation; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, transportation services
brief: The Service Excellence Committee is asking the Executive Committee to have Parks and Recreation, Transportation Services, and Municipal Licensing and Standards report back on May 14, 2026, on how they use 311 and Listening to Toronto survey data to spot trends and improve services. It is a reporting request on customer-service analytics.

title: Protecting migratory birds at Metro Hall and all City-owned buildings
topics: [activities in public safety and protection], animals, buildings, migratory birds; fauna
brief: Mayor Chow is asking the Executive Committee to have staff finish bird-friendly retrofits of windows and glass railings up to the fifth floor of Metro Hall as soon as possible, and keep up bird-protection measures there and at City Hall. More than 5,000 birds collided with glass in Toronto in 2025, and bird-friendly glass or film is proven to cut collisions by up to 95 per cent.

title: Little Jamaica and Oakwood Vaughan Planning Framework - Proposals Report
topics: community development, neighbourhoods (planning); community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development
brief: A draft planning framework for Little Jamaica and Oakwood Vaughan would guide future development while supporting the area's culture and community priorities. City Council is asked to send the draft out for community and stakeholder consultation, with final recommendations expected later in 2026. The framework covers how development can deliver on what residents have asked for and how public spaces can celebrate the area's cultural identity.

title: Impact Assessment of Extended Flightpath at Billy Bishop Airport
topics: airports, assessment;
brief: A motion asks city staff to study how expanding the Billy Bishop Airport flightpath to allow jets would affect future housing supply. The mover presents the question as one the city should answer with full information during a housing crisis, noting both the economic case made for jets and the competing potential of waterfront land for attractions and housing. The Planning and Housing Committee will consider the study request.

title: Introduction of By-laws
topics: bonds, draft by-laws, finance (sc); debentures; notes, draft bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Debenture Committee will introduce a general bill and a confirming bill to put its March debenture decisions into law. No policy change is proposed.

title: City of Toronto Sustainable Debenture Program
topics: bonds, finance (sc), programs; debentures; notes
brief: This is an information item: the City is launching a Sustainable Debenture Program that merges its 2018 green and 2020 social bond frameworks, letting Toronto sell green, social, or sustainability bonds for capital projects with environmental or social benefits. An independent review by Moody's gave the framework its highest Sustainability Quality Score, SQS1 (Excellent), and the program may slightly lower borrowing costs. The Debenture Committee is asked to receive the report; no decision is required, and the framework shapes how future City infrastructure debt is sold to investors.

title: Authority to Issue a Debenture
topics: bonds, finance (sc); debentures; notes
brief: A $450 million, 30-year bond sale is on the table to finance approved City capital projects; the sale, led by CIBC, closed March 31, 2026, with delivery to investors on April 17, 2026. The Debenture Committee is asked to approve the borrowing and introduce the enabling by-law, with all borrowing costs already budgeted in the 2026 tax-supported operating budget. The decision locks in debt that Toronto will repay over three decades.

title: Selection of Candidates for Interview for the Toronto Licensing Tribunal
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Nominating Panel – Toronto Licensing Tribunal must select five candidates to interview at its next meeting, then recommend two to City Council for appointment to the Tribunal. The City Clerk recommends selecting five of the candidates listed in a confidential attachment; the details stay confidential.

title: Election of Chair - Nominating Panel - Toronto Licensing Tribunal
brief: This is a procedural item: the Nominating Panel for the Toronto Licensing Tribunal elects its Chair under Municipal Code Chapter 27, Appendix A2, for a term lasting until a successor is appointed. The panel interviews candidates and recommends appointments to the Toronto Licensing Tribunal.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Sign Variance Committee
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Nominating Panel – Sign Variance Committee will conduct interviews and recommend two public members to City Council for appointment to the Sign Variance Committee for a term ending April 24, 2030, and until successors are appointed, and recommend one public member as Chair. Candidate details remain confidential.

title: Toronto Francophone Affairs Advisory Committee: Request for Term Progress Report
topics: [activities in planning and development], agendas, planning, work plans;
brief: The Francophone Affairs Advisory Committee wants a term report on how its recommendations have been handled. It asks the Economic and Community Development Committee to have the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture prepare a progress report on City actions taken on the committee's recommendations this term, reporting back to the advisory committee on June 18, 2026.

title: Rexdale-Casino Woodbine Community Benefits Agreement: 2025 Progress Update
topics: community benefits;
brief: This is a progress update on the Rexdale-Casino Woodbine Community Benefits Agreement, adopted in 2018 as a condition of expanded gaming at Woodbine Racetrack, with most targets reported as met or on track. The report's figures include $113.3 million, $2.34 million, and $5 million. Council is asked to receive the update; no new decision is proposed, and the item affects local hiring and community benefits around the casino site.

title: Toronto Action Plan to Confront Anti-Black Racism: Year Five Update
topics: accessibility, racial discrimination; anti-racism; racism, barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible
brief: This is an information item: the committee receives the year-five update on Toronto's Action Plan to Confront Anti-Black Racism, covering the final 2023-2024 implementation period and progress from 2018 to 2024. The report says 96 per cent of the plan's actions were delivered and outlines priority work for 2026 and early 2027. No policy change is proposed.

title: Minimizing Sleep Disruption from Siren Noise
topics: noise, noise control; amplified music; construction noise; loud music; noise pollution; traffic noise, noise barriers; sound barriers
brief: Residents near downtown emergency stations and hospitals, including in Ward 11, report chronic sleep disruption from frequent late-night sirens and air horns. This motion asks the committee to have the Fire Chief and Toronto Paramedic Services review all options for reducing that noise and report back in the first quarter of 2027. It affects residents living near EMS and fire stations.

title: Addressing Evictions through Disaggregated Race-Based Data in Social Housing
topics: eviction, social housing; community housing; housing allowance; housing projects; low income housing; non profit housing; non-profit housing; public housing; rent geared to income assistance; rent geared to income housing; rent subsidies; rent supplement; subsidized housing; subsidized rent; subsidized units
brief: The Confronting Anti-Black Racism Advisory Committee is asking Council to request that Toronto Community Housing consider pausing evictions for unpaid rent from July 30 to November 15, 2026, until Council sees a plan to address rising evictions and their disproportionate impact on Black, Indigenous, racialized, and low-income tenants. It also asks for a rehousing and housing-stability pathway for tenants already evicted, prioritizing Black, Indigenous, and racialized tenants, seniors, people with disabilities, families with children, and youth. The item affects tenants in social housing, the housing of last resort for many residents.

title: Advancing Community Development through Evidence-Based Planning
topics: community development, neighbourhoods (planning); community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development
brief: The Confronting Anti-Black Racism Advisory Committee is asking Council to have staff report, as part of the 2027 budget process, on a citywide framework to scale neighbourhood Social Development Plans, with priority neighbourhoods, resident-led decision-making, and links to existing City strategies. It also asks the Mayor to consider ongoing funding of $250,000 to $500,000 per neighbourhood per year for neighbourhood associations or community-led coalitions to implement the plans. The item affects how community development money flows to priority neighbourhoods, including those with significant Black and racialized populations.

title: Further Direction on Report on Rejoining the Association Francophone des Municipalités de l’Ontario
topics: [organizations in culture], organizations; corporate bodies
brief: The Francophone Affairs Advisory Committee is asking for the City Manager's upcoming report to cover whether Toronto should rejoin the Association francophone des municipalites de l'Ontario, the association of French-speaking Ontario municipalities. Staff have met with the association and expect to report back to the committee in June 2026. The decision affects the City's ties to francophone municipal advocacy.

title: Request for a Report on Existing Services Available to French-Speaking Torontonians
topics: bilingual status, employment opportunities; bilingualism; services in french, careers; employment; job applications; job boards; job openings; job opportunities; job postings; job vacancies; jobs; vacancies (jobs)
brief: The Francophone Affairs Advisory Committee wants a clearer picture of what the City offers in French. It asks the Economic and Community Development Committee to have staff include, in a June 2026 report on services for French-speaking Torontonians, how many City jobs require French and how many such positions exist.

title: Maintaining Housing Working Group Chair Update
topics: housing, tenants; homes; residences, renters; tenancy agreements
brief: This is a procedural item: the chair of the Maintaining Housing Working Group updates the Housing Rights Advisory Committee on its engagement with city staff on monitoring the effects of Ontario's Bill 60, Fighting Delays, Building Faster Act, 2025, on Toronto tenants. No decision is attached.

title: Supporting Unhoused Rights Holders Working Group Chair Update
topics: community outreach, housing; awareness programs; community engagement; outreach; promotion (communication); public outreach, homes; residences
brief: This is a procedural item: the chair of the Supporting Unhoused Rights Holders Working Group updates the Housing Rights Advisory Committee on the group's engagement with city staff on outcomes from the city's Enhanced Outreach Model as part of its encampment response. No decision is attached.

title: Presentation from the Co-operative Housing Federation of Toronto
topics: co-operative housing, housing; co-op housing; coop housing; cooperative housing, homes; residences
brief: This is an information item: the Co-operative Housing Federation of Toronto presents to the Housing Rights Advisory Committee on how households access co-operative housing and how supply could grow to meet demand for safe, affordable housing. No decision is attached.

title: Addressing Barriers to Adequate Housing for Women and Gender-Diverse People
topics: affordable housing, housing; affordable homes; housing projects, homes; residences
brief: This is an information item: representatives from Nellie's present findings and recommendations from its paper, Breaking Barriers, on challenges women and gender-diverse people face accessing the affordable housing system, and proposed solutions in the municipal context. No decision is attached.

title: The Role of Property Standards on Maintaining Adequate Housing
topics: housing, property standards; homes; residences
brief: This is an information item: the Federal Housing Advocate delivers a presentation to the Housing Rights Advisory Committee on why tenants need robust access-to-justice mechanisms so their housing stays adequate and compliant with property standards. No decision is attached.

title: Chair Update
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: This is a procedural item: the chair of the Housing Rights Advisory Committee, Elizabeth McIsaac, provides an update to the committee. No decision is attached.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order Number 6052967 with Coolearth Architecture Inc., for the Mount Dennis Early Learning and Child Care Centre Project
topics: child care facilities, construction, contracts, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, building, child care agencies; child care centres; day cares; day nurseries; home care agencies; home child care providers; nursery schools
brief: The city wants to amend its purchase order with Coolearth Architecture Inc. for continued oversight of the Mount Dennis Early Learning and Child Care Centre at 1234 Weston Road, to manage corrective work on outstanding deficiencies left by the terminated general contractor M.J. Dixon Construction Ltd. (formally terminated in July 2025 after a default notice in June). The centre reached substantial completion in September 2024, 17 months late after pandemic-era delays, and opened to the public in September 2025; staff say the deficiencies are minor and don't affect safety or operations. The report cites financial figures of $386,978, $374,449, $381,039, $295,910, $301,118, $670,359, and $682,157 related to the amendment and estimated corrective costs.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order 6051950 with WSP Canada Inc., for Engineering Services for the Rehabilitation and Upgrades of Eight Group Seven Sewage Pumping Stations at Various Locations
topics: construction, contracts, purchasing, sewers, wastewater treatment; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, building, sewage systems; sewerage, sewage treatment; waste water treatment; wastewater management
brief: The city wants to add $1,764,477 ($1,795,532 net of HST recoveries) to WSP Canada Inc.'s engineering contract for rehabilitating eight Group Seven sewage pumping stations across Toronto, raising the purchase order from $3,180,416 ($3,236,392) to $4,944,893 ($5,031,924). The increase stems from a scope change: the city split the work from one large construction contract into four smaller ones, which requires more contract administration and full-time inspection. Council approval is needed for the amendment.

title: Summary of Open Competitive Awards Made by the Chief Procurement Officer from February 14th to March 6th, 2026
topics: awards, contracts, projects, purchasing, suppliers; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Procurement Officer reports to the General Government Committee on competitive contracts awarded from February 14 to March 6, 2026 — 17 awards ranging from $0.596 million to $13.9 million — under the officer's authority to award solicitations up to $30 million with terms up to five years. The committee is asked only to receive the report.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Administrative Penalty Tribunal
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Nominating Panel – Administrative Penalty Tribunal will conduct interviews and recommend 13 public members, including one as Chair, to City Council for appointment to the Tribunal for a term ending April 25, 2030, and until successors are appointed. Candidate details remain confidential.

title: Update on OMERS Climate Action Plan
topics: climate, climate change, finance (sc), investment, pensions; climate protection
brief: This is an information item: OMERS officials give the Infrastructure and Environment Committee their annual update on the OMERS Climate Action Plan, including progress to date. No decision is attached.

title: Review of Highly Polluting Personal Watercraft
topics: noise, recreational watercraft, water pollution; amplified music; construction noise; loud music; noise pollution; traffic noise, boat launching; boats; leisure water vehicles; pleasure boats; pleasure craft, marine pollution; stormwater pollution
brief: The item asks the Infrastructure and Environment Committee to direct the General Manager of Parks and Recreation, with the Executive Director of Environment, Climate and Forestry, the Toronto Region Conservation Authority, and Toronto Hydro, to study pollution from personal watercraft and two-stroke boat engines at waterfront boat clubs — noting lease renewals recently included a ban on jet ski rentals on leased lands, that most clubs would support extending it to privately owned jet skis, and that cleaner electric engine alternatives exist. A separate personal-watercraft safety study is already underway. The item affects noise and water pollution on the waterfront. The committee decides on the request.

title: Utility Construction Photo Documentation
brief: This is a procedural item: the Audit Committee asks City Council to have the General Manager of Transportation Services provide permits, timing, and sequencing for utility work on four Ward 14 (Toronto-Danforth) streets — Woodfield Road, Riverdale Avenue, Grant Street, and Danforth Avenue — and to report on pylon removal after construction. Council decides on the direction.

title: 1233 Yonge Street and 9 Woodlawn Avenue East - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: demolitions, rental housing, tenants; rental properties; rental units, renters; tenancy agreements
brief: Forty rental units at 1233 Yonge Street and 9 Woodlawn Avenue East would be demolished for the proposed 47-storey, 730-unit building, and City Council is asked to approve the rental housing demolition application. All 40 rentals would be replaced within the new development, with a tenant assistance plan giving existing tenants a right of return at similar rents plus financial compensation for hardship. The report also recommends a residential demolition permit and attaches a $20,000.00 financial condition to the approval.
address: 7 Woodlawn Toronto Ontario; 1233 Yonge Toronto Ontario

title: 1233 Yonge Street and 9 Woodlawn Avenue East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 47-storey mixed-use building with 730 homes is proposed for 1233 Yonge Street and 9 Woodlawn Avenue East, and City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments — including an Official Plan change to permit the height. Forty rental units would be demolished and replaced with 40 rental replacement units, with a tenant assistance plan giving existing tenants a right of return at similar rents plus financial compensation for hardship. A companion rental demolition report goes to community council on April 1, 2026.
address: 9 Woodlawn Toronto Ontario; 1233 Yonge Toronto Ontario

title: Introduction of By-laws
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will formally introduce the by-laws it approved during the meeting so they can be enacted. No policy change is proposed — this is the routine final step that puts the meeting's decisions into legal effect.

title: Building New Infrastructure in Liberty Village by Advancing Liberty New Street in Alignment with the Opening of Exhibition Station
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: infrastructure, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: The push continues to get Metrolinx to finish Liberty New Street — the promised east-west road for Liberty Village — in time for the opening of Exhibition Station. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to keep holding Metrolinx to that commitment and to have staff report back on the project's status in July 2026. The new road is meant to relieve congestion on East Liberty and Liberty Street, the only road connecting the growing neighbourhood, which also funnels visitors to BMO Field, Coca-Cola Coliseum, Rogers Stadium, and Exhibition Place.

title: Camberwell Road - Parking and Traffic Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking regulations, traffic regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Three parking spots on the west side of Camberwell Road near Eglinton Avenue West would be removed and replaced with a no-standing zone, after residents asked for relief from peak-time congestion that blocks turning traffic onto Eglinton near Allen Road. Councillor Josh Matlow's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to approve the change and rescind the parking-machine rules there, where the rate is $3.25 per hour. The easterly lane would also be designated for right turns only; staff say they would look at bringing parking back after the Eglinton and Allen intersection redesign is complete.

title: Davies Avenue and Carroll Street - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking;
brief: The temporary parking added on Davies Avenue and Carroll Street during the Queen Street East watermain and track replacement project would become permanent. Councillor Paula Fletcher's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to keep the spots after residents and the local BIA asked for them: on the east side of Davies Avenue, that means no parking from Queen Street East to 30 metres north, one-hour parking from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. between 30 and 50 metres north of Queen, and no parking overnight. The project had removed 25 paid spaces between Davies and Broadview.

title: 1 to 7 Yonge Street, South Block - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The existing 25-storey office building at 1 to 7 Yonge Street would be converted into a hotel with 487 suites, and City Council is asked to approve the zoning amendment for the south block of the property. Staff describe the adaptive reuse of the building as an appropriate and efficient use of land that fits provincial policy and the Official Plan.
address: 1 Yonge Toronto Ontario; 7 Yonge Toronto Ontario

title: Price Street Loading Zone
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking machines, parking prohibitions; no parking, pay and display machines; pay-and-display machines
brief: Some on-street parking on Price Street — the short, narrow dead-end running east from Yonge Street to the Toronto Lawn and Tennis Club — would become a commercial loading zone to improve safety around the club. Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to make the change: large trucks serving the club have been driving onto the sidewalk where children walk to lessons, and the club's wheelchair-accessibility renovation has added heavy construction vehicles to the mix. The item would also remove the north-side parking machines, where the rate is $4.50 per hour.

title: Plan for Joe Pantalone Lane
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: lanes, naming, street names; renaming; road names; street naming, traffic lanes; turn lanes; turning lanes
brief: The Little Italy Business Improvement Association has asked that the public lane west of Grace Street, between Harbord and Grace Streets north of College Street, be renamed Joe Pantalone Lane to honour the former councillor and deputy mayor, who served on Toronto and Metro councils from 1980 to 2010 and as deputy mayor from 2003 to 2010. Because public notice has not yet been given, Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to direct staff to report back to the April 30, 2026 meeting with recommendations. No renaming is being approved yet.

title: Mirvish Village - Parking and Traffic Amendments (Delegated)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking regulations, traffic, traffic regulations; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Parking and traffic changes around the Mirvish Village redevelopment would implement parts of the 2021 site plan agreement with Westbank Project Corp, the developer behind the 2- to 27-storey mixed-use project spanning Bloor, Bathurst, Lennox, and Markham Streets. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to make Markham Street one-way northbound between Lennox Street and Bloor Street West, ban stopping on the east side at all times, and allow curbside activity on the west side only in two lay-bys — one a 10-minute delivery zone and the other a passenger loading zone. The changes go with a widened boulevard, a narrowed roadway, and a new private east-west driveway south of Bloor between Bathurst and Markham under a public easement.

title: Re-opening and Amending TE25.42 - Accessible Parking Spaces
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: accessibility, parking, parking spaces; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, parking spots
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to reopen its September 2025 decision and cancel the accessible parking space approved on the east side of Gladstone Avenue, south of Hallam Street, because the original applicant told Transportation Services it is no longer needed. Councillor Alejandra Bravo's motion would delete that entry from the installation list. No policy change is proposed.

title: Establishing a Commercial Loading Zone on Salem Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: commercial areas, loading zones, parking prohibitions, stopping prohibitions; commercial districts; retail areas, drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, no parking, no stopping
brief: A commercial loading zone would be created on Salem Avenue just north of Bloor Street West after residents and business owners told the ward councillor's office that delivery trucks block laneways and there are not enough loading zones in the area. Councillor Alejandra Bravo's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to establish the zone, shifting parking to the west side of Salem Avenue. The change is meant to deter illegal parking, keep laneway access clear, and support local businesses receiving deliveries.

title: Ossington Street Parking and Traffic Review
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, safety, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, public safety
brief: Staff would review pedestrian safety, traffic, and parking on Ossington Street between Dupont Street and Dundas Street and report back in the first quarter of 2027. Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to direct the review, in consultation with the TTC, because changes planned south of Dundas — round-the-clock parking on both sides, pedestrian bump-outs, and one lane of traffic each way — are expected to affect the street north of Dundas, where some residents have also asked for rush-hour parking as a buffer near schools.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item TE24.61 - Brock Avenue - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to reopen its July 2025 Brock Avenue parking decision and delete Part 6, which contained an incorrect parking amendment, while keeping the parking changes residents requested. Councillor Alejandra Bravo's motion would correct the error; no new policy is proposed.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Moss Park Arena Board
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: appointments, arenas, board members, public appointments; indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to appoint Karin Fritzlar and Stephen Graham to the Moss Park Arena Board for terms ending April 2, 2030. The City Clerk's confidential attachment with candidate details would stay private. No policy change is proposed.

title: Gamble Avenue - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming measures; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Ten speed humps would be installed on Gamble Avenue between Pape Avenue and Donlands Avenue. Staff assessed the street and found it meets the criteria in the city's traffic calming policy. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to authorize the humps.

title: Dockside Drive and Knapp Lane - All-Way Stop Control
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: stop signs, traffic regulations, transit stops; all-way stop controls; technical warrants, stops (public transportation)
brief: An all-way stop would be installed at Dockside Drive and Knapp Lane. Staff assessed the intersection and recommend the stop to improve safety for all road users. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to approve it.

title: Labatt Avenue - Pedestrian Way Designation and Streetscape Improvements
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking regulations, pedestrians, traffic regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws, pedestrianization
brief: The dead-end stretch of Labatt Avenue near Defries Street would become a pedestrian way once the 37-storey condo at 1-25 Defries Street and its new parkland are finished. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to designate the section from 17 metres east of Defries Street to the dead-end as car-free, keeping access for pedestrians, cyclists, and emergency and maintenance vehicles. The change would create a seamless walking link between the new park and the street; the developer committed to the parkland and streetscape improvements in a 2020 agreement.

title: Mid-Block Pedestrian Traffic Control Signal - Jarvis Street, between Carlton Street and Maitland Street/Maitland Place
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: safety, traffic control systems, traffic regulations, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, public safety, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: A mid-block traffic signal would be installed on Jarvis Street about 190 metres north of Carlton Street — between Carlton and Maitland — to give pedestrians a protected crossing. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to approve the signal; staff say it would improve safety for all road users, particularly vulnerable ones.

title: Westview Boulevard - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Parking would be banned at all times near six intersections on Westview Boulevard — at Amsterdam, Galbraith, Tiago, Selwyn, Gardens Crescent, and Joanith Drive — to support new geometric safety improvements and keep vehicles moving through the turns. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to approve the prohibitions, identified through the city's transportation safety and state-of-good-repair programs.

title: Archer Street - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking prohibitions, parking regulations, standing prohibitions; no parking, no standing, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Standing would be banned on both sides of the north-south stretch of Archer Street near Cobourg Avenue, and mismatches between the posted signs and the parking by-law for Archer Street and Cobourg Avenue would be fixed. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to approve the changes, which are meant to keep sightlines clear and passage open on the two-way street.

title: Accessible Parking Spaces - April 2026 (Delegated)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: accessibility, parking, parking receipts; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible
brief: This is a routine item with final authority at community council: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve installing and removing on-street accessible parking spaces for people with disabilities at the locations listed in the April 2026 delegated report, along with related parking-regulation updates. No policy change is proposed.

title: Safety Improvements on Davenport Road, Cottingham Road, Poplar Plains Road, and Macpherson Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: [activities in transportation], community councils, safety; public safety
brief: Road safety changes along Davenport Road, Cottingham Road, Poplar Plains Road, and Macpherson Avenue are back before the Toronto and East York Community Council. The package adds a parking lane on the west side of Poplar Plains Road between Cottingham Road and Boulton Drive, a stop sign for southbound drivers on Glen Edyth Drive at Cottingham Road, and traffic signals at the Davenport–Poplar Plains–Macpherson intersection — lifting the westbound right-turn-only rule while keeping the southbound left-turn ban. Staff say the changes would give drivers clearer direction and create safer crossings for pedestrians and cyclists.

title: Vehicle Width Restriction - Public Lane System bounded by Beaver Avenue, Lightbourn Avenue, Brandon Avenue, and Primrose Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: lanes, traffic regulations, transit vehicles, transportation (sc); traffic lanes; turn lanes; turning lanes
brief: Vehicles wider than two metres would be banned from the public laneway system bounded by Beaver, Lightbourn, Brandon, and Primrose Avenues, to reduce damage to the surrounding infrastructure and private properties. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to approve the restriction.

title: Vehicle Width Restriction - Public Lane south of Gerrard Street East, west of Boulton Avenue and Public Lane east of Broadview Avenue, south of Gerrard Street East
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: [land vehicles by function], road restrictions, transportation (sc); lane restrictions; road information; traffic restrictions; trip info; tripinfo
brief: Wide vehicles would be banned from two narrow laneways near Gerrard Street East and Broadview Avenue to reduce damage to surrounding private properties. The City Clerk recommends the panel interview ten of the candidates listed in a confidential attachment; the candidate details stay confidential as personal information about identifiable individuals.

title: Election of Chair - Nominating Panel - Compliance Audit Committee
brief: This is a procedural item: the Nominating Panel for the Compliance Audit Committee elects its Chair under Municipal Code Chapter 27, Appendix A2, for a term lasting until a successor is appointed. The panel is the body that interviews candidates and recommends appointments to the Compliance Audit Committee, which reviews compliance with municipal election finance rules.

title: Re-open Items HL30.1, HL30.2 and HL30.3 to Correct Appointment End Dates
topics: health, letters; health coverage
brief: This is a procedural item: Re-opening the February 23, 2026 chair, vice chair, and committee appointment items to correct the end date from November 16, 2026 to November 14, 2026, matching the actual end of board directors' terms would get the Board of Health's approval. Councillor Chris Moise was elected chair and director Abinaya Chandrabalan vice chair. The board decides on the correction.

title: 2025 Performance Appraisal - Medical Officer of Health
topics: health; health coverage
brief: This is a procedural item: the board's performance-appraisal committee brings its 2025 appraisal of the Medical Officer of Health to the Board of Health, with the detailed appraisal kept confidential as it concerns personal matters about an identifiable employee. The board decides on the confidential recommendation.

title: City Approved Toronto Public Health 2026 Capital Budget and 2027-2035 Capital Plan
topics: capital budgets, health; health coverage
brief: This is an information item: the city approved Toronto Public Health's 2026 capital budget of $8.051 million across four projects (electronic medical records for TB, inspection management, a mobile dental van, and the morning meal program), plus $2.129 million in future-year commitments ($10.180 million total), and a 2027-2035 capital plan totalling $17.867 million. Key changes include moving the Downtown HART Hub construction project to Corporate Real Estate Management. The board is asked only to receive the report.

title: City Approved Toronto Public Health 2026 Operating Budget
topics: operating budgets, public health;
brief: City Council adopted Toronto Public Health's 2026 operating budget on February 10, 2026: $307.421 million gross and $103.489 million net, with 1,865.5 full-time positions — lower than the board recommended by $8.846 million gross and $9.038 million net, with a $75.0 million corporate savings target noted in budget detail. The cuts fall mainly on the phased Student Nutrition Program expansion and three food-safety positions, while 19 new provincially funded positions were added for the Downtown HART Hub addiction recovery program. The figures affect public health staffing and school nutrition funding for 2026 — the year-over-year increase is $5.911 million gross and $9.526 million net.

title: Toronto Public Health Capital Budget for the Year Ending on December 31, 2025
topics: health; health coverage
brief: This is an information item: for the year ended December 31, 2025, Toronto Public Health spent $5.551 million — 74.9 percent of its approved $7.415 million capital budget. The board is asked only to receive the report.

title: Toronto Public Health Operating Budget for the Year Ending on December 31, 2025
topics: health, operating budgets; health coverage
brief: This is an information item: for the year ended December 31, 2025, Toronto Public Health underspent gross expenditures by $41.4 million and underachieved revenues by $26.2 million, for a favourable net variance of $15.2 million. The board is asked only to receive the report.

title: Health Impacts of Homelessness and Update on the Downtown CORE Pilot
topics: health, homelessness; health coverage
brief: At the end of January 2026 there were 11,094 people experiencing homelessness in Toronto, and the report before the board summarizes how homelessness drives premature death and higher rates of infectious disease, diabetes, cardiovascular and respiratory disease. Toronto Public Health evaluated its Downtown CORE pilot — public health nurses paired with police constables doing mobile outreach and case management for homeless people with mental health and substance-use challenges around Yonge-Dundas (Sankofa Square) — and found it is connecting clients with medical care and social supports. The board is asked to have the Medical Officer of Health extend the pilot. The board decides.

title: Actions to Advance Indigenous Health
topics: First Nations, health; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples, health coverage
brief: The question before the Board of Health: whether to endorse continued and strengthened public health work on Indigenous health, reported with $420,000 in funding context. Toronto Public Health's Indigenous Health Strategy — guided by the Ontario Public Health Standards, the city's Reconciliation Action Plan (2022-2032), and Indigenous service providers, Knowledge Keepers, and community leaders — covers Indigenous cultural safety training, mental health and substance-use response including harm reduction, Indigenous-led vaccination and primary care partnerships, and Indigenous health data sovereignty. The work affects the health of Indigenous residents and the city's reconciliation commitments. The board decides.

title: Response to Provincial Defunding of Consumption and Treatment Services (CTS)
topics: funding, harm reduction; crack kits; methadone clinic; methadone maintenance; methadone treatment; needle exchanges; safer crack kits; safer crack smoking materials; safer injection, financing
brief: Ontario's Ministry of Health notified remaining Consumption and Treatment Services sites on March 13 that provincial funding ends June 13, 2026, leaving only two public supervised-consumption sites in Toronto — with the Fred Victor and Moss Park sites affected. The city's public health leadership describes the sites as a starting point toward treatment and a trusted source of community for clients, and has convened an interdivisional response table plus a working group of service providers, shelters, researchers, and physicians to track impacts. The item affects front-line overdose-prevention services and the people who rely on them.

title: New Appointments to the Board of Health
topics: appointments;
brief: This is an information item: City Council appointed Charna Gord and Rebecca Mador to the Board of Health on March 25-26, 2026, for terms ending November 14, 2026, filling the seats left by Suman Roy and Lindsay Kretschmer.

title: 2025: A Year-in-Review of Toronto Public Health
topics: health; health coverage
brief: This is an information item: the Medical Officer of Health presents Toronto Public Health's 2025 year-in-review, covering work during Ontario's largest measles outbreak in over 25 years, rising living costs, the ongoing drug toxicity crisis, climate-related extreme weather, and the spread of health misinformation, serving more than three million residents. The board is asked only to receive the report.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto Mobility Plan
topics: sports, sports tournaments, traffic management, transportation; tournaments, traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations, transportation services
brief: This is an information item: City Council receives the FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto Mobility Plan, developed with consultant Arcadis and partners including Transportation Services, the TTC, Metrolinx, the Ministry of Transportation, Toronto Police, and Emergency Management. The plan sets out coordinated transportation and traffic measures to move residents, visitors, transit, emergency vehicles, and event operations around venues, fan zones, transit hubs, and key corridors during the tournament. No decision beyond receiving the plan is attached.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: By-law exemptions to facilitate planning and delivery of the FIFA World Cup 2026 events at Fort York and the Bentway, and at Nathan Phillips Square
topics: by-laws, sports, sports tournaments; bylaws, tournaments
brief: To host FIFA World Cup 2026 events, City Council is asked to grant by-law exemptions and delegated authorities for the FIFA Fan Festival at Fort York and the Bentway (June 10 to July 19, 2026) and events at Nathan Phillips Square (May 18 to July 20, 2026). The exemptions include allowing the sale and distribution of plastic bottled water for hydration needs alongside HTO To Go water trailers, and authorizing special-effects pyrotechnics as part of events. The report was prepared jointly by the FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto Secretariat, Solid Waste Management, Economic Development and Culture, Corporate Real Estate Management, and Parks and Recreation. City Council decides; the measures affect how fan events operate at both sites during the tournament.

title: 3434 Eglinton Avenue East, 502 - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number 26 111452 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee will hear the property owner's appeal of a property standards order issued February 4, 2026 for 3434 Eglinton Avenue East, unit 502 (file 26 111452 PRS 00 IV). The committee can confirm, change, or cancel the order. The hearing gives the owner a chance to challenge the city's maintenance or repair requirements.

title: 1360 Danforth Road, 606 - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number 26 102148 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the owner of 1360 Danforth Road, unit 606 is appealing a property standards order issued January 12, 2026 (file 26 102148 PRS 00 IV) to the Property Standards Committee. The committee hears the appeal and can uphold, amend, or rescind the order.

title: 10 Macey Avenue, 1606 - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number 26 105076 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: an appeal of the property standards order for 10 Macey Avenue, unit 1606 goes before the Property Standards Committee. The order was issued January 19, 2026 (file 26 105076 PRS 00 IV). The committee will decide whether the order stands, changes, or is cancelled.

title: 10 Macey Avenue, 404 - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number 26 105165 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee will hear the property owner's appeal of a property standards order issued January 19, 2026 for 10 Macey Avenue, unit 404 (file 26 105165 PRS 00 IV). The committee can confirm, change, or cancel the order. The hearing gives the owner a chance to challenge the city's maintenance or repair requirements.

title: 14 Ivan Road - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number 26 102824 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee will hear the property owner's appeal of a property standards order issued January 12, 2026 for 14 Ivan Road (file 26 102824 PRS 00 IV). The committee can confirm, change, or cancel the order. The appeal is the owner's chance to challenge the city's repair or maintenance requirements.

title: 56 Yonge Street - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: community councils, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The eight-storey designated heritage hotel at 56 Yonge Street would be kept in place while a new 65-storey, 648-unit tower rises on the adjacent lot at 60 Yonge Street, cantilevering 2.6 metres over the hotel about four storeys above its roof. City Council is asked to approve the alterations to the heritage property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and to amend the existing heritage easement agreement, in connection with the 65-storey mixed-use proposal. The undesignated 12-storey building at 60 Yonge would be demolished; the heritage hotel was previously approved for full in-situ retention in 2019.

title: 56-60 Yonge Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: A 65-storey mixed-use tower with 648 homes is proposed for 56-60 Yonge Street, partially cantilevering over the eight-storey designated heritage hotel at 56 Yonge Street, which would be kept. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments, including a change to the Downtown Plan so the site no longer has to replace its existing office space and can provide less non-residential floor area overall. A separate heritage conservation report for the hotel building comes to council alongside this item.

title: Bathurst Quay Neighbourhood Transportation Study
topics: capital budgets, safety, traffic, transportation; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, public safety, transportation services
brief: A full transportation study and road safety audit of the Bathurst Quay neighbourhood would be commissioned, with a report back in the third quarter of 2027. City Council is asked to direct the study because the waterfront area has changed substantially since the last studies in 2017 — a new park at the Malting Silos, development along Queens Quay, the airport, and proposed marine links like Hoverlink and a water-taxi pilot — while residents keep raising concerns about traffic and pedestrian safety at Bathurst and Lake Shore and at Eireann Quay and Queens Quay.

title: Speed Limit Reduction - King Street West, between Dufferin Street and Strachan Avenue
topics: speed limits, traffic calming, traffic speed;
brief: The speed limit on King Street West between Dufferin Street and Strachan Avenue would drop to 40 km/h, matching the rest of the street. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik's motion asks City Council to set the limit after a field investigation found no posted signs on that stretch — it currently defaults to 50 km/h — while the sections east of Strachan and west of Dufferin are already signed at 40. Residents, including those on Joe Shuster Way near King and Dufferin, raised speeding concerns on a neighbourhood safety walk.

title: Euclid Avenue Traffic Calming Turn Restrictions
topics: traffic calming, traffic calming measures, turn prohibitions (traffic); traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Afternoon rush-hour drivers would be barred from turning left off northbound Euclid Avenue onto Bloor Street West or Harbord Street from 3 p.m. to 7 p.m. daily, with bicycles exempt. Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion asks City Council to impose the restrictions — Euclid is a residential street with schools and a children's park, and the two intersections have no traffic lights. The goal is to discourage cut-through traffic between Dundas and Bloor, following up on the earlier TE28.47 traffic-calming direction.

title: 2004, 2006 and 2008 Bathurst Street - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: Six rental units at 2004, 2006, and 2008 Bathurst Street would be demolished for the proposed 19-storey, 71-unit mixed-use building, and City Council is asked to approve the rental housing demolition application. The seven replacement rental units would be protected for 20 years, with a tenant assistance plan giving existing tenants a right of return at similar rents plus financial compensation for hardship. The report also recommends a residential demolition permit and attaches a $20,000.00 financial condition to the approval.

title: College Street/Carlton Street Toronto Transit Commission (TTC) Turning Exemptions
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, [transportation management], traffic regulations, turn prohibitions (traffic); ttc
brief: Starting as early as March 1, 2026, streetcar track repairs at College Street and Bay Street will force the 506 Carlton streetcar and 19 Bay bus onto detours, with buses replacing the 506 for about six weeks. Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion asks City Council to exempt TTC vehicles from two existing left-turn bans — eastbound lefts at Gerrard and Yonge (7 a.m. to 7 p.m., Monday to Saturday) and northbound lefts at Carlton and Jarvis (7:30 a.m. to 6:30 p.m., Monday to Saturday) — so replacement buses can legally run the detour route closer to the original streetcar line. A long-term exemption would also give the TTC operational flexibility.

title: Jones Avenue - Parking Amendments
topics: community councils, parking, parking prohibitions; no parking
brief: The no-parking rule on the east side of Jones Avenue between Ravina Crescent and a point 20 metres south would be upgraded to a no-stopping rule at all times, to improve sightlines for drivers turning from Ravina Crescent. City Council — which must vote on changes on Jones Avenue because the TTC operates there — is also asked to scrap an outdated no-parking ban on the west side between Harcourt Avenue and 30.5 metres north, fixing a mismatch with the posted signs.

title: Accessible Parking Space - Jones Avenue (Non-Delegated)
topics: accessible permit parking; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled)
brief: Designating a new on-street accessible parking space for people with disabilities on the east side of Jones Avenue, just south of Ravina Crescent, in effect at all times heads to City Council for a decision. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Jones Avenue.

title: 2004-2008 Bathurst Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: The call on whether to approve a 19-storey mixed-use building with 71 homes at 2004-2008 Bathurst Street, including an Official Plan change to allow commercial use in a non-house-form building belongs to City Council. Six rental units would be demolished and replaced with seven rental replacement units, with a tenant assistance plan giving existing tenants a right of return at similar rents; the building would also include 218 square metres of ground-floor commercial space, 73 car parking spots, 72 bicycle spaces, and a 4.5-metre pedestrian walkway linking Bathurst Street to the rear laneway. A companion rental demolition report goes to community council alongside this item.

title: 1233-1243 Queen Street East - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction; building
brief: Woodbourne Canada Management is building a 10-storey condo at 1233-1243 Queen Street East, on the southeast corner of Leslie Street and Queen, and needs part of Leslie Street and all of Memory Lane closed for 22 months. City Council approval is required because the TTC runs on Leslie Street; staff recommend closing a 3.5-metre strip of the northbound curb lane on Leslie between Queen Street East and Memory Lane, and all of Memory Lane from Leslie east 24.5 metres, from March 26, 2026 to December 31, 2027. Pedestrians would use a 1.8-metre covered walkway on Leslie's east side and a covered walkway on the south sidewalk of Queen Street East, with signs posted about the Memory Lane closure.

title: Permanent Closure of Part of the Public Laneway Abutting 1684-1702 Queen Street East
topics: community councils, laneways, transportation; back alleys; mews, transportation services
brief: A slice of public laneway just west of Penny Lane, north of 1702 Queen Street East, would be permanently closed — Transportation Services says it is not needed for public use — and sold to the neighbouring developer, Queen Kingston Holdings Inc., through the city's property disposal process. City Council approval is required; the closure would let the land merge with the redevelopment site at 1684-1702 Queen Street East, consistent with council's earlier direction and the site's holding provisions.

title: Use of Nathan Phillips Square for Various Events - May 1 - September 30, 2026
topics: [events in community and life], [events in culture], festivals and special events; community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals
brief: It's City Council's call whether to grant exemptions from the public-square rules so about 21 events — from Pride Toronto and the Toronto Outdoor Art Fair to VegTO, Panorama India, and the Caribbean Scholarship Foundation — can use Nathan Phillips Square between May 1 and September 30, 2026. Some events would operate a VQA beer and wine garden and serve alcohol, contingent on approval from the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario and the Medical Officer of Health and compliance with city conditions. The permitting is administered by Economic Development and Culture; the exemptions apply only to the listed events.

title: 1909 Yonge Street - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: community councils, heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties, planning; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The late-Victorian building at 1909 Yonge Street — a two-storey brick building with a gabled roof at Yonge and Davisville, once the heart of the historic village of Davisville — would be altered and folded into the approved high-rise project next door at 1913-1951 Yonge Street. City Council is asked to approve the alterations under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and to amend the existing heritage easement agreement to include the property. Heritage staff recommend approval with conditions; the change would let the 19th-century building sit within the larger development.

title: 377 Dundas Street West, 160 Huron Street and 1 Edmund Gate - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: community councils, heritage properties, planning; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Three properties — 377 Dundas Street West, 160 Huron Street, and 1 Edmund Gate — are proposed for listing on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register for their cultural heritage value. Listing recognizes the properties' history and is the first step toward possible future designation and protection. City Council is asked to approve all three listings.

title: 102 Glen Road - Demolition of a Structure within the South Rosedale Heritage Conservation District and Approval of a Replacement Structure
topics: community councils, demolitions, heritage conservation districts; heritage districts; historic areas
brief: An 'unrated' — non-contributing — building at 102 Glen Road in the South Rosedale Heritage Conservation District is proposed for demolition, with a three-storey detached house designed by FrankFranco Architects to take its place. City Council is asked to approve both the demolition and the replacement design under the Ontario Heritage Act; staff say the new house meets the district plan's guidelines and would not detract from nearby rated heritage buildings.

title: 402 and 440 Unwin Avenue - Official Plan Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments;
brief: The owner of the decommissioned Hearn generating station site at 402 and 440 Unwin Avenue wants to bring housing to the Port Lands — a concept with 19 residential towers and about 8,400 homes, plus 2,000 to 2,500 jobs — and has appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal after council missed its decision deadline. City Council is asked to direct the City Solicitor to oppose the application, which would introduce residential uses, remove portions of the natural heritage and open space system, and reconfigure the area's streets and transit network. The Port Lands sit under a 50-plus-year revitalization plan backed by $1.4 billion in tri-government investment starting in 2017 and another $975 million committed in 2025 for flood protection and enabling infrastructure.

title: 29-45 Berwick Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: The applicant for a 49-storey, 165-metre tower at 29-45 Berwick Avenue appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on December 15, 2025, after City Council failed to make a decision within the Planning Act's time frame. Council is now asked to direct the City Solicitor to oppose the application in its current form at the tribunal hearing while staff keep negotiating with the applicant to resolve outstanding issues. The proposal would redesignate the site from Neighbourhoods to Apartment Neighbourhoods, and a rental housing demolition application has also been submitted.

title: 1684, 1698, 1700 and 1702 Queen Street East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: A 10-storey mixed-use building with 168 rental homes is proposed for 1684 to 1702 Queen Street East, and City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments to allow it. The project includes ground-floor commercial space and one level of underground parking, with a future realignment of Penny Lane to connect the garage to Orchard Park Boulevard. Staff describe the proposal as appropriate intensification that fits the existing and planned character of the area.

title: 115 Saulter Street South - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Two towers of 51 and 47 storeys, joined at five- and six-storey bases, are proposed for 115 Saulter Street South in the McCleary District, and City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments. At least 6.5 percent of the homes would be affordable rentals, with ground-floor shops and about 4,643 square metres of production, interactive and creative workspace. The 74,734-square-metre proposal conforms to the Central Waterfront Secondary Plan and provincial planning policy, according to staff.

title: Zoning By-law Amendment for Garden Suites on Parkmount Road Facing Craven Road - Final Report
topics: zoning;
brief: The final report on backyard garden suites on Parkmount Road homes that back onto Craven Road, between Danforth Avenue and Hanson Street, recommends tailored zoning rules — including setbacks from Craven Road — so the small homes fit the area better. City Council ordered the review in October 2024 to allow a more thorough look, asking staff to weigh provincial planning changes, earlier consultation, and design integration. Garden suites have been permitted citywide since early 2022, and the city has received more than 900 building permit applications for them; the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to recommend that City Council adopt the zoning changes.

title: 435 Ellerslie Avenue - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number 26 107449 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee will hear the property owner's appeal of a property standards order issued January 26, 2026 for 435 Ellerslie Avenue (file 26 107449 PRS 00 IV). The committee can confirm, change, or cancel the order. The hearing gives the owner a chance to challenge the city's maintenance or repair requirements.

title: Council Member Appointments to Fill Vacancies on the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority Board of Directors
topics: appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Striking Committee is asked to consider members' preferences and recommend that City Council appoint three Council Members to fill vacancies on the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority Board of Directors. The terms run until November 14, 2026, and until successors are appointed. The appointments put councillors on the conservation authority's board.

title: Council Member Appointment to Fill a Vacancy on the Aboriginal Affairs Advisory Committee
topics: appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Striking Committee is asked to consider members' preferences and recommend that City Council appoint one Council Member to fill a vacancy on the Aboriginal Affairs Advisory Committee. The vacancy follows the resignation of Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, effective May 9, 2025. The term runs until November 14, 2026.

title: Council Member Appointments to the Canadian National Exhibition Association Municipal Section and Board of Directors
topics: appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Striking Committee is asked to consider members' preferences and recommend that City Council appoint five Council Members to the Canadian National Exhibition Association Municipal Section and Board of Directors. The term runs from the Annual Meeting in spring 2026 to the following Annual Meeting. The appointments put councillors on the CNE's governing bodies.

title: 2650 Lawrence Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment Application and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: applications, development, mixed use areas, official plan amendments, rezoning; application process, developing land; development (land); land development, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Scarborough Community Council and City Council are considering a staff report on the appealed application for two towers at 2650 Lawrence Avenue East. The proposal was revised in August 2025 from 25 and 35 storeys to 33 and 43 storeys, with more units and floor area and the public park removed. The buildings would share an eight-storey podium and a three-level underground garage. The report gives council's position in the appeal process.

title: Morningside Avenue - Corridor Review
topics: assessment, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: Councillor Neethan Shan is asking City Council to request a comprehensive review of traffic and transportation conditions along Morningside Avenue, working with the TTC. The request follows residents' concerns about congestion and unsafe intersections along the corridor. The review would identify possible improvements for commutes along Morningside.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council reviews the Order Paper, the list of business before it. No decision is involved beyond organizing the meeting's work.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions, and announcements are made at the council meeting. No decision is involved.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: council members may file petitions at the meeting. No decision is involved.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: council members declare any interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act before business begins. No policy decision is involved.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council formally introduces the committee reports coming forward to this meeting, including reports from the Executive Committee, Audit Committee, Board of Health, Civic Appointments Committee, and Striking Committee. The item sets the agenda for what council will consider. No decision is made at this step.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council confirms the minutes from its regular meeting of December 16 and 17, 2025 and special meetings of February 4 and February 10, 2026. No policy decision is involved.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council opens its meeting with O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is involved.

title: 2026 Toronto Heritage Grant Awards
topics: awards, subsidies and grants; financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs
brief: Seven heritage conservation grants totalling $110,000.00 are up for approval, expected to unlock about $668,696.28 in private spending on historic properties. The matching grants cover up to half of eligible restoration work: owners of house-form buildings can receive up to $10,000.00, or up to $20,000.00 every ten years for replacing an entire cedar or slate roof. The program's 2026 budget is $317,000.00, and City Council will decide whether to award the grants.

title: A Shared Vision to Create More Affordable and Supportive Homes and Sustain Community Networks in South Parkdale
topics: [activities in community and life], [organizations in health], affordable housing, redevelopment, supportive housing; affordable homes; housing projects, alternative housing; special needs housing; supported housing, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: University Health Network-owned lands in South Parkdale could be redeveloped into more affordable and supportive homes under a shared vision between the City, UHN, and United Way Greater Toronto. City Council is asked to adopt the vision and design principles, advancing a 2019 agreement aimed at linking housing, health, and social services for vulnerable residents. The decision sets the direction for what gets built on the hospital network's land.

title: Advancing Partnerships with the Community Housing Sector to Build More Affordable and Supportive Homes
topics: affordable housing, housing providers; affordable homes; housing projects, community housing corporations
brief: The City wants to deepen its partnerships with community housing providers to build more affordable and supportive homes. City Council is asked to authorize staff to advance the partnerships under the HousingTO 2020-2030 plan, building on more than 1,000 supportive homes built since 2020 and over 800 more now under construction. The report notes a $21.6 million federal investment through Build Canada Homes for 54 supportive homes in South Parkdale with the City and University Health Network, plus $2.6 million a year in provincial operating funding. It says more federal capital funding is needed beyond the initial $1 billion announced through Build Canada Homes, flags an outstanding provincial operating-funding request of about $16 million in 2026 growing to $23 million in 2027 for more than 700 supportive homes under construction, and recommends up to $8,100,000 in city capital funding for 54 supportive homes on University Health Network-leased land (Dunn House 2).

title: North York at the Centre: Directions Report for an Updated Secondary Plan
topics: Secondary Plans;
brief: North York's downtown planning rulebook, in place since 1997, is headed for an update. City Council is asked to endorse the 'North York at the Centre' directions report, shaped by two rounds of community engagement, as the basis for rewriting the North York Centre Secondary Plan. The update will set the framework for future development and public investment in the area.

title: 1-97 Dorney Court, 2-8 Flemington Road and 21-39 Varna Drive - Toronto Builds - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, redevelopment, social housing; community housing; housing allowance; housing projects; low income housing; non profit housing; non-profit housing; public housing; rent geared to income assistance; rent geared to income housing; rent subsidies; rent supplement; subsidized housing; subsidized rent; subsidized units, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Demolishing 121 social housing units -- townhouses at 1-97 Dorney Court, four two-storey rental apartment buildings at 2-8 Flemington Road, and ten detached homes at 21-39 Varna Drive -- as part of the Lawrence Heights revitalization goes to City Council for approval. Toronto Community Housing would replace 175 social housing units in phases two and three of the Toronto Builds project, with a tenant relocation and assistance plan. If the conditions are not met within the specified time, the City Clerk can add a charge of $20,000.00 per dwelling unit to the tax roll, like property taxes, as a lien on the land.

title: Lawrence Heights Revitalization (Phase 2) - Toronto Builds - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment  Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, redevelopment, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Phase two of the Lawrence Heights revitalization would bring eight mixed-use buildings of 6 to 28 storeys, a four-storey community recreation centre, and new parkland to Toronto Community Housing lands. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan, including the Lawrence Allen Secondary Plan, and zoning amendments to enable the TCHC-led redevelopment. The project continues a revitalization TCHC has advanced for more than two decades.

title: 1-154 Swansea Mews (21 Windermere Avenue) - Toronto Builds - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, redevelopment, rental housing; rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization, rental properties; rental units
brief: Demolishing 154 social housing units at 1-154 Swansea Mews (21 Windermere Avenue) so they can be replaced within the new Toronto Builds development on the site goes to City Council for approval. A tenant relocation plan gives existing tenants the right to return to replacement social housing units at similar rents, with moving services and assistance. If the conditions are not met within the specified time, the City Clerk can add a charge of $20,000.00 per dwelling unit to the tax roll, like property taxes, as a lien on the land.

title: 21 Windermere Avenue (1-154 Swansea Mews) - Toronto Builds - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: mixed use areas, official plan amendments, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Two mixed-use towers of 35 and 20 storeys with 649 homes are proposed for 21 Windermere Avenue (1-154 Swansea Mews) under the Toronto Builds program. The plan includes 154 rent-geared-to-income replacement rentals, ground-floor retail and community uses, publicly accessible spaces, and shared pick-up and drop-off areas. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes.

title: 150 College Street (University College - 15 King's College Circle) - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: University College at 15 King's College Circle, addressed as 150 College Street, is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The designation would protect one of the defining historic buildings of the University of Toronto's St. George campus.

title: 401 King Street West - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The property at 401 King Street West, including entrance addresses 407 and 409 King Street West, is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The property sits on the south side of King Street West between Spadina Avenue and Blue Jays Way in the Wellington Place neighbourhood.

title: 53 Strachan Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The City-owned property at 53 Strachan Avenue, at the southeast corner of Wellington Street West and Strachan Avenue on the southern edge of West Queen West, is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The city has owned the property since 1858.

title: 40 Wabash Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: A property at 40 Wabash Avenue, including entrance address 50 Wabash Avenue, is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The property sits on the north side of Wabash Avenue between Sorauren and MacDonell avenues, west of the rail corridor.

title: 150 Queens Wharf Road - Toronto Builds - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: housing, mixed use areas, rezoning; homes; residences, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Toronto Community Housing wants to build bigger at 150 Queens Wharf Road: a 37-storey mixed-use tower with 268 rental homes, up to 80 of them affordable, replacing a 2021 approval for a 29-storey building with 282 rentals.
