The plan also adds a new EarlyON Centre with outdoor space and a pedestrian link through the site to the future Lower Garrison Creek Park. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change under the Toronto Builds program.

title: Inn on The Park Drive - Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2560 with IOTP Development Inc.
topics: assumption of services, development, highways; developing land; development (land); land development, freeways; motorways; parkways
brief: Staff recommend City Council assume the municipal services installed by IOTP Development Inc. under a February 6, 2020 subdivision agreement for Plan of Subdivision 66M-2560 on Inn on The Park Drive, and release the performance guarantee held for those services. Assumption means the City takes over maintenance of the infrastructure.

title: 22-36 Greenbriar Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: building plans, demolitions, development, rental housing, zoning; building records, developing land; development (land); land development, rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a 32-storey (105 metres plus 7.5-metre mechanical penthouse) residential building at 22-36 Greenbriar Road with 517 units and a two-level underground garage with 142 parking spaces including 25 visitor spaces; the applicant says the tenure will be rental. A related rental-housing demolition application was previously considered. The approval would add more than 500 rental homes.

title: 7 and 11 Rochefort Drive - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, demolitions, rental housing; application process, rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve demolishing two 4-storey apartment buildings with 128 rental units at 7 and 11 Rochefort Drive, with the units replaced in the new development on the site. A Tenant Assistance Plan gives existing tenants the right to return to replacement rental units at similar rents plus financial compensation — the report cites $20,000.00. A related zoning application for the new development is also before council. The decision affects 128 renter households.

title: 250 Ferrand Drive - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: land use, zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve retrofitting the existing 15-storey office building at 250 Ferrand Drive into a rental apartment development with 331 loft-style units — mostly two- and three-bedroom family-sized units — plus about 112 square metres of ground-floor space for a neighbourhood cafe. Staff say the proposal is consistent with the Provincial Planning Statement and conforms to the Official Plan. The conversion would add hundreds of rental homes, including family-sized ones.

title: 120 Dallimore Circle - Addressing Changes to Parking Provisions, Community Bus Stop
topics: bus stops, on-street parking, stopping prohibitions; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, no stopping
brief: Residents near 120 Dallimore Circle say a new community bus stop removed about three on-street parking spaces and imposes no stopping at all times, even though the community bus only runs Monday to Friday. A member motion proposes North York Community Council limit the no-stopping rule to weekdays so visitors can park up to three hours on weekends. The change would free weekend parking near the stop while keeping it clear when the bus runs.

title: 1, 3, 5 and 7 Saguenay Avenue, and 59R Otter Crescent - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: building plans, planning & development (sc), residential properties, zoning, zoning bylaws; building records, residential real estate, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning change for 1, 3, 5 and 7 Saguenay Avenue and 59R Otter Crescent to allow additions to the existing dwelling and a second detached dwelling on a future subdivided lot. The proposal would add one new single-family detached home and is described as consistent with the Provincial Planning Statement and the City's Official Plan.

title: 11 Greenbriar Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development review process, urban planning, zoning bylaws; city planning; community planning; regional planning, development control; development reviews, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning change to allow a three-storey residential building at 11 Greenbriar Road, with one level of underground parking accessed from Dervock Crescent — 24 vehicle spaces including 3 visitor spaces, plus 22 bicycle parking spaces. The Director of Community Planning for North York District recommends amending Zoning By-law 569-2013 to permit it. The decision would add new homes on the street.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to the Huron Street Garden - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: funding; financing
brief: In 2015, $50,000 in Ward 11 Section 37 funds was earmarked for the Huron Street Garden at 180 Huron Street, now Lillian H. Smith Park. Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion asks council to create a new $57,263 capital project for long-planned improvements: a shed for the community garden, a picnic table and three benches on concrete pads, a sign or plaque, and three raised garden planters. The money comes from Ward 11 Section 37 community benefits with no debt.

title: Standing in Solidarity with Iranian-Canadians - Declaring Persian Heritage Month at the City of Toronto - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: community & life (sc), culture (sc);
brief: The item asks council to declare March as Persian Heritage Month in Toronto, matching the Province of Ontario's recognition. The motion cites a recent demonstration of more than 350,000 people in Willowdale in solidarity with the people of Iran, and describes heightened anxiety and grief among Toronto's Iranian diaspora amid violence, unrest and internet shutdowns affecting loved ones. The declaration would celebrate Iranian-Canadians' history, culture and contributions and acknowledge the community's resilience.

title: Review of Applicability of Type G Loading to Address Specialized Housing Types - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: housing, solid waste management; homes; residences, solid waste management planning; swm; waste management
brief: The item asks council to make sure specialized housing is included in the city's review of Type G loading requirements for mid-rise buildings. Type G loading forces buildings to fully internalize truck maneuvering, waste collection and bin swinging, driving up ground-floor ceiling heights and eating floor area; the Planning and Housing Committee's October 2025 review covers the 31-unit trigger, smaller trucks, turntables and on-street collection, with a report due in the second quarter of 2026. Specialized housing combines bed-sitting rooms with conventional units for seniors, people with disabilities and others needing supports, and the motion says the review should explicitly capture these projects.

title: Authority to Enter into Agreements to Facilitate the Implementation of FIFA World Cup 2026 Legacy Initiatives - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: economic development, soccer; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing
brief: This is a procedural item: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to authorize the Executive Director of the FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto Secretariat to negotiate and enter into agreements to deliver the tournament's approved and budgeted legacy initiatives without delay. The legacy suite was outlined through council and Executive Committee decisions in November 2025 and March 2026, with details in a confidential attachment. The motion is described as urgent so implementation agreements can be signed immediately.

title: Authority to Provide a Neighbour Authorization Form to the Owners of 53 Lake Shore Drive for Shoreline Retaining Wall Construction - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: natural environment; environment; natural heritage systems
brief: The owners of 53 Lake Shore Drive want to replace their aging shoreline revetment with a new retaining wall, at their own cost, to satisfy Toronto and Region Conservation Authority concerns tied to planned home renovations. Because part of the wall sits on public Crown land, the permitting process requires a Neighbour Authorization Form from adjacent landowners, including the City of Toronto. Councillor Amber Morley's motion asks council to delegate authority to Transportation Services, which manages the adjacent city land as part of Fourth Street, to complete the form. Fisheries officials have set a late-summer deadline for the work.

title: Implementing the Cultural Districts Program - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: culture (sc);
brief: Council has directed staff to build a Cultural Districts Program since 2020, starting with the Church-Wellesley Village, then Little Jamaica along Eglinton West, with a full program design due in the third quarter of 2022, a deadline that has passed. Councillor Chris Moise's motion notes extensive community consultations were completed and program design was advanced enough for the December 2025 council cycle, yet no report came forward. The motion asks council to move the program to implementation, which would give formal recognition and support tools to the city's cultural districts.

title: Building a Made-in-Toronto Community Safety Plan Protecting Residents at Bathurst Street and Sheppard Avenue and Across Toronto - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson
topics: community safety, safety; public safety
brief: The item asks council to develop a made-in-Toronto community safety plan, citing weekly demonstrations at Bathurst Street and Sheppard Avenue since September 2024 near a predominantly Jewish neighbourhood. The motion describes noise amplification and harassment directed at residents and a vigil on the west side of Bathurst, cites victim impact statements signed by local residents, and points to Toronto Police figures of 443 reported hate crime occurrences in 2024, up 19 percent from 2023 and 80 percent from 2022. It asks council to act on public safety for residents across the city.

title: Accelerating Sod Repairs Resulting from Snow Clearing - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
topics: snow;
brief: The item asks council to speed up repairs to sod torn up by sidewalk snowplows, arguing the current 311 service standard of up to 12 months is far too long for work that can be done in weeks after winter. The motion asks council to direct Transportation Services to create a dedicated 311 service-request code for snowplow sod damage so the repairs can be tracked and finished faster, with the goal of completing last winter's repairs by June 30. The push follows the 2025-26 winter season.

title: 221 Donlea Drive - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: appeals;
brief: This is a procedural item: Authorizing the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body and oppose the owner's appeal of a Committee of Adjustment refusal at 221 Donlea Drive would get Council's approval. The owner had sought variances to build a three-storey fourplex with a rear-yard garden suite, narrowing ten requested variances to six after talks with planning staff; the North York panel refused the modified application on March 5, 2026, and the owner appealed March 16. The motion also lets the solicitor bring appropriate city staff.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Toronto Public Library - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: library branches, public libraries; branches
brief: Back in 2005, $103,251.33 in Section 37 funds from the 35 Balmuto Street and 764 Yonge Street developments was set aside for public art, and after 20 years of interest the pot has grown to $110,605.48. Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion asks council to finally put it to work, adding it to the Toronto Public Library's capital budget for public art at the Toronto Reference Library tied to its forthcoming Centre for Democracy. The money would cover fabrication and installation in 2027.

title: 180 Queen's Drive - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: This is a procedural item: Confirming direction for the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body as a party to oppose the owner's appeal of the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of a lot severance at 180 Queen's Drive is up for a decision by Council. The committee refused the consent and variance applications in August 2025 for a proposal to sever the lot and build a fourplex; the owner appealed in September 2025. A separate October 2025 council item already directed the solicitor to oppose the variance appeal, and this motion extends that to the consent appeal, with authority to retain consultants and negotiate a settlement.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.TE24.12 - 21 to 25 Imperial Street - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: This is a procedural item: Council votes on amending the zoning approval for a 19-storey mixed-use building at 21 to 25 Imperial Street with a set of technical refinements. The changes would allow 1.5-metre-deep balconies on the north and south elevations, cap canopy and related encroachments at 1.5 metres, allow rooftop trellises and pergolas up to 2.5 metres, and add a density string to the zone label. Development Review staff confirm they are satisfied with the updated wind study and the draft amendment.

title: Amending Item 2023.TE6.18 - 1404-1428 Yonge Street - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: demolitions;
brief: This is a procedural item: Council decides whether to amend the 2023 rental-housing demolition approval for 1404-1428 Yonge Street so the owner can demolish the eight vacant rental units at 1404 and 1408 Yonge Street before site plan and excavation permits are issued. The tenants have moved out with tenant assistance, and the owner cites break-ins and safety risks at the empty property. City Planning staff support the change, which would speed construction and the tenants' return to replacement units.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.IE25.6 - Redesign Study of Intersection of Eglinton Avenue West and the Allen Road Expressway - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: expressways; municipal highways
brief: This is a procedural item: The item asks council to re-open its 2025 traffic changes for Cedarvale and Forest Hill and remove two provisions that are not working as intended. The left-turn restriction at Strathearn and Bathurst and the westbound through-prohibition at Burton and Bathurst, meant to keep commuters on arterial roads around the Eglinton West and Allen Road intersection, have pushed traffic onto neighbouring residential streets, some without sidewalks. The motion cites safety concerns on those streets as the reason for urgency.

title: Supporting Interim Uses on Vacant Development Sites - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: employment opportunities; careers; employment; job applications; job boards; job openings; job opportunities; job postings; job vacancies; jobs; vacancies (jobs)
brief: With approved development sites sitting vacant for years as the condo market stalls, the item asks council to address a tax penalty that discourages interim uses like public courts, markets and pop-up programming. When a site is activated, the Municipal Property Assessment Corporation can reclassify it from residential or industrial to commercial, triggering a much higher tax rate; the motion cites public racket courts at Yonge and Rosehill in Toronto-St. Paul's, now at risk after such a reclassification. The motion asks the city to find a way to keep interim community uses viable.

title: Two Loons Brewing By-the-Glass Permit Application to the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Two Loons Brewing at 122 Brock Avenue needs a council resolution to obtain a Manufacturer's Limited Liquor Sales Licence for by-the-glass sales from the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario. Councillor Alejandra Bravo's motion asks council to advise the AGCO of its support for the application. The motion is described as urgent so the application can proceed without further delay.

title: School Safety Enhancements through "SCHOOL" Pavement Markings - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: school zone review;
brief: The item asks council to let Transportation Services paint large SCHOOL stencils across all lanes of multi-lane roads in School Safety Zones, not just a single lane as traditionally done. The approach was piloted on Kingston Road east of Midland Avenue, where the councillor says visibility for drivers improved markedly and the community responded well. The motion frames it as a low-cost, high-impact safety measure for students and families near schools, and is described as urgent while staff are working on the file.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.MM30.8 - Accepting a Donation from Tennis Canada to Enhance the Tennis Courts at Malvern Park - by Councillor Neethan Shan, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: recreation policies, recreational facilities; recreation facilities; recreational amenities
brief: This is a procedural item: Council re-opens its 2025 approval for the Malvern Park tennis court refurbishment because the $100,000 from Tennis Canada was miscategorized. The money comes through the National Bank Play Your Court Program and is conditional on branded signage on the nets and court entrance, a grand opening event, and up to two days a year of free court access for programming, so it is a grant, not a donation. The financial contribution remains $100,000, and the motion updates the agreement parties to reflect the program's actual funders and administrators.

title: Investing in Community Capacity and Essential Supports in York South-Weston - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: funding, senior programs; financing, older adult programs; seniors classes
brief: The item asks council to direct $75,000 in 2026 operating budget funding to three York South-Weston community organizations: $0.020 million to Weston Area Emergency Support for food relief focused on the Weston-Mount Dennis community, $0.025 million to the St. Fidelis Golden Age Club for seniors' programs, and $0.030 million to the Canadian Somali Association for youth and seniors programming. The investments are framed as stabilizing neighbourhood-level services in an area facing social and economic pressures.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds for Toronto Community Housing Corporation for the St. James Town Open Space Project - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: funding, housing; financing, homes; residences
brief: The St. James Town Open Space and Public Realm project, which council funded in 2023 at up to $4.722 million ($4.615 million in Section 37 funds plus $107,000 from Transportation Services' capital budget), came back from tender over budget even after the lowest bidder trimmed its bid. Councillor Chris Moise's motion asks council to approve about $2.6 million in additional funding to Toronto Community Housing Corporation to cover the gap between the approved amount and the lowest bid, rather than cancelling the procurement and risking further cost escalation and delay. The project's costs are shared between the city and Toronto Community Housing.

title: Short Term Parking at the Price Street Green P Lot - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: parking;
brief: The 71-spot Green P lot on Price Street, relied on by local restaurant and business customers, is being filled all day by construction workers' personal vehicles from nearby sites, and more construction is on the way. Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion asks council to request that the Toronto Parking Authority board convert at least 20 of the lot's spots to non-renewable short-term parking of three hours maximum, freeing customer turnover. Workers' vehicles can use other Green P lots a few blocks north.

title: Authority to Release Section 42 Funds for Waterfront Parks - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: funding, waterfronts; financing, lakefronts; waterfront trail
brief: The item asks council to release $160,000.00 in Section 42 parkland funds for more waste receptacle enclosures at two waterfront parks: Biidaasige Park, opened last summer with a second phase opening this summer, and Leslie Lookout, one of five Claude Cormier-designed waterfront parks. Parks and Recreation previously bought enclosures for the large blue and grey toters, but there were not enough to cover Biidaasige Park evenly. The motion follows the city's Port Lands open house and is described as urgent.

title: Authority to Accept a Donation and Enter into an Agreement for Baseball Diamond Improvements at Martingrove Gardens Park - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: baseball diamonds, donation; ball diamonds; baseball fields; hardball diamonds, bequest; toy drive
brief: Martingrove Baseball Inc., an all-volunteer community baseball organization active since 1958, has offered an in-kind donation valued at up to $125,000.00 to improve the Jim Horton diamond at Martingrove Gardens Park, moving and angling the infield away from the trees and upgrading fencing, on top of city-funded bench, bleacher and backstop work. Councillor Stephen Holyday's motion asks council to accept the donation and enter the necessary agreement, since the city's donation policy requires council approval for gifts over $50,000.00. The work is timed to finish before the season.

title: Appointment of Chair of the TO Live Board of Directors - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: public appointments;
brief: The item asks council to appoint Brian Astl as Chair of the TO Live Board of Directors, filling the seat vacant since Lori DeGraw's resignation in November 2025. TO Live, the city agency running Meridian Hall, the St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts and Meridian Arts Centre, presents more than 1,000 performances a year for over 500,000 attendees, with a board overseeing an annual operating budget of more than $45 million and 250-plus staff. The chair is drawn from the board's public members.

title: Amending Item 2022.TE34.11 - 40 Raglan Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Final Report - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: demolitions;
brief: This is a procedural item: Amending its 2022 zoning approval for 40 Raglan Avenue to fix a technical error in the required mid-block connection calculation would get Council's approval. The motion also addresses the approved 174-square-metre on-site parkland dedication, after the owner flagged that recent legislative changes to development-charge payment timing affect the earlier plan to split base and above-base park improvements with the neighbouring 32 Raglan Avenue development. Staff say the public record contained enough information to understand the proposal.

title: 55 to 75 Brownlow Avenue - Construction Staging, by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: The owner of 55-75 Brownlow Avenue, approved in 2024 for two residential towers of 59 and 55 storeys with 1,374 units, is conveying the full 571-square-metre on-site parkland dedication early, before the first above-grade permit for phase one. Councillor Josh Matlow's motion asks council to let the owner use that conveyed parkland for construction staging and material stockpiling at nominal cost for the duration of construction. The motion is described as urgent because the project is already under construction.

title: Proclaiming April 11 to 17, 2026, as Black Maternal Health Week in the City of Toronto - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson
topics: races; marathons; runs; walkathons
brief: The item asks council to proclaim April 11 to 17, 2026 as Black Maternal Health Week in Toronto. The motion cites research showing Black pregnant people experience higher rates of preterm birth, preeclampsia and other poor outcomes than white individuals, pointing to a McGill study finding 8.9 percent of Black women gave birth preterm between 2004 and 2006 versus 5.9 percent of white women, and a 2023 study of Black women in Toronto reporting feeling dismissed by health-care providers. The proclamation builds on the Black Maternal Health Collective Canada's inaugural year.

title: Naming of New Park at 2788 Bathurst Street in Honour of Dr. Joseph Leventhal - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: naming;
brief: The item asks council to name the new park at 2788 Bathurst Street in honour of Dr. Joseph Leventhal, a centenarian described as a family physician, World War II bomber navigator, and award-winning artist who studied under Group of Seven member Arthur Lismer. Born near the Ward and Kensington Market and raised in the Eglinton-Lawrence area, Leventhal served in the Royal Canadian Air Force and later practised medicine in Toronto. The motion commemorates his community and military service.

title: Building a Made in Toronto Community Safety Plan Protecting Residents at Bathurst Street and Sheppard Avenue and across Toronto - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson
topics: [activities in public safety and protection], protests; demonstrations; protest marches
brief: The item asks council to develop a made-in-Toronto community safety plan, citing weekly demonstrations at Bathurst Street and Sheppard Avenue since September 2024 near a predominantly Jewish neighbourhood. The motion describes noise amplification, harassment of residents and a vigil on the west side of Bathurst, cites victim impact statements signed by local residents, and points to Toronto Police figures of 443 reported hate crime occurrences in 2024, up 19 percent from 2023 and 80 percent from 2022. The motion asks council to act on public safety and community confidence.

title: Exploring Public Realm Improvements in Chinatown - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: arts and culture, community & life (sc);
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to direct Economic Development and Culture staff to explore public-realm improvements to the Chinatown Centre mall plaza at 222 Spadina, in consultation with Transportation Services, community stakeholders and the local councillor. The options under study include a historical statue, building frontage work, more seating, litter receptacles, public artwork and plantings. The motion frames the work under the Chinatown Planning Framework's vision of Chinatown as a meeting place and home for Chinese-Canadian identity.

title: No ICE in Toronto - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: immigrants; immigration status; newcomers
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow is asking council to state its opposition to any presence of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Toronto. The motion states that ICE's actions in the United States, including in Minnesota, have created fear, and that any ICE presence in Toronto would undermine residents' and visitors' sense of safety, particularly as the city prepares to welcome FIFA World Cup visitors this summer. The motion asks council to make a clear statement that it will defend constitutional rights with the position: No ICE in Toronto.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Benches and Wayfinding at Toronto Transit Commission Stations - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: The Toronto Transit Commission has asked for $100,000 in Section 37 funds from Ward 11 developments to add 31 three-seat benches across the eight Line 2 subway stations from Castle Frank to Christie, plus better wayfinding at Yonge-Bloor, St. George and Spadina stations. Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion asks council to add the money to the TTC's 2026 operating budget for riders, including children and seniors, who find standing difficult. Deputations to the TTC have stressed wayfinding as key to the rider experience.

title: Toronto Must Have a Say in Waterfront Decisions - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: government (sc), waterfronts; lakefronts; waterfront trail
brief: With other orders of government commenting on the future of Toronto's waterfront without sharing details, Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to make it the city's official position that Ottawa and Queen's Park must include Toronto residents and their elected municipal government in all major waterfront decisions. The motion also has council oppose any unilateral expropriation of city land by the federal or provincial governments. The motion says no proposal or details have been received from the other governments.

title: Amending Item 2023.TE4.12 - 49 Ontario Street and 72-94 Berkeley Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval And Request to Accept Additional In-Kind Community Benefits - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: This is a procedural item: Amending its 2023 zoning approval for 49 Ontario Street and 72-94 Berkeley Street, a three-building project of 11, 39 and 44 storeys with 1,094 homes is up for a decision by Council. The owner has committed the units as secured rental housing, including about 246 affordable units through the city's Rental Housing Supply Program, and the amendment adjusts the parkland deal: 74 of the previously secured 581 square metres along Berkeley Street becomes an in-kind community benefit, keeping 507 square metres as statutory parkland. The owner has also offered to convert the approved low-rise building into more parkland, a 689.4-square-metre expansion, plus convey 154 square metres of additional parkland.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Commemorate the Bathhouse Raids - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: heritage designation, plaques; heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques
brief: The item asks council to release $10,000.00 in Section 37 developer funds to commemorate the 1981 Bathhouse Raids, when 200 police officers raided four Toronto bathhouses and arrested 309 people in what was then the city's largest mass arrest. The raids became a turning point in Canada's 2SLGBTQ+ civil rights movement, sparking protests including a 3,000-person march on 52 Division and Queen's Park the next day. The commemoration would mark a moment the motion says damaged relations between police and the queer community for decades.

title: Respecting, Reflecting and Representing Little Jamaica and Business Improvement Areas in New Eglinton Light Rail Transit Stations - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: arts and culture, business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations
brief: The item asks council to call on Metrolinx to create a Cultural Placemaking and Public Art Plan for Eglinton Crosstown stations that protects and promotes the heritage of Little Jamaica and other historically significant neighbourhoods along the Eglinton West corridor. The motion cites 15 years of construction impacts on corridor businesses and says Metrolinx has not meaningfully involved communities or reflected Little Jamaica's heritage in station design. It also seeks a Little Jamaica advisory committee to co-design the themes and asks Metrolinx to explore free digital ad space for local businesses. The source figures list a $200,000 amount in connection with this motion.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds towards a Fire Fighters Burn Victim Care Centre at 641 Eglinton Avenue West - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos-Lin
topics: firefighters, patient care, victims; fire fighters, interventions
brief: The item asks council to release $2 million in Section 37 developer funds to rehabilitate the city-owned former Fire Station 135 at 641 Eglinton Avenue West into a Burn Victim Care Centre. Toronto Fire Fighters Charities, the charitable arm of the firefighters' union, plans to run a Home Away Program there offering accommodation for burn and trauma survivors and their families being treated at Sunnybrook or SickKids. The official breakdown lists $1,651,027.12 from one development and $348,972.88 from another, fully funding the $2 million with no debt.

title: Commemorative Naming Process for Future Toronto Ferries - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: ferry boat schedules, transportation (sc);
brief: This is a procedural item: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to direct the General Manager of Fleet Services to report back by the fourth quarter of 2027 on a commemorative naming process for future city ferries. Two new electric ferries entering service in 2027 are being named through a separate public vote on non-commemorative names, with a decision expected in May 2026. The motion asks for a future process for honouring names, consistent with the city's property naming policy.

title: Protecting Chinatown as a Cultural District - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: community & life (sc), culture (sc);
brief: The item asks council to take steps to protect Chinatown, centred on Dundas Street between McCaul and Spadina and Spadina Avenue between College and Queen, as a cultural district. The motion traces the neighbourhood from the displacement of the first Chinatown for the current City Hall through waves of Southeast Asian immigration, and says legacy businesses and societies are closing as owners age, rents rise and developers buy land. Community groups have been pushing for protections for the area's character and institutions.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.MM28.1 - Creation of New Park at 819 Yonge Street - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: First Nations, parks; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: This is a procedural item: Council votes on re-opening its March 2025 approval for a new Indigenous-themed park at 819 Yonge Street so it can add city-owned lands at 876 Church Street to the construction agreement. Staff discovered part of the assumed park lands are actually city-owned parcels under Corporate Real Estate Management, now being transferred to Parks and Recreation. The motion lets those lands be included in the Construction Management Agreement with Greybrook, the owner of 148 Yorkville Avenue, before detailed design begins.

title: Fighting for Ontario Place and Ontario’s Democracy - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: courts, government (sc);
brief: The item asks council to have the city seek a role in the Supreme Court case over the Rebuilding Ontario Place Act, the provincial law governing Ontario Place's redevelopment. The motion's stated concerns include the law's limits on legal remedies against government decisions and its exemption of the project from environmental assessment requirements. The motion describes this as the last opportunity to challenge the legislation in court and asks that Torontonians be represented in the case.

title: Safer Subways: Making Public Safety a Priority and Restoring Confidence to Toronto Transit Commission Riders Across Toronto - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: The item asks council to back a package of subway safety measures, citing ridership at about 80 percent of 2019 levels and surveys finding four in 10 Torontonians do not feel safe on transit. The motion proposes a plan with Toronto Police to deploy officers in all subway stations, a commitment to start installing platform edge doors at priority stations, improved cleanliness and lighting standards with public compliance reporting, safety design audits of all stations, and zero tolerance for harassment of TTC drivers and staff. It frames the goal as restoring rider and worker confidence across the system.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Heliconian Club - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: funding; financing
brief: The item asks council to release $30,000 in Section 37 developer funds for the Heliconian Club's Heliconian Hall at 35 Hazelton Avenue in Yorkville. The hall, built in 1876 and home to the women's arts club since 1923, is a rare Carpenter's Gothic building and a National Historic Site whose carved wood details need repair after 150 years. The club, founded in 1909 for women working in the arts, still uses the hall as a concert venue and art gallery.

title: Closing Roads for Watermain Work Requires Proper Notice - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: road closures, watermains; mains; water mains, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: After a contractor closed Dupont Street between Edwin Avenue and Franklin Avenue from February 24 to 27, 2026 for water and sewer work with no advance notice to the councillor's office, local businesses or the TTC, the item asks council to require proper notice for road-closing watermain work. The closure stranded the 26 Dupont bus on alternate routing and cost nearby businesses revenue. The motion points to the cut permit's own conditions requiring 48 hours' notice to affected residents and businesses.

title: Options for Section 37 Agreement Contributions at Bloor and Dufferin - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, subway stations; ttc
brief: The Section 37 agreement for 1141 Bloor Street West, 980 Dufferin Street and 90 Croatia Street originally required the developer to build a below-grade pedestrian tunnel to Dufferin Station, but construction costs have risen sharply since. Councillor Alejandra Bravo's motion asks council to direct staff to report back with an option to take a cash contribution instead of the tunnel, with a minimum indexed amount set in a zoning amendment, so the city can redirect the value to other community priorities. No dollar figure is specified yet.

title: Maintaining Toronto’s Climate and Energy Priorities Through the Review Process for Artificial Intelligence Data Centre Proposals - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: digital libraries, science & technology (sc); online libraries
brief: As artificial intelligence data centres are proposed in Toronto, the item asks council to make sure the city's climate and energy priorities hold through the review process. The motion notes data centres can strain power grids and raise electricity costs, use large amounts of water and cooling chemicals, and increase climate pollution, while also acknowledging reasons to keep Canadian data in Canada. It asks staff to report on how Toronto will assess these proposals against affordability, environmental and climate goals and the city's infrastructure capacity.

title: Re-opening and Amending 2025.CC35.19 - 0, 119-125, 160 and 200 Benny Stark Street and 116-122 Turnberry Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: This is a procedural item: Council decides whether to fix a drafting error in its December 2025 directions for a child care facility at 0, 119-125, 160 and 200 Benny Stark Street and 116-122 Turnberry Avenue. The instructions mistakenly named the Executive Director of Social Development, Finance and Administration where they meant the General Manager of Children's Services, for an owner-built, minimum 929-square-metre child care facility with a 279-square-metre outdoor area to be conveyed to the city. The motion re-opens the item solely to correct that reference.

title: Addressing Recycling in Public Spaces - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: environment (sc), recyclables, recycling;
brief: About 15,000 recycling receptacles sit in Toronto's public spaces, but since the province took over the Blue Box system, what goes into them is collected as garbage and landfilled rather than recycled, and contamination rates were already high. Councillor Lily Cheng's motion asks council to direct the General Manager of Solid Waste Management Services to explore cost-effective options: either restore targeted recycling in public places or remove the receptacles. The motion says the current setup misleads residents who believe they are diverting waste, and sends genuinely recyclable material like aluminum cans and PET bottles to landfill.

title: 2 to 20 Glazebrook Avenue and 391 Broadway Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: appeals, high rise buildings; tall buildings
brief: This is a procedural item: Council decides whether to have the City Solicitor attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body regarding the Committee of Adjustment's approval of bigger variances for 2-20 Glazebrook Avenue and 391 Broadway Avenue. The committee approved adding four storeys to an already-approved 33-storey mixed-use building, bringing it to 37 storeys, with the tower plate growing from 769 to 825 square metres, gross floor area from 29,500 to 31,967 square metres, and units from 428 to 489. The source text is truncated on the exact direction to the solicitor.

title: Raising of the Lion and Sun Flag in Solidarity with Iranian-Canadians - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
topics: flag raising, flags;
brief: The item asks council to raise the historic Lion and Sun flag in solidarity with Iranian-Canadians, following resident requests and similar raisings in Aurora, Barrie, Richmond Hill and Vaughan. The motion describes the flag as a symbol of Iran's cultural heritage that many Iranian-Canadians use to express hopes for freedom, human rights and dignity, and says residents do not feel represented by the current government in Iran. The request responds to peaceful demonstrations in Toronto in support of the people of Iran.

title: Evaluating Changes to Mute Swan Management in Etobicoke-Lakeshore - by Councillor Amber Morley, Seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: ecology;
brief: The item asks council to evaluate changes to the mute swan management program that the city contracts the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority to run in Etobicoke-Lakeshore. The program currently coats mute swan eggs with oil so they do not hatch, a population-control measure premised on concerns about competition with other waterbirds and overgrazing. The motion cites research questioning that rationale and notes the Humber Bay-to-Hamilton Harbour population has fallen 81 percent since 2011, from 413 to 80 birds. The motion adds that many residents value the swans along the waterfront.

title: 35 Elder Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: appeals, committees of adjustment; committee of adjustment
brief: This is a procedural item: Council authorizes the City Solicitor to appear before the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose the owner's appeal of a Committee of Adjustment refusal at 35 Elder Avenue. The owner had sought to sever the property into two lots and build a new dwelling plus a garden suite on each, and the Etobicoke York panel refused the applications in November 2025; revised plans filed in February 2026 dropped the garden suites. The motion notes the matter is time-sensitive, with a hearing scheduled and the city holding party status.

title: Site-specific By-law to Enable a Property Tax Exemption for Thunder Woman Healing Lodge Society at 28 Algoma Street - by Councilor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: This is a procedural item: Passing a site-specific by-law so the property tax exemption it already approved for the Thunder Woman Healing Lodge Society's affordable housing at 28 Algoma Street can take effect would get Council's approval. The Indigenous-led housing provider serves First Nation, Inuit and Metis 2SLGBTQIA+ women leaving correctional institutions and survivors of intergenerational trauma, and tenants are set to move in March 30, 2026. The by-law designates four rental units as affordable housing, which supports the project's financial viability.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to St. Clare's Multifaith Housing Society for Upgrades to Affordable Housing - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: The item asks council to release $555,000 in Section 37 developer funds for capital upgrades at three aging affordable-housing properties run by St. Clare's Multifaith Housing Society in Ward 11: 25 Leonard Avenue, 138 Pears Avenue and the city-owned 877 Yonge Street. The work includes energy efficiency equipment and secure e-bike storage at 25 Leonard, an accessibility lift and kitchen upgrade at 138 Pears, and energy-efficient glazing, doors, locks and balcony amenity upgrades at 877 Yonge. The official breakdown lists $9,800 from the 86-100 Bloor Street West development, $110,000 from the Sultan Street, St. Thomas Street and Charles Street West developments, and $435,200 from the Church Street and Collier Street developments.

title: Authority to Waive Permit Fees for Toronto District School Board and Toronto Catholic District School Board for Use of David Crombie Park - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: catholic schools, public schools;
brief: With Block 2 of David Crombie Park under construction from March 10 to about December 20, 2026, two schools that use its playground for recess, St. Michael Catholic School and Downtown Alternative School, are being temporarily relocated to Block 3 under a Parks and Recreation permit. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking council to waive the permit fees the Toronto District School Board and Toronto Catholic District School Board would otherwise pay for that use. The official figures list fee amounts of $31,994.79, $4,299.78, $21,354.69 and $2,729.58 in the source text. Portable toilets may also be needed at Block 3 since it has no permanent washrooms.

title: Waiving Permit Fees to Support the Bum Run - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: charities; charitable organizations; charity
brief: The Bum Run, a volunteer-run charity run for colon cancer research and screening that has raised more than $1.8 million, returns to Toronto on April 26, 2026, running through Wards 11 and 13. The item asks council to waive the application and event permission fees for partially closing or occupying arterial and collector roads for the run, which total $5,209.14. The run is a registered non-profit with no mandatory participation fees.

title: Response to the Fire in Thorncliffe Park: Best Practices in Community Partnership - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: fire hazards, public safety & protection (sc);
brief: After the November 27, 2025 fire in two connected buildings at 11 Thorncliffe Park Drive and 21 Overlea Boulevard displaced residents of nearly 400 units for more than a month, the item asks council to take stock of the city's response. The motion calls for reviewing lessons learned and best practices in community partnership from the incident, in which a slow-burning fire in the gap between the tower walls complicated firefighting. Community members and organizations provided immediate and ongoing support to displaced residents during the displacement.

title: Addressing Urgent Parking Capacity Gap at 175, 185 and 205 Cummer Avenue (Cummer Lodge, Willowdale Manor, and Seniors Supportive Housing) - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: parking, supportive housing; alternative housing; special needs housing; supported housing
brief: Parking pressure is building at the seniors' campus of 175, 185 and 205 Cummer Avenue, home to Cummer Lodge Long Term Care Home, Willowdale Manor and a soon-to-open seniors supportive housing development at 185 Cummer. Councillor Lily Cheng's motion says on-site parking is essential for physicians, caregivers, staff and visiting families, noting limited transit access and no nearby street or public parking, and asks council to address the parking capacity gap. With 185 Cummer nearing full occupancy, the motion warns demand will grow further.

title: One Country, One Flag; Celebrating the Canadian Flag - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson
topics: flag raising, flags;
brief: The item asks council to rewrite its 1999 flag-raising policy: foreign nations' flags and non-profit or charitable organizations' flags would no longer be flown on city courtesy flag poles, effective immediately. The motion keeps city-hosted raisings for the flags of Indigenous and Treaty partners, the Intersex Pride flag, the Black Liberation flag, professional sports organizations, and cities in the International Alliance program, and leaves the Toronto, Canadian and provincial/territorial flags and half-masting rules unchanged. Flag approvals are currently delegated to the Chief of Protocol.

title: Authorization to Release Section 45 Funds to Parks and Recreation for McNicoll Park Basketball Court Improvements - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: basketball, courts, improvement; enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: The basketball court at McNicoll Park has become a hub for neighbourhood youth, and the item asks council to put up to $500,000.00 in Section 45 developer funds toward its long-term renewal, on top of $125,000.00 already identified through the city's Back on Track program for near-term work like new asphalt, nets, line painting and accessible walkways. The official figures also list a $250,000.00 amount in the source text. The added investment would fund fuller enhancements such as lighting, fencing and public art, and the motion follows an approach from Toronto Police 33 Division to Parks and Recreation about improving the court for youth engagement.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 2, 4 and 6 Teagarden Court for Improvements to the Schoolyard at St. Gabriel Catholic School - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: improvement, schools; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums, enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: The item asks council to put $50,000.00 in Section 37 funds, from the 2, 4 and 6 Teagarden Court development, toward capital improvements to the St. Gabriel Catholic School schoolyard at 396 Spring Garden Avenue in Willowdale. The Toronto Catholic District School Board would sign a 20-year community access agreement, keeping the upgraded schoolyard open to neighbours outside school hours. In dense Willowdale, the schoolyard doubles as neighbourhood open space for families with limited alternatives.

title: 210 Cosburn Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: planning & development (sc);
brief: This is a procedural item: Authorizing the City Solicitor to appeal a Committee of Adjustment decision at 210 Cosburn Avenue, where the owner won approval to convert garage, laundry and storage space in a four-storey apartment building into four basement-level units, bringing the total to 37 units is up for a decision by Council. The city's objections are the lack of indoor and outdoor amenity space for the new units and a drop in lawful on-site parking from 26 to 16 spaces. The motion lets the solicitor retain an outside consultant and negotiate a settlement.

title: 99 Patricia Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: This is a procedural item: Council votes on authorizing the City Solicitor to appeal a Committee of Adjustment decision approving a three-storey fourplex with a rear exterior stairwell plus a two-storey garden suite at 99 Patricia Avenue. City planning staff had recommended refusing two height variances, but the committee approved them on March 5, 2026, and the appeal deadline is March 25, 2026. The motion also lets the solicitor hire outside consultants and negotiate a settlement.

title: Tax Credit Program for Vulnerable Community Institution Security Costs - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: community & life (sc), community centres; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes
brief: Jewish schools, synagogues and community centres are absorbing heavy security costs, including paid duty officers and private security, amid a sustained rise in antisemitic incidents since October 7, 2023, and Councillor Mike Colle's motion asks council to explore a tax credit program to offset security costs for vulnerable community institutions. The motion notes other diaspora and minority communities face similar pressures from conflicts abroad, framing it as a shared public-safety concern. The motion asks staff to design the program; no dollar figure is attached.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Accessibility and Performance Upgrades to Cultural Facilities (TRANZAC, Annex and Al Green Theatres) - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: funding; financing
brief: Three small Ward 11 theatres, TRANZAC at 292 Brunswick Avenue plus the Annex and Al Green Theatres, would share $550,000 in Section 37 developer funds for accessibility and performance upgrades under Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion. The official text lists allocations of $300,000, $187,750.51, $112,249.49 and $50,000 for the upgrades, which target accessibility, climate resilience and performance quality. The motion notes capital funding for these venues has long been scarce, while TRANZAC alone hosts more than 1,400 low-barrier, pay-what-you-can events a year.

title: Addressing Limits of Sidewalk Construction on Taber Road - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: bike paths; bicycle paths; bicycle trails; bike trails; cycling paths; cycling trails; off-road paths (cycling)
brief: A new sidewalk planned for the north side of Taber Road, between Brydon Drive and Kipling Avenue, is scheduled to be tendered this spring and installed in 2026 on a collector road that currently has a sidewalk only on the south side. Nearby businesses have raised concerns about losing parking they use within the city-owned right-of-way. Councillor Vincent Crisanti's motion asks council to shorten the sidewalk's west limit so it ends at the Rexdale Community Health Centre, letting construction proceed where pedestrian need is greatest while preserving business parking.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.TE21.33 - Accessible Parking Space - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: accessible permit parking, parking; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled)
brief: This is a procedural item: Council decides whether to re-open its April 2025 decision that removed an accessible parking space on Dundas Street West near Coolmine Road in Ward 9. The space had been pulled over compliance concerns raised by the original applicant, but the applicant now says losing it created real parking hardship, has withdrawn the concern, and worked with Transportation Services staff on a plan to restore the space. Approving the motion puts the accessible spot back.

title: Grocery Store Pilot Project - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: With food costs squeezing household budgets and food bank use rising across the city, the item asks council to pilot four municipally operated grocery stores, one in each of the city's Community Council districts, with priority for neighbourhoods with limited access to full-service, affordable groceries. The pilot would test whether city-run stores can improve access to affordable, nutritious food in underserved areas. This would be a new kind of city service for Toronto, aimed at food insecurity.

title: 1312 St. Clair Avenue West - Liquor Licence Application - Alpine Espresso Bar Number 3388560 - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Alpine Espresso Bar at 1312 St. Clair Avenue West, operating as the Belvedere Bar and Grill, has applied to the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario for a liquor licence for its indoor area, and nearby residents have raised concerns about noise, litter, safety and other disturbances in the residential area. Councillor Alejandra Bravo's motion asks council to tell the AGCO that the licence is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing those concerns are attached, and to request that the Licence Appeal Tribunal review the application. The AGCO makes the final decision, but council's position is part of the record.

title: Amending the Composition of the Board of Health Due To Provincial Supervision of School Boards - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: boards of health;
brief: This is a procedural item with practical consequences: Council changes the Board of Health's composition for the rest of the term. Since the province put both Toronto school boards under supervision in June 2025 and stripped trustees of their powers, the school-board seat on the Board of Health has sat effectively vacant while still counting toward quorum, making it hard for the board to meet. Councillor Chris Moise's motion would remove the elected school-board representative requirement and add one more citizen member instead. This affects the board that oversees Toronto's public health decisions.

title: Update of Definition and Reporting of the Delegated Authority on Certain Real Estate Matters - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by James Pasternak
brief: The item asks council to update how the city defines and reports delegated authority for certain real estate transactions, after cost details emerged around the city's 233 Carlton Street lease. That 15-year Cabbagetown lease, signed in 2019 at a total cost of $6 million to house a 24-hour women's drop-in centre replacing the Adelaide Women's Resource Centre, carried an initial renovation estimate of $3.7 million; six years in, the city has paid more than $2 million in rent with no women served at the facility, while the contractor's award reached $8.7 million and forecasted completion costs hit $13.5 million, above the $10 million threshold for delegated approval. The motion would tighten the definition and reporting rules for such transactions.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Revitalization of Moss Park Arena - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: funding; financing
brief: Moss Park Arena is in line for a major capital revitalization alongside the John Innes Community Centre reconstruction: a new refrigeration plant, two electric Zambonis, lighting upgrades, washroom and changeroom upgrades, flooring replacement, a new sound system and scoreboard, and a new entrance sign, with construction planned from summer 2027 to 2028. Most of the project is covered by the city's 10-year capital plan, but the item asks council to release $300,000 ($300,000.00) in Section 37 community-benefit funds for enhancements outside that scope. The request follows a governance and operational review that led the arena board to adopt a new strategic plan.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Commemorate Arena Gardens - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
topics: funding, hockey; ball hockey; hockey skills; pick-up hockey; power skating; powerskate; shinny; shinny hockey, financing
brief: The item asks council to give Heritage Toronto $10,000 in Section 37 funds, from the 203 Jarvis Street development, for a plaque at 78 Mutual Street. The plaque would commemorate Arena Gardens, where Toronto's NHL franchise played when the league was founded in 1917, before the team became the St. Patricks and then the Maple Leafs, who played there for 14 seasons before moving to Maple Leaf Gardens in 1931. The plaque would cover a century of the club's history in Toronto.

title: Amending Item 2021.TE25.3 - 111 to 125 River Street - Zoning Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Final Report - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: The owner of 111 to 125 River Street wants to demolish five vacant rental units immediately, citing health and safety concerns, rather than waiting until construction can begin. Council approved the zoning and demolition back in 2021 with conditions, and Councillor Chris Moise's motion re-opens that item to allow an early rental-housing demolition permit for the five units. The applicant has agreed to explore an interim community use for the lot with the councillor's office instead of leaving it fenced and vacant.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.TE22.3 - 72 Perth Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: Re-opening its May 2025 approval for the 72 Perth Avenue development so it can fix the parkland dedication would get Council's approval. The original approval required at least 134 square metres of on-site parkland along the West Toronto Railpath, but the submitted site plan shows only 131 square metres, and a possible Building Code limiting-distance agreement tied to openings in the building's western wall could further restrict the land. Amending the item lets council adjust the parkland terms to match what can actually be delivered.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Public Art at the Toronto Western Hospital - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: funding; financing
brief: Toronto Western Hospital is building a new patient and surgical tower, and leftover Section 37 money is being eyed for public art in its public atrium at 399 Bathurst Street. Back in 2009, the University Health Network paid $25,000 in Section 37 funds for the Krembil Centre development, earmarked for public art on or near the site, and part remains unspent. Councillor Dianne Saxe asks council to forward $15,000.00 to the University Health Network for the atrium installation: $2,163.00 from the 399 Bathurst Street development and $12,837.00 from the 292 Dundas Street development.

title: Authorization to Release of Section 37 Funds for the Preservation of the Zhong Hua Men Archway - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: [objects in culture], culture (sc);
brief: The item asks council to release $28,638.23 in Section 37 funds, from the 90 to 100 Broadview Avenue development, for the preservation of the Zhong Hua Men Archway at Broadview Avenue and Gerrard Street East. The archway, opened in 2009 as a joint City and Chinese Chamber of Commerce project, is the gateway to East Chinatown and is flanked by marble lion statues installed in 2005. The money funds preventative care of the archway and lion sculptures for their long-term preservation.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 to Heritage Toronto for Streetscape Improvements - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: The item asks council to give Heritage Toronto $10,000 in Section 37 funds, from the 2 Fieldway Road development, for a streetscape plaque at Islington station. The plaque would mark where construction workers found the antlers of Torontoceros hypogaeus, the Toronto Subway Deer, an ice-age species whose only known evidence is that 1976 discovery, with the antlers now on display at the Royal Ontario Museum. The money covers production and installation of the plaque near the discovery site.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Schoolyard Improvements at Brock Public School - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: public schools;
brief: The item asks council to release $30,000 in Section 37 developer funds toward the Brock Public School schoolyard revitalization in Davenport. The parent council has been fundraising since 2023 for the project, described as the largest infrastructure effort in the school's history, with a final design adding upgraded play and gathering areas to support outdoor learning. The funds would advance the parent-council-led plan developed with the Toronto District School Board.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for 2025 Participatory Budgeting Projects for Canary District, Corktown, and Distillery District Neighbourhoods - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: funding, recreational facilities; financing, recreation facilities; recreational amenities
brief: Residents of the Canary District, Corktown and Distillery District voted on how to spend a $750,000 allocation of Section 37 funds through 2025 participatory budgeting, and the item asks council to release it for three winning projects: reimagining Lawren Harris Square at $680,000.00, an all-weather ping pong table at Corktown Commons, and additional seating at Corktown Commons. The official text lists $10,000.00 for the smaller Corktown Commons items alongside the $680,000.00 square project within the $750,000 allocation. The funds would be added to the 2026 Parks and Recreation capital budget so these resident-chosen upgrades can move ahead.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for 2025 Participatory Budgeting Projects for Bay Cloverhill, Bloor East, Church Wellesley and Upper Jarvis Neighbourhoods - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: budgets, funding, parks; budgets and accounts, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, financing
brief: Residents of the Bay Cloverhill, Bloor East, Church Wellesley and Upper Jarvis neighbourhoods voted on how to spend a $750,000 allocation of Section 37 funds through 2025 participatory budgeting, and the item asks council to release it for the two winning projects: the Wellesley-Magill Park revitalization at $250,000.00, and a small-dogs off-leash area at James Canning Park at $500,000.00. The money would be added to the 2026 Parks and Recreation capital budget as new sub-projects. This lets the two resident-chosen park projects proceed.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for 2025 Participatory Budgeting Projects for St. Lawrence Neighbourhoods - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: St. Lawrence-area residents voted on how to spend a $750,000 allocation of Section 37 developer funds through the 2025 participatory budgeting process, and the item asks council to release the money for the seven winning heritage projects: a Berczy Park plaque, new heritage street signs on Front Street and in the St. Lawrence Heritage Conservation District and historic Queen East, heritage street banners, advanced shoreline commemoration plaques, and a shoreline commemoration sidewalk etching from Yonge Street to Parliament Street. The official text lists project-level amounts of $500,000.00, $80,000.00, $585,000, $10,000, $5,000.00, $4,000.00 and $2,400.00 within the $750,000 allocation. Releasing the funds lets these resident-chosen capital projects move ahead.

title: Improving Design Quality and Neighbourhood Fit of As-of-Right Multiplex Housing - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: housing, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, homes; residences
brief: New provincial and city rules now allow multiplex homes to be built as-of-right across Toronto's low-rise neighbourhoods, but councillors and city staff say current zoning gives the city limited power over how these buildings look, including design, materials and facades, especially where site plan control does not apply. Councillor James Pasternak asks council to have the Chief Planner review the design quality and neighbourhood fit of recently built multiplexes as part of the upcoming Multiplex Monitoring Program report, and to consider measures to encourage well-designed, context-appropriate buildings. This is about the look and fit of new multi-unit homes on existing residential streets.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Toronto Community Housing Corporation for Affordable Housing Upgrades - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: The item asks council to release $2,366,000 ($2,366,000.00) in Section 37 and Section 45 developer community-benefit funds for upgrades at seven Toronto Community Housing buildings in Ward 11. The line items are: 250 Davenport Road, landscaping, drainage, parking reconfiguration and security cameras, $225,000; 177 Pendrith Street, solar panels, $846,000; 40 Asquith Avenue, security cameras, $275,000; 341 Bloor Street, security cameras, $400,000; 25 Elm Street, in-suite and common-area lighting, $310,000; 72 Clinton Street, landscaping, $220,000; and 34 Oxford Street, solar panels, $90,000. The funds would be added to Toronto Community Housing's 2026-2035 capital budget for security, landscaping and energy work at these affordable-housing buildings. The report also lists $84,634, $260,722, $110,000, $32,997, $168,420, $474,164, $817,366 and $417,697 as additional listed figures.

title: Urgent Action on Violent Residential Break-Ins and Organized Crime Auto Thefts - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: break-in, crime, police officers, police services boards; burglary, illegal activity, police boards
brief: Armed home invasions tied to organized auto theft are the focus of this motion: thieves are breaking into occupied homes and confronting residents to get vehicle keys, with the source pointing to organized crime networks. Councillor Dianne Saxe asks council to request that the Toronto Police Service Board direct the Chief of Police to report back on how many of these break-ins are happening and what is being done to deter, investigate and solve them. The report would cover outcomes for crimes the motion describes as deeply frightening for families, seniors and children in their own homes.

title: Supporting the Role of Trustees in Maintaining an Accountable and Transparent Education System - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: catholic schools, education (sc), public schools;
brief: Councillors Rachel Chernos Lin and Amber Morley are asking City Council to support the role of elected school trustees in an accountable education system, after the Ontario government appointed supervisors to school boards including the Toronto District School Board and Toronto Catholic District School Board in summer 2025, replacing elected trustees. The motion frames the ask around parents' concerns about lost transparency, accountability, and local representation on decisions affecting students. The item affects school governance and parent representation in Toronto. Council decides.

title: Authorization to Release Section 45 Funds to Little Italy Business Improvement Area - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations
brief: Councillors Dianne Saxe and Amber Morley are asking City Council to release $100,000 to the Little Italy Business Improvement Area for designing and implementing its College Street streetscape master plan — including improved lighting, trees, benches, and a Bathurst Gateway — with the BIA funding half of the capital costs. The $100,000 would be a one-time gross budget increase ($0 net), fully funded by Section 37 community benefits from the 297 College Street development, forwarded on signing of a funding undertaking. Council decides.

title: Updates on Vision Zero Road Safety Initiatives: Follow-Up from June and October 2025 City Council Directives, Missing Sidewalk Installations, and Road Safety Improvement Projects
topics: city initiatives, road safety, sidewalks; city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives
brief: The committee is receiving a Vision Zero road safety update responding to June and October 2025 council directives, seeking approval to install missing sidewalks at 16 local-road locations and to approve road safety improvement projects at Sloane Avenue and Brimorton Drive, plus technical bylaw amendments at two more locations. The report cites $99.1 million, $31.7 million, and $67.4 million, and also updates the crosswalk and all-way stop sign policies, community safety zones after the province removed automated speed enforcement as a municipal tool, and missing sidewalk installations. The update affects pedestrian and road safety citywide. The committee decides.

title: Tree By-law Review Report
topics: by-laws, fees, ravines; administrative fees; admission fees; admission prices; rates; service charges; user charges; user fees, bylaws, ravine protection areas
brief: This is an information item: the committee receives the Tree By-law Review report covering the street tree, private tree, and ravine protection by-laws — noting that 98 per cent of survey respondents said trees are important to their quality of life, and Toronto's recognition as a UN Tree City of the World. The report recommends introducing permit application fees for ravine and natural feature protection (currently free): providing the permit service costs about $0.51 million, with fees designed to recover about 90 per cent and the rest staying on the tax base, and fee exemptions for volunteer stewardship applications. No decision is attached.

title: Ravine Strategy 2026 Implementation Update
topics: agreements, ravine protection, ravines; ravine bylaws; ravine protection bylaws, ravine protection areas, tenancy agreements
brief: The committee is receiving the second implementation update on the 2017 Ravine Strategy, which the report says provides $822 million in annual ecological and recreational services. The report cites $12.3 million, $10 million, $2.3 million, $104.9 million, and $50.2 million in related figures, and achievements including 3,760 hectares restored, expanded community stewardship, Loop Trail advancement, intergovernmental capital investment, and international recognition for nature-based solutions. The 2026 operating budget and 2026–2035 capital budget include $83.3 million for Ravine Strategy implementation — $3.6 million in 2026 operating spending (litter picking, invasive species management, student internships, Indigenous engagement, and volunteer stewardship) and the rest in capital work across 49 projects, including $14.8 million in remaining federal grants. The update affects how the city protects and manages its ravine system. The committee receives the report.

title: Lennox Street - Two Way - Markham to Palmerston
topics: bike lanes, bike paths, bikeway networks, cycling; bicycle facilities; bicycle routes; bike routes; bikeway routes; bikeways; cycling routes; shared roadways; signed routes, bicycle lanes; on street bike lanes, bicycle paths; bicycle trails; bike trails; cycling paths; cycling trails; off-road paths (cycling), bicycling
brief: The item asks City Council to reopen the one block of Lennox Street between Palmerston Avenue and Markham Street — currently one-way eastbound with a westbound contra-flow bike lane — to two-way traffic. The councillor says many local residents signed a petition for the change, which would give drivers a legal alternative instead of turning south onto one-way-north Markham Street toward the planned pedestrian-priority area, and asks for a speed hump review and traffic count to protect cyclist safety. Council decides.

title: Authority to Enter into Agreements with the Board of Management of the Bloor Annex Business Improvement Area for Improvements to Seaton Park
topics: business improvement areas, park maintenance, parks; bia; business improvement associations, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, parks maintenance
brief: The question before City Council: whether to authorize agreements letting the Bloor Annex Business Improvement Area deliver improvements to Seaton Park at 14 Albany Avenue, abutting Bathurst Station.
