Council already increased the 2026 Non-Program operating budget by $343,737.02 (gross, $0 net), fully funded by Section 37 and 45 community benefits, for the park upgrades. The agreement lets the BIA — which already manages nearby small parks — play an active role in the park's maintenance, programming, and public-space improvements. Council decides on the agreements.

title: C40 / United Nations Environment Programme Travel Report
topics: environmental programs, environmental reporting, mayor, non-governmental organizations; environmental initiatives; green living, ngos; non government organizations; non-government organizations, office of the mayor
brief: This is an information item: Councillor Dianne Saxe reports back on her October-November 2025 travel as the Mayor's designate to UN Environment Programme Generation Restoration events in São Paulo, the C40 World Mayors Summit and urban nature forum in Rio de Janeiro, and a visit to Rio's emergency operations centre — including Toronto's recognition as a Generation Restoration Role Model City. Council is asked to receive the report.

title: Finch West Goods Movement Study
topics: heavy trucks, light rail transit, research; lrt, studies; surveys (research)
brief: This is an information item: the committee receives the Finch West Goods Movement Study, which reviewed truck operations around the Finch West LRT corridor — an area with over 5,000 businesses and 57,000 employees — jointly funded by the city, Metrolinx, and the Emery Village and DUKE Heights business improvement areas. The study looked at highway access, safety, active transportation, and neighbourhood health. The committee receives the report.

title: 233 Carlton Street
topics: community centres, development; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Councillor Chris Moise (Ward 13, Toronto Centre) has filed an administrative inquiry asking for a public update on delays and costs around the leased 233 Carlton Street property, intended as a future drop-in site for the Adelaide Resource Centre for Women. The inquiry notes the city signed the lease in January 2020, the site has not opened or served any clients, and asks whether leasing and construction costs to date are justified given the absence of service delivery, requesting answers from Corporate Real Estate Management and the Housing Secretariat. The item seeks staff answers rather than a council decision.

title: Appointment of Associate Medical Officer of Health
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: appointing a physician (named in a confidential attachment) as Associate Medical Officer of Health for the Toronto Health Unit — a designation needed for medico-legal signing authority under the Health Protection and Promotion Act — and sending the appointment to Ontario's Minister of Health for approval is up for a decision by City Council. Council decides.

title: Award of Doc5349386217 to ASCO Construction (Toronto) Ltd., for the Sludge Storage Tanks Cleaning and Biofilter Upgrades at the Highland Creek Treatment Plant
topics: construction, contracts, maintenance, wastewater treatment plants, wastewater treatment plants; building, sewage treatment plants; treatment plants; waste water treatment plants, sewage treatment plants; treatment plants; waste water treatment plants
brief: City Council decides whether to reallocate $5,041,274 ($5,130,000 net of HST recoveries) within Toronto Water's 2026 capital budget and 2027-2035 capital plan from projects that finished under budget, and award ASCO Construction (Toronto) Ltd. a $27,996,247 ($28,488,981 net of HST recoveries) contract for sludge storage tank cleaning and biofilter upgrades at the Highland Creek Treatment Plant over 104 weeks. The reallocation and the contract award both need council's approval.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order 6043796 with WSP Canada Inc., and Purchase Order 6052068 with Maple Reinders Constructors Limited for Rehabilitation and Upgrades of Seven Group Six Sewage Pumping Stations at Various Locations
topics: construction, projects, purchasing, wastewater treatment; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, building, sewage treatment; waste water treatment; wastewater management
brief: The city wants to amend two contracts for rehabilitating seven Group Six sewage pumping stations across Toronto: $1,599,436 ($1,627,586 net of HST recoveries) more for WSP Canada Inc. — raising its purchase order from $2,923,091 ($2,974,537) to $4,522,527 ($4,602,123) — for extended construction administration after project conflicts delayed the schedule, and $2,000,000 ($2,035,200) more for Maple Reinders Constructors Limited — raising its order from $27,646,800 ($28,133,384) to $29,646,800 ($30,168,584) — for bypass pumping and extra approved work, with a further $1,300,000 cited in the report's financial details. Council approval is required for both amendments.

title: Amendment to Blanket Contract Number 47023575 and 47020880 issued to ClaimsPro LP for Insurance Adjusting Services
topics: contracts, external services, insurance, insurance claims; bonding; health coverage, consultants; consulting services; professional services
brief: City Council is asked to authorize extending two existing insurance adjusting contracts with ClaimsPro LP and increasing their combined value by $2.8 million, so claims opened before March 31, 2026 that are still unresolved can keep being handled, and to merge the two blanket contracts (47023575 and 47020880) into one for administrative efficiency. The fees cover adjusting work only, not claim payouts, and funding sits in the 2026 operating budget. Council decides on the extension and merger.

title: Emergency Non-Competitive Contract with Webber Infrastructure Management Canada Limited for Snow Removal Services
topics: agreements, contracts, snow emergencies, snow management, snow removal; de-icing; snow clean-up; snow plans, snow emergency, snow melting; windrow clearing (snow), tenancy agreements
brief: The city is reporting to Council a non-competitive emergency contract with Webber Infrastructure Management Canada Limited worth $942,425 net of taxes ($959,012 net of HST recoveries) for snow removal after the January 25-26, 2026 storm dumped about 60 centimetres of snow, bringing January's city-wide total to roughly 90 centimetres after an earlier January 14-15 storm. The emergency exception in the procurement by-law allowed the contract without competitive bidding to clear snow quickly and reduce safety risks.

title: A Programmatic Approach to Delivering State of Good Repair, Accessibility, and Net Zero Programs at City Hall and Metro Hall
topics: accessibility, city-owned properties, maintenance, programs, properties (real estate); barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, city owned properties; city properties, property; real estate
brief: City Council is asked to give the Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management delegated authority to approve purchase-order amendments over $500,000 for the touch-it-once repair, accessibility, and net-zero program at City Hall and Metro Hall, delivered through a construction manager to be selected via Negotiated Request for Proposal Doc5378109215. Total amendments cannot exceed the program's $300 million 2026-2035 capital budget, and staff must report back to committee or council every second and fourth quarter starting in 2027 on progress and amendments issued. The delegation is meant to keep the work moving without delays from market fluctuations.

title: A Portion of 550 Bayview Avenue (Evergreen Brick Works) Evergreen Lease Amendment and Extension Agreement
topics: conservation, contracts, leasing; environmental conservation; environmental improvements; environmental management; environmental protection; environmental stewardship; greening, leases
brief: Approving a 20-year lease amendment and extension with Evergreen for part of 550 Bayview Avenue (Evergreen Brick Works), plus a nominal licence for underground geothermal infrastructure on the same lands is up for a decision by City Council. The current lease, dating to October 2007, expires March 2, 2030, and staff say approving early lets Evergreen keep securing the funding it needs to run the Brick Works. The city manages the lands, the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority owns them, and Evergreen is the tenant.

title: Renewal of Various Boat Club Leases
topics: boat facilities, boating, boating clubs, recreational watercraft; anchoring; boat docks; boat moorings; boat slips; boating facilities; facilities for boaters; facilities for boats; mooring, boat launching; boats; leisure water vehicles; pleasure boats; pleasure craft
brief: The question before City Council: whether to approve renewing the leases of 24 non-profit, volunteer-run sailing, boating, and rowing clubs on Toronto's waterfront for up to 20 years each. Three clubs with unexpired leases (National Yacht Club, Alexandra Yacht Club, Boulevard Club) are excluded, as is a fourth club dealt with separately. Staff frame the renewals as continuing the city's long support for affordable waterfront programming and shoreline upkeep by the clubs. The 24 leases are projected to bring the city about $849,590 in rent in 2026, with the annual rent rising with inflation in each following year of the lease terms.

title: Non-Competitive Extension with Carla Construction & Maintenance Ltd., for Trackless Train Service in High Park for Parks and Recreation
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, construction, contracts, parks, trains; building, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, ttc
brief: City Council votes on approving a non-competitive extension with Carla Construction & Maintenance Ltd. to keep operating the trackless train amusement ride in High Park for the 2026 season. A 2024 request for proposals for a High Park shuttle was cancelled after the preferred proponent said it could not deliver the required accessible electric shuttle; meanwhile the TTC is extending its High Park bus service dates. Staff say the extension preserves a long-standing family amenity alongside the expanded TTC service.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Grascan Construction Ltd., for Emergency Soffit Shoring Repairs to the F.G. Gardiner Expressway
topics: construction, contracts, highways, road repairs; building, crack repairs; cut repairs; fixing potholes; pothole repairs, freeways; motorways; parkways
brief: The city is reporting to Council a non-competitive emergency contract with Grascan Construction Ltd. worth $4,275,568 net of taxes ($4,350,818 net of HST recoveries) for emergency shoring repairs to deteriorating concrete soffits on the Gardiner Expressway. Annual inspections found severe spalling that weakens the deck's load capacity and risks concrete falling through onto traffic below, which staff call a serious safety hazard. The emergency exception in the procurement by-law allowed the contract without competitive bidding.

title: Litigation Arising from the Construction of the St. Lawrence Market North
topics: construction, damages, law (sc); building
brief: The contractor joint venture that built the St. Lawrence Market North redevelopment at 92 Front Street East (Atlas/Buttcon) is suing the city for $81,448,497.40 plus HST in alleged damages and extra costs, mostly tied to delays — the project reached substantial performance on November 30, 2024, against a contract target of December 11, 2021. The city has defended the claim and advanced its own counterclaim, with $8,307,084.19 cited in the report. The item moves through the General Government Committee; the outcome affects the final public cost of the market project, whose provincial offences court opened March 5, 2025 and farmers' market April 5, 2025.

title: Award of Doc5381596310 to The Personal Insurance Company Operating As The Personal General Insurance Inc., for a Group Home and Auto Insurance Program
topics: agreements, contracts, employees, employment & labour (sc), insurance; bonding; health coverage, staff, tenancy agreements
brief: City Council votes on letting the Chief Financial Officer enter a seven-year agreement (April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2033) with The Personal Insurance Company for a voluntary group home and auto insurance program for city employees, council members, agency staff, and retirees. The Personal was the only bidder to pass both the mandatory and technical requirements of the request for proposals. The agreement would generate revenue for the city to offset the cost of administering the program.

title: 2125 Lawrence Avenue West - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Up for a decision before Council: add 2125 Lawrence Avenue West, the City-owned Weston Lions Arena built around 1948-49, to the City of Toronto's Heritage Register for its cultural heritage value.

title: 1455 Royal York Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Up for a decision before Council: direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the appealed townhouse development at 1455 Royal York Road, with 72 proposed homes, and to keep working to resolve outstanding issues including servicing capacity.

title: 2256 Lake Shore Boulevard West - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: mixed use areas, official plan amendments, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Whether to approve a mixed-use development at 2256 Lake Shore Boulevard West with towers of 37 and 10 storeys on a six-storey base, about 575 homes, ground-floor non-residential space, and an on-site expansion of Flora Voisey Park now sits with Council.

title: 250 Wincott Drive and 4620 Eglinton Avenue West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval - and Appeal Report
topics: [buildings by height], mixed use areas, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Up for a decision before Council: approve raising two previously approved mixed-use buildings at 250 Wincott Drive and 4620 Eglinton Avenue West from 11 storeys each to 24 and 29 storeys, permitting about 690 homes, commercial space, community agency space, and 387 parking spaces.

title: Metrolinx Subway Program Update - 2026
topics: executive committees, regional transportation agencies, subways; commuter rail systems; go transit; intercity transportation; interregional public transit systems; interregional transit systems; interurban transit organizations; metrolinx; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; regional transit authorities; regional transportation authorities; transit agencies; transit operating agencies, underground
brief: Up for a decision before Council: authorize the City Manager to amend the Subway Program Real Estate Protocol with Metrolinx and to delegate authority to approve nominal temporary construction licences, for the four provincial subway expansion projects: the Ontario Line, Scarborough Subway Extension, Eglinton Crosstown West Extension, and Yonge North Subway Extension. Staff also seek an agreement on Metrolinx support structures left within City lands. It affects how the City manages its land around subway construction.

title: Pothole Blitz and Local Road Repair Strategy
topics: potholes, road repairs, transportation; crack repairs; cut repairs; fixing potholes; pothole repairs, pot holes; sink holes; sinkholes, transportation services
brief: Mayor Chow is asking Council to have Transportation Services run an ongoing pothole blitz strategy informed by road conditions and 311 data, building on the Fixing Roads Faster program. The 2026 budget put $11 million in new funding into expanding local road resurfacing, after crews filled over 250,000 potholes in 2025. It affects drivers on local roads across the city.

title: Update on Weston Foundation Donation for Queen's Park North Revitalization
topics: agreements, donation, parks; bequest; toy drive, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, tenancy agreements
brief: The City has a first-phase donation agreement with the Weston Foundation and has done community engagement with over 2,900 participants on the Queen's Park North revitalization. Council is asked to approve terms for a further donation agreement of up to $50 million for detailed design and construction, a tri-party maintenance, operations and funding agreement with the Foundation and the University of Toronto, and authority to amend the City's lease with the university. The report's figures also include $500,000.

title: Port Lands Flood Protection Project: Update and Next Steps
topics: executive committees, flood-prevention devices, flooding; floods
brief: The Port Lands Flood Protection project reached substantial completion on September 30, 2025, with four new bridges, the new Don River valley, Biidaasige Park, and new roads and infrastructure delivered. Council is asked to authorize a lease or licence with the Toronto Port Lands Company for lands needed for early works on Ookwemin Minising Phase 1, as the project moves into its final phase.

title: Cracking Down on Bad Landlords
topics: housing, rent, residential landlords; homes; residences, rents
brief: Mayor Chow is asking Council to have the City Manager create a consolidated, publicly available database tracking enforcement at rental properties with multiple complaints by July 2026, and to set up ongoing coordination across divisions on problem buildings. Staff are also developing a framework for when the City uses remedial action powers to hire contractors for repairs and bill landlords through property taxes. It affects tenants in buildings with repeated violations.

title: Winter Surge Capacity Snow Shovellers
topics: snow ploughing, snow removal, winter; snow clearing; snow plowing, snow melting; windrow clearing (snow)
brief: Mayor Chow is asking Council to direct staff to develop a paid surge sidewalk-shovelling program modelled on New York City's approach, for implementation no later than the 2026-2027 winter season. The idea is to pay Torontonians to help clear sidewalks after extreme storms, after staff identified legal and operational challenges with the concept earlier this year.

title: Endorsement for Hosting a National Hockey League Stadium Series Game or Equivalent Outdoor Game in Toronto at Rogers Centre
topics: sports, sports facilities, sports tournaments; sports venues, tournaments
brief: The item asks Council to endorse Toronto as a host city for a major outdoor NHL game, such as a Stadium Series game at Rogers Centre with the roof open, ahead of the 2027 100th anniversary of the Toronto Maple Leafs name. The motion also asks that Maple Leaf Sports and Entertainment be notified of the endorsement. It is an endorsement only, not a funding commitment.

title: Renewal of Corporate Partnership at the Meridian Arts Centre
topics: naming, partnerships;
brief: The TO Live board is recommending that Council adopt the negotiated terms of TO Live's renewed corporate naming-rights partnership at the Meridian Arts Centre, with the financial terms kept confidential to protect negotiating positions. The renewal supports TO Live's cultural investment and capital renewal priorities.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Procurement Plan Update
topics: development, sports, sports tournaments; developing land; development (land); land development, tournaments
brief: Council will weigh whether to direct staff to proceed with the updated procurement plan for the FIFA World Cup 2026 in Toronto, set out in a confidential attachment, to procure the goods and services needed to deliver the event. Awarded contracts and future procurements will be made public at the earliest point that keeps the process competitive.

title: Toronto Wins Bloomberg Philanthropies 2025 - 2026 Mayors Challenge
brief: Toronto has won the Bloomberg Philanthropies 2025-2026 Mayors Challenge prize of $1.4 million for its school food program vision, one of 24 winners from 630 cities worldwide, with two years of expert support attached. Council authorized the Executive Director, Social Development, to receive the award — USD $1,200,000 (CAD $1,643,720) — to negotiate and sign a term sheet for it, and to add that amount to the 2026 operating budget for Social Development. The Mayor's letter also notes a $7 million 2026 budget boost expanding school food programs to 155 more schools and 62,000 more students, and cites almost $900 in grocery-bill savings for families with two kids.

title: Changes to Business Improvement Area Boards of Management
topics: boards of management, business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations, boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is an administrative item: Council is asked to appoint new nominees and remove outgoing directors on the Fairbank Village, Mount Pleasant, and Upper Village Business Improvement Area boards of management, under the City's public appointments policy. BIAs are business-led districts that fund local streetscape and economic development work.

title: Toronto's Festival Strategy
topics: festivals and special events, food festivals; community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals, summerlicious; winterlicious
brief: Toronto hosts roughly 300 festivals, a sector estimated to generate more than $1 billion in GDP across Canada. Council is asked to adopt Toronto's Festival Strategy (2026-2031), with 17 actions to support the festival sector, and to formally establish the Special Events Stabilization Initiative as a funding program. The decision shapes City support for festivals and events citywide.

title: Toronto's Screen Future: A Strategic Plan for Continued Growth 2025-2030
topics: film and television industry, growth, strategic plans; cinema industry; film and television cluster; film production; movie industry; television industry, strategic planning; strategy
brief: Toronto's film and TV industry generates as much as $2.6 billion in annual direct spending and supports 40,000 workers, making the city one of North America's top five production hubs. Council is asked to adopt Toronto's Screen Future, a 2025-2030 strategic plan to keep the industry competitive as other jurisdictions expand tax credits and studio space and U.S. policy shifts create uncertainty. The plan affects a sector that is a major local employer.

title: Public Salary Disclosure for City Agencies and Corporations
topics: corporations, wages; earnings; pay; pay scale; salary; wage rate
brief: This is an information item: Council receives its annual salary-disclosure report for City agencies and corporations not covered by the provincial sunshine list, including staff earning over $100,000 and which agencies still use short-term executive incentive programs. Council directed staff to publish this equivalent information because not all agencies are required to disclose under provincial law. title: Updating the Effectiveness of the Committee of Adjustment
topics: committees of adjustment, housing; committee of adjustment, homes; residences
brief: The Committee of Adjustment, the body that rules on minor zoning variances, could get an overhaul. Mayor Olivia Chow is asking the Planning and Housing Committee to direct staff to consult builders, planners, and other users of the committee and report back on how to make it work better. The review follows years of expanded housing permissions that have changed what the committee handles.

topics: awards, purchasing, zoos; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders

title: Toronto Zoo Individual and Corporate Naming Rights Policy
topics: donation, policies and procedures, sponsorship, zoos; bequest; toy drive, corporate sponsorship; sponsorship opportunities, guidelines; policies
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Zoo's Board of Management will consider adopting an Individual and Corporate Naming Rights Policy aligned with the City of Toronto's corporate framework. The policy sets a consistent approach for soliciting, assessing, approving and managing naming rights while safeguarding zoo integrity, animal welfare and the visitor experience; staff would review it at least every five years and the CEO could negotiate agreements under it. The Chief Transformation Officer recommends the board adopt the policy.

title: Policy and Finance Committee Appointments

The Chief Transformation Officer recommends the board appoint at least one and at most three new members to the committee. The decision determines who sits on the committee that oversees the zoo's policy and finance work.

title: Balancing Conflicts Over Use of Accessible Parking Permits
topics: accessible permit parking, permit parking, permits; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled), on-street permit parking; parking permits, permit renewal
brief: The item asks for work on conflicts over accessible parking permits — more than 840,000 issued by the province — where residents in her ward and downtown complain about permit-holders using exemptions in no-parking or permit-only areas, alleged misuse by people without visible disabilities including construction workers and delivery drivers, and reduced visibility and pedestrian safety at intersections. The committee decides on next steps.

title: Options for Winter Access to Laneway Homes and Garages
topics: laneways, road maintenance, snow management, snow removal; back alleys; mews, de-icing; snow clean-up; snow plans, roads maintenance; sidewalk maintenance; sidewalks maintenance; summer maintenance; winter maintenance, snow melting; windrow clearing (snow)

The item affects laneway homeowners and renters citywide. The committee decides on the request.

title: Response to Council Directions on Sidewalk Clearing Requirements and the Status of Modernizing PlowTO
topics: sidewalk snow ploughs, snow, snow advisory reports, snow management, snow ploughing, snow ploughs, snow removal; bobcats; ploughs; snow plows; snowplows, de-icing; snow clean-up; snow plans, ploughs; sidewalk plows; sidewalk snow plows, snow clearing; snow plowing, snow melting; windrow clearing (snow)
brief: City Council asked staff to report on making select property owners clear the municipal sidewalk next to their property, and on modernizing the PlowTO winter tracking system. Staff say shifting sidewalk clearing to corporate owners would be challenging and could worsen winter accessibility, and note bylaws already require owners to clear sidewalks where the city hasn't assumed responsibility. The report also addresses moving snow from private property onto public property, which bylaws prohibit. The item affects winter sidewalk maintenance citywide. The committee decides on next steps.

topics: arts and culture, performing arts;
brief: Scarborough lacks public spaces for performing arts, and this motion asks Council to have staff report in 2027 on the needs and opportunities for cultural infrastructure in Scarborough, including performing arts spaces, as part of the City's culture plan progress report. The request ties into the 10-year culture plan's priority of bringing new cultural spaces to every part of Toronto.

topics: [activities in business and industry], consumer protection, entertainment, fees, sporting events; administrative fees; admission fees; admission prices; rates; service charges; user charges; user fees, championships

title: Toronto Population Health Status Indicators Update
topics: population;
brief: The Board of Health is being asked whether an intimate partner violence indicator can be added to Toronto Public Health's population health dashboard, in response to a board direction from the fall. Police-reported data underestimate the problem because most victims don't report to police, and staff reviewed possible data sources. The report affects how Toronto measures and publicly shares data on intimate partner and family violence. The board decides on next steps.

The board decides on the request.

title: 509 Parliament Street (Carlton Theatre) - Alterations and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The 1929 Carlton Theatre at 509 Parliament Street — a one-storey brick former movie theatre designated in 2024, though the designation by-law is under appeal — would have some of its heritage features altered and removed to make way for the proposed 10-storey mixed-use building. City Council is asked to approve the changes under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and to enter into a heritage easement agreement. Heritage staff support the proposal, which keeps the theatre's west elevation along Parliament Street in place, and say the heritage impacts are appropriately handled.

title: Ontario Line Gertrude Gate Conditions
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: trucks, winter;
brief: Metrolinx trucks using Gertrude Place for Ontario Line construction would face new permit conditions after residents raised concerns at a February 11 community meeting about the long-term construction gate. Councillor Paula Fletcher's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to require a detailed truck staging and traffic management plan, paid-duty officers and flag persons, clearly visible truck signage, and regular street cleaning as conditions of the access permit. The measures are meant to make the contractor operate as a good neighbour beside a site the community will live next to for years.

title: 60 and 64 Dundas Street East - Residential Demolition Application
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: community councils, demolitions;
brief: The owner of two attached three-storey mixed-use buildings at 60 and 64 Dundas Street East wants to demolish them — they contain four vacant residential units — before getting a permit for a replacement building. The Toronto and East York Community Council, which has the final say, must choose: refuse the demolition, approve it outright, or approve it with conditions. Staff put all three options to the committee because no replacement building permit has been issued.

title: Framework for Event Permitting at Bathurst Quay Common
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: [events in culture], parks and open space areas; green spaces; open spaces
brief: Staff would develop a framework for permitting events at Bathurst Quay Common and the silos — the new waterfront park that opened in 2024 at the historic Canada Malting Silos property — coordinating programming by the Canada Ireland Foundation, OCAD University, and other public users. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to direct Parks and Recreation to build the framework, with a report back in April 2026. The park's 4,000-square-metre plaza hosts special events and cultural programming, and the foundation's new Corleck Building arts centre opens on the site in 2026.

title: Advancing Ongoing Community Engagement on the Bathurst Quay Neighbourhood Community Response Handbook
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: airports, civic engagement; citizen participation; civic participation; community involvement; community participation; public involvement; public participation
brief: Toronto Emergency Management would meet annually with the Bathurst Quay Neighbourhood Association to review and improve the community's emergency response handbook. The handbook was created after an October 2022 incident at Billy Bishop Airport — a suspicious package that turned out to be a spare e-bike battery — led to evacuations lasting past midnight and left residents feeling the crisis communication fell short. The item asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to make the annual review a standing practice so the handbook stays a current resource as the neighbourhood changes.

title: Parking Amendments - Sheppard Street, between Richmond Street West and Adelaide Street West
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Conflicting parking rules on Sheppard Street between Richmond Street West and Adelaide Street West would be cleaned up after residents flagged the inconsistencies. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to scrap a 20-minute delivery zone and a 20-minute parking rule on the west side, correct signage mismatches, and improve sightlines on the narrow two-way street where parked cars force drivers into oncoming traffic and hamper snow clearing. The changes would also let parking officers enforce the rules accurately.

title: Improving Traffic Safety at Gladstone Avenue and Bloor Street West
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: Residents near Gladstone Avenue and Bloor Street West told the ward councillor's office that visitors and food-delivery drivers illegally park on both sides of Gladstone Avenue north of Bloor, blocking sightlines for pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers and forcing cars into oncoming traffic to get around them. Councillor Alejandra Bravo's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to ban stopping on both sides of Gladstone Avenue between Bloor Street West and the first laneway north and to adjust the angle-parking rules. The item also touches parking-machine rules where the rate is $3.00 per hour.

title: Improving Permit Parking on Hallam Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking prohibitions, permit parking; no parking, on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Up to seven visitor and overnight permit parking spaces, plus one accessible space, would be created on Hallam Street by converting a no-parking stretch — replacing some of the parking lost when a cycle track was installed on the south side between Dufferin Street and Bartlett Avenue in September 2025. Councillor Alejandra Bravo's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to approve the changes and fix inconsistencies between the posted signs and the traffic by-law. Staff say the changes would not affect Dovercourt Public School or student safety.

title: Improving a Commercial Loading Zone on St. Clarens Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: loading zones, parking prohibitions; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, no parking
brief: Business owners near St. Clarens Avenue and Bloor Street West say the commercial loading zone is too short for local demand and that parked cars on the west side squeeze traffic when the zone is in use. Councillor Alejandra Bravo's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to extend the east-side loading zone five metres south and ban standing at all times on the east side, while lifting parking bans on both sides of the street. The changes are meant to give delivery vehicles more room and improve traffic flow.

title: 509 Parliament Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: community councils, planning, zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Before City Council for a decision: approve the zoning amendment for a 10-storey mixed-use building with 60 homes and about 278 square metres of ground-floor shops at 509 Parliament Street. The property has been identified for heritage designation, though the designation by-law is under appeal before the Ontario Land Tribunal, so the design keeps part of the front façade within the new building. A separate heritage alterations report will come to council alongside this item.

title: Improving a Commercial Loading Zone on Margueretta Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: loading zones, parking machines, traffic regulations; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, pay and display machines; pay-and-display machines
brief: A business near Margueretta Street and Bloor Street West says illegally parked cars keep blocking its commercial driveway — cutting off access to a boulevard parking space and stopping large waste-collection trucks from emptying overflowing bins, which has led to pest problems. Councillor Alejandra Bravo's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to ban stopping at all times on the east side of Margueretta Street next to the driveway, replacing the existing parking machines there, which charged $3.00 per hour for up to three hours. The change is meant to restore delivery access and waste collection.

title: Traffic Calming - Walter Street (between Kingston Road and Lyall Avenue)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: community councils, traffic calming;
brief: Three speed humps would be installed on Walter Street between Kingston Road and Lyall Avenue after residents petitioned over pedestrian safety concerns on the neighbourhood street. Councillor Brad Bradford's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to authorize the humps, which are aimed at slowing traffic.

title: Queen Street East Replacement Parking
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: community councils, parking, parking spaces; parking spots
brief: The Queen Street watermain and TTC track project has removed 25 paid parking spaces between Davies and Broadview Avenues, and replacement parking is now proposed on Davies Avenue and Hamilton Street. Councillor Paula Fletcher's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to allow one-hour parking from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. on the east side of Davies Avenue between 30 metres north of Queen Street East and Thompson Street — with parking banned there overnight — and to adjust bans on Hamilton Street. Residents and local businesses have been pressing for the changes after the spots stayed occupied through construction delays.

title: Tranmer Avenue Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking prohibitions; no parking
brief: Parking restrictions on the south side of Tranmer Avenue would be scaled back so they apply only between Duplex Avenue and Oriole Parkway, lifting the rules east of Oriole Parkway toward Avenue Road. Councillor Josh Matlow's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to shorten both the 8-to-10 a.m. weekday parking ban and the 10 a.m.-to-6 p.m. one-hour limit. Residents asked for the change, saying the restrictions make it hard to find parking on their street.

title: Glebe Road East Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking prohibitions, traffic regulations; no parking
brief: A 15-minute pick-up and drop-off zone would be created on the north side of Glebe Road East near Yonge Street for students of The Study Academy's Lower School, which serves neurodivergent children ages 8 to 13. Councillor Josh Matlow's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to adjust the standing prohibitions so the zone — between 42 and 67 metres east of Yonge Street — is reserved around school hours. Parents told his office that morning and afternoon drop-offs are difficult because of congestion near Yonge Street.

title: Dewbourne Avenue Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: The weekday morning parking ban on the south side of Dewbourne Avenue — put in place to stop Metrolinx construction workers from parking there — would be lifted at residents' request. Councillor Josh Matlow's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to rescind the 8 a.m. to 10 a.m., Monday-to-Friday prohibition between Glen Cedar Road and Chiltern Hill Road. Residents say the ban is no longer needed and makes it hard to find parking on their street.

title: Renaming Lawton Parkette in Honour of Carolyn Bennett
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: community councils, naming, parkettes, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Lawton Parkette at 1600 Yonge Street would be renamed 'Carolyn Bennett Park' in honour of Dr. Carolyn Bennett, under an application brought by Ward 12 Councillor Josh Matlow. Staff reviewed the proposal against the city's Commemorative Framework and Property Naming Policy and confirm it meets the requirements. The Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to adopt the renaming.

title: Plan for Heather McGregor Way
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: naming, pedestrian walkways; footpaths; pedestrian ways; walking paths; walkways
brief: The YWCA has asked that the walkway section of Chestnut Street between Edward and Elm Streets — behind its head office at 87 Elm Street — be renamed Heather McGregor Way to honour its retiring CEO, who led the charity supporting women for more than 30 years. Because the request arrived late and public notice is required, Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to direct staff to report back to the April 1, 2026 meeting with recommendations on the renaming. No name change is being approved yet.

title: Euclid Avenue Traffic Calming Speed Humps
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: safety, speed humps, traffic calming measures; public safety, sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Euclid Avenue — a residential street with schools and a heavily used children's park — keeps drawing afternoon rush-hour cut-through traffic between Dundas and Bloor. Councillor Dianne Saxe's motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to authorize two more speed humps on Euclid between College Street and Harbord Street, following up on the traffic-calming direction council gave in item TE28.47. The humps are an immediate measure to slow drivers using the street as a shortcut.

title: Dufferin Street and St. Clair Avenue West Action Plan
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: [activities in transportation], community councils, transportation; transportation services
brief: The intersection of Dufferin Street and St. Clair Avenue West — a busy transit hub at the heart of the Davenport community — has seen maintenance lag behind growing use, with residents raising concerns about garbage, streetlighting, signal timing, and street furniture after a neighbourhood walk in October. A motion asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to have city staff develop a coordinated action plan for street cleaning, street furniture, and traffic signal timing ahead of major 2026 community events that will bring more people to the area. The goal is to improve conditions for residents, businesses, and visitors.

title: Appointment of Community Member to the Applegrove Community Complex Board of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: boards of management, community councils, public appointments; boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to appoint Emily Cho to the Applegrove Community Complex board of management, filling the vacancy left by Rachel Power's resignation effective October 6, 2025. The appointment would run to June 30, 2027; the board confirms the nominee meets the city's Public Appointments Policy. No policy change is proposed.

title: Pedestrian Way Designation and Streetscape Improvements - Collier Street between Church Street and a Point 28 Metres East of Church Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: community councils, pedestrian walkways, pedestrians, transportation; footpaths; pedestrian ways; walking paths; walkways, pedestrianization, transportation services
brief: A short stretch of Collier Street between Church Street and a point 28 metres east would be permanently closed to cars and redesignated as a pedestrian way once the nearby 27-storey condo at 717 Church Street wraps up. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to approve the change, which would keep the street open to pedestrians, cyclists, and emergency and maintenance vehicles and add public open space between Church Street and Park Road. Motor traffic is already restricted there for construction staging until January 31, 2027.

title: All-Way Stop Control - Various Locations in Ward 13
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: stop signs; all-way stop controls; technical warrants
brief: Three intersections in Ward 13 would get all-way stops: Front Street East with Cooperage Street, Front Street East with Tannery Road, and Rolling Mills Road with Palace Street. Staff assessed the locations and say the stops would make the intersections safer for all road users. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to approve all three.
address: Toronto Ontario Front Cooperage; Toronto Ontario Front Tannery; Toronto Ontario Rolling mills Palace

title: Durie Street - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: community councils, parking, transportation; transportation services
brief: A pick-up and drop-off zone for the SimplySmart Child Care Centre & Montessori at 2271 Bloor Street West would be created on the west side of Durie Street, just south of Bloor, with the existing alternate-side parking on both sides of that stretch removed so parking is permitted on the west side only. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to approve the changes, intended to give parents and guardians a designated, safe place to pick up and drop off children.

title: Accessible Parking Spaces - February 2026 (Delegated)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: accessibility, accessible permit parking, community councils, parking; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled), barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible
brief: This is a routine item with final authority at community council: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve installing and removing on-street accessible parking spaces for people with disabilities at the locations listed in the February 2026 delegated report, along with related parking-regulation updates such as changes on St. John's Road. No policy change is proposed.

title: Safety Improvements on Davenport Road, Cottingham Road, Poplar Plains Road, and Macpherson Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: [activities in transportation], community councils, safety; public safety
brief: Several intersections around Davenport Road, Cottingham Road, Poplar Plains Road, and Macpherson Avenue would get safety upgrades under a package before the Toronto and East York Community Council. The plan adds a parking lane on the west side of Poplar Plains Road between Cottingham Road and Boulton Drive, a stop sign for southbound drivers on Glen Edyth Drive at Cottingham Road, and traffic signals at Davenport, Poplar Plains and Macpherson — lifting the westbound right-turn-only rule while keeping the southbound left-turn ban. Staff say the changes would give drivers clearer direction and create safer connections for pedestrians and cyclists.

title: Vehicle Width Restriction - Public Lane south of Gerrard Street East, west of Boulton Avenue and Public Lane east of Broadview Avenue, south of Gerrard Street East
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: [land vehicles by function], road restrictions, transportation (sc); lane restrictions; road information; traffic restrictions; trip info; tripinfo
brief: Wide vehicles would be banned from two narrow laneways near Gerrard Street East and Broadview Avenue to stop them from damaging nearby private properties. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to prohibit vehicles over two metres wide on the lane south of Gerrard Street East west of Boulton Avenue, and on the lane east of Broadview Avenue south of Gerrard Street East.
address: Toronto Ontario Gerrard Boulton; Toronto Ontario Boulton Broadview; Toronto Ontario Gerrard Broadview

title: Traffic Management in Ward 14 related to the King Street East and Church Street Intersection Project
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, intersections; ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to receive, for information, a staff report explaining why TTC track and watermain repairs at King Street East and Church Street were scheduled for 2025 and summarizing the traffic management measures in place for the area bounded by the Don River, Eastern Avenue, Broadview Avenue, and Gerrard Street East, including actions at Broadview and Dundas Street East. Council ordered the report in April 2025; no decision is proposed.

title: 117-127 Broadway Avenue - Designation of Fire Routes and amendment to Chapter 880 - Fire Routes
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: by-laws, community councils, fire routes; bylaws, fire access routes
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to designate parts of the private roads at 117-127 Broadway Avenue as fire routes under the city's Fire Routes by-law, keeping access clear so firefighters can reach the properties. No policy change is proposed.

title: 65 Broadway Avenue - Designation of Fire Routes and amendment to Chapter 880 - Fire Routes
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: by-laws, community councils, fire routes; bylaws, fire access routes
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to designate part of the private road at 65 Broadway Avenue as a fire route under the city's Fire Routes by-law, keeping access clear so firefighters can reach the property. No policy change is proposed.

title: 25 Augusta Avenue - Designation of Fire Routes and amendment to Chapter 880 - Fire Routes
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: by-laws, community councils, fire routes; bylaws, fire access routes
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to designate part of the private road at 25 Augusta Avenue as a fire route under the city's Fire Routes by-law, keeping access clear so firefighters can reach the property. No policy change is proposed.

title: 33 Yorkville Avenue - Noise Exemption Permit Refusal Appeal
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: community councils, noise, noise exemption permits; amplified music; construction noise; loud music; noise pollution; traffic noise, exemptions from a noise limitation; exemptions from a noise prohibition
brief: The developer of Concord Canada House at 27-37 Yorkville Avenue is appealing the refusal of a noise exemption permit that would allow construction beyond the noise by-law's hours for the 72-storey, 1,397-unit project. Municipal Licensing and Standards refused the permit after the ward councillor objected, and the applicant appealed. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — can grant the permit with conditions or refuse it.

title: Mirvish Village Business Improvement Area - Encroachment Appeal
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: encroachments;
brief: The Mirvish Village business improvement area wants to add streetscape features on the Markham Street sidewalk — a 1.2-metre decorative screen, nine decorative light poles, and a water bottle-filling station — as part of a new parkette project with the city's BIA office. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to authorize the encroachment and its ongoing maintenance, keeping about 2.5 metres of clear space for pedestrians along Markham Street. The screen's footings and the water station technically contravene the streets and sidewalks by-law.
address: Toronto Ontario Bloor Poulter's Place; Toronto Ontario Markham Bloor

title: 114 Ossington Avenue - Encroachment Appeal
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: encroachments;
brief: The owner of 114 Ossington Avenue is appealing to keep a natural gas-fuelled fire pit installed on public land in front of the property, which contravenes the city's streets and sidewalks rules. Transportation Services does not recommend granting permission. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to refuse the encroachment agreement and require the owner to remove the fire pit.

title: 137 Bond Street - Construction Staging Area
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: community councils, construction, road construction; building
brief: Pomerleau is building an eight-storey Toronto Metropolitan University student centre at 137 Bond Street, at the corner of Bond and Gould, and needs 17 months of staging on the street. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to close the east sidewalk and a 5.3-metre strip of the northbound lane on Bond Street from February 20, 2026 to June 30, 2027, with pedestrians redirected into a 1.5-metre covered walkway inside the closed lane. The item would also lift the parking-machine rules, where the rate is $6.75 per hour.

title: 30 Bond Street (St. Michael's Hospital) - Construction Staging Area
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: [activities in transportation], construction, transportation; building, transportation services
brief: St. Michael's Hospital's renovation at 30 Bond Street needs a construction staging area on Shuter Street for a year. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to close the parking lay-by on the south side of Shuter Street, just east of Victoria Street, from March 10, 2026 to February 28, 2027, and to adjust stopping rules around it. The existing sidewalk and all traffic and bike lanes on Shuter Street would stay open.

title: 140 Merton Street - Construction Staging Area
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: construction; building
brief: EllisDon Community Builders is putting up a 29-storey residential building at 140 Merton Street, between Yonge Street and Mount Pleasant Road, and needs 39 months of construction staging on the street. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to close the north sidewalk and a 2.7-metre strip of the westbound curb lane from March 1, 2026 to May 31, 2029, with pedestrians redirected into a 2.1-metre covered walkway inside the closed lane. The item would also lift the north-side parking-machine rules, where the rate is $4.25 per hour with a three-hour maximum.

title: Tecumseth Street (723 Queen Street West) - Construction Staging Area
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: construction, road construction, transportation; building, transportation services
brief: A four-storey shelter is being built at 723 Queen Street West, on the southeast corner of Queen and Tecumseth, and its construction staging needs part of Tecumseth Street closed for 20 months. The Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — is asked to close the east sidewalk, a 0.4-metre strip of the northbound lane, and the northbound and southbound bike lanes on Tecumseth Street from April 1, 2026 to December 1, 2027. The item would also lift the parking-machine rules on the east side of Tecumseth Street, where the rate is $4.25 per hour.

title: Alberta Avenue (908 St. Clair Avenue West) - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: [activities in transportation], community councils, construction; building
brief: The builder of a 12-storey condo at 908 St. Clair Avenue West wants another year for its construction staging on Alberta Avenue — the west sidewalk and a 5.5-metre slice of the southbound lane — after difficult site conditions during demolition, excavation and shoring delayed the project. The Toronto and East York Community Council, which has final say on this item, is asked to extend the closure from January 4, 2026 to January 1, 2027; since early January the site has been operating under a monthly street occupation permit.

title: Changes to Business Improvement Area Boards of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council, which has delegated authority over local business improvement area boards, is asked to appoint and remove directors on six BIA boards — Downtown Yonge, Historic Queen East, Leslieville, Midtown Yonge, Old Town Toronto, and Toronto Downtown West — for terms running to the end of the council term. The appointments follow the city's Public Appointments Policy; no policy change is proposed.

title: 32 Curzon Street - Application to Remove a City Tree
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: applications, community councils, tree removal; application process
brief: A property owner at 32 Curzon Street is appealing the city's refusal to let them remove a city-owned sugar maple to make room for a new curb and driveway, saying the tree blocks sightlines. Urban Forestry staff recommend the Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say — deny the permit, because the 11-centimetre tree is healthy and maintainable under the city's tree by-laws.

title: 411 Brock Avenue - Application to Remove a City Tree
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: city-owned trees, community councils, tree removal; city owned trees; public owned trees; publicly owned trees; trees on public property
brief: A property owner at 411 Brock Avenue is appealing the city's refusal to let them remove a city-owned Colorado blue spruce, saying its roots are lifting patio stones and cracking a concrete walkway, creating safety hazards, and that limited soil raises stability concerns. Urban Forestry staff recommend the Toronto and East York Community Council — which has the final say on this appeal — deny the permit, because the 45-centimetre tree is healthy and maintainable under the city's tree by-laws.

title: 153 and 185 Eastern Avenue - Alterations to Designated Heritage Properties Under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: community councils, heritage preservation, heritage properties, planning; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Two heritage-designated industrial buildings in the West Don Lands — the Cleaning Room at 153 Eastern Avenue and the Machine Shop at 185 Eastern Avenue, part of the old Dominion Wheel and Foundries complex — would be altered as part of a development of three new residential towers with commercial and community uses. City Council is asked to approve the alterations under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and to enter into a heritage easement agreement to protect the buildings. Heritage staff say the conservation strategy appropriately mitigates the heritage impacts; the buildings were designated in 2023 and reflect the area's evolution from government reserve to a late-19th- and early-20th-century industrial centre.
address: 153 Eastern Toronto Ontario; 185 Eastern Toronto Ontario

title: Naming of a Proposed Public Street for a Development at 215 Lake Shore Boulevard East
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: community councils, economic development, street names; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing, renaming; road names; street naming
brief: Before the Toronto and East York Community Council for a decision: approve 'Chloe Cooley Street' as the name for a proposed public street at 215 Lake Shore Boulevard East. Staff say the name complies with the city's street naming policy and the guidelines for commemorating people in the public realm.

title: 9 Drumsnab Road - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property in the South Rosedale Heritage Conservation District - Refusal
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: community councils, heritage preservation, heritage properties, planning; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff are asking City Council to refuse a request to replace the original windows and enlarge the entryway — sidelights, transom window, and door opening — of the heritage-designated home at 9 Drumsnab Road, a 'B-rated' property in the South Rosedale Heritage Conservation District. The changes do not comply with the district plan, national conservation standards, or the Official Plan, according to the report. If the owner appeals, council would send the City Solicitor to oppose the appeal at the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: 21 Baby Point Crescent - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property in Teiaiagon-Baby Point Heritage Conservation District
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: community councils, heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: This item was withdrawn from the Toronto and East York Community Council agenda, so no decision was made. It concerned a staff recommendation that City Council refuse a request to add a front vestibule to the heritage-designated home at 21 Baby Point Crescent in the Teiaiagon–Baby Point Heritage Conservation District. Staff found the addition, proposed by Starkey Group Architects, did not comply with the district plan, national conservation standards, or the Official Plan. Had council refused it and the owner appealed, the City Solicitor would have defended the refusal at the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: St. Clair Avenue West and Bathurst Street Planning Framework and Forest Hill Village Urban Design Guidelines Review - Final Report
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: community councils, planning, transportation, urban design, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, civic improvements, transportation services
brief: A final report updates the planning framework for growth around St. Clair Avenue West and Bathurst Street, along with the Forest Hill Village Urban Design Guidelines, and the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to adopt it. The review included a transportation assessment aimed at improving safety, traffic operations, and active-transportation links in the transit-accessible, mixed-use area. The item also proposes four speed humps on Claxton Boulevard and the removal of an eastbound one-way rule.

title: Naming of a Proposed Private Street Within the Alexandra Park Revitalization Area
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: street names; renaming; road names; street naming
brief: Whether to approve 'Bob Ellis Way' as the name for a proposed private street in the Alexandra Park Revitalization Area now sits with the Toronto and East York Community Council. Staff say the name complies with the city's street naming policy and its principles for commemoration in the public realm. The applicant would pay the estimated $600.00 for the street name signs and cover their upkeep.

title: Nantucket Boulevard - Parking Amendments
topics: change, parking prohibitions, parking regulations; amendments; conversion; modification, no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Scarborough Community Council will decide whether to amend the parking prohibition on the east side of Nantucket Boulevard, south of Wickware Gate, to allow parking from November to April. Transportation Services says the change would give on-street parking to employees at the city's winter maintenance depot at 1 Nantucket Boulevard, while plowing and salting operations continue. The community council has final decision-making authority.

title: Fallingbrook Road - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
topics: assessment, speed humps, traffic calming measures; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Scarborough Community Council will decide whether to install speed humps on Fallingbrook Road, between Queen Street East and Windsor Avenue. Transportation Services does not recommend installation, finding the warrant criteria were not met. The community council has final decision-making authority on this matter.

title: Faircroft Boulevard - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Scarborough Community Council will decide whether to install speed humps on Faircroft Boulevard, between Kingston Road and Balcarra Avenue/Pine Ridge Drive (south intersection). Transportation Services recommends installation after finding the Traffic Calming Policy criteria were met. The community council has final decision-making authority on this matter.

title: 777 Victoria Park Avenue - Construction Staging Area
topics: [activities in property], affordable housing, construction, rental housing; affordable homes; housing projects, building, rental properties; rental units
brief: City Council will decide whether to authorize temporary road and sidewalk closures on Victoria Park Avenue for construction staging at 777 Victoria Park Avenue, where a 36-storey rental tower and a 12-storey affordable housing tower are being built at the northeast corner of Victoria Park and Denton Avenues. Transportation Services wants to temporarily close the east sidewalk and part of the northbound lane, plus the north sidewalk and part of an adjacent roadway. Because the TTC operates on Victoria Park Avenue, City Council approval is required. The closures would support construction of rental and affordable homes.
address: 777 Victoria Park Toronto Ontario; Toronto Ontario Victoria Park Denton

title: 1505 Danforth Road - Residential Demolition Application
topics: demolitions, planning;
brief: Scarborough Community Council will decide whether to approve or refuse the demolition of the existing residential building at 1505 Danforth Road, under the city's residential demolition control rules. The community council has final decision-making authority and may attach conditions. No redevelopment is described in the summary.

title: 1072 McCowan Road - Residential Demolition Application

title: 153 and 185 Eastern Avenue - Alterations to Designated Heritage Properties Under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council approve alterations to the designated heritage properties at 153 Eastern Avenue (Cleaning Room building) and 185 Eastern Avenue (Machine Shop building) under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act, with authority to enter a Heritage Easement Agreement, in connection with a proposal for three new residential towers with commercial and community uses. The two buildings of the Dominion Wheel & Foundries Ltd. Complex are rare surviving examples of the industrial complex typology in the West Don Lands, reflecting the area's evolution from Government Reserve to late-19th- and early-20th-century industrial centre. Staff are satisfied the proposal conserves the heritage properties.

Designation is the first legal step toward protecting the property's heritage attributes.

title: 53 Strachan Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate 53 Strachan Avenue under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The City-owned property (owned since 1858) contains Strachan House, a large brick 3-storey factory built in 1888 and enlarged in 1899–1901 — one of Canada's largest planing mills when built for John B. Smith & Sons — and the 1901 two-storey Maple Green stable building. Strachan House was converted to housing in 1996 and leased since 1989 to Homes First, which provides supportive housing. Designation is the first legal step toward protecting the property's heritage attributes.

title: 401 King Street West - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act

The former warehouse and headquarters of Warwick Bros. & Rutter Ltd. — completed in 1904 with a 1913 addition, and designed by George Wallace Gouinlock — housed Canada's most prolific publisher during the early-20th-century 'golden age' of postcards, with over 9,000 known postcard designs. Designation is the first legal step toward protecting the property's heritage attributes.

title: 2026 Toronto Heritage Grant Awards
topics: awards, heritage properties, subsidies and grants; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council approve seven grants totaling $110,000.00 under the Toronto Heritage Grant Program, which is expected to generate about $668,696.28 in private investment for conservation work on designated heritage properties. The program matches up to 50% of eligible conservation costs: owners of house-form buildings can receive up to $10,000.00, or up to $20,000.00 every ten years when replacing an entire cedar or slate roof assembly. The program has a budget of $317,000.00 in the City Planning 2026 Operating Budget. The grants help owners restore heritage properties across the city.

The City-owned property contains a former linseed oil mill factory built in phases from 1910 into the 1940s for Canada Linseed Oil Mills Ltd., with a prominent chimney stack visible from Dundas Street West and the rail corridor, and portions designed by Langley & Howland. Designation is the first legal step toward protecting the property's heritage attributes.
