title: 2026 Operating and Capital Budget
topics: capital budgets, operating budgets;
brief: The Mayor's proposed 2026 operating and capital budgets, which the City of Toronto Act requires the Mayor to table for council's consideration, set out how the City plans to spend on services and capital projects in the coming year: an $18.86 billion operating budget and a $63.06 billion 10-year capital budget and plan (2026–2035). The proposal includes a 2.2 percent property tax increase, inclusive of the City Building Fund. The budget documents frame the proposal against a $1.8 billion shortfall in 2023, followed by a credit-rating upgrade to AA+, and project $250 million in revenue from the Vacant Homes Tax and luxury homes tax to fund affordability measures for working families. The budget touches every Toronto household — services, tax rates and projects across all wards. The source tables cite hundreds of additional line-item figures that are not summarized here.

title: Response to Ontario Regulation 286/09 Budget Matters - Expenses
topics: budgets, expenses; budgets and accounts
brief: This is a procedural item: because the City budgets on a cash basis, Ontario Regulation 286/09 lets it exclude non-cash accounting expenses — an estimated $1,919 million for 2026, covering amortization, post-employment benefits and landfill closure costs. City Council is asked to receive the report for information and authorize staff to publish this information on the City website in future years.

title: Budget Implementation Including Property Tax Rates, User Fees and Related Matters
topics: budgets, fees, property tax rates; administrative fees; admission fees; admission prices; rates; service charges; user charges; user fees, budgets and accounts
brief: Approving the 2026 property tax rates and related measures needed to put the 2026 budget into effect: an average budgetary tax rate increase of 0.57 percent — 0.70 percent for residential and industrial properties, 0.35 percent for multi-residential and commercial — plus a City Building Fund levy increase of 1.50 percent (residential/industrial) and 0.75 percent (multi-residential/commercial) for transit and housing capital investment, goes to City Council for approval. Figures cited in the report include $6,174,269,194.00, $74,996,117.00, $2,213,525,317.00, $4,223,129.00, $380 million, $75.0 million, $1,000,000, $700,000.00, $100,000.00, $120,000.00, $62,000.00, $7,274,452.00, $6,771,766.00, $502,686.00 and $500.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: general bills and confirming bills will be introduced at City Council — the formal step that turns Council decisions into law. The source material gives no further detail.

title: Updates on New and Ongoing Music Office Work
topics: entertainment, music;
brief: This is an information item: Music Office staff update the committee on new and ongoing city work supporting the music sector. No decision is attached.

title: Toronto Music Advisory Committee Task Team Updates
topics: entertainment, music;
brief: This is a procedural item: Toronto Music Advisory Committee task team spokespeople update members on ongoing work toward team goals. No decision is attached.

title: Music Sector Future Challenges and Opportunities
topics: entertainment, music;
brief: This is a procedural item: the committee chair leads a discussion on gaps, opportunities, and trends in the music ecosystem and how the city can support sector development. No decision is attached.

title: Introducing Young Music Professionals: Building the Music Leaders of Tomorrow
topics: entertainment, music;
brief: This is an information item: the Toronto Music Advisory Committee hears a presentation from Young Music Professionals executive director Madison Oliver about building a career pipeline in Canada's music industry. No decision is attached.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Procurement Plan Update
topics: purchasing, sporting events, sports; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, championships
brief: City Council is asked to approve an updated procurement plan for delivering the FIFA World Cup 2026 in Toronto — covering contracts awarded so far and requests to negotiate and award further goods and services listed in a confidential attachment, building on the plan council approved in November 2025. Details stay confidential for now to protect the competitiveness of the procurement process and will be made public as awards are made. The update affects how the city buys the capital and operational services needed for the tournament.

title: Appeal of the Chief Building Official's Decision for a Signage Master Plan Application for Multiple First Party Signs at 335 Yonge Street
topics: signs; signage
brief: The Sign Variance Committee will hear an appeal of the Chief Building Official's decision on a Signage Master Plan for 335 Yonge Street. The plan covers 27 first-party wall signs, and the appeal seeks one variance for their erection and display. The applicant is Architect Osama Abo Nassar, acting for owner 2160943 Ontario LTD. The committee will decide whether to grant it.

title: Appeal of the Chief Building Official's Decision for a Sign Variance Application for One First Party Electronic Wall Sign at 33 Yonge Street
topics: appeals, electronic signs, signs; changeable message signs; electronic billboard signs; electronic overhead message signs, signage
brief: The Sign Variance Committee will hear an appeal of the Chief Building Official's decision on a sign variance for one first-party electronic wall sign at 33 Yonge Street, intended for building identification. The applicant is Kramer Design Associates Limited, acting for owner GWL Realty Advisors. The committee will decide whether to grant the one variance.

title: Application for Four Variances, Each Subject to One Condition, Respecting One Third Party Electronic Ground Sign - 1601 Eglinton Avenue East
topics: electronic signs, sign permits, signs; billboard permits; permanent sign permits; sign variances; street banner permits; temporary sign permits, changeable message signs; electronic billboard signs; electronic overhead message signs, signage
brief: The Sign Variance Committee will decide on four variances that would let the Chief Building Official issue a permit for a double-faced third-party electronic ground sign with static electronic copy at 1601 Eglinton Avenue East in Ward 16 - Don Valley East. The site is designated as a Utility sign district, which generally allows such signs, though the truncated report notes it is also situated within an additional area. The applicant is Permit World, and each variance would be subject to one condition. The decision affects advertising signage along Eglinton Avenue East.

title: 137 and 141 Isabella Street- Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: community councils, demolitions, planning, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: Sixty-one rental homes at 137 and 141 Isabella Street would be demolished under a rental housing demolition application before City Council, to be replaced as 61 rental units inside the 69-storey, 809-unit development the Ontario Land Tribunal approved in principle in June 2025. Tenants would receive a tenant assistance plan with a right of return at similar rents, and the replacement units would be secured as rentals for 20 years. The report also attaches a $20,000.00 financial condition to the approval.

title: 5 Huntley Street and 2, 4, 6 and 8 Earl Street and a Portion of 10 Earl Street - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: community councils, demolitions, planning, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: Seven rental units at 6 and 8 Earl Street are proposed for demolition as part of the 63-storey development at Huntley and Earl — and two of the seven were already torn down without a permit in 2024. City Council is asked to approve the rental housing demolition and a residential demolition permit; the nine replacement rental units would be protected as rentals for 20 years, tenants would have a right of return at similar rents, and a tenant assistance plan would provide compensation to ease hardship. The report also attaches a $20,000.00 financial condition to the approval.

title: 5 Huntley Street and 2-8 Earl Street and a Portion of 10 Earl Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: community councils, official plan amendments, planning, zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 63-storey tower with 709 homes is proposed for 5 Huntley Street and 2-8 Earl Street, and City Council is asked to approve an Official Plan change — redesignating the site from Neighbourhoods to Apartment Neighbourhoods — along with the zoning amendment. Seven rental units would be demolished and replaced with nine, and the applicant has agreed to a tenant assistance plan for existing renters. The project would also widen the laneways to the north and east and add a six-metre public right-of-way to improve laneway connections.

title: Recipient of the 2026 Agnes Macphail Award
topics: awards, community councils;
brief: The Agnes Macphail Award, established by the former Borough of East York, honours an outstanding local volunteer each year. Councillor Paula Fletcher asks City Council to name Dr. Blair Bigham the 2026 recipient; the selection committee chose Dr. Bigham unanimously at its January 5, 2026 meeting.

title: 146-150 Vaughan Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: community councils, planning, zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Approving a zoning amendment for a 17-storey, 110-unit purpose-built rental building at 146-150 Vaughan Road, with a small ground-floor commercial space, four car parking spots and 133 bicycle spaces comes before City Council. The plan requires demolishing five occupied rental units, so the owner must provide a tenant assistance plan for the current tenants and six affordable rental units as a community benefit contribution. The decision weighs new rental supply against the loss of five existing rental homes.

title: Left Turn Prohibition from Bathurst Street onto Barton Avenue
topics: community councils, traffic regulations, turn prohibitions (traffic);
brief: For years, residents of Barton Avenue — a narrow residential street in Seaton Village — have complained that afternoon rush-hour drivers, guided by navigation apps, turn left off Bathurst Street and use their street as a shortcut toward Christie Street. A motion asks City Council to ban left turns from northbound Bathurst Street onto westbound Barton Avenue from 3 p.m. to 7 p.m., Monday to Saturday. More than 4,000 homes were surveyed, and while concern about traffic is high, residents were split on reversing the street's direction — so that option is not on the table. If adopted, drivers heading to the area would need to use another route during those hours.

title: 199 College Street Community Benefits Charge, College Streetscape
topics: community benefits, community councils, transportation; transportation services
brief: City Council referred Motion MM35.12 to the Toronto and East York Community Council on December 16-17, 2025, concerning the community benefits charge for the approved redevelopment at 191-199 College Street and 74-76 Henry Street (approved June 26, 2024). Meanwhile, the Little Italy Business Improvement Association has developed a College streetscape plan with community stakeholders. The Community Council will consider how the charge should support the streetscape.

title: 808 Mount Pleasant Road and 247-251 Roehampton Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: community councils, planning, zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving changes to the height, density, and massing rules for a 197.5-metre, 61-storey mixed-use building (excluding the mechanical penthouse) plus a new 317-square-metre park at 808 Mount Pleasant Road and 247-251 Roehampton Avenue, amending site-specific zoning by-law 1208-2022. The current by-law allows 114.4 metres (35 storeys), so the proposal is a significant increase. The report references a $100.00 figure, and City Council will decide.

title: Runnymede Road - Parking Amendments
topics: parking;
brief: Transportation Services is asking City Council to extend the existing stopping ban on the west side of Runnymede Road, north of Annette Street, 11 metres further north. The extension would remove one on-street parking space and fix blocked sightlines between southbound traffic on Runnymede Road and other road users. Because the TTC operates on Runnymede Road, City Council must vote on it.

title: Various Developments to be Excluded from Permit Parking in the Toronto and East York Community Council Area - Non-Delegated
topics: community councils, on-street parking, parking, permit parking; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Excluding the development addresses listed in the report's attachments from the on-street overnight permit parking program, after staff found the exclusions feasible, goes to City Council for approval. Because the TTC operates on the affected streets, City Council must vote on it rather than the Community Council. This is the non-delegated companion to the related item.

title: 409 Huron Street - Alterations and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: community councils, demolitions, heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Altering and demolishing heritage attributes of the designated heritage property at 409 Huron Street, which includes a Queen Anne style building on the east side of Huron Street south of Bloor Street West, in connection with zoning and Official Plan amendment applications for the site, goes to City Council for approval. The application is made under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act, and Council would also authorize a Heritage Easement Agreement. The decision weighs redevelopment against heritage conservation.

title: Ontario Line - Construction Update - Fourth Quarter 2025
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, community councils, public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, ttc
brief: City staff are updating the Toronto and East York Community Council on Metrolinx's Ontario Line construction in Toronto-East York, as directed by Council through Item TE4.70 on a semi-annual basis. The fourth-quarter 2025 update covers Ontario Line South construction and station-specific issues, project-wide matters like haul routes and construction mitigation, community engagement, and Metrolinx's community benefits commitments. The report is for information.

title: 294-300 Sherbourne Street - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction permits (right-of-way); curb cut permits; driveway paving permits; driveway resurfacing permits; driveway widening permits; landscaping permits (right-if way)
brief: Reliance Construction Toronto is building a 21-storey student residence at 294-300 Sherbourne Street, on the west side south of Gerrard Street East, and is asking to temporarily close the west sidewalk and the westerly southbound cycle track for 18 months. Because the TTC operates on Sherbourne Street, City Council must vote on it. The closure would push pedestrians and cyclists around the work zone during construction.

title: Bedford Road (287 Davenport Road and 141-145 Bedford Road) - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, road closures, transportation; building, street closures; temporary highway closings, transportation services
brief: Burnac Enterprises Inc, is building a 13-storey residential condominium at 287 Davenport Road and 141-145 Bedford Road, on the southeast corner of Davenport and Bedford, and needs to close the east sidewalk, the easterly northbound bike lane, and part of the northbound vehicle lane on Bedford Road for construction staging. Because the TTC operates on Bedford Road, City Council must vote on it. The closures would affect pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers during construction.

title: 409 Huron Street- Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: community councils, demolitions, planning, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend approving the demolition of 40 rental units in a three-storey apartment building at 409 Huron Street, with the units to be replaced in the new development on the site. The proposal includes a Tenant Assistance Plan giving existing tenants the right to return to replacement rental units at similar rents, along with $20,000.00 in financial compensation to mitigate hardship. City Council will decide.

title: 280 Commissioners Street - Official Plan Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, community councils, official plan amendments, planning;
brief: The applicant for 280 Commissioners Street appealed the Official Plan Amendment application to the Ontario Land Tribunal on November 4, 2025. The application, submitted December 6, 2024, proposed two residential towers of 40 and 45 storeys with 937 homes including 42 affordable units, plus 16,336 square metres of non-residential space in the base (81,219 square metres total). This report updates the Toronto and East York Community Council on the appeal.

title: 147-151 Liberty Street and 54-68 Fraser Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, community councils, planning, zoning;
brief: The applicant for 147-151 Liberty Street and 54-68 Fraser Avenue appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on September 18, 2025, after Council did not decide on the proposed 55-storey mixed-use building (732 homes) atop an existing heritage-listed building within the Planning Act's time limit. The application was submitted January 24, 2025. This report recommends that the City Solicitor and city staff attend the Tribunal to represent the city's position.

title: 353-355 Sherbourne Street and 157 Carlton Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: community councils, official plan amendments, zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 48-storey mixed-use building with about 440 homes is proposed for 353-355 Sherbourne Street and 157 Carlton Street, with at least 30 percent affordable homes (presently 132 units), under changes to the Official Plan and the site-specific zoning by-law 812-2022. Staff recommend approval. City Council will decide.

title: 494-526 Richmond Street East and 156-162 Parliament Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: community councils, planning, zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Two linked buildings of 45 and 12 storeys with 718 homes are proposed for 494-526 Richmond Street East and 156-162 Parliament Street, with about 440 square metres of non-residential space, an east-west mid-block connection, and a roughly 293-square-metre privately owned public space at Richmond and Berkeley Streets. Staff recommend approval of the zoning amendment. City Council will decide.

title: 409 Huron Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: community councils, official plan amendments, planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: An 11-storey residential building with 136 homes, including 40 replacement rental units, is proposed for 409 Huron Street, requiring the land to be redesignated from Neighbourhoods to Apartment Neighbourhoods and the University of Toronto St. George Campus Secondary Plan to be amended to allow a 40-metre maximum height. Staff recommend approval. City Council will decide.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2536, 85 Keeler Boulevard, Scarborough, Laurier Homes (Keeler) INC.
topics: assumption of services, municipal services; city services
brief: City Council decides whether to assume the municipal services installed under the 2015 subdivision agreement with Laurier Homes (Keeler) Incorporated for Plan of Subdivision 66M-2536 at 85 Keeler Boulevard, and release the performance guarantee the city holds. Assumption means the city takes over maintenance of the roads and services. No new spending is involved.

title: 2912 to 2926 Sheppard Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal Report
topics: Official Plans, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Scarborough Community Council and City Council are considering a staff report on the appealed application for a 50-storey mixed-use building at 2912 to 2926 Sheppard Avenue East, with 590 homes and 280 square metres of non-residential space across 43,370 square metres of floor area. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in October 2025 after council failed to decide on the applications. The report gives council's position ahead of the tribunal process.

title: 20, 40, 50, 70, 80 and 100 Cowdray Court Zoning By-law Amendment and Draft Plan of Subdivision Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: subdivision (land), zoning bylaws; subdivision of land, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The question before City Council: whether to approve a zoning amendment and subdivision for 20 to 100 Cowdray Court that would allow 2,157 homes in multiple tall buildings from 23 to 41 storeys, plus 2,238 square metres of retail space. The total floor area of 167,390 square metres represents a density about 5.2 times the lot area. The lands currently hold commercial buildings. The project would add significant housing density in the area.

title: 1212-1238 Kingston Road - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, redevelopment, rental housing; rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization, rental properties; rental units
brief: City Council decides whether to approve demolishing 10 rental units in a two-storey building at 1222 Kingston Road, as part of the redevelopment of 1212-1238 Kingston Road. The units would be replaced in the new development, and the proposal includes a Tenant Assistance Plan giving existing tenants the right to return at similar rents plus financial compensation. If the conditions are not met within the specified time, the City Clerk can add a charge of $20,000.00 per dwelling unit to the tax roll, like property taxes, as a lien on the land. Approval would allow the redevelopment to proceed.

title: 1883 McNicoll Avenue - Left Turn Prohibition
topics: safety, turn prohibitions (traffic); public safety
brief: City Council will decide whether to prohibit westbound left turns at all times at the intersection of McNicoll Avenue and the private driveway to 1883 McNicoll Avenue, about 75 metres west of Kennedy Road. Transportation Services says the ban would improve traffic flow and safety. Because the TTC operates on McNicoll Avenue, City Council approval is required.

title: Kingston Road and Kildonan Drive/Eastwood Avenue - Traffic Control Signals
topics: traffic, traffic control systems; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: City Council will decide whether to install traffic control signals at the intersection of Kingston Road and Kildonan Drive/Eastwood Avenue. Transportation Services says the signals are justified and would improve safety for all road users. Because the TTC runs transit service on Kingston Road, City Council approval is required rather than a community council decision.

title: 1212 to 1238 Kingston Road - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: commercial properties, mixed use areas, multi-unit dwellings, rezoning; multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings, office real estate; retail space, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: City Council decides whether to approve a zoning amendment for 1212 to 1238 Kingston Road that would allow a 10-storey mixed-use building with 200 homes, including 10 rental replacement units. The proposal has 13,276 square metres of floor area, 596 square metres of ground-floor commercial space, and 101 parking spaces across two underground levels. The project would add housing density and rental replacement units along Kingston Road.

title: Visitor Parking Requirements for New Development
topics: parking spaces, visitors; parking spots, tourists; travellers
brief: Visitor parking rules for new developments would stay exactly as they are. A staff report recommends no changes to the visitor parking standards in Zoning By-law 569-2013, noting that a 2024 provincial law (Bill 185) already stops the city from requiring parking, other than bicycle parking, in major transit station areas, which cover much of Parking Zone A. Monitoring of how visitor spots are actually used in Zones A and B backs keeping the current standards, and City Council will decide whether to accept the no-change recommendation.

title: 405 Sherbourne Street - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: by-laws, heritage properties; bylaws, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The 405 Sherbourne Street redevelopment also touches a designated heritage property in the Cabbagetown Northwest Heritage Conservation District. City Council is asked to approve alterations under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act in connection with the proposed 35-storey building. The heritage permit decision runs alongside the zoning decision for the same site.

title: 405 Sherbourne Street - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City wants to upsize its own housing project at 405 Sherbourne Street from 26 to 35 storeys. City Council is asked to approve a City-initiated zoning change to allow a 35-storey (120-metre) mixed-use building with 301 homes, up to 90 of them affordable, and 229 square metres of ground-floor community space. The current zoning permits 267 rental units; the new plan adds more homes and a higher share of two- and three-bedroom units.

title: 9 Shortt Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A City-owned surface parking lot at 9 Shortt Street would become a Toronto Builds mixed-use residential project with two buildings of 41 and 6 storeys. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change, with a holding provision, to allow 458 market and affordable rental homes, 497 square metres of commercial space, and 35,071 square metres of residential floor area. The project is earmarked for affordable housing delivery on public land.

title: Housing Action Plan: Incorporating Low-rise Residential Lands into Zoning By-law 569-2013 -   Etobicoke York District - Final Report
topics: by-laws, residential properties; bylaws, residential real estate
brief: Low-rise residential lands in the Etobicoke York District would be folded into the city-wide Zoning By-law 569-2013 under the third phase of a cleanup project. City Council is asked to approve the zoning changes, which would align local rules with former municipal standards and recent city-wide amendments. Staff say the change removes barriers, simplifies administration, and helps create more housing under the Housing Action Plan.

title: Scarborough Centre Secondary Plan - Final Report
topics: official plan amendments, urban design; civic improvements
brief: Scarborough's downtown is getting a new long-term growth plan. City Council is asked to adopt the Scarborough Centre Secondary Plan and Official Plan Amendment 871, replacing the 2005 plan for about 175 hectares across Wards 21 and 24. The plan sets the framework for growth around the future Line 2 East Extension subway station, aiming for a connected and sustainable centre.

title: Preserving Employment Lands and Protecting Local Jobs
topics: employment areas; employment districts; employment zones
brief: The item asks council to press the provincial housing minister to approve Official Plan Amendment 804, aimed at preserving Toronto's employment lands and protecting local jobs. The motion comes as four employment-land conversion applications sit before the Ontario Land Tribunal, raising the stakes for where job-supporting land can be kept. The item notes that industrial building permits in the city's employment lands have averaged over $63 million a year from 2021 to 2024, which it presents as a sign of employer confidence in those lands.

title: Toronto Builds - 1631 and 1641 Queen Street East, and 1080 (Portion) and 1090 Eastern Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City-owned land at 1631 and 1641 Queen Street East and 1080 and 1090 Eastern Avenue would be redeveloped under the Toronto Builds program (formerly Housing Now) into a mixed-use mid-rise of up to 6 storeys on Queen Street East and a residential building of up to 18 storeys on Eastern Avenue. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes to allow about 328 homes, 20 to 30 percent of them affordable, plus a childcare facility and street-facing shops. The existing Toronto Community Housing building at 1080 Eastern Avenue would stay. Council previously authorized about $48 million in financial incentives over a 99-year term to support up to 620 affordable rental homes through the Housing Now initiative (item 2020.CC21.3); this rezoning is a step toward delivering them.

title: 510 Jarvis Street - Proposed Designation By-Law under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
topics: by-laws, heritage properties; bylaws, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Like its neighbour at 506 Jarvis, the circa-1888 Annex-style property at 510 Jarvis Street faces an owner objection to heritage designation. City Council is asked to affirm its October 2025 intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The property helps define the 19th-century character of the Upper Jarvis block.

title: 506 Jarvis Street - Proposed Designation By-Law under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
topics: by-laws, heritage properties; bylaws, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The owner of 506 Jarvis Street has objected to heritage designation, and Council decides whether to hold its ground. City Council is asked to affirm its October 2025 intention to designate the circa-1888 Annex-style property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The building stands on the west side of Jarvis Street in Church-Wellesley.

title: 344 Jarvis Street - Proposed Designation By-Law under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
topics: by-laws, heritage properties; bylaws, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The owner of 344 Jarvis Street has formally objected to the city's plan to designate the property, and council must now decide whether to proceed anyway. City Council is asked to affirm its October 2025 decision stating its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The property sits on the west side of Jarvis Street in the Church-Wellesley neighbourhood.

title: 1497 Queen Street West - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: An early-20th-century, three-storey main-street commercial building at 1497 Queen Street West in South Parkdale is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The property sits on the south side of Queen Street West between Dowling and Beaty avenues.

title: 140-150 Borough Drive - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The Scarborough Civic Centre at 140-150 Borough Drive is proposed for heritage designation. City Council is asked to state its intention to designate the civic centre under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The designation would protect the cultural heritage value of the landmark building in the Bendale-Glen Andrew neighbourhood.

title: 350, 360, 364 Evans Avenue and 14 - 16 Arnold Street- Official Plan Amendment- Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments;
brief: The owner of 350, 360 and 364 Evans Avenue and 14 to 16 Arnold Street wants to redesignate the site from Core Employment Areas to Mixed Use Areas, and appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in June 2025 after council missed its deadline. Case management conferences were held in September 2025 and are scheduled again for February 25, 2026. City staff recommend the City Solicitor and planners oppose the conversion, and City Council will decide.

title: 1543 - 1551 The Queensway and 66 and 76 Fordhouse Boulevard - Official Plan Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments;
brief: An application to convert 1543 to 1551 The Queensway and 66 and 76 Fordhouse Boulevard from General Employment Areas to Mixed Use Areas is headed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, after the applicant appealed in June 2025 over council's missed deadline. A case management conference was held in September 2025, with a second set for February 25, 2026. City staff recommend the City Solicitor and planners oppose the conversion at the hearing, and City Council will decide whether to adopt that stance.

title: 125 The Queensway - Official Plan Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments;
brief: The owner of 125 The Queensway applied to redesignate the site from General Employment Areas to Mixed Use Areas, then appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in October 2025 after council did not decide in time. City staff recommend the City Solicitor and planners attend the hearing and oppose the application in its current form. City Council will decide whether to back that position.

title: 20 Leslie Street - Official Plan Amendment- Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments;
brief: The owner of 20 Leslie Street wants to change the site's designation from General Employment Areas to Mixed Use Areas, and after council missed the Planning Act decision deadline, the owner appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in October 2025. City staff want the City Solicitor and planners to attend the tribunal hearing and oppose the conversion in its current form. The Planning and Housing Committee's recommendation goes to City Council, which instructs the City's legal team.

title: Growing Space for Trees: Protecting and Enhancing the Tree Canopy While Supporting Infill Housing and Addressing Concerns with Iceberg Homes - Recommendation Report
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Toronto's tree canopy and new infill housing are on a collision course, and the rulebook for both could change. The Planning and Housing Committee is recommending Official Plan and zoning amendments that would protect growing space for trees as new housing goes up, including curbs on 'iceberg homes' whose basements sprawl wider than the home above. Staff consulted the public and stakeholders and revised the proposals in response, and City Council will make the final decision.

title: 2205 Sheppard Avenue East, Residences at Atria Inc. - Assumption of Services, Plan of Survey 66R-34936
topics: assumption of services, surveys (maps); cadastral surveys; legal boundary surveys; property surveys
brief: Staff recommend City Council assume the municipal services installed by Residences at Atria Inc. under a May 17, 2013 Section 37 agreement for the development at 2205 Sheppard Avenue East (Plan of Survey 66R-34936). Assumption means the City takes over maintenance of the infrastructure, and the report recommends releasing the performance guarantee held for the services.

title: 849 Eglinton Avenue East- Class 4 Noise Area Classification (NPC-300) - Final Report
topics: development, noise, residential properties; amplified music; construction noise; loud music; noise pollution; traffic noise, developing land; development (land); land development, residential real estate
brief: Staff recommend City Council classify the development at 849 Eglinton Avenue East as a Class 4 noise area under provincial guidelines administered by the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change, which allows higher daytime and nighttime sound limits for the residential units, offset by specified noise-control measures. An environmental noise analysis was prepared in support of the development. The classification affects how much nearby noise the new homes must tolerate.

title: 28-32 Evergreen Gardens - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report -  Approval
topics: exemptions, part lot control; exceptions
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve exempting 28-32 Evergreen Gardens from the part-lot-control provisions of the Planning Act so five townhouse units can be created as conveyable lots, along with a road-conveyance strip to widen the Bayview Avenue right-of-way and a shared rear swale. The exemption is the legal step that lets each townhouse be sold separately. The Director of Community Planning recommends approval.

title: Rawlinson Avenue between Eglinton Avenue and Broadway Avenue - Implementation of Permit Parking
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations, permit parking; no parking, on-street permit parking; parking permits, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Residents of Rawlinson Avenue between Eglinton Avenue and Broadway Avenue petitioned strongly for on-street permit parking. North York Community Council is asked to act on the request; under the permit-parking rules, a resident petition of at least 25 percent triggers a poll to decide the matter. If approved, residents on the street could buy permits to park there — a change that affects who can park on the street and when.

title: Recipient of the 2026 Agnes Macphail Award - Dr. Blair Bigham
topics: awards, commendations, nomination;
brief: The Agnes Macphail Award, established by the former Borough of East York to annually honour an outstanding volunteer within its old boundaries who upheld Agnes Macphail's values and causes, goes to Dr. Blair Bigham for 2026. The recognition committee chose him on January 5, 2026, and Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin's motion asks City Council to approve the choice.

title: Blue Bin Litter
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe (Ward 11, University-Rosedale) has filed an administrative inquiry asking city staff about Blue Bin litter since the province's Circular Materials took over Blue Bin collection on January 1. The inquiry's framing says residents have reported late and missed collections and sloppy bin handling that has scattered material, some now mixed into snowbanks, and asks: what are the city's plans to collect the litter, how many extra tax dollars the city expects to spend, and what steps it will take to recover those costs from Circular Materials. The item seeks a public staff response rather than a council decision.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Non-Competitive Contract with AmpThink for Temporary Network Expansion and Integration at Toronto Stadium
topics: executive committees, soccer, sports;
brief: City Council decides whether to approve a non-competitive contract with AmpThink Inc., worth $500,000 ($500,000 net of HST recoveries), for temporary network expansion and Wi-Fi at Toronto Stadium (BMO Field) for the World Cup. AmpThink is the stadium's incumbent network provider with equipment already mobilized, and staff say using them is the most efficient way to extend the network into Exhibition Place spaces and add temporary Wi-Fi that will be removed after the tournament. The contract affects the stadium's technology setup during and after the event.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2552, Kipling Grove Court, Chimney Swift Court, Minto 19 Glen Agar Inc.
topics: assumption of services, construction; building
brief: The decision on whether to take over the municipal services installed under the subdivision agreement for Plan 66M-2552 at Kipling Grove Court and Chimney Swift Court, contingent on approval of the companion parking and traffic report, and pass an assumption by-law rests with Council.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2564, 4208, 4210 and 4214 Dundas Street West, 4208 Dundas Development GP Inc.
topics: assumption of services;
brief: Taking over the municipal services installed under the subdivision agreement for Plan 66M-2564 near Dundas Street West, release the developer's performance guarantee, and pass an assumption by-law for the public highway goes to Council for a decision.

title: Application for a Clothing Drop Box Location Permit located at 2799 Weston Road
topics: charities, clothing drop boxes; charitable organizations; charity, clothes donation boxes; clothing bins
brief: Council has the final say on whether to decide on a clothing drop box location permit at 2799 Weston Road, after staff declined to issue it; the report presents both denying and approving the application as options.

title: Agreement to Collaborate with Hydro One Network Inc. for Construction on the Etobicoke Greenway Trail Project
topics: construction, trail systems; building, footpaths; multi-pupose trails; multi-purpose paths; multi-use pathways; multi-use trails; pedestrian trails; recreational trails; trail networks; trails; walking paths; waterfront trail
brief: Authorizing an agreement for Hydro One to build a 4 km multi-use trail, the Etobicoke Greenway Trail, in its corridor by late 2027 at its own expense, with the City taking over maintenance in December 2027 and Hydro One helping with costs for four years comes before Council. The report's figures include $1.5 million.

title: 829 The Queensway - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: mixed use areas, official plan amendments, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Council decides whether to approve a 15-storey mixed-use building at 829 The Queensway with about 332 homes and at least 590 square metres of non-residential space, including redesignating the rear of the site from employment to mixed-use lands.

title: 250 The East Mall - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Whether to approve redeveloping Cloverdale Mall at 250 The East Mall into a mixed-use community with 15 buildings of 6 to 41 storeys, about 5,536 homes in four phases, and a child care facility for the City in phase one now sits with Council. The plan also includes community agency space and two new public parks, with the mall, including its grocery store, staying partly open during construction.

title: Team Canada Olympic Spirit(s): Extension of Alcohol Sales and Service Hours During 2026 Milano Cortina Winter Olympics
topics: Olympic Games; olympics; paralympic games
brief: Extending alcohol sales and service hours to begin at 6:00 a.m, goes to City Council for approval. from February 5 to February 22, 2026, so local cafes and restaurants can serve customers watching the Milano Cortina Winter Olympics — some events start at 6:00 a.m. Toronto time. The City Solicitor would introduce the by-law.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37/45 Funds for upgrades to Seaton Park
topics: finance (sc);
brief: Authorizing a one-time $343,737.02 increase to the 2026 operating budget — funded by $343,737.02 in development-related community benefit (Section 37/45) funds — so the Bloor-Annex Business Improvement Area can upgrade Seaton Park, a small park near Bathurst station plagued by vandalism and trash that the BIA now maintains daily, goes to City Council for approval. The funds come from five Annex-area developments: $245,346.80, $12,995.35, $62.57, $332.30 and $85,000.

title: Amending Item 2022.NY33.7 - 241 Redpath Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Final Report
topics: demolitions;
brief: City Council approved demolishing and replacing 46 rental units at 241 Redpath Avenue in 2022, with tenant assistance based on an estimated 36-month displacement — but the project ran long after tenants moved out. Council is now asked to require the owner to amend its tenant assistance agreement to provide enhanced support, including top-up rent gap payments when tenants sign leases for replacement units. The owner has separately asked to reduce a cash contribution from a minor variance, saying it would offset the cost of the extra tenant help.

title: Rorschach Brewing Company By-the-Glass Permit Application to the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Telling the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that it supports a by-the-glass Manufacturer's Limited Liquor Sales Licence for Rorschach Brewing Company's new innovation brewery, taproom and retail store at 815 Kipling Avenue in Etobicoke-Lakeshore, goes to City Council for a decision. Rorschach opened in Leslieville in 2017.

title: C'est What Brewing at the Market By-the-Glass Permit Application to the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Telling the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that it supports a by-the-glass Manufacturer's Limited Liquor Sales Licence for C'est What Brewing at the Market — a proposed craft brewery, beer store and tasting room from Durham Brewing Company on the lower level of the St. Lawrence Market's south building at 91 Front Street East — goes to City Council for a decision. The team founded C'est What, Toronto's first craft beer bar, in 1988.

title: Development Charges By-law 1137-2022 - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: development charges;
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor is seeking Council's direction on the one remaining appeal of the City's Development Charges By-law 1137-2022, from Dunpar Developments Incorporated, ahead of a 14-day hearing starting June 1, 2026. The matter is urgent given procedural timelines. The recommendations are confidential as legal advice.

title: 250 to 258 Viewmount Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor is seeking Council's direction on an Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of a proposed 40-storey residential building with 477 homes at 250 to 258 Viewmount Avenue, ahead of an April 13, 2026 hearing. The applicant appealed in January 2025 after Council failed to decide in time; the matter is urgent. The recommendations are confidential as legal advice.

title: 278 to 280 Viewmount Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor is seeking Council's direction on an Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of a proposed 33-storey residential building with 342 homes at 278 to 280 Viewmount Avenue. The applicant appealed in December 2023 after Council failed to decide in time; the matter is urgent. The recommendations are confidential as legal advice.

title: 1799 St. Clair Avenue West - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: high rise buildings, zoning bylaws; tall buildings, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor is seeking Council's direction on an Ontario Land Tribunal hearing about a proposed three-tower development at 1799 St. Clair Avenue West. The recommendations are confidential as they are legal advice.

title: Business Improvement Areas - 2026 Operating Budgets - Report 1
topics: business improvement areas, operating budgets; bia; business improvement associations
brief: Adopting and certify the 2026 operating budgets and levy requirements of the first group of Business Improvement Areas — 64 of the City's 85 BIAs, with the remaining 21 coming by the second quarter of 2026, goes to City Council for approval. Approval lets the City collect the special levy from commercial and industrial properties in those areas; no City funding is required.

title: Council Member Appointments to the Hockey Hall of Fame Board of Directors
topics: appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is asked to consider members' interest and appoint three councillors as nominees for election to the Hockey Hall of Fame Board of Directors, for a term from the spring 2026 annual general meeting to spring 2027.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Authority to Install FIFA World Cup 2026 Banners on Bridge Structures
topics: sports, tourism;
brief: With Toronto hosting FIFA World Cup 2026 matches, City Council is asked to let the General Manager of Transportation Services approve FIFA World Cup 2026 banner locations on bridge structures and issue permits beyond the current 14-day display limit. Current rules restrict banners to pre-approved bridge spots for 14 days, which staff say is insufficient for an event of this scale.

title: Waiving Application Fees to Support the Redevelopment of Safehaven, 1173 Bloor Street West
topics: non-profit organizations, zoning bylaws; non profit; nonprofit; not-for-profit organizations, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Safehaven, a non-profit providing residential and respite care to children and adults with medical complexities and developmental disabilities for over 35 years, is redeveloping its 1173 Bloor Street West facility to serve 68 clients (38 children's beds, 30 adult beds), plus affordable barrier-free rental homes. City Council is asked to waive the City's development application fees for the Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendments the project needs, since existing affordable-housing fee waivers cannot cover the non-residential clinic and retail spaces.

title: 353 to 355 Sherbourne Street and 157 Carlton Street - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
brief: Approving alterations to the St. Luke's United Church property at 353 to 355 Sherbourne Street and 157 Carlton Street, designated under the Ontario Heritage Act, to allow a 48-storey tower with a 4-storey mixed-use podium, and to authorize a heritage easement agreement with the owner, goes to City Council for approval. The property sits in the Cabbagetown Northwest Heritage Conservation District and includes an 1887 church by architects Langley and Burke.

title: Amending Item 2024.TE15.12 - 1266 Queen Street West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal of Official Plan Amendment and Approval of Zoning By-law Amendment
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Amending its 2024 decision on the zoning by-law amendment for 1266 Queen Street West, swapping in an updated attachment so minor changes requested by the new owner are reflected now that the preconditions for introducing the bills are met, goes to City Council for approval. Council had approved the zoning change in July 2024 and refused the Official Plan amendment as unnecessary.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will introduce general bills and confirming bills, the formal by-laws that enact Council's decisions as law. The source material gives no further detail.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will introduce general bills and confirming bills — the formal by-laws that turn Council's decisions into law. The source material gives no further detail.

title: Fare Collection Update
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, fare media, fares, transit fares; air fares; airline fares; rail fares; taxi fares; transportation fares, transit tickets; transit tokens, ttc
brief: TTC staff update the Board on the TTC-Metrolinx Master E-Fare Collection Outsourcing Agreement, the 2012 deal whose initial 15-year term expires on November 28, 2027, with renewal options. The Board is asked to adopt the recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 and keep that information confidential until final negotiations are complete and all agreements are executed. The decision shapes how the TTC's fare collection system is managed after 2027.

title: SRT Busway Acceleration Plan
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, bus lines, urban transit systems; coach lines; intercity bus lines; intercity buses; motor coach lines; motorcoach lines; tour bus operators, local transit authorities; municipal transit authorities; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; transit agencies; transit operating agencies, ttc
brief: TTC staff update the Board on the acceleration plan targeting the start of revenue service on the SRT Busway by September 30, 2026. The report follows up on the July 2025 update and the Board's May 2025 direction to work with the City Manager, Transportation Services and the Transit Expansion Division to expedite land acquisitions and permits for the busway. The Board is asked to keep the information in Confidential Attachment 1 private.

title: Declaration of Surplus Property - 1870 Avenue Road, Southern Portion of Roe Loop
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, [attributes in property], lots; ttc
brief: Declaring the southern portion of Roe Loop at 1870 Avenue Road, currently used as a bus loop, surplus to the TTC's operating needs goes to the TTC Board. The roughly 620-square-metre parcel would be released to the City of Toronto for disposal under the TTC's surplus property policy and the city's surplus property process. The decision determines whether the land can be sold or repurposed by the city.

title: Revitalizing TTC Branded Merchandise: Progress, Insights, and Strategic Direction
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, revenue generation, sales (events), special sales; auctions, bankruptcy sales; closing sales; fire sales; going out of business sales, revenue tools, ttc
brief: TTC staff report back to the Board on the revitalization of TTC-branded merchandise, following the Board's June 2025 direction to assess a standalone TTC retail store at Davisville Station or another location. The 2025 program added new merchandise, pop-up retail and partner collaborations, but the review of peer agencies and market interest concluded that a standalone brick-and-mortar store is not the most effective approach at this time. The Board is asked to receive the progress report and consider the strategic direction.

title: Presentation: Developing a Surface Transit Revitalization Plan
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, streetcars; street-cars, ttc
brief: Jonathan English, founding principal of Infrastory Insights, will present to the TTC Board on developing a surface transit revitalization plan. The presentation covers steps to improve the speed and reliability of the streetcar network as well as new LRT lines. The Board is asked to receive the presentation.

title: Presentation: Opportunities to improve Transit Signal Priority in Toronto
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, traffic signal timing, traffic signals; advanced green; amber light phase; coordination of traffic signals; left turn arrow phase; left turn phase; pedestrian crossover timing; signal timing; traffic light timing; traffic signal operations; traffic signal phases; traffic signal synchronization, fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, ttc
brief: Narayan Donaldson, an integrated mobility consultant with Mobycon, will present to the TTC Board on opportunities to improve transit signal priority in Toronto. The presentation covers the strengths and weaknesses of the signal priority system used on Toronto's streetcar, bus and LRT networks, compares it with a system used in the Netherlands and suggests improvements. The Board is asked to receive the presentation.

title: Approved Minutes of the Advisory Committee on Accessible Transit (ACAT) General Monthly Meeting of November 27 and December 18, 2025
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, accessibility, accessibility standards, accessible taxicabs; accessibility legislation; aoda, barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the TTC Board will receive the approved minutes of the Advisory Committee on Accessible Transit (ACAT) general monthly meetings of November 27 and December 18, 2025. The November meeting covered the Wheel-Trans e-bus procurement plan, the community safety and well-being plan and the cancelled 2025 Halloween Fest; the December meeting covered the Line 6 Finch West LRT opening and accessibility feedback, plus bus stop changes in the East Mall-Burnhamthorpe area. The Board is asked to receive the minutes for information.

title: Chief Executive Officer’s Report - February 2026
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, subway stations, subways; ttc, underground
brief: This is a procedural item: the TTC Board will receive the CEO's Report for February 2026, the monthly performance overview created in 2012. This edition focuses on subway service, with key performance indicators through the end of November 2025 and station makeovers; copies also go to City Council members, the City Manager and the CFO and are posted publicly. The Board is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Summary of Contract Awards Over $5 million from June 23, 2025 to December 31, 2025
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, contracts, delegation of authority, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, signing authorities, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the TTC Board will receive a summary of contracts awarded between June 23, 2025 and December 31, 2025 under the CEO's delegated authority that exceed $5 million. The reporting follows the Board's June 2025 decision to raise the CEO's contract award authority from $5 million to the approved budget amount, with a requirement for semi-annual reports on awards over $5 million. The Board is asked to receive the summary.

title: Chief Executive Officer Performance and Objectives
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, employees; staff, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the TTC Board will receive information on the Chief Executive Officer's performance and objectives. The Board is asked to keep the information in Confidential Attachment 1 private in its entirety, as it concerns personal matters about an identifiable individual.

title: Collective Bargaining Update
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, labour relations, unions; collective bargaining; employee relations; labor relations; union-management relations, labour unions; trade unions, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the TTC Board will receive an in-camera (private) update on collective bargaining. The Board is asked to keep the information confidential in its entirety, as it concerns labour relations and employee negotiations.

title: Building on Inclusive Governance Practices
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, accountability, equity, governance; employment equity; fair wage; pay equity, governance structure; municipal governance, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the TTC Board, in confidential session, will receive education and training on building inclusive governance practices, covering reflections on governance since the first session, accountability frameworks and strategies for aligning board actions with the TTC's strategic directions. The Board is asked to authorize the public release of the training materials.

title: Film Office Staff Updates
body: Film, Television and Digital Media Advisory Board
brief: This is an information item: the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture will report on organizational and staffing changes in the Film Office, and staff will present a year-end overview of 2025 film permitting activity. No decision is attached.

title: FIFA 2026 Update
body: Film, Television and Digital Media Advisory Board
brief: This is an information item: the FIFA Secretariat will outline key World Cup 2026 initiatives and host-city operations, and Film Office staff will update the board on expected impacts to film production during the tournament and strategies to manage them. No decision is attached.

title: McCleary Development Update
body: Film, Television and Digital Media Advisory Board
topics: boards of management, committee meetings, film and television industry; boards of directors; boards of governors, cinema industry; film and television cluster; film production; movie industry; television industry
brief: This is an information item: CreateTO and City Planning staff will update the board on development activities in the McCleary District in the Port Lands. No decision is attached.

title: Indigenous Identity Verification
topics: First Nations, community & life (sc); aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples
brief: The Aboriginal Affairs Advisory Committee discussed Indigenous identity verification and possible City requests on this topic. The committee established a working group to conduct an in-depth review and develop guidelines on Indigenous identity verification, to be brought back to the committee as recommendations. The working group members are Cynthia Bell, Suzanne Brunelle, Paige Kimiksana-Kreps, Millie Knapp and Patti Pettigrew, with Dawn Sutherland as chair.

title: Council Advisory Committee Authorities and Processes
topics: advisory committees, council items; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups, clauses; items (council); items before council
brief: This is a procedural item: City Clerk staff will give the committee a presentation on how Council advisory committees are structured, their powers, and how motions move through the Council agenda. No decision is required.

title: Terms of Reference Review
topics: advisory committees; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups
brief: This is a procedural item: the Aboriginal Affairs Advisory Committee will discuss Indigenous-led governance to support its Terms of Reference review, as directed by Council. Parts of the meeting will be held in closed session.

title: Recognition of Staff at Exhibition Place - United Way Campaign and Community Events Program
topics: Exhibition Place, employee recognition; 25 year club; employee awards; public service awards; service awards; service recognition; years of service; years of service awards
brief: A decision on recognizing Catherine de Nobriga for her work on the 2025 United Way campaign, which raised $1,017.35 toward a 21-year Exhibition Place total of $101,785.78 sits with the Exhibition Place board. The board is also asked to recognize the pay-what-you-can 2025 Community Events Program, which raised $2,754.76 in total, with $1,629.76 donated to CAMH and $1,125.00 to HeARTLab CAMH.

title: Community Liaison Meeting - November 20, 2025
topics: Exhibition Place, community outreach; awareness programs; community engagement; outreach; promotion (communication); public outreach
brief: This is an information item: the Exhibition Place board receives a summary of the community liaison meeting held November 20, 2025, attended by 25 community members in person and online. No policy change is proposed.

title: Tenant Liaison Meeting - December 11, 2025
topics: Exhibition Place, commercial tenants;
brief: This is an information item: the Exhibition Place board receives a summary of the tenant liaison meeting held December 11, 2025, at the Enercare Centre. No policy change is proposed.

title: Nighttime Economy - Letter of Support
topics: Exhibition Place, economic development, night; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing
brief: Exhibition Place hosts more than 2,000 events and over 6 million visitors a year, generating over $594 million in annual economic impact. The board is asked to direct its CEO to keep providing letters of support for late-night extended-hours events at tenanted facilities, so tenants can apply for temporary extensions to sell alcohol at licensed locations. The letters are part of the City's nighttime economy support.

title: Community Partnership Policy Update
topics: Exhibition Place, community partners, partnerships;
brief: This is an information item: the Exhibition Place board receives an update on its community partnership engagements and commitments for 2025 under the Community Partnership Policy approved in 2025. No policy change is proposed.

title: Business Travel IAVM and participation in Venue Management School
topics: Exhibition Place, business travel (municipal), expenses; corporate travel
brief: The decision on whether to authorize travel costs of up to $6,500 each plus HST for two staff to attend the International Association of Venue Managers school in Palm Springs, California, from June 6 to June 11, 2026 rests with the Exhibition Place board. The trip covers the second year of the program for one coordinator and the first year for another.

title: Multi-year Agreement with a Consumer Show Client

brief: The Exhibition Place board has the final say on whether to approve multi-year licence agreements for 2026-2028 with a consumer show client for the Enercare Centre and the Better Living Centre, on the standard licence terms. The financial details stay confidential to protect negotiating positions.

title: Multi-year Agreement with a Tradeshow Client
topics: Exhibition Place, agreements; tenancy agreements
brief: The Exhibition Place board decides whether to approve multi-year licence agreements for 2027-2028 with a tradeshow client for the Enercare Centre, on the standard licence terms. The financial details stay confidential to protect negotiating positions.

title: Structural, IT Infrastructure, and Electrical Upgrades at the Administration Building

brief: The Exhibition Place board decides whether to approve a $649,900.00 contract (excluding HST, and including a $10,000.00 cash allowance) with Ritestart Limited for structural, IT infrastructure, and electrical upgrades at the Administration Building. The project is urgent: the IT systems are at end of life and the main floor structural framing is deficient, posing a potential safety concern. Ritestart was the sole compliant bidder.

title: 10-Year Circular Economy Road Map

brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council approve alterations to the St. Luke's United Church complex at 353-355 Sherbourne Street and 157 Carlton Street — a significant building in the Cabbagetown Northwest Heritage Conservation District designed by Langley and Burke in 1887, with additions in 1912, 1929 and 1962 — in connection with a proposed 48-storey residential tower with a 4-storey mixed-use podium, and authorize a Heritage Easement Agreement with the owner. title: 405 Sherbourne Street - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council approve alterations to the designated heritage property at 405 Sherbourne Street — part of the Cabbagetown Northwest Heritage Conservation District — in connection with a proposed 35-storey mixed-use building replacing a surface parking lot. The City-owned site is part of the Toronto Builds (formerly Housing Now) initiative; a new zoning application seeks more density than the 25-storey building approved in July 2021 to allow more two- and three-bedroom units. The proposal would provide 301 new rental housing units, with design intended to fit the heritage district.

title: 377 Dundas Street West, 160 Huron Street and 1 Edmund Gate - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council add three properties to the City's Heritage Register: 377 Dundas Street West (a two-and-a-half-storey house-form building in Kensington-Chinatown), 160 Huron Street (three buildings dating from about 1890 and 1913–1914, including a four-storey walk-up apartment) and 1 Edmund Gate in the Casa Loma area. title: 140-150 Borough Drive - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate 140-150 Borough Drive — the Scarborough Civic Centre — under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. Completed in 1973 and designed by Canadian architect Raymond Moriyama (1929–2023) as a shared facility for the former Borough of Scarborough and the Scarborough Board of Education, it is a Modern Expressionist building with a circular central core, two half-pyramid office wings, Albert Campbell Square and the Ceremonial Plaza. Designation is the first legal step toward protecting the property's heritage attributes.

title: 1497 Queen Street West - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage properties, planning; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Heritage staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate 1497 Queen Street West in South Parkdale under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. Built in 1924–1925 with a third storey added in 1925–1926, the early-20th-century 3-storey main street commercial block — with Edwardian Classical elements — housed the Lakeside Recreation Club (later Lakeside Bowling & Billiards) with bowling lanes and a billiards room for fifty-five years between 1925 and 1980. Designation is the first legal step toward protecting the property's heritage attributes.

brief: The recommended 2026-2035 Capital Budget and Plan, totalling $16.657 billion including a 2026 capital budget of $1.635 billion, goes to the TTC Board for approval, along with endorsement of the updated 2026-2040 Capital Investment Plan and companion Real Estate Investment Plan, representing about $54 billion in 15-year investments. The 10-year plan allocates 63 percent to keeping transit in a state of good repair, 4 percent to safety and legislated requirements, and 33 percent to service improvement and growth projects; the documents also cite figures of $302.8 million, $168.8 million, $253.4 million, $141.6 million, $53, $616 million, $37, $15, $14, $28.7 million, $135.0 million and $106.3 million.
